# ForkMesh documentation

> **Serving stack note.** Since 2026-09-24 the App runs on three
> self-hosted core nodes instead of Cloudflare Workers, D1 and Durable Objects
> (see `docs/README.md` in the repository for the developer docs). Pages that
> describe the earlier Cloudflare deployment and do **not** apply as written:
>
> - Cloudflare Worker deployment, limits and bootstrap:
>   [operations/worker-split.md](operations/worker-split.md),
>   [operations/cloudflare-free-tier-audit.md](operations/cloudflare-free-tier-audit.md),
>   [operations/automation-and-cloudflare-bootstrap.md](operations/automation-and-cloudflare-bootstrap.md),
>   [cloudflare-workers-ai-coding-agent.md](cloudflare-workers-ai-coding-agent.md).
> - The production D1 database: [operations/d1-database-cleanup-plan.md](operations/d1-database-cleanup-plan.md)
>   (the database is now rqlite; see `docs/REKEY.md`).
> - The production desktop control node and its `wrangler tail` streams:
>   [operations/desktop-control-node.md](operations/desktop-control-node.md).
> - The production mirror fleet (`mirrorN.forkmesh.com`, Cloudflare Tunnel):
>   [operations/mirror-node.md](operations/mirror-node.md),
>   [operations/direct-https-mirror-gateway.md](operations/direct-https-mirror-gateway.md),
>   [operations/git-ssh-gateway.md](operations/git-ssh-gateway.md). The
>   core nodes and runners are in `docs/deploy/README.md` and `docs/RUNNERS.md`.
> - [external-dependency-map.md](external-dependency-map.md) lists
>   the Cloudflare-era outside services; the core nodes drop most of them.
> - Legacy custody and historical plans: [operations/legacy-solana-custody-migration.md](operations/legacy-solana-custody-migration.md),
>   `superpowers/`.
>
> Protocol, security and product pages apply to both.

- `sync-status.md` — shared synchronization state model, fixture, and client parity.
- `forge-sync.md` — two-way issue sync with external forges: provider contract, conflicts, and controls.
- `availability-proof.md` — availability proof, trusted quorum, and risk score model.
- `crisis-preservation.md` — crisis scenarios, time- and access-bound preservation plans, evidence-only coverage, and drills.
- `offline-sync.md` — signed removable-media exports, resumable bounded fetches, limited-replica advertisements, reconciliation, and rollback.
- `transports.md` — transport adapters, anonymity postures, leak tracing, failover, health states, and address advertisement, bound to `conformance/transports/v1` cases.

- `*.schema.json` — machine-readable configuration and protocol schemas.

pages.title: Getting started with ForkMesh
pages.description: This guide takes you from a new machine to a running desktop node, a repository on the mesh, working chat, and your first change.
pages.markdown:
# Getting started with ForkMesh

This guide takes you from a new machine to a running desktop node, a repository
on the mesh, working chat, and your first change.

## Choose how to install

The fastest path is the published, SHA-256-verified installer:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh | bash
```

If you want to change ForkMesh itself, clone the source and run the desktop app (Qt):

```sh
git clone https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh
cd forkmesh
./desktop/run.sh
```

The source build needs Qt 6.4 or newer with Widgets, Network, SVG, Concurrent,
and, on Linux, D-Bus; CMake 3.16 or newer; OpenSSL development headers; Git; a
C++17 compiler; and the `openssl` command. Exact package commands and manual
build instructions are in the [desktop app guide](qt-client.md).

Which platforms have signed prebuilt packages, and how to upgrade, roll back,
or uninstall, is listed in the
[installation support matrix](install-support-matrix.md).

## Your first five minutes

1. Launch ForkMesh. A local Ed25519 node identity and a fun temporary node name
   are created automatically. The client connects to the default mainnode; no
   server URL is required.
2. Sign in or create an account from **Settings** if you want a portable public
   username. The node identity remains on this device.
3. Wait for the initial ForkMesh project mirror to finish syncing. A fresh
   install opens it automatically.
4. Open **Chat**, choose a conversation or repository channel, type in the
   composer at the bottom, and press Enter. Signed-in users can also reply in
   mirrored World office channels; the client obtains the scoped room access
   and sends the message over its encrypted office socket.
5. Open **Repos** and choose one of these paths:

   - **New repository** creates a Git repository, optional README, local mirror,
     and signed catalog entry.
   - **Add local repo** selects an existing local `git init`/`git clone`
     directory and asks whether it is public or private.
   - **Repos → Fork** makes an independent writable copy of a repository you
     found on the mesh.

Public repositories appear in the network catalog. Private repositories remain
hidden from public browse and clone routes unless you explicitly share them.
ForkMesh publishes signed metadata; it does not publish a local filesystem path.

## Keyboard and accessible browsing

The responsive dashboard supports the same repository journeys with a keyboard,
pointer, or touch screen. Press **Control+K** (or **Command+K** on macOS) to open
the command palette from any dashboard page. Type to filter its actions, use
Up/Down to select, Enter to run, and Escape to close and return focus. Press
**/** outside a text field to search and **T** on a repository to find a file.

The first Tab stop skips directly to main content. Focus stays visibly outlined;
light and dark themes meet the dashboard contrast target; browser zoom up to
200% reflows to the compact layout; and operating-system reduced-motion and
forced-colors preferences are honored. Clone commands remain selectable beside
their Copy buttons, and copy results are announced. If repository discovery is
offline, use **Retry repository list** after reconnecting; the page does not
discard your local theme or repository cache.

## Make a change

You can use normal Git commands in the repository folder:

```sh
git switch -c docs/my-change
# edit files
git add -A
git commit -m "docs: explain my change"
```

Or stay in the desktop application:

1. Open the repository, then **Code → Branches → New branch**.
2. Edit files in your editor or ForkMesh's file view.
3. Open **Code → Changes**, enter a commit message, then choose **Commit** or
   **Commit & push**.
4. For a PR within a repository you own, return to **Code → Branches**, select
   the feature branch, and choose **Create PR**.

For an upstream project, fork it first. In the writable fork, open
**Pulls → New pull request**, select the upstream owner as **Target node**, and
choose `main` as the base and your feature branch as the head. That sends the
signed PR to the owner's inbox; the relay queues it even when the owning node is
offline.
See [Contributing](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-a-pull-request) for the complete
review checklist.

## Where ForkMesh stores data

Use **Settings → Data** for the authoritative paths on your machine. That page
can open each directory and export or restore configuration data.

Everything ForkMesh keeps on disk lives in one place, the projects folder:

```text
~/projects/forkmesh/                the ForkMesh project
  src/                              the source checkout it builds and updates from
  data/                             identity, chat, agents, mirrors, local stores
  config/ForkMesh/ForkMesh.conf     preferences
  ssh/                              keys and known hosts for hosts and mirrors
  logs/diagnostics/                 action and UI-stall journals
  state/  cache/                    lock file; disposable cache
  toolchain/  builds/  worktrees/   shared build tooling
~/projects/<project>/               any other project, fully isolated:
  data/ config/ ssh/ logs/ state/ cache/   its own files, nothing shared
```

Pick or add a project with the logo at the far left of the top bar. A project
can start with no repository, no relay and only the plugins you choose; each
one runs as its own process with its own identity folder, settings and logs.

An install from before this layout kept these in `~/.local/share/ForkMesh`,
`~/.config/ForkMesh`, `~/.cache/ForkMesh` and `~/.forkmesh`. ForkMesh moves them
into `~/projects/forkmesh` the first time it starts (a rename, so it is instant)
and leaves a link at each old path so other tools keep working; **Settings →
Data** lists those links and can remove them. If you run ForkMesh from a source
checkout at `~/projects/forkmesh`, run `python3 tools/forkmesh_layout.py` first:
it shows, and with `apply` performs, the move of the checkout into `src/`.
Setting `FORKMESH_HOME` or `FORKMESH_PROJECTS_DIR` places the layout elsewhere;
a non-default `XDG_DATA_HOME` keeps a run on the XDG paths it names.

Do not delete application data casually: it contains the private identity key
for this node. Prefer **Settings → Data → Export configuration** before moving
machines or testing recovery.

Upgrading, rolling back, and uninstalling keep these directories.
`curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/uninstall.sh | bash` removes only the program.
Add `-s -- --purge` to erase your data as well; it asks for confirmation first.

## If something does not work

- Build failure: check the dependency and clean-build sections in the
  [desktop app guide](qt-client.md#build-and-run-from-source).
- Cannot type or send in chat: select a conversation first. World office replies
  also require a signed-in account on this node; reconnect after signing in so
  the client can obtain room access.
- Repository is read-only: use **Fork** to create a local working copy.
- A branch has no **Create PR** action: it must differ from the default branch
  and the repository must have a writable working tree. For an upstream PR, use
  **Pulls → New pull request** and select the upstream target node.
- Network or UI problem: use the built-in diagnostics and logs described in
  [desktop app diagnostics](qt-client.md#logs-and-diagnostics).

Next: [learn the desktop app](qt-client.md), [open a pull
request](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-a-pull-request), or browse the
[documentation index](README.md).

pages.title: ForkMesh product promise: proof and measurement
pages.description: ForkMesh lets developers collaborate on, mirror, and preserve source-code repositories across independent hosts—without relying on any single hosting provider.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh product promise: proof and measurement

> ForkMesh lets developers collaborate on, mirror, and preserve source-code repositories across independent hosts—without relying on any single hosting provider.

This is the canonical product promise. Keep the sentence unchanged on primary
product and commercial surfaces. `Your Code, Your World.` is the supporting
slogan, not a replacement promise.

## Four-step proof

Use a disposable **public** repository. The public failover proof does not apply
to a private repository, an unverified endpoint, or a repository with only one
eligible copy. Record the source and mirror node names, the stable clone URL,
the expected commit, and start/end times. Never delete the source repository as
part of this drill.

### 1. Collaborate

Open the repository in the [ForkMesh app](https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh/issues)
and create or review a signed issue, discussion, or pull request. Confirm the
record appears from the live repository view. Familiar Git terms—repository,
mirror, host, commit, issue, pull request, and clone—are intentional.

### 2. Add an independent mirror

Use the repository **Mirrors** tab to ask another node to mirror it, then accept
the request on that node. Operators may instead use **Network → Hosts** to add
and deploy a separate host. Wait until the repository profile reports that the
mirror is online, integrity is `ok`, its signed health is fresh, and its commit
matches the expected source commit. A configured or syncing host is not proof.

### 3. Take the source mirror offline

On the managed source host, stop `forkmesh-mirror-node` through its service
manager. The desktop is only a client and is not part of the serving path.
Wait until the source mirror is reported offline while the independent mirror
remains eligible. Do not stop the relay or the mirror under test.

### 4. Clone again

Clone the same stable URL into a new directory and compare the checked-out
commit with the commit recorded before the source went offline:

```sh
git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY forkmesh-failover-clone
git -C forkmesh-failover-clone rev-parse HEAD
```

The proof passes only when the fresh clone completes from an eligible mirror
and the commit matches. Keep the clone output and the source/mirror health
snapshot with the test-run record.

## Expected failures and recovery

- **No eligible mirror:** cloning must report repository or mirror unavailable;
  it must not claim preservation succeeded.
- **Stale, unhealthy, or integrity-mismatched mirror:** routing must exclude the
  mirror. Fix sync or integrity and repeat from step 2.
- **All serving hosts offline:** the stable URL is unavailable. Bring one
  integrity-matching host back before retrying.
- **Private repository:** do not use the public proof. Private reads require an
  authorized opaque-replica path and are outside this promise demonstration.

Rollback is explicit: restart `forkmesh-mirror-node` on the managed source host
and wait for fresh signed health. Preserve the failed clone directory and
sanitized logs until the result has been reviewed. The
[desktop control-node guide](operations/desktop-control-node.md) and
[mirror-node operations guide](operations/mirror-node.md) contain the service
and fleet recovery details.

## Supported proof surfaces

- Public browse, signed collaboration, and clone actions use the web app and a
  standard Git client.
- The signed `latest` release manifest is the authority for native package
  availability. At this review, it publishes Linux x86_64 only; macOS, Windows,
  Linux arm64, and repository build instructions must not be presented as
  published native packages. See the [desktop guide](qt-client.md) for source
  prerequisites.
- A managed independent server mirror uses the Linux headless mirror service.
- Mobile and editor integrations can participate in collaboration, but are not
  claimed as source-host controls for this drill.

## Measurement and closure gate

Optional analytics stays disabled by default. With explicit consent, ForkMesh
records only a coarse surface and a fixed action name for proof-link opens and
clone-command copies. It never records a repository, owner, URL, command, ref,
or form value. Report `home-proof-opened`, `proof-clone-copied`, and
`repository-clone-copied` as aggregate funnel counts, alongside an explicit
unsupported-claim count from the primary-surface audit.

Human comprehension remains a release gate and cannot be inferred from a
content test. For every five-person cohort, include maintainers, contributors,
and operators; ask each person to read one primary surface and then, without
prompting, answer:

1. What three jobs does ForkMesh do for source-code repositories?
2. What dependency does the independent-host design remove?
3. How would you demonstrate that benefit?

A person passes only by restating **collaborate**, **mirror**, **preserve**, and
the benefit of not relying on one hosting provider. A cohort passes at 4/5 or
better. Store role, surface, pass/fail, paraphrase, date, facilitator, and a link
to consented research notes. Do not mark this gate complete with blank,
synthetic, or inferred results.

## Linked automated evidence

- Supported release platforms: `app/tests/test_installer_release.py`
- Source-offline and mirror failure paths: `app/tests/test_mirror_serving.py`
  and `app/tests/test_https_mirror_routing_integration.py`
- Service restart and recovery: `app/tests/test_mirror_service_recovery.py`
- Product wording, action links, and documentation: `app/tests/test_product_promise.py`
- Privacy-safe telemetry: `app/tests/test_first_party_analytics.py`

Automated checks support the release gate; they do not replace a recorded
end-to-end drill, the five-person comprehension results, security review,
current documentation, or production telemetry evidence.

# When ForkMesh fits, and when it does not ForkMesh lets developers collaborate on, mirror, and preserve source-code repositories across independent hosts—without relying on any single hosting provider. That is not what every team needs. This page compares ForkMesh with the other ways teams host and keep Git repositories, so you can decide whether it fits before you spend time migrating. Status: issue #509. Evidence ledger: [`ledger.json`](../../conformance/category-comparisons/v1/ledger.json). Check tool: [`category_comparisons.py`](../../tools/category_comparisons.py). ## How to read the comparison - **Two ForkMesh columns.** *ForkMesh protocol and self-hosted software* is what anyone can run from this repository. *ForkMesh hosted service* is what ForkMesh operates at forkmesh.com. A capability in one column does not imply the other. - **Categories, not scorecards.** The other columns describe a kind of tool. Decentralized, Git-native tools are sometimes called peer-to-peer tools. Where a cell names a product, it quotes that product's own documentation, linked under *Primary sources* with the date it was checked. - **By definition** marks a statement that follows from what the category is, such as "you run the server" for a self-hosted forge. - **No claim made** means we found no primary source that supports a category-wide statement, so we do not make one. Read the provider's own documentation for that row. ## How the claims stay honest The ledger is the source of truth; the block below is generated from it. If this page and the JSON disagree, the JSON wins. `python3 tools/category_comparisons.py check` fails when: - a matrix cell is missing, or a ForkMesh cell cites no test, specification, or product evidence, or cites a test or heading that no longer exists; - a cell about another category cites anything other than a dated primary source, or names a vendor none of its sources is published by; - any claim, source, or the page review is older than the review cadence, so the comparison goes stale on the calendar rather than silently ageing; - claim or next-step copy uses an overclaiming phrase such as "unlimited" or "guaranteed"; - a measured next-step link carries a UTM value that attribution would record as `other`; or - this generated block is out of date. Run `render` to refresh it. The `category-comparison-claims` quality gate and the *Category comparisons* workflow run the check on Linux, macOS, and Windows every week and on every change, and keep the `report` JSON as evidence. ### Reviewing and correcting a claim At each review, open every primary source again, confirm the quoted text is still there, and re-run the linked ForkMesh tests. Update `verifiedOn` only for what you checked. When a claim was wrong, change it and add an entry under `corrections` with the date, the claim ids, and what changed; the page lists every correction. A claim you cannot verify again becomes **No claim made** rather than staying up with an old date. ### Measures `python3 tools/category_comparisons.py report` prints the claim freshness measures: the review due date, the oldest verification date, cells by basis, and the number of corrections. Comparison exits and qualified conversion come from [acquisition attribution](../../docs/attribution.md): the trial and community links carry `utm_source=docs`, `utm_medium=comparison`, and `utm_campaign=category_comparison_509`, so signups and repository visits from this page appear under that channel. Documentation pages themselves are not captured, so exits to the self-hosting guide are not counted. Sales and support mismatches are not measured yet; report one as a correction. ### Rollback Removing a claim is always safe: delete it from the ledger or change it to **No claim made**, then run `render`. The attribution allowlist values can stay; unused values record nothing. ## Review status Reviewed **2026-09-14** by ForkMesh maintainers reviewing issue #509. The next review is due **2026-12-13**, every 90 days; after that date the check fails until every claim is verified again. ## At a glance | Option | What it is | Consider it instead of ForkMesh when | | --- | --- | --- | | ForkMesh protocol and self-hosted software | The MIT-licensed protocol, mirror node, gateways, and desktop app, run on hosts you or your community operate. | — | | ForkMesh hosted service | The forkmesh.com and app.forkmesh.com relay, accounts, public index, and website that ForkMesh operates. | — | | Centralized Git hosting | One company runs Git hosting, issues, pull requests, and related services for you, for example GitHub. | You need to push over HTTPS or through a read mirror. ForkMesh accepts pushes only over SSH to a gateway.
You need a contractual uptime SLO, a support response time, or a managed private workspace today. None of these is sold yet.
Your team depends on GitHub Desktop, Sourcetree, or GitKraken being certified. They are not yet.
You need a notarized macOS app, a container image, or a cluster deployment. macOS is preview and containers are planned. | | Self-hosted forges | You install and run a complete forge on your own server, for example Gitea. | You need to push over HTTPS or through a read mirror. ForkMesh accepts pushes only over SSH to a gateway.
You need search and organization administration with no hosted service and no Cloudflare account. Those roles are hosted-only today.
You want one private server on an internal network with no independent copies. A single host is exactly the single-operator risk ForkMesh exists to reduce.
You need a notarized macOS app, a container image, or a cluster deployment. macOS is preview and containers are planned. | | Decentralized, Git-native collaboration tools | Tools that keep issues or reviews inside Git and sync them between copies without a central forge, for example git-bug. | You want only an issue tracker inside an existing Git repository, with no accounts, relay, or mirror hosts. ForkMesh's collaboration comes with signed identities, a relay, and mirrors to run or trust. | | Replicated storage and Git backups | Copies of repositories on other disks, buckets, or machines, made with git clone --mirror, bundles, or storage replication. | You only want an offline copy of Git data. ForkMesh's mirror health, routing, and signed collaboration would be overhead you do not use. | | Basic Git servers | A bare repository served over SSH, HTTP, or the Git daemon, with no forge features. | You want one private server on an internal network with no independent copies. A single host is exactly the single-operator risk ForkMesh exists to reduce. | ## Not for you - **You need to push over HTTPS or through a read mirror. ForkMesh accepts pushes only over SSH to a gateway.** Consider: Centralized Git hosting, Self-hosted forges. Verified 2026-09-14 | | Basic Git servers | category | If the server is offline, clones and pushes to it fail until it returns. | By definition of the category | ## Known limitations - HTTPS and mirror-failover Git paths are read-only; publish branches with the SSH URL. Evidence: [`git-compatibility.md` §https-and-failover-paths-are-read-only](git-compatibility.md#https-and-failover-paths-are-read-only). Verified 2026-09-14. - Hooks pushed with a repository never run on a mirror; shared checks belong in ForkMesh Actions or another CI system. Evidence: [`git-compatibility.md` §repository-controlled-server-hooks-are-disabled](git-compatibility.md#repository-controlled-server-hooks-are-disabled). Verified 2026-09-14. - Failover happens only before a response starts; an interrupted fetch must be retried. Evidence: [`git-compatibility.md` §a-response-cannot-change-mirrors-mid-stream](git-compatibility.md#a-response-cannot-change-mirrors-mid-stream). Verified 2026-09-14. - No network service role is fully independent of the hosted deployment yet. Evidence: [`service-roles.md` §role-status](operations/service-roles.md#role-status); [test `test_no_role_overclaims_independence`](../../app/tests/test_service_roles_contract.py). Verified 2026-09-14. - Private repositories are not commercially generally available until keyless inspection, recovery drills, and an independent review pass. Evidence: [`private-repository-confidentiality.md` §ga-evidence](security/private-repository-confidentiality.md#ga-evidence). Verified 2026-09-14. ## Migration cost - Imports from GitHub, GitLab, and Codeberg run as resumable jobs with checkpoints; a failed or abandoned import can be recovered or rolled back. Evidence: [`repository-imports.md` §failure-abandonment-and-rollback](repository-imports.md#failure-abandonment-and-rollback); [test `test_abandon_recover_rollback_and_credential_non_persistence`](../../app/tests/test_repository_migration.py). Verified 2026-09-14. - A public import stops depending on its provider only after a mirror node hosts it. Nodes refresh every 30 minutes, cap imports at 20 GiB and a first clone at 10 minutes, and never host private imports. Evidence: [`repository-imports.md` §ending-the-provider-dependency](repository-imports.md#ending-the-provider-dependency); [test `test_prepare_defers_new_clones_once_the_imports_root_is_full`](../../app/tests/test_hosted_repository_sync.py). Verified 2026-09-14. - Everyone who pushes registers an SSH public key and changes their push remote to the SSH URL; reads keep working over HTTPS. Evidence: [`git-compatibility.md` §https-and-failover-paths-are-read-only](git-compatibility.md#https-and-failover-paths-are-read-only). Verified 2026-09-14. - Teams that keep an existing forge can sync issues and comments both ways with GitHub, Gitea, Forgejo, or Codeberg instead of moving everything at once. Evidence: [`forge-sync.md`](forge-sync.md); [test `test_every_registered_adapter_implements_the_whole_contract`](../../app/tests/test_forge_sync.py). Verified 2026-09-14. ## Hosted dependencies - The hosted service, and any self-hosted app Worker, needs Cloudflare Workers, D1, KV, Durable Objects, and Queues. The Go mirror node does not. Evidence: [`external-dependency-map.md` §self-hosting-and-offline-use](external-dependency-map.md#self-hosting-and-offline-use); [test `test_mandatory_hosted_dependencies_name_a_self_host_path_and_a_drill`](../../app/tests/test_external_dependency_map.py). Verified 2026-09-14. - Repository search and organization administration run only on the hosted Worker. Evidence: [`service-roles.md` §role-status](operations/service-roles.md#role-status). Verified 2026-09-14. - A direct-HTTPS mirror needs a certificate authority to issue and renew its certificate. Evidence: [`external-dependency-map.md` §summary](external-dependency-map.md#summary). Verified 2026-09-14. ## Next steps - **[Create a Hosted Free account](https://app.forkmesh.com/signup?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=comparison&utm_campaign=category_comparison_509)** — Public preview: best effort, no SLO, no support response time. A 14-day Supporter trial can then be started from account settings; it adds membership perks only. Measured with UTM attribution. - **[Run your own mirror and service roles](operations/service-roles.md)** — No role is fully independent yet; search and organization administration still need the hosted service. Not measured: Documentation pages are static assets that attribution does not capture, so exits to this guide are not counted. - **[Ask in the ForkMesh repository discussions](https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh/discussions?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=comparison&utm_campaign=category_comparison_509)** — Community support: public and reproducible, with no response or resolution time. Measured with UTM attribution. ## Primary sources | Source | Verified | What it says | | --- | --- | --- | | [Git: Pro Git: Git on the Server — The Protocols](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-on-the-Server-The-Protocols) | 2026-09-14 | “Git can use four distinct protocols to transfer data: Local, HTTP, Secure Shell (SSH) and Git. … a bare repository is the contents of your project's .git directory and nothing else. … [the Git daemon provides] absolutely no authentication or cryptography.” | | [Git: git-clone documentation, --mirror](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clone) | 2026-09-14 | “Set up a mirror of the source repository. … --mirror not only maps local branches of the source to local branches of the target, it maps all refs (including remote-tracking branches, notes etc.) and sets up a refspec configuration such that all these refs are overwritten by a git remote update in the target repository.” | | [Git: git-bundle documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-bundle) | 2026-09-14 | “Bundles are used for the "offline" transfer of Git objects without an active "server" sitting on the other side of the network connection.” | | [GitHub: GitHub Terms of Service, section M (Cancellation and Termination)](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service) | 2026-09-14 | “GitHub has the right to suspend or terminate your access to all or any part of the Website at any time, with or without cause, with or without notice, effective immediately.” | | [GitHub: Backing up a repository](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/archiving-a-github-repository/backing-up-a-repository) | 2026-09-14 | “You can take a backup of a Git repository, including the revision history, by performing a mirror clone with the Git CLI. … Migration archives do not include all data related to a repository. For example, Git Large File Storage objects, discussions, or packages are not included. … There is no supported, documented way to restore migration archives on GitHub.” | | [Gitea: Gitea backup and restore](https://docs.gitea.com/administration/backup-and-restore) | 2026-09-14 | “Gitea currently has a dump command that will save the installation to a ZIP file. … To ensure the consistency of the Gitea instance, it must be shutdown during backup. … There is currently no support for a recovery command. It is a manual process that mostly involves moving files to their correct locations and restoring a database dump.” | | [git-bug: git-bug README](https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug) | 2026-09-14 | “Distributed, offline-first bug tracker embedded in git … you only need your git repository to have a bug tracker … use your normal git remote to collaborate, push and pull your bugs … works offline.” | ## Corrections No published claim has been corrected yet.

pages.title: Terminology and voice guide
pages.description: ForkMesh is a Git forge. People already know how repositories, branches, forks, pull requests, and reviews work, so ForkMesh keeps those words and explains its network ideas…
pages.markdown:
# Terminology and voice guide

ForkMesh is a Git forge. People already know how repositories, branches, forks,
pull requests, and reviews work, so ForkMesh keeps those words and explains its
network ideas (mirrors, seeding, trusted maintainers) where they come up. It
does not rename Git workflows.

The machine-readable contract is [`terminology.json`](terminology.json). It holds
the approved glossary, the discouraged-term list, allowances, and compatibility
aliases. `tools/terminology_lint.py` checks primary surfaces against it.

## Approved glossary

| Say | Meaning | Instead of |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **repository** | A Git repository: its files, commits, branches, and tags, with its issues, pull requests, and releases. Use "repo" only in URLs, commands, and tight labels. | project (for source code) |
| **branch** | A named line of commits. The default branch is the one a clone checks out. | |
| **commit** | A recorded change, identified by its hash. | |
| **fork** | Your own copy of a repository under your account. Change it and open pull requests back to the original. | |
| **clone** | Download a repository with Git. | |
| **issue** | A tracked bug report, task, or request. | |
| **pull request** | A proposal to merge commits from one branch or fork into another, with discussion, checks, and reviews. "PR" is fine in compact labels and CLI output. | merge request, patch |
| **review** | An approval, a request for changes, or comments on a pull request. | peer approval |
| **mirror** | A complete copy of a repository on another host that stays in sync and can serve clones when the source is offline. | peer, seed node, mesh node |
| **seed** | The first push that fills a new mirror from an existing copy. After seeding, the mirror keeps itself in sync. | seeder |
| **trusted maintainer** | A person the owner trusts to merge, release, and change settings. Every mirror accepts their signed actions. | delegate |
| **host** | A computer that serves repositories: your machine, a server you run, or a ForkMesh-managed host. | mesh node |
| **desktop app** | The ForkMesh desktop application. Write "desktop app (Qt)" only in build instructions. | Qt client, Qt app |

## Voice guide

- **Lead with the Git task.** "Open a pull request", "Add a mirror", "Clone
  again". Name the button or tab the person will press.
- **Explain a network idea once, in place.** The first time a page mentions
  seeding, say what it does: "ForkMesh seeds the new mirror with a first push;
  after that it stays in sync."
- **Protocol terms stay in advanced detail.** Operator runbooks, protocol specs,
  and diagnostics may say node, relay, attestation, lease, or outbox. A primary
  journey (home page, onboarding, getting started, repository pages, mobile
  screens) uses the plain explanation below, or puts it next to the term.
- **Errors say what happened and what to do next,** in the same words as the
  surface: "The mirror merge could not reach the relay. Retry in a moment."
- **Never rename identifiers for wording.** Change labels, not routes, JSON
  fields, event kinds, or flags. See [compatibility aliases](#compatibility-aliases).

## Protocol terms and plain explanations

| Protocol term | Plain explanation for primary surfaces |
| --- | --- |
| node | A running copy of ForkMesh (desktop app, server, or phone) that signs and syncs for an account. |
| relay | The ForkMesh web service that routes requests to healthy mirrors. It is not the canonical Git store. |
| refs attestation | The signed list of branch and tag commits a mirror must match before it can serve a repository. |
| signed repository proof | A host's signature over the branch and tag commits it serves. |
| commit DAG | Commit history: each commit points at its parents. |
| CRDT / fold | How signed issue and pull request events merge into one current state without conflicts. |
| lease | A short-lived claim that stops two hosts from processing the same issue or pull request at once. |
| outbox | The queue of signed events waiting to be delivered to other hosts. |
| opaque replica | An encrypted copy of a private repository that a host stores without being able to read it. |
| federation | Sharing repository activity with Mastodon and other ActivityPub servers. |

## Discouraged terms

`discouragedTerms` in the contract lists each term's pattern, its replacement,
and whether it must be **replaced** or may appear **explained**:

- Replace: merge request, peer approval, peer-to-peer / P2P, Qt client / Qt app
  / Qt desktop node, delegate, seeder / seed node, mesh node.
- Explain: attestation, refs pin / sigrefs, DAG, CRDT, gossip, lease, outbox.

Run the lint before changing user-facing copy:

```sh
python3 tools/terminology_lint.py            # primary surfaces; exits 1 on a finding
python3 tools/terminology_lint.py --extended # also report desktop, all pages, and all docs
python3 tools/terminology_lint.py --json     # counts for the measurement review
python3 tools/terminology_lint.py path/to/file.html
```

The lint reads only visible text: HTML text and `aria-label`, `title`,
`placeholder`, and `alt` values; Markdown outside code and link targets; and
sentence-like string literals in JavaScript and C++. Comments, code,
and URLs are skipped.

When a term is right in context, either:

- add an entry to `allowances` with the file, term id, and a `reason`. For an
  explain-category term, also give the exact `explanation` text. The lint fails
  if that text disappears from the file, and fails on an allowance that no
  longer matches anything.
- put `terminology: allow=<term-id>` in a comment on the same line or the line
  above.

Allowances exist for exact source names (GitLab calls them merge requests)
and personal biographies. They are not a way around the guide.

## Compatibility aliases

Wording changes never break scripts or links:

- **Routes.** Familiar forge URLs redirect permanently (308) to the repository
  page and keep the query string. `/OWNER/REPOSITORY/pull/12`,
  `/pull-requests/12`, `/merge_requests/12`, `/merge-requests`, and GitLab's
  `/-/merge_requests/12` go to `/OWNER/REPOSITORY/pulls/12`. GitLab-scoped tabs
  such as `/-/issues/5` and `/-/tree/main` drop the `/-/`. The older
  `/dashboard?section=repos` and `/referrals` redirects stay too.
- **Documentation URLs.** A renamed page keeps its old URL. The desktop app
  guide still lives at `/docs/qt-client/`.
- **APIs, events, config, and CLI.** Route names, JSON fields (`pull`, `pulls`,
  `repoKey`), signed event kinds, config keys, and command-line flags are never
  renamed for wording. If a clearer name is ever needed, it is added next to
  the old one, and both are accepted indefinitely.

Every alias in `compatibilityAliases` is a one-way door. Redirects are cached by
browsers, so an entry is never removed.

**Rollback.** A copy change is reverted by reverting its commit. Aliases stay,
because removing one would break links that already point at it.

## Measurement and closure gate

- **Discouraged-term count.** `python3 tools/terminology_lint.py --json --extended`
  reports `discouragedTermCount` and `countsByTerm`. Primary surfaces must stay
  at zero; record the extended count at each monthly review and track it down.
- **Alias usage.** Measure 308 responses on alias paths from Cloudflare zone
  analytics. The Worker adds no logging for aliases, consistent with its
  no-logging design.
- **Support vocabulary.** At the monthly review, sample support threads and bug
  reports and note which discouraged terms people used or asked about.
- **Task comprehension.** Content tests cannot prove this. For every
  five-person cohort, include maintainers, contributors, and operators. Without
  a glossary, each person tries to: fork a repository and open a pull request;
  review and merge a pull request; add a mirror and tell when seeding has
  finished; and say who can merge in a repository. A person passes by finishing
  all four without asking what a term means. A cohort passes at 4/5 or better.
  Record role, surface, pass/fail, the terms that caused hesitation, date,
  facilitator, and a link to consented research notes. Do not mark this gate
  complete with blank, synthetic, or inferred results.

## Linked automated evidence

- Glossary, lint behavior, primary-surface audit, failure paths, and aliases:
  `app/tests/test_terminology_contract.py`
- Repository deep links the aliases land on: `app/tests/test_repo_deeplink_frontend.py`
- Legacy page redirects: `app/tests/test_referrals.py`
- Documentation hosting and links: `www/tests/test_docs_library.py`

The `terminology-contract` quality gate runs the contract test in the `core` and
`release` profiles. Automated checks support closure; they do not replace a
human audit, the comprehension cohort, or production alias-usage evidence.

pages.title: ForkMesh free-protocol / paid-services contract
pages.description: Published 2026-08-20. Contract version 1.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh free-protocol / paid-services contract

Published 2026-08-20. Contract version 1.

> ForkMesh lets developers collaborate on, mirror, and preserve source-code
> repositories across independent hosts—without relying on any single hosting
> provider.

The public, machine-readable source for this contract is
[`/business-model.json`](../public/business-model.json). The public
[entitlement matrix](https://forkmesh.com/docs/business-model) and homepage
pricing section render the same boundary in plain language.

## The durable boundary

ForkMesh sells work and infrastructure, not permission to participate in the
protocol.

The protocol, reference software, and self-hosting unit are MIT-licensed. Using,
studying, modifying, forking, and independently implementing them does not
require a ForkMesh account or payment. Public reading and cloning, standard Git
data, signed `.forkmesh` collaboration records, independent operation, and
protocol governance cannot become paid-plan entitlements.

Paid services may operate replaceable roles for a customer: hosting, team
administration, indexing, managed replicas, verified recovery, reliability,
hosted runners, support, and infrastructure. Payment buys accountable service,
reserved capacity, and human time. It gives ForkMesh no special authority over
protocol objects, independent operators, or exported repositories.

Tokens, blockchains, rewards, tips, bounties, and other speculative or
experimental incentives are strictly optional. No plan, protocol right, or
permission requires a wallet or token. No incentive, payment, or asset holding
changes identity, permissions, ranking, moderation, or governance. The
machine-readable contract publishes this as `tokenOrBlockchainRequired: false`
and `incentivesAffectIdentityPermissionsRankingModerationOrGovernance: false`.
See [incentive independence](incentive-independence.md) for the adapter
boundary and the payment and no-payment paths.

## Initial plans

| Plan | Price and status | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol + self-hosted | $0 forever; available | Complete MIT rights. The operator supplies capacity, backups, moderation, uptime, and support. |
| Hosted Free | $0; public preview | One personal account, anonymous public reads/clones, and best-effort shared relay/index. No managed private workspace, reserved replica, SLO, or priority support entitlement. |
| Supporter membership | $5/member/month; launch membership | Funds public infrastructure and adds membership recognition, but no hosted capability, reserved capacity, SLO, priority support, or protocol authority. |
| Pro membership | $10/member/month; launch membership | The currently published Pro workflows where configured and membership recognition. It is bounded by safety/capacity controls and is not an infrastructure SLO or unlimited plan. |
| Managed services | Research preview; not for sale | Proposed metered hosting, team administration, indexing, replicas, recovery, runners, support, and reliability. Checkout remains disabled until the research, cost, security, portability, and recovery gates pass. |

`Hosted Free` is deliberately described by its service boundary, not by an
invented unlimited allowance. Public relay and index use is best effort under
published security, abuse, and provider-capacity safeguards. There is no
reserved capacity, private-workspace GA claim, contractual uptime, or human
response time. When a numeric free allowance becomes enforceable, it must be
added to `business-model.json`, the UI, and the metering tests in the same
change.

## Usage units

Managed proposals use units that map to an observable cost driver:

- active member-month;
- indexed project-month;
- managed replica GiB-month;
- verified egress GiB;
- hosted runner minute;
- priority support hour;
- edge Worker request;
- Durable Object request; and
- Durable Object GB-second.

No paid plan may use `unlimited` for a variable-cost service. An allowance and
overage are not publishable until the unit can be reconciled to its provider
invoice or support ledger. Unknown usage or cost remains **unknown**; it is
never converted to zero to improve margin.

## Portability commitments

Canonical repository data remains Git objects and refs. Canonical
collaboration data remains signed `.forkmesh` repository records. Customers
may clone and export those formats without an upgrade or export fee, including
before cancellation. Billing-provider identifiers, abuse evidence, and
operational logs are service records, not canonical protocol data.

Before a managed plan can be sold, an end-to-end drill must export a managed
project, import it into a clean self-hosted deployment, compare Git object ids
and signed collaboration records, then restore the managed service from the
same export. Cancellation must not rotate project identity, rewrite signatures,
or require a proprietary verifier.

## Support boundary

Community support covers public documentation, discussions, and reproducible
issue reports. Security and network-safety incidents may be prioritized, but
free use and memberships carry no response or resolution time.

A future paid support order must name its supported platform, contact channel,
hours, response target, exclusions, escalation path, data-access boundary, and
the quantity of human time included. ForkMesh does not promise a service level
for a self-hosted system it does not operate. The current supported proof
surfaces are a modern browser plus standard Git, desktop clients on macOS,
Windows, and Linux, and the Linux headless mirror service. Mobile and editor
integrations do not become managed source-host controls merely because a
customer pays.

A repository-preservation order is written as a
[repository availability contract](availability-contract.md). The contract
names its copies, operator and region diversity, uptime, coverage,
verification frequency, recovery and response objectives, exclusions, and
credits. Only capacity that continuous probes and restore drills have
demonstrated can back one, and every period report reproduces from its
evidence. The contract model does not open managed checkout; the gates above
still apply.

## No data sale

ForkMesh does not sell personal data, repository data, collaboration data,
telemetry, or derived profiles, and does not use them to sell advertising.
Data is processed only to provide, secure, support, measure, and improve the
selected service under the public privacy policy. Optional product analytics
stays disabled by default and accepts only fixed, coarse action names after
explicit consent.

[ForkMesh Ads](operations/ad-network.md), the first-party text ad network,
is built inside that rule: an ad is placed by product surface and never by
viewer, the serve call reads no account or history, and the only measurement
is an aggregate click count. Its membership allowances are the `advertising`
block of the machine-readable contract.

## Acquisition and paid adoption model

The public-project loop is the acquisition product, not a loss leader that can
later be revoked:

1. A maintainer discovers ForkMesh through a public project or preservation
   need and completes an anonymous read or clone.
2. The project adds a signed contribution or independent mirror and observes
   the four-step product proof.
3. Repeated collaboration creates a qualified service need: less operator
   toil, coordinated team policy, faster indexing, managed recovery, an SLO,
   or accountable support.
4. A buyer enters a bounded trial for that paid job. Export stays available
   throughout the trial.
5. A paid proposal is accepted only when observed service cost supports the
   target gross margin; protocol rights and public-project value remain free.

The funnel reports aggregate public projects reaching proof, qualified service
conversations, trials, paid customers, trial-to-paid conversion, recognized
revenue, service cost, gross profit, and infrastructure margin. It does not
identify public readers or treat optional analytics as required surveillance.

## Unit-economics model and instrumentation

For a closed accounting window:

```text
qualified-demand rate = qualified service conversations / projects reaching proof
trial conversion      = paid customers / completed trials
service cost          = metered infrastructure + managed hosts + runners + support
gross profit          = recognized service revenue - service cost
gross margin          = gross profit / recognized service revenue
```

The admin-signed `/api/accounts/admin-usage-report` already reads actual
Cloudflare account analytics and now emits a stable `unitEconomics` projection
for Worker requests, Durable Object requests, and duration. It retains storage
operations and observed response bytes as provider diagnostics.
`tools/unit_economics.py` validates a period record, combines those quantities
with invoice-backed infrastructure, managed-host, runner, and support costs,
and calculates the funnel and margin without binary floating-point money.

The report is network aggregate. A paid trial that shares infrastructure must
add privacy-reviewed tenant attribution using a keyed blind index; raw account,
repository, path, IP, or request data must not enter economics exports. Provider
analytics unavailability is a failed sample, not a zero-cost day.

## Pricing research gate

The initial managed plan is a hypothesis, not validated pricing. The
[pricing-interview register](research/pricing-interviews.md) currently records
zero qualifying buyer interviews and therefore keeps managed checkout off.
Only consented, attributable real interviews can validate economic buyer,
budget ownership, and top paid jobs. Blank, synthetic, inferred, employee-only,
or public-comment records do not count.

## Failure, rollback, and recovery

- If the public JSON and visible matrix diverge, the business-model contract
  test fails and the site must not deploy.
- If telemetry, invoice, runner, host, or support cost is missing, the period is
  incomplete and gross margin is not reported as healthy.
- If interview evidence is below its threshold, managed checkout stays disabled
  and the page remains a research preview.
- If an entitlement change would remove a permanent commitment, roll back the
  marketing deployment; no protocol object or user data migration is involved.
- If a managed-service trial fails, export canonical data, verify it in a clean
  self-host, restore the last tested service configuration, and retain sanitized
  operational evidence for review.

The operational sequence, owner checklist, and exact evidence commands are in
[business-model rollout and recovery](operations/business-model-rollout.md).

## Linked automated evidence

- Public entitlement, portability, support, research, privacy, and plan
  contract: `app/tests/test_business_model_contract.py`
- Unit-economics success, malformed input, missing cost, and zero-revenue paths:
  `app/tests/test_unit_economics.py`
- Live provider-usage projection and analytics failure paths:
  `app/tests/test_admin_usage_report.py`
- Supported installer platforms: `app/tests/test_installer_release.py`
- Source-offline failure and recovery: `app/tests/test_mirror_serving.py`,
  `app/tests/test_https_mirror_routing_integration.py`, and
  `app/tests/test_mirror_service_recovery.py`
- Default-off, allowlisted commercial telemetry:
  `app/tests/test_first_party_analytics.py`
- Optional incentives isolated from canonical state and decisions:
  `app/tests/test_incentive_independence.py`
- Repository availability contracts, demonstrated capacity, simulated
  operator and regional failure, SLO misses, and credits:
  `app/tests/test_availability_contract.py`

Automated evidence does not replace actual interviews, provider invoices, an
export/restore drill, security review, current support documentation, or a
production rollout window.

pages.title: Incentive independence
pages.description: Status: P0 product invariant (issue #516). Machine-readable conformance requirements: conformance/incentives/v1/requirements.json.
pages.markdown:
# Incentive independence

Status: P0 product invariant (issue #516). Machine-readable conformance
requirements: [`conformance/incentives/v1/requirements.json`](../../conformance/incentives/v1/requirements.json).

> Repository access, identity, contribution, governance, and essential network
> participation work fully without a token, blockchain, reward system, or
> speculative asset.

ForkMesh offers optional incentives: Solana tips and bounties, the community
reward pool, microjob payouts, hackathon prizes, and paid memberships. Each one
is an **adapter**. An adapter may read canonical state to decide whom to pay or
thank. Canonical state must never read an adapter.

## Architecture

Canonical state is:

- Git objects and refs, and the signed refs pins that route reads to mirrors.
- Accounts, device keys, SSH keys, sessions, and portable identities.
- Signed `.forkmesh` collaboration records: issues, pull requests, reviews,
  comments, moderation decisions, and their repository policy documents.
- Organizations, teams, repository roles, and organization succession.
- Discovery: the catalog, public snapshots, mirror health, and routing.
- Governance: marketplace publication review and community ad votes.

Incentive and payment adapters are:

| Adapter | Code | Tables |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Solana read/write plumbing | `app/src/solana.py` | `wallet_balances`, `chain_intents` |
| Community reward pool | `app/src/reward_policy.py` | `reward_*`, `pending_rewards`, `central_fund`, `funds_received` |
| Public ledger | `app/src/ledger.py` | `ledger_backfill_*` |
| Tips and bounties | `entry.py` tip/bounty handlers | `issue_bounty`, `bounty_wallet`, `tip_notice`, `contributor_reward_estimates`, `reward_wallet_reminders` |
| Microjobs | `app/src/microjobs.py`, `microjobs_runtime.py` | `microjob_claims` |
| Hackathon prizes | `app/src/hackathon.py`, `hackathon_runtime.py` | `hackathon_*` |
| World purchases | `entry.py` element purchases | `world_element_purchases` |
| Legacy custody migration | `entry.py` custody audit | `legacy_custody_*` |
| Conventional memberships | `app/src/patreon.py`, `patreon_handler.py` | `patreon_*` |

The isolation rules are:

1. **Imports flow one way.** Canonical modules (`collaboration.py`,
   `catalog.py`, `catalog_routes.py`, `git_http.py`, `hosted_git.py`,
   `mirrors.py`, `mirror_replica.py`, `edge_routing.py`, `ssh_keys.py`,
   `portable_sessions.py`, `security_controls.py`, `organization_succession.py`,
   `marketplace_governance.py`, `repository_imports.py`,
   `repository_migration.py`, `public_snapshots.py`) never import an adapter.
2. **Hooks are best effort.** When a canonical write notifies an adapter (for
   example, a signup, a credited referral, or a first mirror notifying the
   hackathon), the call is optional and wrapped so that an adapter exception
   cannot fail the canonical write.
3. **No foreign keys point into adapter tables.** Removing every adapter table
   leaves every canonical table, and every foreign-key relation between
   canonical tables, unchanged.
4. **No asset signal in decisions.** Identity, authorization, ranking,
   moderation, and governance code never reads a wallet, payout address,
   balance, token, stake, tip, bounty, or payment history. A payout address is
   optional display metadata stored inside the account record. It is never an
   eligibility, verification, or trust requirement.

Wallet and tip leaderboards are views of an adapter. They are labelled as
such, are not used for search, catalog, roster, or trust ordering, and can be
removed without affecting any other ranking.

Marketplace publication is the one decision that used to depend on assets:
reviewers needed a SOL address and were listed by wallet value. Since #516, any
five distinct active members may approve and reviewers are listed in approval
order. The legacy `wallet_address`, `value_lamports`, and `value_checked_at`
approval columns are retired. New approvals store blanks, and nothing reads the
columns.

## Commercial commitment

The [business-model contract](business-model.md) publishes two permanent
commitments in `/business-model.json`:

- `tokenOrBlockchainRequired: false`: no ForkMesh product, plan, or protocol
  right requires a token, a blockchain account, or a speculative asset.
- `incentivesAffectIdentityPermissionsRankingModerationOrGovernance: false`:
  no incentive, payment, or asset holding changes identity, permissions,
  ranking, moderation, or governance.

ForkMesh never sells or issues a token and never presents rewards as an
investment.

## Protocol governance

Signed collaboration objects derive authority only from the repository policy
document (maintainer, moderator, and notifier keys). The
[collaboration protocol](design/conflict-safe-collaboration.md) forbids
inferring any role from asset ownership or transaction history. A change to
this invariant is a breaking protocol change. It requires a new protocol
version and cannot be made through a hosted configuration switch.

## Payment and no-payment paths

Every optional incentive has a no-payment path. Where money is accepted, a
conventional path is preferred:

| Offer | No-payment path | Conventional payment path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Supporter or Pro membership | Hosted Free and self-hosting keep every protocol right | Patreon |
| Community reward pool contribution | Not required for anything | Supporter membership |
| Tips to members | Stars, follows, and signed reactions | Membership funds public infrastructure |
| Bounties and microjob payouts | Contribute without claiming a payout. Review and merge are unchanged. | Not yet offered: payouts are SOL-only today and stay optional |
| Hackathon prizes | Entry, judging, and votes need no wallet | Prize months are membership grants, not assets |
| Public-interest grants and matching | Applying, review, and selection need no wallet, account, or plan | Bank transfer, Open Collective, or Liberapay. Solana only if the recipient chooses it. |

Grant awards follow the [public-interest funding](funding/README.md) program. Its ledger rejects any award that grants access, identity rights, votes, or a network obligation.

A gap in the conventional column is tracked as open work. It never becomes a
reason to require a wallet.

## Disabled deployment

An adapter is disabled when its configuration is absent. That means no reward
pool signer, no `NODE_SOLANA_ADDRESS`, no Patreon credentials, and a
hackathon left in `draft`. A clean deployment in that state must pass:

- account signup, sign-in, device and SSH key registration;
- repository create, push, public browse, and clone through a mirror;
- signed issue, pull request, review, comment, and moderation records;
- organization roles and succession;
- catalog discovery and mirror routing; and
- marketplace submission, member approval, and owner publication.

Unconfigured adapters answer explicitly: `patreon_oauth_not_configured` and
`patreon_webhook_not_configured` with HTTP 503, and the microjob payout queue with `pool_not_configured`. They never block
a canonical response.

## Failure, rollback, and recovery

- **An adapter provider fails or is removed** (RPC outage, provider shutdown,
  revoked credentials): payouts and badges pause; canonical state is untouched.
  Unset the adapter's configuration, then drop or keep its tables. No canonical
  migration is involved.
- **A replacement provider:** add a new adapter that reads canonical state. Do
  not copy asset data into canonical tables.
- **A coupling regression reaches review:** `app/tests/test_incentive_independence.py`
  fails and the `incentive-independence` quality gate blocks the release. Revert
  the coupling change; do not waive the gate.
- **Legacy asset data in canonical rows** (for example, pre-#516 marketplace
  approval values): it is inert, and the next approval upsert blanks it.

## Telemetry and measures

Report these per release:

- **Essential no-incentive journey pass rate:** the disabled-deployment
  journeys above, from the quality-gate run with adapter configuration unset.
- **Adapter coupling violations:** the number of failing
  `test_incentive_independence.py` assertions. The target is zero.
- **User comprehension:** ask each person in a five-person cohort whether they
  need a wallet or token to use, contribute to, or govern a repository. A person
  passes by answering "no" without prompting. The cohort passes at 4/5.

Product analytics stay default-off and allowlisted. No wallet, address,
balance, or transaction identifier is recorded. Do not mark the comprehension
gate complete with blank, synthetic, or inferred results.

## Linked automated evidence

- Adapter import isolation, best-effort hooks, schema removal, asset-free
  decisions, unconfigured adapters, and published commitments:
  `app/tests/test_incentive_independence.py`
- Wallet-free marketplace governance: `app/tests/test_marketplace_governance.py`
- Non-custodial user-facing boundary: `app/tests/test_non_custodial_surfaces.py`
- Commercial contract: `app/tests/test_business_model_contract.py`
- Collaboration authorization from policy keys only:
  `app/tests/test_collaboration_protocol.py`

Automated checks support the release gate. They do not replace a recorded
disabled-deployment run, comprehension results, security review, or production
telemetry evidence.

pages.markdown: # Stock Git compatibility Conformance suite **forkmesh-stock-git 1.0.0**. Statuses were computed **2026-09-14** from 2 retained stock-Git runs: **39 of 39** support claims have a passing run from the last 30 days. Supported rows use an unmodified Git executable (minimum 2.34.0); every run records the exact client and platform version in its JSON evidence. A claim is never published on its own: with no passing run it is **unverified**, when its newest passing run ages past the freshness window it is **stale**, and when a retained run failed it is **failing**. [Filter results by client and workflow](/docs/git-compatibility/) or download [results.json](/docs/git-compatibility/results.json). The offline reference probe uses disposable repositories and the same smart-HTTP framing as the public read path. Product gateway contract tests cover authorization, hidden refs, read-only failures, and rollback behavior. Repository shape: A bare repository whose main branch has three commits: an SSH-signed commit adding a README, a 128 KiB binary payload, and a gitlink submodule at deps/fixture resolved through a relative URL, followed by two history commits. A lightweight tag points at the signed commit; receive and transfer fsck are enabled, and a read-only replica rejects every push. ## Statuses | Status | Meaning | | --- | --- | | **supported** | Covered by an automated stock-Git probe and part of the public contract. | | **local** | Runs in the stock client checkout; the transport preserves the required objects and refs. | | **conditional** | Supported when the condition in the matrix is satisfied. | | **unsupported** | Rejected or deliberately unavailable; follow the linked recovery or alternative. | | **failing** | A retained run for this cell failed; the claim is withdrawn until the same configuration passes again. | | **stale** | The newest passing run is older than the freshness window; re-run the suite before relying on it. | | **unverified** | No retained run covers this cell; treat it as experimental. | ## Paths | Path | Read | Write | Transport | Authentication | Contract | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Direct owner SSH | yes | yes | SSH (ssh://); the offline probe uses a stock smart-HTTP origin with the same pack negotiation | Registered SSH public key with repository read or write permission | A stock Git SSH session terminates at the owner-authorized forced-command gateway. | | Stable relay HTTPS | yes | no | HTTPS smart protocol under the stable repository URL | Anonymous read of a public repository; HTTPS writes are rejected | The stable repository URL proxies upload-pack in place from one integrity-matching HTTPS mirror. | | Relay mirror failover | yes | no | HTTPS smart protocol through a relay-selected mirror | Anonymous read of a public repository; no credentials reach a mirror | Before response bytes are committed, the relay retries another healthy mirror with the same attested refs. | ## Operations | Operation | Direct owner SSH | Stable relay HTTPS | Mirror failover | Reproduce | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Clone | **supported** — SSH upload-pack. Applies to: relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: Git receives HTTP 501 with error code direct_https_receive_pack_required before ForkMesh reads the push body. - Reproduce: `git push https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY HEAD` - Action: Register an SSH public key, copy the repository's published ssh:// URL, and push that remote instead. - Recovery: No remote ref or object is changed. Correct the remote URL and retry the same push. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · app/tests/test_git_http.py::test_receive_pack_fails_closed_without_consuming_request_body ### Repository-controlled server hooks are disabled - Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: Client-side hooks in a checkout run normally. Gateways set core.hooksPath to the null device so pushed repository configuration cannot execute code on a mirror. - Reproduce: `git -C worktree commit -m 'exercise local hook'` - Action: Keep developer hooks local; put shared required checks in reviewed ForkMesh Actions or another CI system. - Recovery: A rejected local hook leaves the index and remote unchanged; fix or intentionally bypass the local hook according to project policy. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 hooks probe ### A response cannot change mirrors mid-stream - Applies to: mirror-failover. - Expected result: ForkMesh retries another eligible mirror only before response bytes are committed. An interrupted pack fails as a normal Git transport error. - Reproduce: `git fetch --prune origin` - Action: Retry the fetch; Git reuses valid local objects and ForkMesh may select another matching mirror for the new request. - Recovery: Run git fsck --full --strict if the client or disk reported corruption. Do not delete the existing clone before collecting diagnostics. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 mirror-failover and integrity probes ### Partial clone requires Git protocol v2 - Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: A protocol-v0 filtered clone may receive the initial commits and trees, but its first lazy blob fetch is rejected as an unadvertised-object request so hidden ForkMesh objects remain inaccessible. - Reproduce: `git -c protocol.version=0 clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout '{clone_url}' worktree` - Action: Use Git 2.34 or newer and retry with -c protocol.version=2, or omit --filter for a full clone. - Recovery: Remove the incomplete disposable clone, or keep it for diagnostics and clone into a new directory with protocol v2; no remote ref or object was changed. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 protocol-v0 rejection and protocol-v2 partial-clone probes ### Submodules are separate repositories - Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: The superproject clone succeeds, then Git names the exact submodule whose independent URL is unavailable or unauthorized. - Reproduce: `git clone --recurse-submodules '{clone_url}' worktree` - Action: Confirm every .gitmodules URL uses a published public HTTPS route or an SSH route your key may read, then run git submodule update --init --recursive. - Recovery: The superproject and any completed submodules remain valid; Git resumes the missing child without recloning successful repositories. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 submodules probe ### Third-party desktop UI certification is not complete - Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: GitHub Desktop, Sourcetree, and GitKraken are not release-supported rows until their exact application and bundled-Git versions produce a retained report. - Reproduce: `python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --git /path/to/the/client/bundled/git --client-label 'CLIENT VERSION'` - Action: Use a tested Git CLI or ForkMesh Qt build, or run the versioned probe with the desktop application's bundled Git before relying on it. - Recovery: The probe uses disposable repositories and makes no production write. Attach its JSON report when requesting a new supported row. - Last tested: not yet tested · not applicable · No support claim is published without retained evidence. ## Run the suite ```sh python3 tools/git_conformance.py validate python3 tools/git_conformance.py render --check python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --protocol-version 0 \ --output artifacts/git-conformance-v0.json python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --protocol-version 2 \ --output artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json python3 tools/git_conformance.py attest \ artifacts/git-conformance-v0.json artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json python3 tools/git_conformance.py gate ``` Use `--git /path/to/git --client-label 'client version'` to exercise a desktop application's bundled, unmodified Git. Reports contain operation status, elapsed milliseconds, exact client/platform versions, generalized request counts, and test object IDs. They exclude temporary paths, URLs, repository contents, credentials, and client addresses.
