pages.markdown:
# Empty repositories created from the web

You do not need the desktop app, and you do not need an account on another
forge, to start a repository on ForkMesh. Create an empty one in the browser
and push to it with the `git` you already have.

This is the path issue #676 asked for. The other three sources in the
**Create & mirror a repository** modal each assume something you may not have
yet: a clone URL means the repository already exists somewhere else, a local
path means a ForkMesh node is running on that machine to read it, and the
provider import means a GitHub, GitLab, or Codeberg account.

> **ForkMesh Next:** this page describes production. On
> `app.forkmesh.com` repositories created on the web live on all three
> core nodes, each reconciling its copy against the desired set in the
> database, with no single write node; the create form also offers private
> repositories and README, `.gitignore` and license initialization. The Next
> behaviour is documented in `docs/HOSTED_REPOS.md` in the repository.

## Create it

1. Open **Repositories → New**.
2. Keep the **Empty repository** source (it is the default).
3. Enter a name and, optionally, a description.
4. Press **Create empty repository**.

The repository exists immediately, holds no commits, and is listed publicly in
the catalog. The modal then shows the commands for your first push along with
the username and password `git` will ask for.

## Push to it

```bash
git init -b main
git add .
git commit -m "first commit"
git remote add forkmesh https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<name>
git push -u forkmesh main
```

`git` prompts for a username and password on the first push:

- **Username** — your ForkMesh account name.
- **Password** — the push credential shown in the modal.

The remote URL deliberately carries no credential, so nothing secret lands in
`.git/config`. Use your platform credential helper
(`git config --global credential.helper`) if you would rather not paste the
password on every push.

The first push is what creates the bare repository on the hosting node; from
then on the repository is served, cloneable, and browsable like any other
ForkMesh repository. ForkMesh records the refs attestation (the signed list of branch and tag
commits) that public reads are routed against from the hosting node's own signed repository proof at the end
of each accepted push, because a repository created in a browser has no node
of its own to publish one.

## About the push credential

- It is issued to the browser session you created the repository from, and it
  is valid for seven days.
- ForkMesh does not store it. It is a keyed MAC over your account name, the
  repository, that session, and the expiry, checked on each push.
- Signing that session out (**Settings → Sessions**) revokes it at once.
- It can do nothing your account cannot: ownership and organization write
  permission are re-checked on every push.
- Need a new one after it expires? `POST
  /api/hosted-repositories/push-credential` with `{"owner", "name"}` and your
  session token, from the signed-in browser or with
  `Authorization: Bearer <session>`.

## Limits

- **Public only.** A private ForkMesh repository is an owner-sealed encrypted
  mirror, and only a node holding your account key can seal one. Creating a
  private repository still requires the desktop or mobile node; the web
  refuses rather than publishing a "private" repository the host could read.
- **Pack size.** A push is streamed through the Worker to the hosting node,
  so a large repository (well past 100k lines of source, including its
  history) can be imported in one `git push`. The pack is bounded by the
  hosting node's `receiveMaxInputBytes` (256 MiB unless its operator lowers
  it) and by Cloudflare's per-request body ceiling on the app origin (100 MB
  on the Free plan). Pushes above that go over SSH, or in several commits'
  worth of smaller packs. Only a pack the Worker can hold (8 MB,
  `HTTPS_MIRROR_BODY_MAX_BYTES`) is bound to its exact digest in the routing
  capability; a larger one is bound to the single-use capability and the
  node's TLS session instead.
- **Availability.** A relay only offers this when its operator runs a hosted
  write node (`HOSTED_GIT_WRITE_NODE`, plus `writableRepositoryRoot` and
  `writableOwners` on that node). Where it is not configured, the create modal
  answers `hosted_git_unavailable` and falls back to the desktop handoff.

## On ForkMesh Next: hosted by the core nodes

Where the relay's own core nodes host repositories (`HOSTED_GIT_CORE_NODES`,
as on `app.forkmesh.com`), **New repository** offers more:

- **Private.** Only you, and your organization's readers, can clone or read
  it, with the same credential. The core nodes hold it unencrypted, as any
  hosted forge does. An owner-sealed private mirror still needs your own
  node.
- **A first commit.** Choose a README, a `.gitignore` and a license. The
  commands then start from `git clone`.
- **An organization owner.** You need the maintain permission in that
  organization.
- **Import.** Paste a public `https://` repository URL from GitHub, GitLab or
  Codeberg under **Remote clone URL**, and ForkMesh hosts a real, cloneable
  copy of it.
- **Every core node holds a copy.** Pushes go to one core, and the others
  catch up within seconds.

Each account can host up to 10 repositories, and each one can be up to
200 MB. To grow past that, move the repository to your own node: clone it
with `--mirror`, add it to your desktop or headless node, and publish it.
Once that signed publication takes over the listing, the core nodes release
their copies. Operator details are in `docs/HOSTED_REPOS.md` of the Next
repository.

## Operator notes

The node side is the hosted write gateway described in
[direct-https-mirror-gateway.md](operations/direct-https-mirror-gateway.md)
under "Push-created repositories": an authorized first push creates
`<writableRepositoryRoot>/<owner>/<repo>.git`, records it in the
`hosted-pushes.json` sidecar, and the ordinary refresh/registration cycle then
serves and health-registers it. A node that holds website-created repositories
cannot enumerate the accounts it will host, so it sets
`"writableOwners": ["*"]`; every request that reaches a write already carried a
verified router capability from the Worker, which applies the account's real
push permissions before signing one.

The Worker side lives in `app/src/hosted_git.py`:

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/hosted-repositories` | Create the empty record, return the first push credential |
| `POST /api/hosted-repositories/push-credential` | Re-mint a credential for a repository the session may push |

Because a web-only account holds no signing key, the catalog record for a
hosted repository is written by the Worker rather than published with a node
signature, and is marked `source: "hosted-web"`. A later signed publication
from the owner's own node takes the record over through the normal catalog
path.

pages.title: External repository imports and resumable migrations
pages.description: Racing a shutdown, a takedown, a lost account, or censorship? Start with preservation-first crisis onboarding. It orders this import against the time and access you have left…
pages.markdown:
# External repository imports and resumable migrations

Racing a shutdown, a takedown, a lost account, or censorship? Start with
[preservation-first crisis onboarding](crisis-preservation.md). It orders this
import against the time and access you have left, and reports what is
actually preserved.

## Three-minute setup path

On **Repositories**, choose **New repository**, select **GitHub / GitLab /
Codeberg**, paste the repository URL, and select **Start resumable import**. A
read-scoped provider token is optional for public repositories and required for
private repositories. ForkMesh durably accepts the job after one repository
lookup; repository size and collaboration-history transfer are not part of the
hands-on setup timer.

The status panel reports these clocks separately:

- **Hands-on setup** runs from opening the form until the durable job is
  accepted. The browser supplies a monotonic duration and the relay rejects
  implausible values; a request-duration fallback is labelled separately.
- **Transfer** starts when the first provider page is requested and ends when
  the canonical state is signed. Closing the page does not discard progress.

The repositories list shows **Continue import** for an interrupted, paused, or
rate-limited job. Public imports resume without a credential. A private import
asks for a current token again because ForkMesh never stores provider tokens.
The setup telemetry endpoint reports `setupP50Ms` and `setupP95Ms` separately,
both overall and by supported provider:

```http
GET /api/repository-imports/migration-metrics
Authorization: Bearer <ForkMesh session>
```

`setupMedianWithinThreeMinutes` is true only when recorded p50 is at most
180,000 ms. Transfer p50, completion, retries, object volume, and abandonment
are separate fields, so a large repository cannot make setup appear slow or a
fast form cannot hide a stalled transfer.

The checked conformance dataset deliberately uses setup samples of 60, 120,
and 240 seconds for each provider. Its reported result is therefore p50 **120
seconds** (passes the three-minute gate) and p95 **240 seconds**, separately,
for GitHub, GitLab, and Codeberg. These are deterministic acceptance samples,
not a claim about production users; the endpoint above is the source for
current operational p50/p95 after rollout.

ForkMesh keeps GitHub, GitLab, and Codeberg metadata imports in a separate data
model from its live mirror catalog:

- `/api/repositories` contains published ForkMesh mirrors.
- `/api/repository-imports` contains external metadata entries and stubs.

An external entry is never routed, cloned, or described as mirrored until its
status is linked to a separately published and verified ForkMesh mirror.
ForkMesh does not own or control an external repository. A signed import
receipt therefore means the provider *metadata* is captured; the Git contents
become independent of the provider only once a node hosts them, which is what
[Ending the provider dependency](#ending-the-provider-dependency) describes.

## Importing metadata

An authenticated user can submit:

```http
POST /api/repository-imports
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/owner/repository",
  "providerToken": "request-only token, if needed",
  "targetOwner": "user-or-organization",
  "mode": "import",
  "sessionToken": "ForkMesh account session"
}
```

`mode` is `import` or `stub`. Only canonical `github.com`, `gitlab.com`, and
`codeberg.org` HTTPS repository URLs are accepted. `targetOwner` may be the
signed-in user or an organization where that user is an owner or administrator.
Provider access tokens are used for that request and never written to D1, a
Worker log, the response, or browser storage. Private repositories require a
token that can read the repository.

The World importer can expand a Codeberg user/organization profile into its
public repositories before importing them one at a time:

```http
POST /api/repository-imports/discover
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "sourceUrl": "https://codeberg.org/m33",
  "sessionToken": "ForkMesh account session"
}
```

Discovery is authenticated, paginated, restricted to canonical Codeberg URLs,
and bounded to 200 repositories. It never imports a private repository.

A community member can list a public stub without claiming ownership. If a
provider administrator later imports the same stable provider repository id
with a current token, they can adopt moderation of the entry; the original
lister remains attributed. A read-only collaborator cannot adopt or overwrite a
private import.

The legacy `POST /api/repository-imports` endpoint creates a bounded external
metadata entry or stub. A full migration uses the durable endpoint instead:

```http
POST /api/repository-imports/migrations
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/owner/repository",
  "providerToken": "request-scoped token, if needed",
  "setupDurationMs": 42000,
  "sessionToken": "ForkMesh account session"
}
```

The `202` response is the end of setup and includes a deterministic `mig_…`
job id. `POST /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/resume` advances exactly
one provider page and returns the next durable checkpoint. The web UI repeats
that request while it remains open. API clients should do the same and stop on
`completed`, HTTP `429`, or another explicit error. Provider credentials are
request-scoped, never placed in a job/checkpoint/report, and should be supplied
again only when resuming a private source.

### Supported fidelity contract

All three adapters—GitHub, GitLab, and Codeberg—emit the same versioned object
families:

| Family | Preserved source records |
| --- | --- |
| `git_refs` | Branch and tag names, object ids, and protection metadata |
| `issues` | Complete issue provider payloads, authors, labels, state, and timestamps |
| `pull_requests` | Pull/merge request payloads, heads/bases, state, and timestamps |
| `reviews` | Reviews, review discussions, and inline review comments available from that provider |
| `releases` | Releases, tags, asset manifests/links, and timestamps |
| `documentation` | Provider README document, exact encoding/content, path, and blob id |
| `labels` | Provider label ids, names, colors, descriptions, and timestamps |
| `users` | Contributor/collaborator source identities and provider metadata |
| `collaboration_history` | Issue comments/events, merge-request notes, and commit comments exposed by the adapter |

Each encrypted object retains the original JSON provider payload alongside a
common projection. The source provider, repository id, object id/id kind,
stream, relationships, URLs, and timestamps are preserved for audit and later
two-way sync. Credential-shaped fields fail closed into an explicit redaction
marker and increment the signed report’s redaction count; unsupported values,
oversize objects, or invalid response shapes fail the page rather than being
silently dropped.

Git repository object transfer continues through ForkMesh’s normal bare-mirror
path; the adapter preserves ref names and object ids so the mirror result can be
compared without rewriting Git ids. Provider wikis are separate Git
repositories on all supported platforms and are listed explicitly as requiring
a separate mirror operation. Workflow logs and artifact bytes are also
reported as out of scope rather than presented as migrated. Private source is
never sent to an image generator or other external model.

Provider rate-limit headers are honored. When a limit is reached, further
calls stop, the checkpoint remains on the unprocessed page, `Retry-After` is
forwarded, and the job becomes `rate_limited`. Resuming repeats that page; its
deterministic keys make this safe even if the first response reached storage
but the client missed the acknowledgement.

## Idempotence, checkpoints, and signed completion

Object identity is `SHA-256(object family + preserved source id)`. A page uses
an upsert on that key before its phase/stream/page checkpoint advances. A crash
between those writes can therefore repeat work but cannot create a duplicate;
a crash after the checkpoint cannot precede its object writes. Pull requests
are imported before provider-specific review streams are constructed, so those
relationships survive a process restart too.

A new completed-source scan increments the job generation. Objects observed
again are updated in place. An object must be absent from two consecutive
complete scans before pruning, so offset-page movement at an active source can
delay a deletion but cannot silently delete a live record; provider edits never
create a second logical record. When all phases finish,
ForkMesh sorts the surviving `(objectType, sourceKey, payloadHash)` tuples,
hashes the canonical document, and authenticates that digest with the relay’s
`hmac-sha256` migration key. Local run numbers, retry counts, and timestamps are
excluded, so an unchanged source produces the exact same state hash and
signature on every rerun.

The job owner can audit the preserved objects and receipt without accessing D1:

```http
GET /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}
GET /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/objects?type=reviews&limit=100
```

The object export returns at most 200 records and an opaque `nextCursor` for
the next `after=` request. Both endpoints are owner-only and `no-store`.
Provider tokens are absent from all responses and durable rows.

## Failure, abandonment, and rollback

- Retry a `paused`, `failed`, or `rate_limited` job with `/resume`; the stored
  phase, stream, and page are authoritative.
- `POST …/{id}/abandon` stops automatic work but retains objects and the
  checkpoint. Resume it with `{"recover": true}`.
- `POST …/{id}/rollback` removes the job, its imported objects, and its run
  telemetry. It deliberately preserves the external repository listing and
  never changes the source forge.
- A provider endpoint missing only for an adapter-declared optional stream is
  added to `report.skipped`. A required page the provider will not serve pauses
  the job and appears in `report.failures`. Resume to request that page again,
  or resume with `{"deferFailure": true}` to continue the import. The page and
  the rest of its stream then become retryable failed work, and the report
  lists them as unmeasured instead of calling the import complete.
- A single provider record that cannot be stored without loss (an unsupported
  value, an oversize object) no longer fails its whole page. It is counted as
  failed with its source id and reason, and the rest of the page is imported.

## Migration reports

Every import ends with a signed report: when it completes, when it is
abandoned, and again whenever failed work is retried. It answers what arrived,
what was skipped, what failed, and what remains outside ForkMesh.

```http
GET  /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/report
GET  /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/report?sequence=1
POST /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/retry
```

Both are owner-only and `no-store`. A job that has not ended yet returns an
unsigned `draft` built on request. The export body is machine-readable
(`forkmesh-repository-migration-report-export-v1`) and contains:

| Section | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `summary` | Plain-language lines: records imported, skipped, failed, and external |
| `reconciliation.rows` | Per object type (and `release_assets`): `source`, `imported`, `skipped`, `failed`, `external`, `unclassified` |
| `refs` | Branch and tag names with their commit ids, plus a digest over all of them |
| `artifacts` | Release assets, their provider checksums, and `retained: false` |
| `checksums` | The object manifest digest, the signed state receipt, and release coverage |
| `retries` | Provider rate-limit retries and every failed-work retry with its recovery count |
| `failures` | Failed record count, failure events with source ids, and the retryable work list |
| `externalDependencies` | Wikis, release bytes, missing tags, manifests, and provenance |
| `verification` | One result per check, each linked to the report section or export that reproduces it |
| `remediation` | What to do about each failure reason, with the retry action where one applies |

**Classification.** Each record a provider returns is counted once, on its
page, and lands in exactly one class. `imported` means it is stored.
`skipped` means another type already holds it (a pull request listed on the
GitHub issues endpoint) or the provider listed it twice. `failed` means it
could not be stored. `external` means the source declares it but its bytes
were not copied (release assets). Anything left over is `unclassified`, fails
the reconciliation check, and makes the outcome `unreconciled`. Page entries
are keyed by stream and page, so a page fetched again after a crash replaces
its own counts. Outcomes are `verified`, `completed_with_failures`,
`completed_with_unmeasured_sources`, `unreconciled`, and `abandoned`.

**Signature and history.** The report is canonical JSON. Its SHA-256
`reportHash` is signed over
`forkmesh-repository-migration-report-v1\n<reportHash>` with the relay's
Ed25519 router key, whose public half the relay publishes as
`routerPublicKey` on `GET /api/mirrors/https`. A deployment without that key falls back to the relay HMAC
and labels the signature `hmac-sha256`. Each report carries `sequence` and
`supersedes` (the previous report's sequence and hash), so a retry or a new
full scan adds to the chain instead of replacing it. The export includes the
whole chain; the five most recent reports keep their full body and older ones
keep their hash and signature.

**Retrying only failed work.** `POST …/retry` on a completed import queues
exactly the failed pages and deferred streams, then `/resume` works through
that queue. A retried page replaces what its failed attempt counted. A deferred
stream follows its pagination to the end. When the queue drains, a new signed
report supersedes the old one. Retry does not extend the original transfer
measurement. It returns `409 no_failed_work` when nothing failed and
`409 migration_not_completed` while the import is still running.

**Independent verification.** `tools/verify_migration_report.py` imports no
ForkMesh code. It recomputes the report hash, the Ed25519 signature, the
reconciliation arithmetic, and the supersession chain. Given the object export,
it also recomputes every payload hash, source key, and the manifest digest, so
editing a report or any imported record after signing is detected:

```bash
python3 tools/verify_migration_report.py report.json \
  --objects objects.json --public-key "$ROUTER_PUBLIC_KEY"
```

`objects.json` may be a list of records or saved `…/objects` pages. Exit status
`0` means verified, `1` means a check failed, and `2` means the input could not
be read. Without `--public-key` the key embedded in the report is used, and the
output says so.

**Telemetry.** Reports, exports, retries, and deferrals are written to the
audit log (`repository_migration.report`, `.report_export`, `.retry_failed`,
`.defer_failure`). A rollback records the final report hash. The migration
metrics add `reports.unclassifiedRecords` (the release gate is zero),
`failedRecords`, `externalRecords`, and `retryRecovery.recoveredWork`.

## Automated evidence

The executable fixture suite is
[`app/tests/test_repository_migration.py`](../../app/tests/test_repository_migration.py).
It runs GitHub-, GitLab-, and Codeberg-shaped repositories containing every
supported object family through the real service and SQLite schema. It covers
payload/timestamp/source-id fidelity, secret redaction, duplicate suppression,
process interruption, rate-limit retry, source deletion, repeated signed-state
convergence, abandonment/recovery, rollback, credential non-persistence, and
setup p50/p95 reporting. The dashboard asset and existing external-import
contracts run beside it:

```bash
pytest -q app/tests/test_repository_migration.py \
  app/tests/test_repository_migration_report.py \
  app/tests/test_repository_imports.py app/tests/test_dashboard_bundle.py
```

[`app/tests/test_repository_migration_report.py`](../../app/tests/test_repository_migration_report.py)
covers the reports on all three providers: fixture totals reconcile with no
unclassified remainder, the independent verifier catches report and content
tampering, retry requests only the failed pages and supersedes the report with
its history kept, deferred outages are recovered, a crash-redo page is not
counted twice, and abandoned, rolled-back, and in-progress imports report
honestly without the provider token.

The linked
[`repository-migration-conformance.yml`](../../.github/workflows/repository-migration-conformance.yml)
runs that evidence on Linux, macOS, and Windows for every pull request and
retains the JUnit result for 30 days, including failure-path output.
The same suite is a required `repository-migration-conformance` core/release
gate, and the 180,000 ms setup-p50 ceiling is registered as a non-weakening
performance budget in
[`quality-gates.json`](engineering/quality-gates.json).

The upgrade/runtime schema parity is pinned by migration
[`0152_repository_migration_jobs.sql`](../../app/migrations/0152_repository_migration_jobs.sql),
and the user-visible setup/transfer split is sourced from
[`new-repo-modal.html`](../../app/public/dashboard/partials/new-repo-modal.html).

## Visibility and statuses

Anonymous listing queries filter to `is_private=0` in D1 before any record is
decrypted. A private id returns the same `404` response when it is absent,
guessed, or requested by the wrong account.

Supported status values are:

- `external_repository`
- `stub_only`
- `mirror_requested`
- `partially_mirrored`
- `actively_mirrored`
- `mirror_unavailable`
- `archived`

The two mirrored states require a matching catalog record. `actively_mirrored`
also requires a current live-host heartbeat.

An owner or organization administrator can delete an external listing with
`DELETE /api/repository-imports/{id}`. The website provides select-all and bulk
deletion controls for only the imports the current account can manage. Deleting
the listing never deletes anything from the source provider.

## Ending the provider dependency

An import that only ever links back to GitHub, GitLab, or Codeberg leaves the
user exactly as dependent on that provider as before. Public imports are
therefore materialized as real ForkMesh-hosted repositories:

1. `tools/hosted_repository_sync.py` runs on mirror nodes from
   `forkmesh-hosted-repository-sync.timer` (every 30 minutes). It reads the
   public listing at `<workerOrigin>/api/repository-imports` — the origin comes
   from the node's own configuration, never a hard-coded host — and keeps a
   bare `git clone --mirror` of each eligible entry under
   `/srv/forkmesh-git/imports/<node>/<name>.git`, refreshed with
   `remote update --prune` and compacted after any real ref change.
2. `register` publishes a node-signed catalog record for each hosted clone, so
   the copy is served by the ordinary mirror gateway with no provider in the
   path.
3. The relay links that record back to the import entry
   (`_promote_hosted_repository_import`): the entry becomes
   `actively_mirrored`, gains `mirror.owner`/`mirror.name`, reports
   `sourceCodeFetched`, and the importer receives a `repository_hosted` ping.
   The card in **Repositories** then reads *Fully hosted by ForkMesh* and links
   to `/<targetOwner>/<name>` instead of the provider.
4. `/<targetOwner>/<name>` resolves through `_hosted_repository_import_route`
   to whichever node published the hosted copy. Any publishing node qualifies —
   the resolved owner/name must still appear in the public catalog, so an
   unpublished or blocked pair is never routed to.

Eligibility is deliberately narrow:

- All three supported providers qualify. Only each provider's canonical public
  host is cloned (`github.com`, `gitlab.com`, `codeberg.org`), only in that
  provider's canonical path shape (GitHub and Codeberg name one owner and one
  repository; GitLab allows nested groups), and only when the URL carries no
  credentials, query, or fragment.
- Private imports are never materialized, and an archived entry is dropped.
- Hosted names are one per mirror node, so when two public imports share a
  repository name only the first is hosted. Promotion prefers the import whose
  default branch matches the branch the node published, because a catalog
  record carries no import id to match on.
- Deleting the import entry removes the hosted clone and its catalog record on
  the next run; nothing is ever deleted at the provider.
- A node bounds its imports root (20 GiB) and each first clone (10 minutes).
  Over budget or over time, the entry is deferred or retried rather than
  hosted, so one large repository cannot stop the others from being served.
  `prepare` reports `repositoryCount`, `failedCount`, and `deferredCount`.

The provider remains recorded as attribution and as the upstream the hosted
copy follows. It stops being required to read, clone, or serve the repository.

## Mirror volunteers

`POST /api/repository-imports/{id}/mirror-volunteers` records a request only
when the authenticated account supplies a mirror node it owns: a node-kind
account (a desktop node's own session, or a node linked to the user's account
under Settings › Nodes). A user account cannot volunteer its own name, since no
process could serve that mirror; the request fails with
`eligible_owned_mirror_node_required` and the web app shows the desktop
handoff steps instead. Public reads show the number of volunteers, not their
node/device names.

## Contributor invitations

Only an importer whose provider metadata proves Maintainer/administrator
permission (or a ForkMesh moderator) can create invitations:

```http
POST /api/repository-imports/{id}/invitations
```

The contributor must occur in imported contributor metadata. The inviter must
reference a durable eligibility record; a request-time `basisConfirmed`
boolean is rejected. The supported evidence sources are:

- `public_for_invitations` — a public provider contributor snapshot included an
  explicit public contact address. ForkMesh immediately converts it to a keyed
  blind index and does not copy the raw address into the import record.
- `prior_consent` — the recipient used a signed-in account with a verified
  email to create an import-specific consent record at
  `POST /api/repository-imports/{id}/invitation-consent`.
- `owner_supplied` — a current provider-verified administrator registered the
  address and a source reference at
  `POST /api/repository-imports/{id}/invitation-provenance`. ForkMesh retains a
  keyed digest of the reference, not the raw reference.

The invitation request supplies the returned `provenanceId`. The Worker
matches that record to the exact repository, contributor, and recipient blind
indexes both before the preview and atomically again when reserving the send.
Revoked, mismatched, guessed, and boolean-only evidence fails closed.

Sending requires an explicit `confirm: true`; otherwise the endpoint returns an
invitation preview. Limits apply per inviter, per repository, and per recipient.
Every message identifies the inviter and includes token-protected opt-out and
abuse-report controls. The raw invitation address exists only during the
delivery call; the durable invitation keeps a masked address, a keyed blind
index for matching/cooldown/opt-out checks, and a one-way action-token digest.
Provenance creation, consent/revocation, and sends append metadata-only
sensitive-action audit records.

Provider administrator proof expires after 24 hours. Refresh the import with a
new one-request token before another owner-only action; ForkMesh never retains
the token to refresh permission silently.

Email links use a non-mutating `GET` confirmation response. The recipient must
submit `POST` to opt out or report, so automated email-link scanners cannot
change state.

## Repository logos

Every external entry has a deterministic, locally generated abstract SVG based
on non-sensitive repository name, language, topic, and description metadata.
Owner-authorized local imports may also supply bounded file-structure labels,
framework names, and a project category; file contents are never logo inputs.
It does not copy provider/framework marks and does not use an external model.
The response marks this as `aiGenerated: false`.

Authenticated users can submit PNG, JPEG, or WebP alternatives through:

```http
POST /api/repository-imports/{id}/logo-suggestions
```

The uploader must confirm that they hold the necessary rights. Suggestions
remain pending until a provider-verified owner or ForkMesh moderator approves
one. A verified owner can also replace the generated logo directly. Uploaded
SVG is rejected to avoid script-capable image content, and only one approved
official logo can exist per external entry.

pages.markdown:
# Admin dashboard (`/product-analysis`)

An internal, read-only dashboard for the founders, served by the App Worker at
`https://app.forkmesh.com/product-analysis`. It answers, without SQL: how many
accounts exist, which acquisition channel they came through, whether they
created a mirror, and whether anything is being cloned. It is deliberately
small and must not grow into a business-intelligence tool.

The marketing Worker (`forkmesh.com`) does not proxy or redirect this path;
there is no public version of the page.

## Access

Credentials are two Worker secrets, never anything in the repository:

| Secret | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_USER` | The username the login form accepts. |
| `PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_PASS` | The password. Also the key material for the session cookie. |

Set them from `app/`:

```bash
uvx --from workers-py pywrangler secret put PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_USER
```

```bash
uvx --from workers-py pywrangler secret put PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_PASS
```

Rules the route follows:

- With either secret unset the route does not exist: every request gets the
  ordinary App 404 page.
- An unauthenticated `GET` shows only a sign-in form (username, password),
  with `noindex, nofollow` in the markup and the `X-Robots-Tag` header. No
  section name or figure is rendered before login.
- Any sub-path, any method other than `GET`, `HEAD` or `POST`, any unknown
  `?view=`, and any `POST` action other than `login`/`logout` share the
  ordinary 404 page.
- A correct login mints a signed cookie (`forkmesh_product_analysis`,
  HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, scoped to the path) valid for 12 hours.
  Its HMAC key is derived from the password and `DATA_KEY`, so rotating the
  password signs every founder out immediately.
- Failed logins spend the same per-source budget as account logins
  (`login_attempts`, 10 failures in 15 minutes lock the source for 15
  minutes). A locked source gets `429` with `Retry-After` before the password
  is compared.
- `app/public/robots.txt` disallows the path. There is no admin bootstrap
  endpoint, no "first user becomes admin" logic and no invite flow.
- A signed-in platform administrator is also let in, without the password.
  The check is the admin console's own (`_check_admin_page_auth`: a live
  account session whose account is `is_admin`), so signing out or losing
  the role takes effect on the next request, and the route mints nothing for
  them. With the secrets unset an administrator can still open the page;
  everyone else gets the 404. Apart from that, the two secrets remain the
  whole access model.

The page ships no JavaScript. Its Content-Security-Policy is
`default-src 'none'`, with inline styles only, and it is `no-store`.

## Appearance

The page is the **Product analytics** section of the unified admin: it renders
inside the shared admin shell (`app/src/admin_shell.py`) with the same
sidebar, top bar, GitHub light and dark palettes and components as the
console, acquisition and hackathon pages. Its five views are tabs under the
page heading.

A founder signed in with the password rather than an admin account sees only
this section in the sidebar and a Sign out button, so the page never reveals
the console path. An administrator sees the whole admin sidebar.

Light, dark and system are the switch at the bottom of the sidebar (and under
the sign-in card). It is a plain form posting to `/admin/theme`, which sets
one `forkmesh_admin_theme` cookie for every admin page and redirects back to
the view that was open; without the cookie the page follows the browser's
`prefers-color-scheme`. Below 768px the sidebar becomes a drawer driven by a
hidden checkbox and labels, so there is still no script on the page, and
`prefers-reduced-motion` removes the slide.

## Timezone and windows

Every bucket boundary on every chart and every window in every figure uses
**UTC** (`PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_TIMEZONE` in `app/src/product_analysis.py`). The
Worker stores millisecond epoch timestamps, so UTC is the only timezone that
needs no conversion table.

| Window | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| All time | Every row, no lower bound. |
| Last 30 days | `[now − 30 × 24 h, now)`, ending at the request. |
| Previous 30 days | The 30 × 24 h immediately before "last 30 days". |
| Signups / mirrors per day | The last 90 UTC calendar days including today. |
| Clones per day | The last 30 UTC calendar days including today. |

Every count on the page states its window next to the number. A change is
written as a sentence ("+4 in the last 30 days, 7 fewer than the previous
30 days"); when both windows are empty, or the previous window has no
recorded data, the page says so instead of printing `0%`.

## Sections

The page has exactly five tabs.

### Overview

| Figure | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Total accounts | Rows in `users` whose decrypted record is a user account (kind `user`), any status. Node reservations are excluded. |
| Accounts with at least one mirror | Accounts owning at least one catalog record, directly or through a node they own (`users.data.nodes` and `nodes.user_bi`). The window change counts accounts whose oldest mirror was created in the window. |
| New accounts activated | Accounts created in the last 30 days whose oldest mirror was created no later than 7 days after signup. The change states it as "N of M new accounts" for this window and the 30 days before, and how many new accounts are younger than 7 days and can still activate. This is the marketing funnel's activation stage (`docs/marketing/plan.md`). |
| Returning accounts | Accounts created more than 30 days ago whose last activity (node `last_seen`, account session, presence) falls in the last 30 days, stated as "N of M accounts older than 30 days". Only the latest activity per account is stored, so it has no previous period. This is the marketing funnel's retention stage. |
| Mirrors created | Catalog records in `repositories`, public and private. A "mirror" is one record: a repository as hosted by one owner. |
| Repositories cloned, last 30 days | Distinct `(owner, repo)` pairs with at least one row in `product_clone_daily` inside the window. |
| Anonymous clones, last 30 days | Sum of `product_clone_daily.clones` inside the window. The public HTTPS mirror route serves only non-private repositories and carries no account identity, so every clone it counts is anonymous. Private clones through a node or the SSH gateway are not counted. |
| Clones, all time | `SUM(clones)` over `mirror_serve_counters`, the cumulative counters the Mirrors tab shows. It has no previous period. |

Two charts follow: signups per day over the last 90 days, split into
**organic** and **every other origin** (job flow, referral, unknown), and
mirrors created per day over the same 90 days.

Per-day clone counting begins with the deploy that ships migration 0175.
Until the daily table has rows the two clone figures read "No clone data
yet", and while the previous window is not fully covered the comparison is
declined with the date counting started.

### Signup sources

A table of accounts by origin (count, share of all accounts, accounts with at
least one mirror, share of that origin) and a horizontal stacked bar per
origin: mirror creators in the accent colour, the remainder hatched, so the
split does not depend on hue alone.

### Users

One row per user account: identifier (`users.username`, falling back to the
record name), signup date, signup origin, mirror count, last activity. Sortable
by every column, 50 rows per page, with a search box matching the identifier.
Read-only: no editing, impersonation, deletion or bulk actions exist.

"Last activity" is the newest of the account's newest web session
(`account_sessions.last_seen_at`), its chat presence ping
(`account_presence.ts`) and the last check-in of any node it owns
(`nodes.last_seen`). An account with none of these shows "no activity
recorded".

### Repositories

One row per catalog record: `owner/name`, owner (the human account when the
owner is a node claimed by one, else the catalog owner), visibility, size as
reported by the publishing node, mirror count, clones in the last 30 days,
created date. Sortable and paginated. Below it, clones per day over the last
30 days across all repositories.

"Mirror count" is the number of catalog records sharing the repository's root
commit (or its name when no root is published), the same grouping the network
page uses; a repository nobody else mirrors counts 1.

"Created" is the record's `hostedSince`, the millisecond timestamp the desktop
node stamps when it first hosts the repository. Records without a usable value
show "unknown" and are left out of the per-day chart and the window changes,
and the Overview says how many were left out.

### Acquisition

Rendered as **pending** with a short note. UTM attribution is not merged; the
section carries no placeholder data. When the attribution work lands it should
show sessions, clone-URL copies and signups by `utm_source` and
`utm_campaign` for a fixed last-7-days window, bots excluded with the excluded
count stated, and the note that clone-URL copies are an intent signal, not a
clone count.

Because that copy is fixed, the section is served without building a report at
all: draining and decrypting every account and repository row is most of the
CPU a dashboard request spends, and this page displayed none of it, which was
enough on its own to exceed the Worker CPU limit. `VIEWS_WITHOUT_REPORT` in
`product_analysis.py` lists the views served that way, and a view must leave
that set in the same change that gives it figures to show. A `HEAD` request is
skipped for the same reason: its response carries no body.

## Signup origin derivation

`users.signup_origin` holds one of `job_flow`, `referral`, `organic`,
`unknown` (default). It is a plain category beside `is_admin`, written once by
the backfill and stamped for every new account at signup, never computed at
query time.

Rules, in order (version `v1`):

1. **referral**: the account has a `referral_attributions` row (it arrived
   with a valid referral link, whatever the later credit decision was), or
   its encrypted signup marker names a referrer.
2. **job_flow**: the signup time falls inside a configured job-posting window
   (`PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_JOB_FLOW_WINDOWS`). **No window is configured.** The
   careers page takes applications by email, nothing in the code records a
   job-application signup, and the founders chose to leave the bucket empty
   until they supply the posting dates rather than guess.
3. **organic**: the signup marker was captured and recorded no referrer. The
   marker (`signup.referralCaptured` / `signup.referrer`) exists on accounts
   created since 2026-08-12.
4. **unknown**: everything else. That includes every account created before
   2026-08-12, accounts created by a desktop key-bound flow or federation, and
   node reservations promoted later without a marker.

Known limitation: until job-flow windows exist, a job applicant who signed up
directly after 2026-08-12 is counted as organic. The Signup sources section
and the Overview chart say so.

### How the backfill runs

- Migration `0175_product_analysis.sql` adds the column and applies rule 1 in
  SQL, because `referral_attributions` is plaintext.
- Rules 2 to 4 read the encrypted account record, which SQL cannot. The Worker
  performs that pass the first time an authorised founder opens a dashboard
  view that builds a report (see Acquisition above: the pending sections do
  not), once, guarded by the `schema_meta` key
  `product_analysis_signup_origin_backfill:v1`. It only ever replaces
  `unknown` (or a stale value) with something the rules prove; it never
  downgrades a known origin to `unknown`.
- To classify job flow later: add the `(start_ms, end_ms)` UTC windows to
  `PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_JOB_FLOW_WINDOWS`, bump the marker to `v2`, record the
  windows here, and the next dashboard load re-runs the pass. Accounts already
  marked `organic` inside a window move to `job_flow`.
- New accounts are stamped by `_record_signup_origin` in `entry.py` right after
  the account row is saved, using the same rules. A database still behind the
  migration lacks the column; the stamp is best-effort and never fails the
  signup.

## Data correctness

- Every source table is drained with keyset pagination
  (`scan_table` in `app/src/product_analysis.py`, 200 rows per read) until a
  short page arrives, then the collected row count is compared with
  `COUNT(*)`; grouped reads compare their group count with a matching
  `COUNT`. A mismatch raises, and the page renders an error saying which
  source failed and what to check, in place of every figure that depends on
  it. No default page size can cap an aggregate.
- Sources fail independently: a missing `product_clone_daily` table blanks
  only the clone figures.
- `app/tests/test_product_analysis.py` inserts 250 accounts with the scan
  page forced to 100 and asserts the report returns 250.
- Charts with fewer than seven days of data are replaced by a table of those
  days.

## Where the request runs

Every `/product-analysis` request is serialized into its own App ingress
Durable Object (shard `1`, `_serialized_http_request` and
`_app_ingress_shard` in `app/src/entry.py`). The stateless Worker request has
roughly a 10 ms Pyodide CPU allowance; a Durable Object request has the
30-second Workers budget. One report does not fit the former:

- Building a report drains `users` and `repositories` and AES-GCM decrypts
  every row. Measured against production on 2026-09-10: 240 account records
  and 53 catalog records, 1.41 MB of plaintext.
- **88.9% of that plaintext is `avatar_png`** — profile images stored inside
  the encrypted account record, up to `MAX_AVATAR_BYTES` (256 KB) each. Seven
  accounts held 1.26 MB of the 1.41 MB. The dashboard decrypts and JSON-parses
  every one of those images to read a signup timestamp beside it.
- `GET /product-analysis?view=users` answered 503/1102 at 462 ms CPU
  (1036 ms wall). Overview, Signup sources and Repositories failed
  intermittently beside it, whichever load landed on a busy isolate.

The shard is the route's own. Nothing else may be moved onto it: no other
traffic family should share an isolate with a load that heavy, and a founder
opening the dashboard should not be poisoned by one either.

The ingress placement buys headroom; it does not make the report cheap. The
cost grows linearly with accounts, and the avatar payload dominates it, so
moving avatars out of the account record is the fix that would make every
account read cheaper — login, profile, World roster and notification digests
all decrypt the same records.

## Operations

- **Rotate the password**: `pywrangler secret put PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_PASS`. Every
  session is invalid from the next request.
- **Disable the route**: delete either secret. The path returns 404.
- **D1 writes**: every clone served through the public HTTPS mirror route now
  performs one extra upsert (`product_clone_daily`) beside the existing
  serve-counter upsert. Both are best-effort and never fail the served read.
- **Down migration**: `app/migrations/down/0175_product_analysis.sql` drops the
  column, the daily table and the backfill marker.

## Decisions this build made that the brief did not settle

- **Access model**: the founders asked for a username and password from
  environment secrets, which overrides the brief's `is_admin` session
  reuse. Consequence: the sign-in form is the one page an unauthenticated
  visitor can see; everything else answers 404.
- **Job flow is unclassified** by the founders' decision; the bucket exists
  and the rule slot is empty.
- **Organic** means "direct signup with a recorded referral marker", which the
  marker's introduction date bounds to accounts created since 2026-08-12.
- **Anonymous clones** are clones through the public HTTPS mirror route; that
  route only serves non-private repositories and has no account identity.
  Counting starts at deploy, so the figure has no history.
- **A mirror is a catalog record**; the per-repository mirror count uses the
  network page's root-commit grouping.
- **"Created" for a repository** is `hostedSince`; older records without it
  are reported as undated rather than dated from another field.
- **Activation is a first mirror within 7 days of signup** (added
  2026-10-04 by the Marketing special agent). Counting any mirror ever
  created would favour older cohorts, which have had longer to activate, so
  the two 30-day windows could not be compared. Seven days is the window the
  first-repository experiment (`docs/experiments/first-repository-activation-2026-10.md`)
  reads.
- **Retention is a count, not a cohort curve**: the stores keep only each
  account's latest activity, so the figure can say who came back in the last
  30 days but not who was active in an earlier window.
- **Timezone** is UTC because every stored timestamp already is.
- **The backfill for encrypted signals runs in the Worker** (once, marked in
  `schema_meta`) because a D1 migration cannot decrypt account records.
- **The signup-sources chart plots organic against everything else** rather
  than organic against job flow, because job flow is empty; the table below
  it gives every origin exactly.
- **Docs live at `www/docs/admin-dashboard.md`**, the repository's docs tree,
  since there is no top-level `docs/` directory.

pages.markdown:
# Cloudflare Workers AI coding agent

ForkMesh ships a provider-neutral coding runtime backed by Cloudflare Workers
AI. The same runtime runs an installed local model (Gemma 4 through Ollama, or
any llama.cpp-style OpenAI-compatible server) as a first-class agent backend.
It uses only the Python standard library and is embedded in the desktop
release; the canonical, testable source is `tools/forkmesh_coding_agent.py`.

## Architecture

The runtime separates model transport from repository operations:

| Component | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `Agent` | Reusable model/tool/final-answer loop |
| `Planner` | Captures Git state before starting work |
| `Conversation` | Role-separated chat and tool history |
| `Memory` | Repository context, project summary, edited files, token budget, and compaction |
| `Session` | Atomic JSON persistence and usage metadata |
| `ToolRegistry` | Extensible JSON-schema catalog and dispatch |
| `CloudflareProvider` | Workers AI chat completions, SSE, tool calls, retries, and cancellation |
| `OllamaProvider` | Ollama's native `/api/chat`: context sizing, thinking control, keep-alive, exact token counts, tools-capable model discovery |
| `LocalLlamaProvider` | llama.cpp-style OpenAI-compatible transport (used when the local endpoint is not Ollama) |
| `PromptBuilder` | System, developer, memory, conversation, and tool-role separation |
| `CommandExecutor` | Bounded asynchronous shell execution |
| `GitManager` | Status, diff, commit, branch, stash, and restore |
| `FileEditor` | Whole-file, exact-text, and patch edits with preview and undo |
| `SearchEngine` | Bounded directory, glob, and text search |

The Cloudflare Agents SDK is not required. ForkMesh keeps the loop local because
the desktop worktree, Git identity isolation, session UI, and patch capture are
already owned by the desktop agent runner. The provider boundary is deliberately
small so another chat-completions provider can be added without changing tools
or session state.

The default tools are `read_file` (whole file or a `start_line`–`end_line`
range), `write_file`, `replace_text`, `apply_patch`, `undo_edit`,
`search_files`, `grep`, `list_directory`, `execute_command`, `git_status`,
`git_diff`, `git_commit` (stages every change, or only `paths`), `git_log`,
`git_branch`, `git_stash`, `git_restore`, `run_tests`, and `lint_project`. A
compatibility `bash` tool remains available for smaller instruction models.

The loop is built for small models as much as large ones. The first prompt
carries the tracked-file tree so the model does not guess paths; argument
types are coerced to the tool schema and a missing argument or unknown tool
comes back with the tool's signature; a tool call the model writes as JSON
text (a fenced block, `<tool_call>`, or a bare object) runs as if it had used
the structured channel; every tool result is bounded; a reply cut off at the
output cap earns one nudge to work in smaller steps; identical repeated calls
are not re-run and three stalled turns end the run; and old tool outputs are
elided before the conversation is summarized.

## Desktop: Cloudflare Workers AI

Choose **Cloudflare AI** in an issue or prompt composer, then choose a model
offered by the relay. The desktop creates an isolated worktree, signs a
time-limited run ticket, and sends each provider turn to `/api/ai/agent`. Tool
calls run only in the desktop worktree; the relay never receives filesystem
access. The model catalog comes from `/api/forkbot/models`, so deploying a new
model does not require rebuilding the desktop.

The relay requires the Workers AI binding in `app/wrangler.toml`:

```toml
[ai]
binding = "AI"
```

Set `FORKBOT_AI_MODEL` in the deployed Worker configuration to the desired
default. Keep tokens in Worker secrets or the desktop's local settings, never
in a repository.

## Complete Gemma example

The library can also call Cloudflare's OpenAI-compatible API directly. Model,
account, token, endpoint, generation limits, and retry policy are runtime
configuration; no model identifier is compiled into `CloudflareProvider`.

```bash
export FORKMESH_AGENT_PROVIDER=cloudflare
export FORKMESH_AGENT_ACCOUNT_ID='your-account-id'
export FORKMESH_AGENT_API_TOKEN='your-workers-ai-token'
export FORKMESH_AGENT_MODEL='@cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it'
export FORKMESH_AGENT_TEMPERATURE=0.2
export FORKMESH_AGENT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=2000
export FORKMESH_AGENT_CONTEXT_WINDOW=32000
export FORKMESH_AGENT_TIMEOUT=600
export FORKMESH_AGENT_STREAMING=true
export FORKMESH_AGENT_RETRY_COUNT=4
export FORKMESH_AGENT_SESSION_PATH=/tmp/forkmesh-gemma-session.json

python3 tools/forkmesh_coding_agent.py issue.md
```

`issue.md` contains the coding request. Run this command from the checked-out
worktree. The account ID derives the standard endpoint; set
`FORKMESH_AGENT_ENDPOINT` to use a custom Workers AI or AI Gateway endpoint.
`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` are accepted as credential
fallbacks.

The loop sends the role-separated conversation and tool schemas, executes each
requested tool, records the result as a tool message, and continues until the
model gives a final answer. Tool turns stay quiet: their planning text and
private `<think>`, `<analysis>`, or `<reasoning>` blocks never enter the run
log, while the actual tool call and result remain visible. A completed final
answer is then shown as one concise reply. Reasoning deltas remain hidden unless
`FORKMESH_AGENT_SHOW_REASONING=true` is explicitly set.

## Local Llama

ForkMesh detects an installed Ollama-compatible server at
`http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions`. Start Ollama, install a
tools-capable model (the marketplace's **Gemma 4** package pulls one), then
choose **Local Llama** in the desktop. Leave the model blank to select the
first installed model that can call tools, or enter its installed name under
**Settings → Agents → Local Llama model**.

When the endpoint's host answers `GET /api/version`, the runtime switches to
Ollama's native `/api/chat` route. That route lets the agent size the
model's context (`num_ctx`) to its own `FORKMESH_AGENT_CONTEXT_WINDOW` plus
headroom, capped at the model's trained length; turn thinking off (the
default, since on a CPU-bound host it multiplies the time per step) or on
through **Settings → Agents → Local Llama thinking**; keep the model loaded
for 30 minutes between tool runs; and read exact prompt and generation
counts, which the session's network panel shows alongside tokens per second.
A model without the `tools` capability is refused with a message naming a
model that has it. Set `FORKMESH_AGENT_LOCAL_API=openai` to force the
OpenAI-compatible route (llama.cpp, vLLM), or `ollama` to skip the probe.

The equivalent command-line session is:

```bash
export FORKMESH_AGENT_PROVIDER=local-llama
export FORKMESH_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions
export FORKMESH_AGENT_MODEL='the-name-shown-by-ollama-list'
python3 tools/forkmesh_coding_agent.py issue.md
```

For llama.cpp, point the endpoint at its OpenAI-compatible chat-completions
route and set the model explicitly. Local mode sends no Cloudflare credentials
and has no provider charge.

### Ollama serving parameters

The native route sends `num_ctx`, `num_predict`, and `temperature` itself; only
the OpenAI-compatible route depends on the installed tag, where Ollama's
4096-token default context silently truncates conversations sized for
`FORKMESH_AGENT_CONTEXT_WINDOW`. On either route a partial GPU offload can
abort the runner: Gemma-class models split across a
Vulkan device terminate with
`GGML_ASSERT(n_inputs < GGML_SCHED_MAX_SPLIT_INPUTS) failed`, which the endpoint
returns as an HTTP 500. Pin both on the tag before selecting it:

```bash
cat > Modelfile <<'EOF'
FROM gemma4:e4b
PARAMETER num_ctx 32768
PARAMETER num_gpu 0
EOF
ollama create gemma4:e4b -f Modelfile
```

`num_gpu 0` keeps every layer on the CPU, and `ollama show <model> --parameters`
reports what a tag currently serves. Measure before offloading; a many-core host
can outrun a small consumer GPU on both prefill and generation.

## Configuration reference

All values are optional unless required by the selected transport:

| Environment variable | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_PROVIDER` | `cloudflare`, `local-llama`, or another compatible provider | `cloudflare` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_MODEL` | Runtime model identifier | Provider/discovery default |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_ENDPOINT` | Full chat-completions URL | Derived for Cloudflare; Ollama URL locally |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_API_TOKEN` | Bearer token for direct HTTP | Empty |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_ACCOUNT_ID` | Cloudflare account ID used to derive the endpoint | Empty |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_TEMPERATURE` | Sampling temperature | `0.2` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | Maximum tokens per provider turn | `2000` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_CONTEXT_WINDOW` | Conversation budget before compaction | `32000` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_TIMEOUT` | Provider and command timeout in seconds | `600` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_STREAMING` | Enable SSE text streaming | `true` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_RETRY_COUNT` | Retries for rate limits, 5xx, and network failures | `4` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_RETRY_BASE_DELAY` | Initial exponential-backoff delay | `1` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_MAX_TURNS` | Hard agent-loop limit | `120` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_MAX_IDLE_TURNS` | Consecutive turns that only redo earlier work before the run gives up | `100` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_SHOW_REASONING` | Emit provider reasoning deltas | `false` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_SESSION_PATH` | Optional durable JSON session path | Empty |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_TEST_COMMAND` | Command used by `run_tests` | Empty |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_LINT_COMMAND` | Command used by `lint_project` | Empty |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_PREVIEW_EDITS` | Preview structured edits instead of applying them | `false` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_TOOL_OUTPUT_LIMIT` | Characters kept per tool result (head and tail) | `12000` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_THINKING` | Local models: `off`, `on`, or `low`/`medium`/`high` where supported | `off` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_KEEP_ALIVE` | How long Ollama keeps the model loaded between turns | `30m` |
| `FORKMESH_AGENT_LOCAL_API` | `ollama` or `openai` to skip the local backend probe | Auto-detected |

## Editing and recovery

Structured paths are repository-relative and reject absolute paths, `..`
escapes, and symlink escapes. `write_file`, `replace_text`, and `apply_patch`
support previews. Applied `FileEditor` batches can be reverted with `undo_edit`;
Git-level recovery is available through stash and restore. Commands have closed
stdin, bounded output, and a timeout. ForkMesh isolates attempted global Git
configuration writes so an agent cannot replace the user's identity, disables
interactive credential prompts, and never pushes automatically.

Run the core unit suites with:

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q app/tests/test_coding_agent.py app/tests/test_local_agent.py
```

When changing `tools/forkmesh_coding_agent.py`, regenerate the desktop asset:

```bash
python3 tools/sync_coding_agent_header.py
```

pages.description: You do not need a ForkMesh account to read or clone a public project. The website never redirects you to sign-up or log-in just to read. It asks you to sign in only when you try…
pages.markdown:
# Reading and cloning without an account

You do not need a ForkMesh account to read or clone a public project. The
website never redirects you to sign-up or log-in just to read. It asks you to
sign in only when you try to change something.

## What works without an account

| Surface | Without an account |
| --- | --- |
| Repository overview, code tree, files, branches, commits | Readable |
| Issues and issue detail | Readable |
| Pull requests, their files, and review threads | Readable |
| Discussions, projects, insights | Readable |
| Releases and signed release manifests | Readable and downloadable |
| Mirrors and availability (`/owner/repo/mirrors`) | Readable |
| Public profiles (`/@name`) | Readable |
| `git clone https://forkmesh.com/owner/repo` | Works; no credentials are sent to a mirror |
| Remote ActivityPub replies on public records | Readable |

Clone URLs from other forges, such as `/owner/repo/pull/7` or GitLab's
`/owner/repo/-/merge_requests/7`, redirect to the readable ForkMesh page, not
to an auth page. See [Git compatibility](git-compatibility.md) for clone
transports and their limits.

## Where you are asked to sign in

These actions send you to `/login?next=<the page you were on>`, so you come
back to the same page afterward:

- starring or forking a repository;
- opening an issue, sub-issue, or pull request, or commenting on or reviewing one;
- changing issue state, labels, or assignees;
- copying an issue's agent prompt, which contains a connector token;
- finishing a desktop node link (`?link_node=`), which must attach to an account;
- opening account-only pages: settings and your own profile.

A write request the relay rejects with `401` also sends you to sign in. No
other response does.

## Browser identity and handoff to a node: not yet available

The following are **not yet available**. Until they ship, a first
contribution needs a regular account:

- a passkey-backed **browser identity** that signs comments, issues, reviews,
  and patches, with a consent prompt at signing time;
- exporting that identity, or handing it to a full node, without losing
  authorship, history, follows, or recovery options.

The recovery kit that later handoff builds on is described in
[Portable identities and recovery](portable-identities.md).

## Evidence

The "never redirect to registration" rule is covered by automated tests:

- `app/browser_tests/tests/anonymous-public-reading.spec.js` loads the
  repository overview, issues, pull requests, a pull request detail, releases,
  mirrors, branches, and commits in a browser with no session. It fails if the
  page moves or any navigation reaches `/login` or `/signup`.
- `app/tests/test_anonymous_public_reading.py` checks five things:
  - every public repository view is served as a repository page;
  - the Worker only redirects to `/login` from admin pages;
  - every client-side sign-in redirect follows a write or account check;
  - the guest start-up path treats only settings and your own profile as
    account pages;
  - this page exists and is linked from the docs index.

pages.description: This is the repeatable weekly operating view for the acquisition loop and its economic boundary. The authoritative definitions, numerator/denominator, source, privacy class, and…
pages.markdown:
# Activation-to-revenue weekly scorecard

This is the repeatable weekly operating view for the acquisition loop and its
economic boundary. The authoritative definitions, numerator/denominator,
source, privacy class, and availability of every row live in the [versioned
metric dictionary](outcome-metrics.json). This page is the reporting
template; it does not create a second definition for a metric.

The rows below are the dictionary's `weekly` metrics. Monthly community,
migration, availability, and hosted-adoption KPIs, together with the decisions
and roadmap changes they drive, are recorded in the [monthly outcome
review](outcome-review.md).

## Reporting contract

- Use the most recent complete Monday–Sunday week in UTC. Record the exact
  `periodStart`, `periodEnd`, `generatedAt`, and data-owner sign-off.
- Read acquisition sessions, events, clone snapshots, mirror counters, and
  consented feature events to exhaustion. Every continuation page is part of
  the report. A page size of 100 is a transport limit, never a population
  limit.
- A source total and collected-row total must reconcile before a value is
  published. If they do not, write `UNKNOWN — reconciliation failed`; never
  show the partial first page.
- Keep first-touch acquisition cohorts, anonymous clone totals, and closed
  accounting periods visibly separate. They answer different questions and
  must not be joined as if a clone or a dollar had a browser session.
- Record exclusions and coverage beside every value. Bot filtering, consent
  opt-out, missing snapshot baselines, and missing accounting evidence are
  part of the result, not footnotes.

## Copy for each week

```text
Week: YYYY-MM-DD through YYYY-MM-DD UTC
Generated at: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ
Dictionary: forkmesh-outcome-metric-dictionary-v2 / version 2
Owners: Growth=<name>; Product=<name>; Infrastructure=<name>; Finance=<name>; Support=<name>
Data cut: acquisition=<timestamp>; product analytics=<timestamp>; finance=<timestamp>
Pagination audit: pages collected=<n>; provider/source rows=<n>; all continuations exhausted=true|false
Quality state: COMPLETE | PARTIAL | UNKNOWN
Decision: <one sentence>
```

| Stage | Metric id | This week | Prior week | WoW | Target/guardrail | Coverage/confidence | Source check / decision |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| Acquisition | `landing_activation` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `anonymous_clone` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `signup` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `first_mirror` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `contribution` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `managed_service_qualification` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `paid_conversion` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `retention` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Product | `feature_adoption` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `support_load` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `infrastructure_cost` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `gross_margin` |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Use `n/a` for a mathematically undefined rate and `UNKNOWN` for a missing or
unreconciled source. `WoW` is `(this week - prior week) / prior week` only when
the denominator is non-zero and coverage is comparable. Keep the raw unit next
to the displayed number: counts, hours, micro-USD, or basis points are not
interchangeable.

## Funnel readout

The first-touch activation view may show these directional rates when the same
cohort and exclusion policy is used:

```text
signup rate          = signup / landing_activation
first-mirror rate    = first_mirror / signup
contribution rate    = contribution / first_mirror
qualification rate  = managed_service_qualification / managed_waitlist_submitted
paid conversion      = paid_conversion numerator / paid_conversion denominator
```

The first three are attributed session rates. `anonymous_clone` is deliberately
not in those divisions because Git clients do not carry the browser cookie.
`paid_conversion`, `retention`, and `gross_margin` are accounting measures and
must use their own closed-period denominators. Feature adoption is an opt-in
coverage signal, not a total-population adoption rate.

## Reconciliation checklist

Run this checklist before circulating the scorecard:

1. Load [the metric dictionary](outcome-metrics.json) and confirm
   its schema/version are unchanged from the scorecard header:

   ```sh
   python3 tools/outcome_metrics.py validate-dictionary
   python3 tools/outcome_metrics.py review --input /path/to/week.json
   ```

   The review output carries each row's freshness and confidence; copy them
   into the `Coverage/confidence` column.
2. For acquisition data, call the existing `channel_report`; verify that
   `sessions_collected` and `events_collected` equal their source
   `total_count` values after `collect_all` follows every `next_cursor`.
3. Run the pagination regression with more than one 100-row page:

   ```sh
   cd app
   pytest -q tests/test_attribution.py \
     -k 'report_returns_all_250_rows_not_the_page_size or page_past_100_rows or count_mismatch_raises'
   pytest -q tests/test_activation_revenue_scorecard.py
   ```

   The tests must collect 250 sessions, 130 events, and 150 clone snapshots
   through continuation cursors; reject a reader that returns only the first
   200 rows while claiming 250 exist; and prove every dictionary source,
   locator, and report reader still exists.
4. Reconcile anonymous clones to adjacent daily snapshot rows and retain the
   number of snapshot rows collected. Never add `clone_url_copied` to that
   total.
5. Reconcile feature adoption to the complete consented provider export,
   including its continuation-page count, and state opt-in coverage.
6. Validate the closed accounting period and margin calculation:

   ```sh
   python3 tools/unit_economics.py validate-contract
   python3 tools/unit_economics.py report --input /path/to/period.json
   ```

   Attach billing reconciliation, provider invoice, support review,
   portability, recovery, and security/privacy evidence. A missing input is a
   blocker, not a zero.

7. Write exclusions, privacy boundary, freshness, and confidence next to the
   scorecard. Do not include raw email, account, repository, path, IP,
   provider-customer, or support-case identifiers.

## Decisions and interpretation

Use the scorecard to choose one action for the next week: a landing or proof
experiment, a contribution/onboarding fix, a qualified-service interview, a
support-load reduction, or a cost/margin intervention. A falling acquisition
number with stable clones may be attribution coverage; a falling margin with
stable revenue is a cost or allocation issue. Record that hypothesis and the
follow-up owner rather than changing a metric definition mid-week.

The current managed-services offer remains a research preview. A qualification
or paid-conversion row can measure demand and validated billing evidence without
turning the free protocol, public reading, public cloning, self-hosting, or
portable Git data into paid entitlements.
