pages.markdown:
# Repository availability contracts

A repository availability contract is a precise preservation promise. It names
how many verified copies a repository keeps, how many independent operators
and regions hold them, which transports and refs they serve, how often that is
checked, how fast incidents are answered and recovered, and what the customer
is credited when the promise is missed.

Each contract period produces a `forkmesh-availability-contract-report-v1`
report. The report is computed only from an evidence bundle, so anyone holding
the bundle can recompute it and check its signature. It shows every
verification slot that missed, every SLO miss, the credit each miss earned, the
capacity that was actually demonstrated, and what a simulated operator or
regional failure leaves behind.

This is the contract model and its verifier. Managed checkout stays disabled
until the gates in the [business model](business-model.md) pass; the model does
not open it.

## Evidence bundle

A bundle has the schema `forkmesh-availability-contract-evidence-v1`:

| Field | Contents | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contract` | `id`, `repository`, `periodStart`, `periodEnd`, `feeMicrousd`, `terms`, `remedies`, `exclusions` | The signed order |
| `observations` | `GET /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/mirrors` payloads, each with its `generatedAt` | The mirrors API, carrying signed endpoint receipts and direct clone probes |
| `drills` | Restore drill records | `forkmesh-mirror-node --restore-drill` (`mirror-gateway/node-ops/last-restore-drill.json`) |
| `responses` | `incidentStart` and `acknowledgedAt` for each acknowledged incident | The incident log |
| `capacity` | `node` and `class` (`community` or `contracted`) | The order's capacity declaration |

Each observation is scored by the [availability proof](availability-proof.md)
exactly as the Mirrors tab scores it. Observations outside the period are
ignored and counted in `evidence.ignoredObservations`.

## Contract terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `copies` | Verified copies that must hold the counted state in every slot. |
| `operators` | Distinct operators that must hold the same verified state in every slot. At least 2, the availability proof's quorum target, and no more than `copies`. |
| `regions` | Distinct declared regions among verified copies in every slot. |
| `uptimeBps` | Share of counted slots, in basis points, that must meet every check. |
| `verificationIntervalMs` | Slot length, at least one minute. A period can have at most 10,000 slots. |
| `transports` | Transports that each need at least one verified copy: `router`, `directHttps`, `smartHttp`. |
| `refCoverage` | When true, at least `operators` verified copies must carry every branch. |
| `artifactCoverage` | When true, at least `operators` verified copies must carry every release artifact. |
| `recoveryTimeObjectiveMs` | Longest allowed incident, and the slowest allowed restore drill. |
| `drillIntervalMs` | Oldest allowed restore drill at period end. |
| `incidentResponseMs` | Longest allowed time from an incident's start to its acknowledgement. |
| `failureTolerance` | How many operators, and separately how many regions, may fail at once while the quorum holds (0 to 2). |
| `maxExcludedBps` | Share of slots that exclusions may remove. |

Malformed terms stop evaluation with a closed error code, such as
`invalid_operators` or `too_many_slots`. A bad contract never yields a
partial report.

## Verification slots

The period is split into slots of `verificationIntervalMs`. Every observation
in a slot must pass every check. A slot with no observation is `unverified`,
because missing evidence is a miss, not a pass.

| Check | The slot misses when |
| --- | --- |
| `unverified` | No observation was recorded in the slot. |
| `quorum_below_contract` | Fewer than `operators` distinct operators held the same verified state. Copies whose clone probes disagree on the refs digest do not count. |
| `copies_below_contract` | Fewer than `copies` verified copies held the counted state. |
| `regions_below_contract` | Verified copies spanned fewer than `regions` regions. |
| `transport_missing` | A contracted transport had no verified copy. |
| `ref_coverage_incomplete` | Fewer than `operators` copies carried every branch, or no branch count was known. |
| `artifact_coverage_incomplete` | Fewer than `operators` copies carried every release artifact, or no artifact count was known. |

Availability is `met slots * 10000 // counted slots`. The division rounds
down, so any rounding favors the customer.

## Exclusions

An exclusion removes whole slots from the count. Evidence in those slots is
still recorded, but it cannot miss or meet. It is honored only when:

- its kind is `scheduled-maintenance`, `customer-requested`, or `legal-hold`;
- it was announced (`announcedAt`) no later than its start; and
- the exclusion budget (`maxExcludedBps` of all slots) is not used up. Earlier
  exclusions use the budget first.

Every exclusion is listed with the slots it removed and, when it did not remove
everything it asked for, a reason:

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `unknown_kind` | The kind is not one of the three contract kinds. |
| `announced_late` | It was announced after it started, so it cannot be applied retroactively. |
| `over_budget` | It was honored, but some of its slots were beyond the exclusion budget and still count. |

## Incidents, recovery, and response

Consecutive missed slots form one incident. An excluded slot neither ends nor
extends an incident, but its time still counts toward recovery. An incident
recovers at the start of the next counted slot that meets every check. Recovery
is measured in whole slots, so it is never shorter than what the evidence
shows. An incident still open at period end is measured to period end.

Response is measured from the incident's start to the earliest
acknowledgement recorded for that start:

| Response | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | Acknowledged within `incidentResponseMs`. |
| `late` | Acknowledged after `incidentResponseMs`. |
| `missing` | Not acknowledged, and the response window has closed. |
| `pending` | Not acknowledged yet, but still inside the response window at period end. |

## Restore drills

A drill record counts when it has `drill: true`, a node name, a `completedAt`
time (Go RFC 3339 with nanoseconds, or epoch milliseconds), a `durationMs`, and
at least one restored repository. The **latest** drill for a node at period end
decides its state, so an older passing drill cannot hide a newer slow one:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | The latest drill is within `drillIntervalMs` and took no longer than `recoveryTimeObjectiveMs`. |
| `drill_missing` | The node has no drill record. |
| `drill_stale` | The latest drill is older than `drillIntervalMs`. |
| `drill_beyond_objective` | The latest drill took longer than `recoveryTimeObjectiveMs`. |

See [node backup and recovery](operations/node-backup-and-recovery.md) for how
operators run drills.

## SLOs

| SLO | Target | Met when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `availability` | `uptimeBps` | Attainment is at least the target over at least one counted slot. |
| `recovery` | `recoveryTimeObjectiveMs` | No incident outlasted the objective. |
| `incident-response` | `incidentResponseMs` | No incident was acknowledged late or left unacknowledged. |
| `restore-drills` | Every contracted node | Every node declared `contracted` has an `ok` drill. |

The period `outcome` is `met` only when all four SLOs are met.

## Misses and remedies

Every miss is listed, even when its SLO is still met. A short incident inside
the uptime target is visible, but it earns no credit.

| Miss | SLO | Listed for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `availability_window` | `availability` | Every incident. |
| `recovery_objective_exceeded` | `recovery` | Every incident that outlasted the recovery objective. |
| `response_late` | `incident-response` | Every incident acknowledged late. |
| `response_missing` | `incident-response` | Every incident never acknowledged. |
| `drill_missing` | `restore-drills` | Every contracted node without a drill. |
| `drill_stale` | `restore-drills` | Every contracted node whose latest drill is too old. |
| `drill_beyond_objective` | `restore-drills` | Every contracted node whose latest drill was too slow. |

Credits come from the contract's `remedies`:

- When availability is missed, the largest `availabilityTiers` credit whose
  `belowBps` is above the attained value applies once. It covers every
  availability window. No tier may start above `uptimeBps`, so a met SLO can
  never earn a tier credit.
- Each recovery, response, and drill miss earns its fixed
  `recoveryMissCreditBps`, `responseMissCreditBps`, or `drillMissCreditBps`.
- The total is capped at `maxCreditBps`, and `capped` says when the cap applied.

Money is integer micro-USD: `fee * creditBps // 10000`. Each miss names the
remedy line that covers it, and each remedy line lists its misses.

## Demonstrated capacity and admission

A contract may only be backed by capacity that was demonstrated. A node is
demonstrated when both of these hold:

- **Continuous probes.** Every observation in at least `uptimeBps` of the
  counted slots verified it, so it must have a fresh signed endpoint receipt or
  a passing clone probe each time.
- **A restore drill.** Its latest drill is `ok`.

`capacity.nodes` lists every observed or declared node with its class, opaque
operator, region, verified slots, and drill state. Totals are reported
separately for `community` capacity (independent mirrors the customer does not
pay for) and `contracted` capacity (paid, controlled nodes). A declaration
other than `contracted` is treated as community, so a typo can never claim paid
capacity.

The contract is admissible only when demonstrated capacity alone meets the
terms. Otherwise `admission.reasons` lists why:

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `no_evidence` | The period has no observation. |
| `copies_not_demonstrated` | Fewer demonstrated copies than `copies`. |
| `operators_not_demonstrated` | Fewer demonstrated operators than `operators`. |
| `regions_not_demonstrated` | Fewer demonstrated regions than `regions`. |
| `failure_simulation_failed` | A simulated failure broke the quorum or its recovery, or there was nothing to simulate. |

Run the report over a trailing qualification window before accepting an order.
Run it again each period, so capacity that stops demonstrating is flagged.

## Simulated failures

The simulation takes the period's latest observation and keeps only
demonstrated nodes. It then removes every combination of `failureTolerance`
operators, and separately every combination of `failureTolerance` regions, and
recomputes the availability proof on what is left. Nodes that declared no
region share one `undeclared` failure domain. With `failureTolerance` 0, the
simulation checks the demonstrated capacity once, with nothing removed.

A simulation passes when the remaining operators still meet `operators` and a
surviving node's restore drill finished within `recoveryTimeObjectiveMs`. That
survivor can rebuild the lost copies within the objective.

## Correlated-risk disclosures

These do not change the outcome. Each one names a way the promise could fail
together, and it links back to this section.

### `community_capacity_relied_on`

Contracted capacity alone does not reach the promised operator quorum. The
promise then depends on independent community mirrors that are not under
contract and can leave at any time.

### `contracted_single_operator`

Two or more contracted copies are demonstrated, and one operator runs all of
them, so contracted capacity fails together.

### `operator_concentration`

A single operator runs more than half of the demonstrated copies.

### `region_concentration`

More than half of the demonstrated copies share one region, or declared no
region.

### `no_failure_headroom`

Demonstrated operators do not exceed the promised quorum, so losing any one
operator breaks it.

### `capacity_not_demonstrated`

A node declared as contracted capacity lacks continuous verified probes or a
qualifying restore drill, so it does not count toward the contract.

## Privacy

Operator accounts are never shown. Copies run by the same operator share an
opaque operator number for the whole bundle. Endpoint addresses, mirror URLs,
drill archive paths, and node keys are never shown either. The shared fixture
plants private strings in its evidence, and the tests fail if any of them
appears in a report.

## Signed reports

A signed report is a `forkmesh-availability-contract-signed-report-v1`
document holding `report`, `reportHash`, and an Ed25519 `signature`. The hash
is `sha256:` over the report's canonical JSON: sorted keys, no whitespace, and
UTF-8. The signature covers
`forkmesh-availability-contract-report-v1\n<reportHash>`. The report's
`evidence` section records digests of the contract, capacity, observations,
drills, and responses, so a report names exactly what it was computed from.

```sh
tools/forkmesh_availability_contract.py explain bundle.json         # plain-language summary
tools/forkmesh_availability_contract.py explain --json bundle.json  # full report
tools/forkmesh_availability_contract.py sign bundle.json --private-key seed.txt > signed.json
tools/forkmesh_availability_contract.py verify bundle.json signed.json --public-key <base64url key>
tools/forkmesh_availability_contract.py fixture                     # verify the shared fixture
```

`verify` recomputes the report from the bundle, checks the hash, and checks the
signature. It rejects a report that was edited after signing, even when the
hash is recomputed, and it rejects evidence edited after signing. Without
`--public-key` it still checks the signature, but only against the key embedded
in the document, and says the key is not pinned.

`explain` exits 0 when the contract was met with admissible capacity, and 3
otherwise. `verify` and `fixture` exit 0 on a match and 1 on a mismatch.
Unreadable input or invalid terms exit 2.

## Conformance

- `conformance/availability-contract/v1/model.json` sets out the terms,
  checks, SLOs, misses, states, reasons, disclosures, and policy.
- `conformance/availability-contract/v1/fixture.json` holds one case for every
  check, miss, drill and response state, admission reason, exclusion reason,
  disclosure, and simulation scope. The cases include a regional outage that
  keeps its quorum and an operator failure beyond tolerance.
- `conformance/availability-contract/v1/generate_fixture.py` builds the
  fixture. Each case carries a hand-written outcome, admission reason list,
  miss list, and disclosure list, so a reference change that moves any of them
  fails loudly. Run it with `--check`.

Run `python -m pytest app/tests/test_availability_contract.py` to check the
reference, CLI, signatures, and documentation against the fixture.

## Limitations

- Restore drill records are node-local operation records, not signed. The
  report records their digest, but it cannot prove a node ran the drill it
  reports.
- A drill record counts restored repositories, not which ones, so a drill
  proves the node can restore its backups in general, not this repository
  specifically.
- No Worker API, dashboard panel, or billing flow publishes these reports yet.
  The report is produced and signed offline from exported evidence.

## Rollout and rollback

The model is additive. No Worker route imports it, and it is listed in
`LAZY_MODULES` so it never counts toward Worker startup. To roll back, delete
the module, CLI, suite, and this page; no stored data changes. To change the
model, edit `model.json` and the reference implementation, run
`generate_fixture.py`, and update this page until the suite passes.

pages.description: The Mirrors tab on every repository answers three questions: is this repository actually preserved, how independently, and what is still at risk. The answer is the…
pages.markdown:
# Availability proof and repository risk

The Mirrors tab on every repository answers three questions: is this repository
actually preserved, how independently, and what is still at risk. The answer is
the `forkmesh-availability-proof-v1` report. The Worker computes it from the
same mirrors payload it publishes, so anyone can recompute it and get the same
result.

## Evidence

The report reads only timestamped evidence that already appears in
`GET /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/mirrors`:

| Evidence | Fields | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Signed endpoint receipt | `endpointFresh`, `endpointHealthy`, `endpointIntegrity`, `checkedAt` | The router's challenge of the node's signed endpoint registration |
| Direct clone probe | `directVerified`, `directCheckedAt`, `directRefsSha256` | A Smart HTTP probe of the registered mirror URL against its signed refs |
| Integrity gate verdict | `integrity`, `behind`, `status`, `lastSeen` | The clone integrity gate and presence |
| Operator and region | `ownerUser` or `owner`, `region` | The signed catalog record and endpoint registration |
| Coverage | `branchCount`, `artifactCount`, `operations` | The node's signed catalog record |

`generatedAt` is the observation time. Nothing else feeds the report.

**Freshness objective.** A signed endpoint receipt counts for 10 minutes, the
same window the router trusts it for. So dashboard values are never older than
10 minutes, and the API's edge cache adds at most 3 seconds. Direct clone probes
run when someone asks for one, so a passing probe counts for 24 hours.

## Copy classes

Each copy gets one class. When more than one could apply, the earlier row wins:

| Class | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `failing` | The integrity gate rejected the copy, the node is blocked for abuse, or its latest clone probe (within 24 hours) failed. |
| `verified` | The copy is online, current, and has integrity `ok`. It also has a signed endpoint receipt within the freshness objective, or a clone probe that passed within 24 hours. |
| `declared` | Only a catalog record exists; nothing has ever observed the copy. |
| `stale` | The copy was observed before, but is now offline, behind, or has no evidence within the freshness objective. |
| `observed` | The copy is online and was seen within the freshness objective, but has no signed receipt or passing probe yet. A copy that declares a `replicaScope` other than `full` (a filtered, metadata-only, or deferred-object replica; see [Offline and low-bandwidth sync](offline-sync.md)) is `observed` with `limited_replica` even when its evidence is fresh. |

Each copy also lists closed reason codes: `integrity_rejected`, `abuse_blocked`,
`probe_failed`, `offline`, `behind`, `evidence_expired`, `awaiting_receipt`,
`never_observed`, `limited_replica`.

## Trusted quorum

A repository has a quorum when at least **2 distinct operators** hold the same
verified state. The count is of operators, not nodes, so one operator running
several machines can never make a quorum alone.

If clone probes on verified copies return different refs digests, only copies
matching the digest backed by the most operators count. Copies with no digest
are left out, and `state_disagreement` is reported. A copy that is failing,
stale, observed, or only declared never counts, so a limited replica can never
make or inflate a quorum.

| Proof | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `quorum` | Independent operators hold the same verified copy. |
| `partial` | At least one copy is verified, but not by enough independent operators. |
| `none` | No copy has fresh signed evidence. |

A source-host outage raises risk (`source_offline`) but does not remove a quorum
that mirrors already prove. A mirror outage removes that mirror from the quorum
as soon as its receipt expires.

## Risk score

The score is the sum of the weights of every risk code that applies, capped at
100. Levels: `critical` from 60, `high` from 30, `moderate` from 10, otherwise
`low`. Risks are listed heaviest first.

## Risk codes

### `no_verified_copy`

Weight 50, critical. No copy has a fresh signed endpoint receipt or a passing
clone probe. **Remediation:** ask a node to mirror the repository. Repository
owners can do this from the Mirrors tab ("Ask a node to mirror this repo").
Anyone can also [run a mirror node](operations/) and mirror it themselves.

### `quorum_not_met`

Weight 25, high. Fewer than 2 independent operators hold the same verified
state. **Remediation:** ask a node run by a different operator to mirror the
repository.

### `state_disagreement`

Weight 20, high. Clone probes on verified copies returned different refs
digests. **Remediation:** run the direct URL check again on each mirror
(**check** in the Endpoint column). A mirror that stays on a different digest
should re-sync from the source.

### `single_operator`

Weight 10, medium. Two or more copies are verified, but one operator runs all of
them. **Remediation:** ask a different operator to mirror the repository.

### `failing_copy`

Weight 10, medium. At least one copy was rejected by the integrity gate, blocked
for abuse, or failed its latest clone probe. **Remediation:** the node's
operator re-syncs the mirror from the source and runs the direct URL check again.

### `source_offline`

Weight 10, medium. The working-copy source is offline, so mirrors that fall
behind cannot re-sync. **Remediation:** start the ForkMesh desktop or headless
node that holds the working copy.

### `no_direct_clone_url`

Weight 10, medium. No verified copy has passed a direct clone probe in the last
24 hours, so clones depend on the ForkMesh router. **Remediation:** the mirror
operator registers a direct mirror URL, and anyone runs its direct URL check.

### `partial_ref_coverage`

Weight 10, medium. Fewer verified copies carry every branch than the quorum
target requires. The reference is the highest branch count among the source and
the verified copies. **Remediation:** re-sync the mirrors with every branch.

### `stale_copy`

Weight 5, low. At least one copy is offline, behind, or has expired evidence.
**Remediation:** bring the mirror back online or let it catch up; it becomes
verified again at its next signed receipt.

### `partial_artifact_coverage`

Weight 5, low. Fewer verified copies carry every release artifact than the
quorum target requires. **Remediation:** re-sync the release artifacts to the
mirrors.

### `single_region`

Weight 5, low. Two or more copies are verified, every one declared a region, and
all declared the same region. **Remediation:** ask a node in another region to
mirror the repository.

### `declared_only_copy`

Weight 3, low. A node published a catalog record, but nothing has ever observed
it serving. **Remediation:** check that the node's endpoint is registered and
reachable.

## Privacy

Operator accounts are never shown. Copies run by the same operator share an
opaque operator number (1, 2, …), so you can see how independent the copies are
without learning who runs them. Endpoint addresses, mirror URLs, and free-form
probe reasons from the evidence are never shown either. Node names and
operator-declared regions already appear on the public mirrors payload. The
shared fixture plants private strings in its evidence, and the test suite fails
if any of them appears in a report.

## Where it appears

| Client | Where | Implementation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API | `availability` on `GET /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/mirrors` | `app/src/availability_proof.py` |
| Web | Availability proof panel on the repository Mirrors tab, with risk remediation and per-copy evidence | `app/public/dashboard/js/07-repo-compose-branch.js` |
| CLI | `tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py` | reuses the API implementation |

## Reproduce a report

```sh
curl -s https://app.forkmesh.com/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/mirrors > mirrors.json
tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py verify mirrors.json         # recompute and compare
tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py explain mirrors.json        # plain-language summary
tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py explain --json mirrors.json # machine-readable report
tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py fixture                     # verify the shared fixture
```

`explain` exits 0 when the quorum is proven and 3 when it is not. `verify` exits
0 when the published `availability` matches the recomputed report and 1 when it
does not. Both exit 2 when the input cannot be read.

## Conformance

- `conformance/availability-proof/v1/model.json` sets out the classes, reasons, proof states, levels, risk weights, and policy.
- `conformance/availability-proof/v1/fixture.json` holds a case for every risk code and class. It also holds sequences for a mirror outage, a source-host outage, and an integrity failure; each one ends recovered.
- `conformance/availability-proof/v1/generate_fixture.py` regenerates the expected output. Every entry also records a hand-written proof, risk list, and class list, so a reference change that moves any of them fails loudly. Run it with `--check`.

Run `python -m pytest app/tests/test_availability_proof.py` to check the
reference, CLI, API wiring, and web rendering against the fixture.

## Rollout and rollback

The `availability` field is additive, and older clients ignore it. Rolling back
the Worker removes the field, and the Mirrors tab hides the panel; the mirror
table and the `syncStatus` line are unaffected. To change the model, edit
`model.json` and the reference implementation, then run `generate_fixture.py`
and update this document until the suite passes.

pages.markdown:
# Community-reviewed contextual placements

ForkMesh calls these placements “community-reviewed,” not “ethical company”
badges. Approval means disclosed public evidence met an instance’s current
criteria for a limited period. It is not a universal endorsement and it may be
appealed, suspended, or expire.

The machine-readable criteria are returned by
`GET /api/world/community-ads/criteria`. Proposals disclose the sponsor,
beneficial-ownership context, product, data use, tracking, labor,
accessibility, environmental and community-impact evidence. At least two
distinct public HTTPS sources are required.

Voting is one eligible verified account per proposal, never wallet-weighted.
Accounts must be active, email-verified, and at least seven days old. Voters
declare conflicts; a conflicted voter may only abstain and publish a
disclosure. Approval needs the proposal quorum and at least two-thirds of
non-abstaining votes. Records preserve evidence provenance, moderation,
appeals, and a review deadline no later than 180 days.

Each independently operated instance is disabled by default and explicitly
selects placement contexts and a public revenue purpose. Placements receive
only a coarse page context such as `town-square` or `repository`; ForkMesh does
not use profiles, browser/OS/country badges, search terms, repository privacy,
wallets, or behavioral history for targeting. Every response says
“Community-reviewed placement” and `tracking: none`.

Member-written text ads reviewed by an instance's administrators are a
separate system, [ForkMesh Ads](operations/ad-network.md). A community-reviewed
placement always takes priority over one where both could appear.

Advertising receipts use the dedicated `community_ad_revenue` ledger class.
They are not user funds, pending rewards, completed on-chain transfers, or the
community reward pool. A revenue record references an external accounting
event; the Worker does not custody or transfer the money.

pages.title: Preservation-first crisis onboarding
pages.description: Use this guide when a project could disappear soon: a planned shutdown, a takedown risk, a lost account, censorship, or a provider shutting down. It helps you do three things
pages.markdown:
# Preservation-first crisis onboarding

Use this guide when a project could disappear soon: a planned shutdown, a
takedown risk, a lost account, censorship, or a provider shutting down. It helps
you do three things:

1. Pick a plan that fits the time and access you still have.
2. Preserve the most important data first.
3. Get an honest account of what is actually safe and what is still at risk.

The plan is `forkmesh-crisis-preservation-plan-v1`. The assessment of what was
preserved is `forkmesh-crisis-preservation-assessment-v1`, and a timed drill is
`forkmesh-crisis-preservation-drill-v1`. All three come from one pure
reference implementation, so the API, the CLI, and the shared fixture always
give the same answer.

## Start here

1. Get a plan. Name your scenario, and add the time you have if you know it:

   ```sh
   curl -s 'https://app.forkmesh.com/api/preservation/crisis-plan?scenario=urgent_takedown&minutes=45'
   tools/forkmesh_crisis_preservation.py plan urgent_takedown --minutes 45
   ```

2. Work through `steps` in order. Each included step has an `action`: start
   the [resumable import](repository-imports.md), push a local clone, export
   your [portable identity](portable-identities.md), or ask another operator to
   mirror the repository.
3. Read `tradeoffs` before you start. In urgent mode, a plan that leaves
   anything out sets `acknowledgementRequired`. Every item there will be
   reported as skipped or unavailable, never as preserved.
4. When the work ends, download the migration report and the mirrors payload,
   then assess them:

   ```sh
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SESSION" \
     https://app.forkmesh.com/api/repository-imports/migrations/$JOB/report > report.json
   curl -s https://app.forkmesh.com/api/repo/$OWNER/$REPO/mirrors > mirrors.json
   tools/forkmesh_crisis_preservation.py assess request.json \
     --report report.json --availability mirrors.json
   python3 tools/verify_migration_report.py report.json --objects objects.json
   ```

## Scenarios

Each scenario sets a default time window, default access, a priority order, and
a drill budget. You can override the window and access. A lost account caps
access at `public`, because without the account only public data can be read.

### `planned_shutdown`

You are closing the project or its hosting on a known date, and you still
control the account. Default window 30 days, default access `owner`.
Priority: `refs`, `releases`, `documentation`, `issues`, `artifacts`, `identity_proofs`, `trusted_mirrors`.
Drill budget: **120 minutes**.

There is time for everything. Import all of it and publish the artifacts. Then
have two independent operators prove the copy before the shutdown date.

### `urgent_takedown`

A takedown, suspension, or removal could happen at any moment. This scenario is
always in urgent mode. Default window 1 hour, default access `owner`.
Priority: `refs`, `identity_proofs`, `trusted_mirrors`, `releases`, `documentation`, `issues`, `artifacts`.
Drill budget: **30 minutes**.

Get the Git history and your identity proofs out first, then a copy held by a
second operator. Anything the window cannot hold is listed as skipped.

### `lost_account`

You no longer control the provider account that owns the repository. Default
window 1 day, access capped at `public`.
Priority: `refs`, `identity_proofs`, `trusted_mirrors`, `releases`, `documentation`, `issues`, `artifacts`.
Drill budget: **60 minutes**.

Preserve the public data. Prove you are the maintainer with the keys and proofs
you still hold, not with the lost account. A private repository can only be
preserved from a local clone (`localClone`). Its issues, releases, and artifact
files stay unavailable.

### `censorship`

The repository is blocked, or likely to be blocked, in a region or by the
provider. Default window 4 hours, default access `public`.
Priority: `refs`, `trusted_mirrors`, `identity_proofs`, `releases`, `documentation`, `artifacts`, `issues`.
Drill budget: **60 minutes**.

Independence matters more than completeness here. Copies held by different
operators in different regions keep the project readable when one path is
blocked. The [availability proof](availability-proof.md) counts operators, not
nodes.

### `provider_eol`

The hosting provider or product is being discontinued. Default window 7 days,
default access `owner`.
Priority: `refs`, `releases`, `documentation`, `issues`, `artifacts`, `identity_proofs`, `trusted_mirrors`.
Drill budget: **120 minutes**.

Everything the provider holds goes with it, including artifacts and
integrations. Import all of it, and replace every provider-only dependency
before the end date.

## How a plan is built

The request is `scenario`, and optionally `minutes` (1 to 525,600), `access`
(`owner`, `read`, `public`, or `none`), and the repository's `sizeMb`, `issues`,
`releases`, `assetsMb`, `private`, and `localClone`. Any size you leave out uses
a default (100 MB, 500 issues, 20 releases, 200 MB of artifacts). The plan lists
those defaults in `assumed`.

The plan walks the scenario's priority order. It includes each category whose
estimate fits the time that remains, and records why it left anything out.
Estimates are deliberately conservative:

| Category | Estimate |
| --- | --- |
| `refs` | 2 minutes + 1 minute per 50 MB of repository |
| `identity_proofs` | 5 minutes |
| `trusted_mirrors` | 10 minutes for the first signed receipt + 1 minute per 50 MB |
| `artifacts` | 2 minutes + 1 minute per 50 MB of artifact files |
| `releases`, `documentation`, `issues` | Provider pages at 30 pages a minute with a token, 1 a minute without one |

**Import order.** One import job copies provider data in a fixed phase order:
issues, pull requests, and reviews first; then releases and documentation; then
labels, users, and discussion history. So it finishes `releases`, then
`documentation`, then `issues`, and it cannot skip ahead. Each estimate is the
extra time until the import finishes that category. It can be 0 when two
categories finish in the same minute. If one import category does not fit, every
later one is deferred with `import_order`.

**Urgent mode.** A plan is urgent when the scenario is `urgent_takedown` or the
window is 240 minutes or less. In urgent mode, a plan with any tradeoff sets
`acknowledgementRequired: true`. The summary names every category that is not
planned.

**Git history always starts.** `refs` is required. If it cannot fit, it is still
included, flagged `over_budget`, and the summary says so.

## Reasons

Every step that is not included, and every over-budget step, carries one reason
and a tradeoff with its consequence and follow-up.

### `time_budget`

Higher-priority data uses up the time available. Run a follow-up when time
allows. Until evidence arrives, the category stays skipped.

### `requires_token`

The source is private, and the access you have cannot read it. Resume the
import with a read-scoped token if you get access back.

### `source_unreachable`

The source can no longer be reached (`access: none`), and no local clone holds
this data. Check the repository's Mirrors tab for copies other operators already
hold.

### `import_order`

The import copies provider data in a fixed order, and an earlier part did not
fit, so this part will not be reached in the window.

### `needs_refs`

Mirrors can only be requested once the Git history is being preserved. Preserve
`refs` first.

### `over_budget`

`refs` is required, but its estimate is longer than the time available. Start it
now. The plan cannot promise it finishes.

## Coverage states

An assessment gives each category exactly one state. **Only evidence can make a
category `preserved` or `empty`.** Without evidence, the plan's decision picks
the label: included becomes `missing`, deferred becomes `skipped`, and
unavailable stays `unavailable`.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `preserved` | Evidence proves a complete copy. |
| `empty` | Evidence proves the source has nothing of this kind. |
| `partial` | Evidence proves some of it, but records failed, stayed external, went unread, or are unaccounted for. |
| `failed` | Evidence shows the attempt produced nothing usable. |
| `missing` | Planned, but no evidence has arrived. |
| `skipped` | Deferred by the plan, with no evidence. |
| `unavailable` | Out of reach with the access available, with no evidence. |

The evidence for each category:

| Category | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `refs` | An availability proof with a verified copy that carries every branch. A migration report alone is only `partial`, because it captures ref names, not the Git history. |
| `identity_proofs` | `identity.recoveryKitVerified` (the recovery-kit restore drill passed) and `identity.externalProofVerified` (an external-account proof verified). One of the two is `partial`. |
| `trusted_mirrors` | An availability proof with `quorum` is `preserved`, and `partial` is `partial`. |
| `issues` | Report rows `issues`, `pull_requests`, `reviews`, `labels`, `users`, and `collaboration_history`. |
| `releases` | Report row `releases`. |
| `documentation` | Report row `documentation`. The wiki is a separate repository. |
| `artifacts` | Availability artifact coverage on a verified copy. The report's `release_assets` row can only prove `empty`, because the import does not copy artifact bytes. |

The assessment recomputes each report row. It does not trust the report's
`reconciled` flag. A category is `preserved` only when the report completed,
every one of its rows adds up, and nothing failed, stayed external, or went
unread. The assessment does not check the report's signature. Check it with
`tools/verify_migration_report.py`.

`verifiedUsableMirror` is true when an availability proof is `quorum` or
`partial` and `refs` is `preserved`. `status` is `preserved` when every category
is preserved or empty, `partial` when a verified usable mirror exists, and
`at_risk` otherwise.

## Risks to understand

Every plan lists these six topics, in the order that matters most for its
scenario.

### `ownership`

A copy does not transfer ownership. Keep the license, copyright notices, and
contributor attribution with every copy. Record who may act for the project.

### `legal`

Each node operator answers legal requests for their own node. A lawful takedown
of one copy does not remove the others, and ForkMesh cannot make an operator
keep or remove a copy. See the [node operator policy](operations/node-operator-policy.md).
Get legal advice before you republish content that is subject to a notice.

### `secrets`

A mirror copies every secret ever committed. Rotate exposed credentials before
mirroring, and see [secret scanning](security/secret-scanning.md). Never put
provider tokens into a copy. ForkMesh never stores them.

### `verification`

Only evidence counts: a reconciled, signed migration report and an availability
proof with verified copies. Check the report signature yourself.

### `external_dependencies`

A metadata import does not copy release artifact files, wikis, CI logs, package
registries, or links to the old provider. The migration report lists each one
under `externalDependencies`.

### `emergency_contacts`

Report a compromised account or leaked key to **security@forkmesh.com**. Name
recovery contacts for your [portable identity](portable-identities.md) before
you need them.

## Getting help without lock-in

Every plan lists the same routes. Every route has the same exit: `git clone
--mirror`, the signed migration report export, and the portable identity kit all
work without ForkMesh.

| Route | Who | Payment | Available |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `self_serve` | You: a resumable import and your own mirror node, free and MIT-licensed | No | Yes |
| `community_mirror` | Independent operators asked from the Mirrors tab; they choose what they carry | No | Yes |
| `managed_recovery` | Paid verified recovery | Yes | No: a research preview, not for sale |

Paid recovery is never offered as available before it is sold. Under the
[business model](business-model.md), it would run a replaceable role with no
authority over your repository.

## Drills

A drill proves a scenario works before you need it. Start the plan, then record
`startedAt` and the time a verified usable mirror and a migration report both
existed (`verifiedAt`, in milliseconds):

```json
{
  "id": "2026-09-urgent",
  "request": {"scenario": "urgent_takedown"},
  "startedAt": 1800000000000,
  "verifiedAt": 1800001500000,
  "evidence": {"migrationReport": {}, "availability": {}, "identity": {}}
}
```

```sh
tools/forkmesh_crisis_preservation.py drill drill.json
```

A drill passes when it meets its scenario's budget and has no failures:

| Scenario | Drill budget |
| --- | --- |
| `urgent_takedown` | 30 minutes |
| `lost_account` | 60 minutes |
| `censorship` | 60 minutes |
| `planned_shutdown` | 120 minutes |
| `provider_eol` | 120 minutes |

| Failure | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_timing` | `startedAt` or `verifiedAt` is missing, or the drill ends before it starts. |
| `over_time_budget` | The verified copy and report took longer than the budget. |
| `no_migration_report` | No readable migration report was supplied. |
| `migration_report_unreconciled` | The report has not completed, or its rows do not add up. |
| `no_verified_mirror` | No verified copy carries every branch. |

A passing drill can still have skipped categories. `residualRisks` lists each one.

## API and CLI

```http
GET /api/preservation/crisis-plan
GET /api/preservation/crisis-plan?scenario=lost_account&private=1&localClone=1
```

Without `scenario`, the endpoint returns the `forkmesh-crisis-preservation-catalog-v1`
catalog: scenarios, access levels, categories, states, and routes. With one, it
returns the plan. Both are public and cached for five minutes. A bad value
returns `400` with a closed code: `unknown_scenario`, `invalid_minutes`,
`unknown_access`, or `invalid_<field>`.

Assessments and drills read owner-only migration reports, so they run locally in
`tools/forkmesh_crisis_preservation.py` and never send a report to the Worker.
The CLI exits 0 for a built plan, a fully preserved assessment, or a passed
drill. It exits 3 for at risk, partial, or failed, and 2 for unreadable input.

## Conformance

- `conformance/crisis-preservation/v1/model.json` sets out the scenarios, policy constants, reasons, states, routes, and drill failures.
- `conformance/crisis-preservation/v1/fixture-input.json` holds shared evidence blocks and hand-written expectations. It covers 9 plans, 11 assessments, 12 drills, and 3 sequences (retry, mirror outage, and import rollback), and each sequence ends recovered.
- `conformance/crisis-preservation/v1/generate_fixture.py` checks the reference output against those expectations, then writes `fixture.json`. Run it with `--check`.

Run `python -m pytest app/tests/test_crisis_preservation.py` to check:

- The reference, the fixture, and the CLI.
- The Worker route, using the real handler source.
- A drill built from a real migration report and a real availability proof.
- Sweeps over every scenario, window, access level, and repository shape. They
  prove that no plan exceeds its window unless `refs` is over budget, that every
  tradeoff is explained, and that data without evidence is never marked
  preserved.

## Telemetry

`GET /api/preservation/crisis-plan` is listed in the endpoint catalog, so its
traffic appears in the API metrics groups. The plan endpoint stores nothing
about the request. Crisis migrations themselves show up in the
[migration metrics](repository-imports.md#migration-reports).

## Rollout and rollback

The route and module are additive. Rolling back the Worker removes the endpoint.
Imports, reports, and availability proofs are unaffected. To change the model,
edit `model.json`, the reference implementation, and `fixture-input.json`, run
`generate_fixture.py`, and update this document until the suite passes.

## Not covered yet

- A guided web journey. Today the plan is served by the API and the CLI.
- A directory of recovery partners beyond community mirror operators.
- Crisis-specific outcome telemetry: time to verified copy and recovery success
  per scenario, measured from production drills.

pages.title: Stable repository identity and dependency workflows
pages.description: A build that depends on source mirrored through ForkMesh should keep working, and keep installing exactly the same bytes, when the hosting provider changes or the original host…
pages.markdown:
# Stable repository identity and dependency workflows

A build that depends on source mirrored through ForkMesh should keep working,
and keep installing exactly the same bytes, when the hosting provider changes or
the original host disappears. This guide defines the identity and pinning rules
that make that true, and gives tested recipes for stock Git, pip, npm, Go, and
Cargo. No client is modified and no ForkMesh tool is needed at install time.

The contract is `conformance/dependencies/v1/contract.json`. The reference
rules are `app/src/stable_repository.py`, and
`tools/dependency_conformance.py` proves every recipe with unmodified clients.

## Identity: what a dependency really names

| Concept | Value | Changes when the repository moves? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Logical identity | `urn:forkmesh:repository:sha256:<64 hex>` | No |
| Pinned content | A full 40- or 64-hex commit object ID | No |
| Routes | `https://HOST/OWNER/REPOSITORY`, `https://HOST/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git`, `ssh://git@HOST/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git` | Yes, and that is fine |

- The **logical identity** is protocol requirement FM-ID-001 applied to the
  verified root `git-root-commit:<root commit>`. The root commit comes from the
  account-key-signed catalog record. Every faithful mirror of a repository has
  the same root commit, so every mirror has the same identity.
- Hosts, owners, organization aliases, repository names, and URLs are routing
  hints only. Renaming, transferring, or re-hosting a repository never changes
  its identity.
- A record with no root commit (an empty repository, or a record from an old
  client) has no identity. ForkMesh returns an empty string rather than
  inventing one from a name, because a name-based identity would change when
  the repository moved.

The public [repository index](repository-index.md) returns `identity` on every
search result.

Both HTTPS spellings reach the same repository. The `.git` form matters because
Go module paths, Cargo, and the published SSH URL all use it.

## Pinning rule

A dependency is pinned by **identity plus full commit object ID**. Branch names,
tags, and abbreviated IDs are routing conveniences, not pins:

- The resolver rejects a branch, tag, or short ID with `mutable_pin`.
- It rejects a malformed identity with `identity_invalid`.
- It rejects a pinned ref outside `refs/heads/` or `refs/tags/` with `ref_invalid`.

Git object IDs are content hashes, so a client that holds a full commit ID
detects substituted content on its own. The route rules below make sure that
failure is visible and explained, not silent.

## Switching providers without editing a lock

Write manifests and locks against one **logical base URL**, for example the
URL you first depended on. Then point that base at whichever provider is active
with Git's standard URL rewrite:

```sh
git config --global url."https://ACTIVE-PROVIDER/".insteadOf "https://LOGICAL-HOST/"
```

Every recipe below runs Git under the hood, so this one line moves all of them
together. Lock files keep naming the logical URL and the same commit, so they
stay byte-for-byte identical. To roll back, restore the previous `insteadOf`
line; no manifest or lock changes. In CI, set the rewrite in the job
environment (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` or `git config --global`) rather than in the
repository.

## Recipes

Each recipe shows the manifest line and the lock evidence the probe compares
across providers. `LOGICAL_URL` is `https://LOGICAL-HOST/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git`,
and `COMMIT` is the full commit object ID.

### Git

```sh
git clone LOGICAL_URL dependency
git -C dependency checkout --detach COMMIT
```

Lock evidence: the checked-out commit (`git rev-parse HEAD`).

### Git submodule

```sh
git submodule add LOGICAL_URL deps/dependency
git -C deps/dependency checkout --detach COMMIT
git add deps/dependency && git commit -m "Pin dependency"
```

Consumers run `git clone --recurse-submodules`. Lock evidence: the gitlink
object ID in the superproject tree. Each submodule URL is its own repository;
see the [Git compatibility matrix](git-compatibility.md#submodule-authorization).

### pip

```text
dependency @ git+LOGICAL_URL@COMMIT
```

Put this line in `requirements.txt` or in `dependencies` in `pyproject.toml`.
Lock evidence: `vcs_info.commit_id` in the installed package's
`direct_url.json`.

### npm

```json
{ "dependencies": { "dependency": "git+LOGICAL_URL#COMMIT" } }
```

Lock evidence: `resolved` for the package in `package-lock.json`, which names
the logical URL and the commit.

### Go modules

```sh
GOPROXY=direct GOPRIVATE=LOGICAL-HOST go get LOGICAL-HOST/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git@COMMIT
```

Lock evidence: the `h1:` module and `go.mod` hashes in `go.sum`. The module
path keeps the `.git` suffix, so Go talks to Git directly and needs no HTML
discovery page. `GOPRIVATE` (or `GONOSUMDB`) is required because the public
checksum database cannot see this host; `go.sum` still verifies every later
download. A tag re-pointed after the lock was written fails with a
`checksum mismatch`.

### Cargo

```toml
[dependencies]
dependency = { git = "LOGICAL_URL", rev = "COMMIT" }
```

Set `CARGO_NET_GIT_FETCH_WITH_CLI=true` so Cargo uses the Git CLI and therefore
the `insteadOf` rewrite. Lock evidence: the `source = "git+LOGICAL_URL?rev=COMMIT#COMMIT"`
line in `Cargo.lock`.

## Fallback: deterministic, visible, verified

The stable HTTPS URL is served by the ForkMesh relay. Before it sends any
response bytes, it checks candidate hosts **in their declared order**, never by
load or latency:

1. The host must answer (`unreachable` otherwise).
2. It must serve the same logical identity (`identity_mismatch` otherwise).
3. Its refs must hash (FM-ID-005) to a repository state the source signed
   (`state_unverified` otherwise).

For a dependency pin, two more checks apply:

4. The host must hold the pinned commit (`commit_missing` otherwise).
5. A pinned ref must still point at that commit (`ref_moved` otherwise).

Every resolution reports a status:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `resolved` | The first declared route proved the content. |
| `failed_over` | A later route proved it; each skipped route is listed with its reason. |
| `unavailable` | No route proved it (`no_verified_route`). Nothing is served in its place. |
| `rejected` | The pin itself is unusable (for example `mutable_pin`). |

A route that fails any check is never selected. When every route fails, the
build fails with a normal transport error. It never silently falls back to
mutable or unverified content.

## Tested scenarios

`tools/dependency_conformance.py run` builds disposable loopback providers:
an origin, a faithful mirror, a tampered copy whose `main` was rewritten
without being signed, and a retagged copy. It runs each available client
through these scenarios:

| Scenario | Active route | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `install` | Origin | Installs the pinned commit; records lock and content digests. |
| `provider-switch` | Mirror, through `insteadOf` | Installs; lock and content identical to `install`. |
| `origin-lost` | Relay: lost origin, then mirror | Installs; resolution `failed_over`; lock identical. |
| `unverified-fallback` | Relay: lost origin, then tampered copy | Refused before any bytes; resolution `unavailable` with `state_unverified`. |
| `missing-commit` | Origin, pinned to an absent commit | Every client fails; the resolver reports `commit_missing`. |
| `moved-tag` | Retagged copy | Go fails with a `go.sum` checksum mismatch; the resolver reports `ref_moved`. |
| `rollback-recovery` | Relay: restored origin, then mirror | Installs; resolution `resolved`; lock identical to `install`. |

A client that exits successfully but records a different commit counts as
`substituted`, which always fails the suite.

## Report and telemetry

Each run writes a `forkmesh-dependency-conformance-report-v1` JSON report:
exact client versions, platform, per-scenario outcomes, lock and content
digests, and every relay resolution with its attempts. The summary carries the
primary measures:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `resolutionSuccess` / `resolutionAttempts` | Relay requests that selected a verified route, out of all relay requests. |
| `failoverSuccess` / `failoverAttempts` | Requests whose first route was unreachable and that still resolved, out of all such requests. |
| `reproducibleLocks` / `lockChecks` | Installs after a provider switch, origin loss, or recovery whose lock and content digests matched the original install. |
| `verificationFailures` | Routes or pins rejected for `state_unverified`, `identity_mismatch`, `commit_missing`, or `ref_moved`, plus Go checksum refusals. |
| `unexpectedResults` | Scenario outcomes that did not match the contract. Must be 0. |
| `unavailableClients` | Selected clients not installed or below the minimum version. |

Reports never contain temporary paths, loopback URLs or ports, file contents,
credentials, or client addresses.

## Supported clients and platforms

| Client | Minimum | Continuous evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Git and Git submodules | 2.34.0 | `dependency-conformance.yml` on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows |
| pip | 23.0 | same |
| npm | 9.0.0 | same |
| Go modules | 1.21 | same |
| Cargo | 1.70.0 | same; optional locally, required in CI |

Every CI run uploads its report as an artifact. The workflow passes `--require`
for every client, so a runner image that drops a client fails the run instead
of skipping it.

## Run the suite

```sh
python3 tools/dependency_conformance.py validate
python3 tools/dependency_conformance.py run --output artifacts/dependency-conformance.json
python3 tools/dependency_conformance.py run --clients git,pip --require git,pip
python3 -m pytest -q app/tests/test_dependency_workflows.py
```

`run` exits 0 when every scenario matched, 1 on an unexpected result or a
missing required client, and 2 when the probe could not run at all.

## Limits

- HTTPS routes are read-only. Publish changes over SSH; see the
  [Git compatibility matrix](git-compatibility.md#https-receive-pack).
- Public repositories only. Private repositories use owner-sealed replicas and
  have no public route.
- Packages served from a registry (PyPI, the npm registry, crates.io, a Go
  module proxy) are outside this contract. These recipes install directly from
  Git.
- A relay can prove only the states the source signed. The client-side pin (a
  commit ID, `go.sum`, or a lock file) is what protects content once it has
  been accepted.

## Rollout and rollback

The `.git` route spelling and the index `identity` field are additive, and
older clients ignore them. Rolling back the Worker removes both. Existing
`https://HOST/OWNER/REPOSITORY` URLs are unaffected, but a `.git`-suffixed HTTPS
URL would again look up a repository literally named `REPOSITORY.git` and fail.
To change the contract, edit `contract.json`, the reference, and this guide
together until `validate` and the test suite pass.

pages.title: Disaster recovery
pages.description: Use this guide to prepare a community for the day its normal infrastructure is gone: the origin host is wiped, forkmesh.com is down, names stop resolving, a signing key is lost…
pages.markdown:
# Disaster recovery

Use this guide to prepare a community for the day its normal infrastructure is
gone: the origin host is wiped, forkmesh.com is down, names stop resolving, a
signing key is lost, a region is cut off, or a backup turns out to be corrupt.
It covers what to prepare, how to recover, and how to prove recovery works
before you need it.

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [runbook.md](runbook.md) | The printable runbook: triage, roles and checklists, prerequisites, a decision tree per scenario, procedures with verification and rollback, and an exercise worksheet. |
| [exercise-register.md](exercise-register.md) | Every recorded exercise, its findings and corrective owners, and what closure still needs. |
| [`conformance/disaster-recovery/v1/runbook.json`](../../../conformance/disaster-recovery/v1/runbook.json) | The runbook source (`forkmesh-disaster-runbook-v1`). `runbook.md` is generated from it. |
| `tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py` | Validates and renders the runbook, builds and verifies the bootstrap kit, manages the roster and key rotations, and runs drills. |

Tracking issue: #518. The runbook builds on
[offline and low-bandwidth sync](../offline-sync.md),
[transports and anonymity postures](../transports.md),
[self-hostable service roles](../operations/service-roles.md),
[node backup and recovery](../operations/node-backup-and-recovery.md), and
[portable identities](../portable-identities.md).

## Start here: prepare before a disaster

1. **Make keys.** One kit key, one export key per mirror operator, and one
   recovery key for each custodian. Keep the seeds on separate devices, held by
   different people.

   ```sh
   tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py keygen kit.key          # prints the kit public key
   tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py keygen export.key
   tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py keygen recovery-1.key   # one per custodian
   ```

2. **Write the community roster** (below), then check it:

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster check roster.json
   ```

3. **Build the bootstrap kit** onto removable media, and write the kit public
   key and the manifest digest it prints on paper:

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py kit build /media/usb/forkmesh-kit \
     --signing-key kit.key --roster roster.json
   ```

4. **Print [runbook.md](runbook.md)** and keep it with the kit. Write the
   runbook digest and the kit public key on it.
5. **Run the drills** (below), then a tabletop and a live exercise with people.
   Record each exercise in the register.

## The community roster

The roster (`forkmesh-recovery-roster-v1`) is how members find each other
without the website. It lists pinned keys, mirrors, and contacts, and it
travels inside the signed kit.

```json
{
  "schema": "forkmesh-recovery-roster-v1",
  "community": "example community",
  "updated": "2026-09-14",
  "recoveryThreshold": 2,
  "keys": [
    {"keyId": "export-1", "publicKey": "<base64url>", "role": "export", "holder": "Mirror operator A", "status": "active"},
    {"keyId": "recovery-1", "publicKey": "<base64url>", "role": "recovery", "holder": "Custodian 1", "status": "active"},
    {"keyId": "recovery-2", "publicKey": "<base64url>", "role": "recovery", "holder": "Custodian 2", "status": "active"},
    {"keyId": "recovery-3", "publicKey": "<base64url>", "role": "recovery", "holder": "Custodian 3", "status": "active"}
  ],
  "mirrors": [
    {"name": "library mirror", "urls": ["http://mirror.example.lan:8080/project.git", "http://10.0.0.20:8080/project.git"],
     "pinnedHosts": {"mirror.example.lan": "10.0.0.20"}}
  ],
  "contacts": [{"role": "coordinator", "name": "Alex", "channel": "phone +1 555 0100"}],
  "rotations": []
}
```

Key roles are `export` (signs removable media), `kit` (signs bootstrap kits),
and `recovery` (signs key rotations). A key's status is `active` or `revoked`.

`roster check` exits 3 when the roster is invalid, has no active export key, or
has fewer distinct recovery key holders than `recoveryThreshold`. It warns when
no mirror address works without DNS (`dnsFree` is false), when one custodian
can rotate keys alone, or when an export key holder also holds a recovery key.
A URL works without DNS when its host is a literal address, an onion address,
or a name in the mirror's `pinnedHosts`.

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster check roster.json [--json]
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster keys roster.json --role export
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster profile roster.json --out lan.json
```

`roster profile` writes a `lan-only` [transport profile](../transports.md#postures)
that dials the roster's pinned local addresses, so a clone needs no DNS.

## The bootstrap kit

A kit is a directory that holds exactly the files a community needs to recover
with no network: the runbook source and its printable copy, the recovery
tools, the guides they cite, and the roster. Its manifest,
`forkmesh-recovery-kit.json`, is a `forkmesh-recovery-kit-signed-v1` envelope
over a `forkmesh-recovery-kit-v1` manifest that lists every file's SHA-256 and
size, the runbook version and digest, the build date, and a review date
(`reviewBy`, the build date plus the runbook's review interval).

```sh
python3 -B tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py kit verify /media/usb/forkmesh-kit \
  --trusted-key <kit key from paper>
```

Run it from the kit itself on the disconnected machine. `kit verify` never
opens a network connection. It checks that:

- the signature verifies, and the signer is the key you passed (always read it
  from paper, never from the kit);
- every listed file is present with its digest, with no extra files and no
  symbolic links;
- the runbook inside the kit validates against the kit's own tools and guides,
  matches the digest in the manifest, and matches the printable copy;
- the roster inside the kit verifies.

The tool never writes bytecode caches, so running it from the kit does not add
files. `-B` makes that explicit for any Python started by hand.

| State | Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verified` | `0` | Everything checked, and the kit is before its review date. |
| `stale` | `4` | Everything checked, but the kit is past `reviewBy`. Use it, then rebuild it from a current roster. |
| `failed` | `3` | Do not run anything from this kit. |

`--today YYYY-MM-DD` checks freshness as of another date.

## Key recovery

A lost or stolen export or kit key is replaced by a signed rotation. The
recovery key custodians sign it, and no single custodian and no lost key can
do it alone.

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py key rotate --roster roster.json \
  --recovery-key recovery-1.key --revoke <lost key> --successor <new key> \
  --holder "Mirror operator A" --reason "laptop stolen" --issued 2026-09-14 --out rotation.json
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py key cosign rotation.json --recovery-key recovery-2.key --roster roster.json
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py key apply roster.json rotation.json --out roster-rotated.json
```

The statement is `forkmesh-recovery-key-rotation-v1`, wrapped in
`forkmesh-recovery-key-rotation-signed-v1`. `key apply` refuses a rotation with
the first matching problem codes:

| Code | Refused because |
| --- | --- |
| `statement_digest` | `statementSha256` does not match the statement. |
| `community_mismatch` | The rotation names another community. |
| `already_applied` | The roster already lists this rotation. |
| `bad_signature` | A signature does not verify. |
| `signer_not_recovery_key` | A signer is not an active recovery key. The lost key cannot sign its own replacement. |
| `below_threshold` | Fewer distinct recovery signatures than `recoveryThreshold`. |
| `revoke_unknown` | A revoked key is not an active key in the roster. |
| `revoke_recovery_key` | Recovery keys change only by building a new kit with the custodians present. |
| `successor_known` | The successor key is already in the roster. |
| `successor_role` | The successor must be an export or kit key. |
| `statement_invalid` | The successor key or issued date is malformed. |

After the rotation, media signed by the revoked key fails import against the
new roster's export keys. Re-export from a verified copy with the successor key.
Never lower the threshold during an incident.

Mirror node identity keys move with the node's sealed identity export
([moving or replacing an identity key](../operations/node-backup-and-recovery.md#moving-or-replacing-an-identity-key)).
Personal identities recover with the portable recovery kit
([recovery drills](../portable-identities.md#recovery-drills)).

## Drills

Each scenario has a live drill that builds a small community in scratch space:
an origin, a mirror, a maintainer clone, a signed export, and a roster. The
drill then causes the disaster and recovers using the same tools the runbook
names, and measures the result.

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run all --report drills.json --telemetry drills.jsonl
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run origin-loss --fault no-local-clone
```

| Scenario | What the drill does | Fault injection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `origin-loss` | Deletes the origin after a push the mirror missed, restores from the mirror plus the maintainer's clone, and refuses a stale overwrite. | `no-local-clone`: the newest commit is lost, and the drill fails. |
| `main-service-loss` | Stops the hosted copy, detects it as unreachable, serves a read-only static mirror, and has a newcomer clone and verify it. | `no-surviving-mirror` |
| `dns-loss` | Clones by name over a `lan-only` route with the address pinned from the roster. On Linux, Git runs under strace, which flags any DNS query. | `no-pinned-address` |
| `key-loss` | Refuses a rotation signed by the lost key and one below threshold, applies a 2-of-3 rotation, refuses media forged with the lost key, and imports the re-export. | `threshold-unreachable` |
| `regional-isolation` | Two regions diverge and exchange signed media both ways; diverged `main` is kept aside and every commit reaches both regions. | `unpinned-region-key` |
| `corrupted-backup` | Rejects the corrupted newest backup, proves importing it changes nothing, and restores the previous verified backup, recording the commits lost. | `all-copies-corrupt` |
| `offline-bootstrap` | Builds a kit, verifies it and runs its roster check and offline import with the network blocked, and refuses a tampered kit. | `wrong-kit-key` |

A `forkmesh-disaster-drill-report-v1` report records `recoveryMs` (from the
disaster to the last verification), `withinObjective` against the scenario's
automated budget, `dataLoss` (refs and commits lost, and whether the
scenario's policy allows it), `missingPrerequisites`, `unsafeSteps` refused or
taken, each step with its runbook procedure and duration, every verification
check, and `verdict`. A drill passes only when every check passes, it finishes
within budget, the data loss is allowed, and no blocking prerequisite is missing.

`--telemetry FILE` appends one count-only `forkmesh-disaster-drill-telemetry-v1`
line per drill: scenario, fault, verdict, operating system, recovery time, and
counts. It never includes paths, keys, names, or addresses.

## Exercises and evidence

Record every exercise, by people or by automation, as
`conformance/disaster-recovery/v1/exercises/DRX-NNNN.json`
(`forkmesh-disaster-exercise-v1`). Each record has a kind (`tabletop` or
`live`), a status, the runbook version and digest, whether only the offline
runbook was used, and participants with their runbook roles and familiarity
(`unfamiliar`, `familiar`, or `automation`). Each scenario row records its
result, recovery time, whether a verified repository network was restored,
data loss, missing prerequisites, and unsafe steps.

Every missing prerequisite, and every unsafe step that was taken, must name a
finding. Every finding has a corrective owner: a `person`, a runbook `role`,
or an `issue`.

Retain automated drill reports as content-addressed evidence, then cite them:

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py attest drills.json   # prints evidence/<sha256>.json references
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py render
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py gate
```

When a row cites `drillReport`, validation recomputes it from the report: the
scenario, runbook digest, recovery minutes, result, commits lost, missing
prerequisites, and counts of unsafe steps must match. Editing the runbook
without bumping its version fails validation for any exercise that used that
version.

## Closure

`closure` lists what issue closure still needs, and exits 1 until all of it is
met. The [register](exercise-register.md) shows the same status.

| Check | Met when |
| --- | --- |
| `automated-drills-current` | Every scenario has a passing drill report on the current runbook digest. |
| `platform-evidence` | Those reports cover Linux, macOS, and Windows. |
| `tabletop-drills-recorded` | Every scenario was run as a tabletop exercise with at least two people. |
| `live-drills-recorded` | People recovered every scenario in a live exercise. |
| `unfamiliar-team-restored` | A team of at least two people unfamiliar with ForkMesh restored a verified repository network in a live exercise using only the offline runbook. |
| `findings-owned` | Every open finding has a named person as its corrective owner. |

Automation cannot meet the people checks. Do not record an exercise that did
not happen.

## Clean restoration

When normal infrastructure returns:

- compare its refs with the restored network before anything syncs, and push
  restored work to it as fast-forwards only;
- keep any diverged branches under review, never force-push over them;
- stop emergency static mirrors and delete temporary transport profiles;
- apply any key rotations to every roster copy, then rebuild and re-sign the
  kit, and write the new key and digest on paper;
- write the exercise or incident record, with a corrective owner for every
  finding.

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py validate` | Check the runbook against the repository: roles, prerequisites, decision trees (every node reachable, no cycles, a recovered outcome), commands (each tool, command, and option exists), guide headings, and kit completeness. |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py render [--check]` | Write or check `runbook.md` and `exercise-register.md`. |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py gate` | Validate the runbook and every exercise, and check rendered output. It does not depend on the date. |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py closure` | Report the closure checks. |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster check`, `roster keys`, `roster profile` | Roster commands (above). |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py key rotate`, `key cosign`, `key apply` | Key rotation (above). |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py kit build`, `kit verify` | Bootstrap kit (above). |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run` | Live drills (above). |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py attest` | Retain drill reports as evidence. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Done. |
| `1` | Validation, a drill, the gate, or closure failed. |
| `2` | Usage error or unreadable input. |
| `3` | A kit, roster, or rotation did not verify. |
| `4` | The kit verified but is past its review date. |

## Supported platforms

The drills need Git 2.40 or newer and Python 3.9 or newer. The quality gate
`disaster-recovery-conformance` runs the test suite, and the
`disaster-recovery.yml` workflow runs the suite, the gate, and every drill on
Linux, macOS, and Windows, and uploads the reports. DNS leak tracing in the
`dns-loss` drill needs strace, so it runs only on Linux. Elsewhere the report
records the tracer as a non-blocking missing prerequisite.

## Not covered yet

- No exercise with people has been recorded. The closure checks for tabletop,
  live, and unfamiliar-team exercises stay open until one is.
- The drills do not build the Go mirror node, so node archive restores
  (`--restore-drill`, `--restore`) and node identity imports are documented
  but not drilled here. `server/nodeops_test.go` covers them separately.
- The `search` and `organization-service` roles are hosted-only, so
  main-service loss cannot restore search or organizations.
- Rosters and kits are signed by one kit key. There is no threshold signature
  on the kit itself.
- Desktop and mobile apps do not show the runbook, roster, or kit state.
