pages.title: Fediverse daily digests
pages.description: ForkMesh does not publish a separate automated ActivityPub post for every repository event. Public issue, pull-request, discussion, commit, and release hooks are reduced to a…
pages.markdown:
# Fediverse daily digests

ForkMesh does not publish a separate automated ActivityPub post for every
repository event. Public issue, pull-request, discussion, commit, and release
hooks are reduced to a small metadata record and placed in an encrypted,
bounded queue.

Each queued record contains only:

- an event category;
- a short public title;
- a stable public ForkMesh link with its query string removed;
- a UTC timestamp; and
- a repository or organization-alias scope.

Bodies, source excerpts, form values, private paths, request metadata, and
credentials are not retained in the digest queue. Private repositories are
rejected before enqueueing. If a public repository becomes private or its owner
turns automatic federation off, its queued automatic posts are deleted.

## Cadence and delivery

A new queue waits 24 hours before its first eligible post so events can be
combined. After publication, the same repository actor cannot publish another
automatic digest for at least 24 hours. Empty queues do not create posts.
Duplicate events receive deterministic IDs, and each digest contains at most 12
updates from a queue capped at 80 records.

The scheduled Worker processes at most 12 due scopes per run. It creates a
deterministic ActivityPub Note and retryable delivery rows in the same D1 batch
that removes the published event IDs. Delivery then uses the existing
ActivityPub outbox, including remote `Retry-After` handling, exponential
backoff, domain blocking, and capped attempts.

Every generated post starts with “ForkMesh automated daily update” and ends
with an automated-post label. Links point to the relevant public repository
resource.

## Repository controls and preview

Repository owners manage the existing “Post updates” switch in the repository
About settings. The switch now means “include meaningful public updates in at
most one automated daily digest.” The same form shows the exact currently
queued digest text. The owner-only API is:

```text
GET /api/repo/{owner}/{repo}/fediverse-digest
```

It requires the owner’s authenticated session (or the existing owner-key
proof), returns `Cache-Control: no-store`, and returns `404` for private
repositories.

Explicit owner-authenticated announcements sent to `ap-publish` with
`"manual": true` retain the immediate publication behavior. All calls without
that explicit flag enter the daily queue.

## Organization controls

Organization owners and administrators can enable or disable organization-alias
digests and preview every eligible linked public repository at:

```text
GET  /api/orgs/{org}/fediverse
POST /api/orgs/{org}/fediverse
```

The POST body is `{ "enabled": true|false }`. This is a suppress-only control:
the backing repository owner’s `federate` and `broadcastEvents` settings remain
authoritative. An organization administrator cannot enable a repository the
owner disabled, and organization membership does not grant visibility into a
private repository.

pages.title: Verified fediverse feedback review
pages.description: ForkMesh World lists sanitized activity only after the inbound ActivityPub Note has passed HTTP-signature verification and has addressed a published public repository actor. The…
pages.markdown:
# Verified fediverse feedback review

ForkMesh World lists sanitized activity only after the inbound ActivityPub
Note has passed HTTP-signature verification and has addressed a published
public repository actor. The Create activity or embedded Note must also
explicitly address the ActivityStreams Public collection; a valid signature
does not turn a direct or private Note into public content. Private and missing
repositories are rejected before a review record is written. Instance blocks
and the repository's `federate` and `acceptComments` controls remain
authoritative.

Repository mentions do not automatically create issues. The lifecycle is:

1. `review`: a verified public post is available for authorized manual review.
2. `pending`: the repository owner previewed and edited the draft, explicitly
   confirmed it, and the encrypted owner inbox accepted it.
3. `created`: the owner node materialized and committed the open event, then
   returned the actual issue number in its signed inbox acknowledgement.

A proposed number is never displayed as a created issue number. Delayed or
offline owner nodes leave the item pending until the owner node confirms the
committed issue number. Queue failures remain retryable and the public feed
exposes only a generalized failure message.

The owner can dismiss or restore reviewable activity with an audited reason.
Redeliveries are deduplicated by a blind index of the public remote Note id.
The public feed exposes a random record id, sanitized public author/post fields,
repository display name, and generalized progress. It does not expose raw IP
addresses, inbox URLs, signing keys, internal evidence, session data, encrypted
payloads, or private repository existence.

Follow-up consent is off by default. The owner must separately consent during
manual creation. Even with consent, no outbound reply is sent while the item is
merely pending. After owner-node confirmation, ForkMesh queues one idempotent
public reply to the original public Note with the confirmed issue backlink. A
delivery failure does not undo the issue and is shown only as delayed follow-up.

API surface:

- `GET /api/world/fediverse-mentions` — privacy-safe public activity feed.
- `POST /api/world/fediverse-mentions/{id}/preview` — owner-authorized draft.
- `POST /api/world/fediverse-mentions/{id}/create` — explicit manual queueing.
- `POST /api/world/fediverse-mentions/{id}/moderate` — audited dismiss/restore.
- `POST /api/world/fediverse-mentions/{id}/materialized` — owner-node signed
  confirmation and idempotent retry path.

The Qt inbox acknowledgement normally carries bounded
`materialized={review-id}:{real-issue-number}` entries, so confirmation and
inbox drain share the same owner signature.

pages.title: Two-way forge sync
pages.description: A ForkMesh repository can stay connected to a repository on GitHub or on a self-hosted Gitea or Forgejo server, so a community can adopt ForkMesh without leaving the forge it…
pages.markdown:
# Two-way forge sync

A ForkMesh repository can stay connected to a repository on GitHub or on a
self-hosted Gitea or Forgejo server, so a community can adopt ForkMesh without
leaving the forge it already works on. Issues, their comments, labels,
assignees, open/closed state, edits, and comment deletions flow both ways.

| Provider | Tier | Adapter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub (github.com, GitHub Enterprise Server) | Centralized | `github` |
| Gitea, Forgejo, Codeberg | Self-hosted | `gitea` |

Branches and tags keep using the ref sync from
[Connecting to GitHub](github-sync.md) (`github_forkmesh_bridge.py git-sync`),
which works with any Git remote: it creates missing refs and fast-forwards,
never forces, and reports diverged branches. Pull requests, reviews, and
discussions are still imported one way by that bridge.

## Connect

```bash
# GitHub
python3 tools/forge_sync.py connect --provider github --repository octo/app

# Gitea / Forgejo
python3 tools/forge_sync.py connect --provider gitea --repository octo/app \
  --base-url https://git.example.org --slo-minutes 15
```

`connect` writes `.forkmesh/forge-sync.json`, the sync ledger. Only issues
opened on ForkMesh *after* connecting are created on the provider; pass
`--export-existing` to publish older ones too. Provider API origins must use
HTTPS.

Then run a pass on a schedule (for example every 5–15 minutes) from a checkout,
and commit and push the changed `.forkmesh` files:

```bash
FORKMESH_FORGE_TOKEN=… FORKMESH_BRIDGE_SIGNING_KEY="$(cat sync-key.pem)" \
  python3 tools/forge_sync.py sync --report sync-report.json
git add .forkmesh && git commit -m "forge-sync" && git push
```

The token needs read/write access to issues. The signing key is an Ed25519 key
in the same format as the GitHub bridge key; it signs every record the sync
writes into ForkMesh.

Exit codes: `0` converged, `1` unresolved conflicts, `2` configuration error,
`75` a retryable provider failure stopped the run (progress is kept).

## How changes are merged

The ledger remembers, per issue, a digest of each field (title, body, state,
labels, assignees) and of each comment as it was when both sides last agreed.
On every pass:

- If only one side changed a value, it is copied to the other side.
- If both sides changed it to the same value, nothing is written.
- If both sides changed it differently, it becomes a **conflict**. Neither
  side is written, and the conflict is reported on every pass until someone
  resolves it.

Nothing is overwritten silently. Repeated passes over unchanged state write
nothing on either side.

### Source-of-truth rules

A repository can publish a rule per field in the ledger, for example:

```json
"sourceOfTruth": { "state": "provider", "labels": "forkmesh" }
```

Each field is `manual` (the default: conflicts wait for a person),
`forkmesh`, or `provider`. When a rule settles a conflict, the discarded value
is still recorded in the ledger `history`, so it can be restored.

### Resolving conflicts

```bash
python3 tools/forge_sync.py status
python3 tools/forge_sync.py resolve --issue 12 --field body --take forkmesh
```

`--field` is `title`, `body`, `state`, `labels`, `assignees`,
`comment:<event id>`, or `issue`. The next pass copies the chosen side over the
other; the discarded value goes into `history`.

An `issue` conflict means the linked provider issue disappeared or was
replaced (for example, deleted and recreated with the same number). The
replacement is imported under a new ForkMesh number and the original record is
left untouched. `--take forkmesh` recreates the issue on the provider;
`--take provider` stops syncing that issue.

## Loop prevention

- A value the sync writes becomes the new agreed value, so its echo on the next
  pass compares equal and is not copied back.
- Issues and comments created on the provider carry a hidden
  `forkmesh-forge-sync:v1` marker and a visible "Synced from ForkMesh" credit
  line. Records written into ForkMesh use `forge-<provider>-` event ids.
- If the ledger is lost or rolled back, or a pass crashes between creating a
  provider issue and saving the ledger, the next pass re-links records by those
  markers instead of creating duplicates.
- Records imported by the one-way GitHub bridge (`github-` ids) are never
  exported back.

## Deletions

Deleting a comment on the provider adds a signed `delete` event in ForkMesh.
Deleting a comment in ForkMesh deletes it on the provider. A deletion on one
side that races an edit on the other is a conflict, so no edit is lost. Issues
themselves are never deleted by the sync.

## Identities

Everything imported from a provider is signed by the sync key and credited as
`<provider>:<login>` (for example `github:alice`). The colon can never appear in
a ForkMesh account name, so provider text cannot pass as a native user's.

Owners can link provider logins to ForkMesh accounts in the ledger:

```json
"identities": { "github:alice": "alice", "gitea:bob": "bob" }
```

Links only translate assignees in both directions; authorship stays credited
to the provider login. A link is **ambiguous**, and ignored with a warning,
when one login maps to several accounts (logins are compared
case-insensitively) or one account is linked from several logins of the same
provider. ForkMesh assignees without a link are kept in ForkMesh and not sent
to the provider.

## Rate limits, outages, and retries

Rate limits (`429`, or `403` with an exhausted quota) are retried after
`Retry-After`; server errors and network failures back off exponentially.
When retries run out the pass stops, keeps everything it already synchronized,
and reports `quota_exceeded` or `provider_unavailable`. An issue that failed
is recreated on the next pass. A rejected token (`401`) fails immediately.

## Pause and resume

```bash
python3 tools/forge_sync.py pause --reason "relabeling on GitHub"
python3 tools/forge_sync.py resume
```

A paused connection sends no requests to the provider and reports `paused`.

## Status, lag, and telemetry

`status` and the `--report` JSON (`forkmesh-forge-sync-report-v1`) use the
shared [synchronization status](sync-status.md) model and include:

| Measure | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `lagMs` / `sloMs` / `sloMet` | Time since the oldest unconverged change, or since the last complete pass, against the published SLO (default 15 minutes) |
| `convergenceRate` | Linked issues with no conflict and no failure |
| `conflictRate` | Open conflicts per linked issue |
| `retries` / `retrySuccesses` | Provider requests retried, and those that then succeeded |
| `conflicts` | Every unresolved conflict, with both values |
| `failing` | Issues whose last attempt failed |

Reports never contain tokens.

## Limits

- Pull requests, reviews, releases, and discussions are not yet synchronized
  back to providers.
- Milestones, reactions, and attachments are not synchronized.
- Issues are never deleted on either side.

The contracts, including edits, deletions, force updates, rate limits,
outages, and identity ambiguity for both adapters, are covered by
[`app/tests/test_forge_sync.py`](../../app/tests/test_forge_sync.py).

pages.markdown:
# Public-interest funding

Program version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Status: **proposed** (issue #515). The pilot
round, [PIF-0001](funding-register.md#pif-0001), is a **draft**. No funder has
committed a pool and no reviewer is seated, so it has no applications,
selections, or payments yet.

The program pays for work that the whole ecosystem uses: public repositories,
volunteer mirrors, accessibility, documentation, education, and independent
tooling. Being funded never changes who can reach a repository, what an
identity may do, who votes, or what the network requires.

The machine-readable program is
[`conformance/funding/v1/program.json`](../../../conformance/funding/v1/program.json).
Each funding round is a JSON record in
[`conformance/funding/v1/rounds/`](../../../conformance/funding/v1/rounds/).
Reviewers and their conflict disclosures come from the
[governance ledger](../governance/README.md). The public
[funding register](funding-register.md) and the searchable
`/docs/funding/register.json` are generated from those files. A hand edit to
either output fails CI.

## What the program offers

| Offer | Status | How it works |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Donation | planned | A one-off gift to the pool. A donor may restrict it to an area, never to a named recipient. |
| Recurring sponsorship | planned | Monthly or yearly support for the pool or one area. A sponsor can stop at any time. |
| Targeted grant | planned | A milestone-based award chosen in a published round. |
| Matching | planned | The pool matches public contributions a recipient raised on their own rail, up to 2:1. |

The pilot round will make targeted grants and matching available. Donations
and sponsorship open once the first round shows the pool can be administered
and reported in public.

These offers are separate from the support that already exists. Solana tips,
issue bounties, and profile and repository donations go straight to the person
who published the address. Memberships fund forkmesh.com. None of them passes
through this pool, and all of them stay optional adapters under
[incentive independence](../incentive-independence.md).

## Eligibility

Areas and their rules:

- **Public repositories:** anyone can read and clone the repository without an
  account, and it uses an OSI-approved or Creative Commons license. It may be
  hosted anywhere.
- **Volunteer mirrors:** a public mirror, relay, or gateway that other people
  have used for at least 60 days, with a health endpoint or status page.
- **Accessibility:** work on a ForkMesh-compatible client, website, or document
  measured against WCAG 2.2 AA or platform guidelines, tested with at least one
  person who uses assistive technology.
- **Documentation:** public documentation, translations, or tutorials under an
  open license.
- **Education:** free courses, workshops, or learning materials about
  decentralized collaboration, under an open license.
- **Ecosystem tooling:** an independent client, relay, index, verifier, or
  library with a public https source under an OSI-approved license. A
  [certification badge](../protocol/certification.md) is welcome but not
  required.

Every applicant must also meet these rules:

- Individuals, informal groups, and organizations may apply from any
  jurisdiction the funder can lawfully pay.
- Applying, being reviewed, and being paid need no ForkMesh account, plan,
  client, wallet, or token.
- The operator of forkmesh.com and the people it pays are not eligible for
  awards.
- A round's funders and reviewers are not eligible in that round.
- Work that needs a paid plan on a ForkMesh-operated service to use is not
  eligible.

## Applying

Each round lists its application channels. Every round offers at least one
channel that needs no ForkMesh account. The pilot accepts an issue labelled
`funding-application` on any forge mirror of `forkmesh/forkmesh`, or a private
email to the address in the round announcement. The application window is at
least 21 days.

An application names the applicant, a public https source, the applicant's
employer or funder (or `none`), the area, the offer, the amount requested, and
milestones.

## Selection

Reviewers score each criterion from 0 to 5:

| Criterion | Weight |
| --- | --- |
| Public benefit | 30 |
| Feasibility | 20 |
| Accessibility and inclusion | 20 |
| Sustainability | 15 |
| Decentralization: a new operator, region, implementation, or maintainer | 15 |

The weighted score is out of 100. An award needs:

- at least 60 points;
- scores from at least 3 reviewers, at least 1 of whom is not a ForkMesh
  maintainer;
- an eligible application; and
- room in the pool after administrative cost.

Awards go to the highest-scoring applications. No recipient may receive more
than 25% of a round's awards. A matching award may not exceed the matched
contributions times the ratio, and the contributions need a public receipt.

## Conflicts

- Reviewers are governance participants with a current disclosure in
  [`participants.json`](../../../conformance/governance/v1/participants.json).
- A reviewer who is the applicant, or who shares an employer or funder with the
  applicant, must record a recusal and must not score that application. The
  ledger detects these matches and fails until the recusal is recorded.
- Any other conflict a reviewer declares is recorded and recused the same way.
- A funder never reviews, never chooses a recipient, and may restrict a gift
  only to an area.
- Recusals are published with the round, beside the selections they affected.

## Payment rails

The recipient chooses the rail for each award. Every rail pays into an account
the recipient controls and needs no ForkMesh account or plan.

| Rail | Kind | Recurring |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bank transfer (SEPA, ACH, or international wire) | conventional | yes |
| Open Collective, through the recipient's own fiscal host | conventional | yes |
| Liberapay | conventional | yes |
| Solana transfer to an address the recipient controls | on-chain | no |

Every round offers at least one conventional rail. Solana is never the only
rail. A rail that needs a ForkMesh account, a plan, or a hosted balance fails
validation.

## Independence

An award, donation, or sponsorship pays for work. It never grants repository
access, identity rights, protocol votes, governance seats, ranking or
discovery, moderation outcomes, required network behavior, or use of a hosted
product. An award's `grants` list must be empty.

The only obligations an award may carry are a milestone report, an outcome
report, an open license, an accessibility statement, a public receipt, and a
conflict disclosure.

The ledger checks that these business-model commitments still hold:
`protocolUseRequiresPayment`, `publicReadAndCloneRequirePaidPlan`,
`governanceRequiresPaidPlan`, `tokenOrBlockchainRequired`, and
`incentivesAffectIdentityPermissionsRankingModerationOrGovernance` are all
`false`. It also checks that the governance charter still protects
`token-free-governance`. If any of these changes, the gate fails.

## Disclosure and reporting

Before applications open, a round publishes:

- its committed pool, and each funder's name, funding kind, amount, conflicts,
  and any area restriction. Funders must cover the whole pool;
- its administrative cost, capped at 10% of the pool. This covers payment fees,
  accounting, and reviewer stipends;
- its reviewers and their disclosures; and
- its application window.

As the round runs, it publishes every application with its eligibility result
and weighted score, every recusal, every award and its milestones, and every
disbursement with a public receipt. A payment is made only after its milestone
report is accepted.

When the round ends, it publishes an outcome report with:

- funds raised, awarded, and disbursed;
- administrative cost;
- applications and recipients;
- milestones accepted out of the total;
- volunteer-mirror operators funded, and how many still operate;
- accessibility impact; and
- lessons, including what did not work.

The ledger recomputes each figure, so a report that disagrees with the ledger
fails validation. A cancelled round also publishes an outcome report and its
lessons.

## Community review

After selections are published, community review stays open for at least 14
days. Anyone may comment through an issue on any forge mirror or by email, and a
maintainer records each finding with attribution. Findings cover three risks:

- **Concentration:** one recipient, area, region, or funder holding too much of
  a round. The ledger warns when more than 50% of awards go to one area or more
  than 50% of the pool comes from one funder.
- **Accessibility:** forms, channels, or criteria that exclude people.
- **Conflict:** undisclosed ties between reviewers, funders, and applicants.

Each finding is `corrected` with the correction recorded, `accepted-risk` with a
rationale, or `open`. A finding raised only by a ForkMesh maintainer does not
count as independent review.

## Round lifecycle

| Stage | What the ledger requires |
| --- | --- |
| `draft` | Areas, offers, rails, and application channels. No applications. |
| `open` | Announcement and application window, pool, funders, administrative cost, and reviewers. |
| `reviewing` | Scores on every criterion. Every detected conflict is recused. |
| `selected` | Published selections. Each eligible application meets the reviewer quorum. Awards meet the minimum score and concentration cap. |
| `disbursing` | Payments against accepted milestones, on round rails, with receipts. |
| `reported` | No pending milestones, a community review window, and an outcome report that matches the ledger. |
| `cancelled` | The stage it was cancelled from, and an outcome report with lessons. |

## Running the ledger

```bash
python3 tools/public_interest_funding.py validate   # program and rounds
python3 tools/public_interest_funding.py render     # regenerate the register
python3 tools/public_interest_funding.py gate       # validate + render --check (CI)
python3 tools/public_interest_funding.py status     # measures, overdue reports, warnings, blockers
python3 tools/public_interest_funding.py closure    # non-zero until #515 can close
```

`gate` never reads today's date, so it cannot fail on the calendar.
`status` and `closure` accept `--as-of YYYY-MM-DD`.

Program changes publish a new version in `program.json`. A change applies only
to rounds announced at least 14 days later, and a round keeps the version it
was announced under.

## Failure, rollback, and recovery

- **A round breaks the program** (unpublished funding, a missing recusal, a
  score below the minimum, a concentrated award, an award that grants a right):
  `validate` fails and the `public-interest-funding` quality gate blocks the
  change. Fix the record. Do not waive the gate.
- **A payment bounces or is sent in error:** mark the disbursement `returned`
  with a note, then record a new `sent` disbursement. Returned payments do not
  count as disbursed.
- **A milestone is missed:** mark it `missed` with its report, or `waived` with
  a note. No payment follows a milestone that has not been accepted.
- **A round cannot proceed** (no pool, no reviewers, a conflict that can't be
  resolved): set `stage` to `cancelled`, record `cancelledFrom`, and publish the
  outcome report and its lessons. Unspent funds stay in the pool or go back to
  funders, as the report states.
- **A finding shows an award was wrongly selected:** record the finding and its
  correction. Stop the remaining disbursements by leaving their milestones
  unaccepted. Records are corrected, never deleted.
- **The register is stale or hand-edited:** run `render` and commit the result.

## Measures

`status` reports these per round, and each monthly
[outcome review](../outcome-review.md) records them:

- funds raised, awarded, and disbursed;
- administrative cost as a share of the pool;
- applications and distinct recipients;
- milestone completion;
- volunteer-mirror operators funded and still operating at the outcome report;
- accessibility awards and reported accessibility impact;
- largest recipient, area, and funder share of a round; and
- overdue milestone and outcome reports. The target is zero.

Measures come only from the ledger. Product analytics record no applicant,
recipient, amount, or payment identifier.

## Closure criteria for issue #515

`closure` exits non-zero until every item holds. At program publication, the
first three are open:

- **pilot-round-reported:** a pilot round is `reported` with applications,
  conflict handling, selections, disbursements, milestones, and an outcome
  report.
- **recipients-paid-on-portable-rails:** every recipient in that round was paid
  on a rail they chose.
- **community-review-corrected:** independent community findings cover
  concentration, accessibility, and conflict. No finding is open, and every
  concentration warning is addressed.
- **reports-on-time:** no milestone or outcome report is overdue.

## Linked automated evidence

- Eligibility, conflicts, selection quorum and score, concentration, rails,
  independence, disbursements, returned payments, cancellation, overdue
  reports, measures, and register checks:
  `app/tests/test_public_interest_funding.py`
- Quality gate: `public-interest-funding` in
  [`quality-gates.json`](../engineering/quality-gates.json), in the `core` and
  `release` profiles. The tests also run in the `incentive-independence` gate.
- CI: `.github/workflows/collaboration-conformance.yml` runs `gate` and the
  tests on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
- Program `closureEvidence` links each kind of evidence (supported platforms,
  failure paths, rollback and recovery, documentation, and telemetry) to a test
  or file. Validation fails if a link goes missing.

Automated checks do not replace a committed pool, seated reviewers, real
applications and payments, or independent community review, all of which
closure requires.

# Public-interest funding register

Program `1.0.0-rc.1` · Status: **proposed**. How to apply, review, and report is in the [program guide](README.md). The same data is published as searchable JSON at `/docs/funding/register.json`.

## Offers

| Offer | Status | Eligibility | Selection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Donation | planned | Anyone may donate. Gifts that carry conditions beyond an area restriction are declined. | Donations join the pool of the next announced round in their area. |
| Recurring sponsorship | planned | Anyone may sponsor. Sponsorship buys no placement, ranking, seat, vote, or say in selection. | Sponsorship funds rounds in the sponsored area. Sponsors are listed as funders of the rounds they fund. |
| Targeted grant | planned | The area eligibility and general eligibility rules. | Disclosed reviewers score the published selection criteria. Awards go to eligible applications above the minimum score, in score order, within the pool and the concentration limits. |
| Matching | planned | The area eligibility and general eligibility rules. Matched contributions need public receipts. | Scored like a targeted grant. The award may not exceed the matched contributions times the ratio. |

## Areas and eligibility

- **Public repositories** (`public-repositories`): The repository is public, and anyone can read and clone it without an account. The code or content is under an OSI-approved or Creative Commons license. Where it is hosted does not matter: forkmesh.com, a self-hosted mirror, or another forge.
- **Volunteer mirrors** (`volunteer-mirrors`): The applicant operates a public mirror, relay, or gateway that people other than the operator have used for at least 60 days. The service publishes a health endpoint or status page.
- **Accessibility** (`accessibility`): The work improves a ForkMesh-compatible client, website, or document against WCAG 2.2 AA or the platform's accessibility guidelines. The plan includes testing with at least one person who uses assistive technology.
- **Documentation** (`documentation`): Public documentation, translations, or tutorials under an open license.
- **Education** (`education`): Courses, workshops, or learning materials about decentralized collaboration, under an open license and free to attend or read.
- **Ecosystem tooling** (`ecosystem-tooling`): An independent client, relay, index, verifier, or library with a public https source under an OSI-approved license. A certification badge is welcome but not required.

Every application must also meet these rules:

- Individuals, informal groups, and organizations in any jurisdiction the funder can lawfully pay may apply.
- Applying, being reviewed, and being paid need no ForkMesh account, plan, client, wallet, or token.
- The operator of forkmesh.com and people it pays are not eligible for awards.
- A round's funders and reviewers are not eligible in that round.
- Work whose use requires a paid plan on any ForkMesh-operated service is not eligible.

## Selection criteria

| Criterion | Weight | What reviewers score |
| --- | --- | --- |
| public-benefit | 30 | How many people outside the applicant benefit, and how directly. |
| feasibility | 20 | Whether the milestones, budget, and schedule are realistic for the applicant. |
| accessibility-inclusion | 20 | Whether the work serves people with disabilities, low bandwidth, or languages the ecosystem under-serves. |
| sustainability | 15 | Whether the result keeps working, or is handed on, after the award ends. |
| decentralization | 15 | Whether the work adds a new operator, region, implementation, or maintainer, and so reduces concentration. |

Reviewers score each criterion from 0 to 5. An award needs a weighted score of at least 60 out of 100, from at least 3 reviewers, of whom at least 1 is not a ForkMesh maintainer.

- Conflicts: A reviewer who is the applicant, or who shares an employer or funder with the applicant, must record a recusal and must not score that application. Any other conflict a reviewer declares is recorded and recused the same way. A funder never reviews, never chooses a recipient, and may restrict a gift only to an area.
- Concentration: at most 25% of a round's awards to one recipient. More than 50% to one area, or more than 50% of the pool from one funder, must be addressed in community review.
- Administrative cost: at most 10% of the pool. Administrative cost covers payment fees, accounting, and reviewer stipends. It is published per round before applications open.

## Payment rails

| Rail | Kind | Recurring | ForkMesh account or plan needed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bank transfer (SEPA, ACH, or international wire) | conventional | yes | no |
| Open Collective, through the recipient's own fiscal host | conventional | yes | no |
| Liberapay | conventional | yes | no |
| Solana transfer to an address the recipient controls | on-chain | no | no |

## Independence

An award, donation, or sponsorship pays for work. It never changes who can reach a repository, what an identity may do, who votes, or what the network requires.

Awards never grant: `repository-access`, `identity-rights`, `protocol-votes`, `governance-seats`, `ranking-or-discovery`, `moderation-outcomes`, `required-network-behavior`, `hosted-product-use`.

The only obligations an award may carry: `milestone-report`, `outcome-report`, `open-license`, `accessibility-statement`, `public-receipt`, `conflict-disclosure`.

## Rounds

| Round | Title | Pilot | Stage | Pool | Awarded | Disbursed | Recipients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [PIF-0001](#pif-0001) | Pilot round: volunteer mirrors, accessibility, and documentation | yes | draft | not published | USD 0 | USD 0 | 0 |

### PIF-0001

**Pilot round: volunteer mirrors, accessibility, and documentation**

Milestone grants and matching for people who run public mirrors, make ForkMesh-compatible clients and documents accessible, and write open documentation. Recipients choose their own payment rail.

- Areas: volunteer-mirrors, accessibility, documentation. Offers: targeted-grant, matching.
- Payment rails: bank-transfer, open-collective, liberapay, solana.
- Apply through: An issue labelled funding-application on any forge mirror of forkmesh/forkmesh. Email to the address in the round announcement, for applicants who cannot apply in public.
- Timeline: announced —; applicationsOpen —; applicationsClose —; selectionsPublished —; finalReportDue —; reported —
- Pool: not published. Administrative cost: not published.

The round opens when:

- A funder commits the pool and publishes the amount, source, conflicts, and any area restriction.
- Administrative cost is published and stays within 10% of the pool.
- At least three reviewers with current governance disclosures are seated, and at least one is not a ForkMesh maintainer.
- The application window is announced with at least 21 days to apply.

#### Funders

None committed.

#### Reviewers

None seated.

#### Applications and selections

No applications.

#### Conflict handling

No conflicts recorded.

#### Milestones and disbursements

No awards.

#### Community review

Window: — to —.

#### Outcome report

Not published.

> No funder has committed a pool and no reviewer is seated, so the round has not opened. It has no applications, selections, or disbursements to report.

pages.title: Git errors when cloning, pulling, or pushing
pages.description: ForkMesh serves Git over HTTPS at https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo>. A clone or pull is usually redirected to one of the mirrors that hold the repository, so a line like…
pages.markdown:
# Git errors when cloning, pulling, or pushing

ForkMesh serves Git over HTTPS at `https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo>`.
A clone or pull is usually redirected to one of the mirrors that hold the
repository, so a line like `warning: redirecting to
https://n2.next.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo>.git/` is normal.

When something goes wrong, the error comes from one of two places:

- **ForkMesh answered with an error.** Git prints our explanation on lines
  that start with `remote:`, followed by a link to this page.
- **The connection failed before ForkMesh could answer.** Git prints only its
  own message, usually with a `curl` error. ForkMesh cannot add text to these,
  because no answer reached your computer.

## Messages from ForkMesh

| `remote:` message | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ForkMesh could not reach a mirror of this repository just now. | No mirror that holds the repository answered in time. | Try again in a minute. The repository's **Mirrors** page (`/<owner>/<repo>/mirrors`) shows which mirrors are up. |
| This ForkMesh mirror could not read the repository just now. | The mirror you were sent to failed while reading the repository. | Try again; the next attempt may use another mirror. |
| ForkMesh has no public repository at this address. | The owner or repository name is wrong, or the repository is private. | Check the spelling in `git remote -v`. Private repositories need their owner's credential. |
| This ForkMesh mirror has no public repository at this address. | Same as above, answered by the mirror itself. | Same as above. |
| Pushing over HTTPS needs your ForkMesh account name and the repository's push credential. | The push had no credential, or a wrong one. | Use your account name as the username and the push credential as the password. See [Hosted repositories](hosted-repositories.md). |
| This repository is private. Sign in with your ForkMesh account name and the repository's credential. | The repository is private and the credential was missing or wrong. | Use the credential its owner gave you. |
| ForkMesh could not reach the node that accepts pushes for this repository. | The node that writes this repository did not answer. | Try again in a minute. Your commits are still local and safe. |
| Use Git protocol version 0, 1, or 2. | Your Git sent a protocol version ForkMesh does not speak. | Remove `protocol.version` from your Git configuration, or set it to `2`. |

## Errors from your own Git client

These lines come from Git and curl on your computer. The request did not
complete, so ForkMesh never saw a failure it could explain.

| Git prints | What happened | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Error in the HTTP2 framing layer`, `HTTP/2 stream … was not closed cleanly`, `curl 16`, `curl 92` | The HTTP/2 connection broke partway through. VPNs, proxies, antivirus that inspects HTTPS, and unstable mobile or Wi-Fi links cause most of these. | Run the command again. If it keeps failing, use HTTP/1.1 for this repository: `git config http.version HTTP/1.1`. Add `--global` to use it everywhere. |
| `RPC failed; curl 18 transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining`, `curl 56`, `early EOF`, `unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet` | The connection dropped while Git was downloading. | Run the command again. If it fails at the same point every time, include a trace in your report (below). |
| `Could not resolve host`, `Failed to connect`, `Connection timed out`, `Connection refused` | Your computer could not reach ForkMesh at all. | Check your network, DNS, and any VPN or proxy. |
| `SSL certificate problem` | Something between you and ForkMesh is presenting another certificate, or your clock is wrong. | Check the system clock, and any proxy or antivirus that intercepts HTTPS. |

The ForkMesh desktop app recognizes these errors too. When a fetch, pull,
clone, sync, or push fails this way, it says that the connection broke and
that trying again usually works.

## Reporting a problem

If an error keeps happening, open an issue on
[forkmesh/forkmesh](https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh/issues) and
include:

- the output of the failing command run with tracing on:

  ```bash
  GIT_TRACE_CURL=1 GIT_TRACE_CURL_NO_DATA=1 git pull origin main 2>&1 | tail -60
  ```

- the output of `git --version` and `curl --version`;
- the date and time it failed, with your time zone.

Git removes passwords and cookies from the trace by default, but read it
before you post it. With the time and the trace, the operators can find your
request in the mirrors' logs.

pages.title: Connecting a repository to GitHub
pages.description: A ForkMesh repository can be connected to a GitHub repository so both stay in sync
pages.markdown:
# Connecting a repository to GitHub

A ForkMesh repository can be connected to a GitHub repository so both stay in
sync:

- **Code**: branches and tags move both ways. A ref that exists on only one
  side is created on the other, and the side that is behind is
  fast-forwarded. Nothing is ever force-pushed or deleted. A branch that has
  moved on both sides is reported as *diverged* and left alone until someone
  merges one side into the other.
- **Collaboration records**: GitHub issues, discussions, and pull requests
  are converted into the repository-native `.forkmesh` records every ForkMesh
  client reads. They show up in the desktop app, on the website, and on
  mirrors exactly like records created on ForkMesh.

Everything runs as a GitHub Actions workflow in the GitHub repository. ForkMesh
Actions run without network egress, so GitHub cannot be reached from the
ForkMesh side. ForkMesh-side changes are picked up by the workflow's
15-minute schedule, and GitHub-side events trigger it immediately.

## Connect

From a checkout of the repository (either remote):

```bash
python3 tools/github_forkmesh_bridge.py connect \
  --github octo/app \
  --forkmesh octo/app \
  --key-out ~/.config/forkmesh/github-bridge-octo-app.pem
```

`connect` writes three files and adds `github` / `forkmesh` git remotes if
they are missing:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.forkmesh/github-sync.json` | The connection (`github`, `forkmesh`, `forkmeshRemote`) and the GitHub → ForkMesh number mapping the workflow maintains |
| `.forkmesh/github-bridge.py` | A copy of the bridge. It is self-contained, so the connected repository does not depend on this one |
| `.github/workflows/forkmesh-github-sync.yml` | The workflow |

It also generates the bridge signing key (mode `0600`, never inside the
repository) and prints the remaining steps:

1. `gh secret set FORKMESH_BRIDGE_SIGNING_KEY < <key file>`: the Ed25519 key
   that signs imported records.
2. `gh secret set FORKMESH_SYNC_SSH_KEY < <ssh private key>`: an SSH key
   whose public half is registered on ForkMesh with write access to the
   repository.
3. `gh variable set FORKMESH_SYNC_REMOTE --body ssh://git@ssh.forkmesh.com/octo/app.git`.
   The workflow does nothing until this variable is set.
4. Optionally, set `FORKMESH_SYNC_KNOWN_HOSTS` to the gateway's
   `known_hosts` line. Without it, the first connection trusts the host key
   it is offered (`StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`).
5. Commit the three files and push them to both remotes.

Any branch protection on GitHub's default branch and on `forkmesh/pulls` must
let the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` push, because imported records are
committed there.

## How records are converted

| GitHub | ForkMesh record |
| --- | --- |
| Issue, labels, milestone, assignees, comments, open/closed | `.forkmesh/issues/{open,closed}/<n>/issue-<n>.json` (`forkmesh-issue-v1`), plus new entries in `labels.json` / `milestones.json` |
| Discussion, comments and replies (flattened in time order), closed | `.forkmesh/discussions/<n>/discussion.md` + `NNNN-comment.md` |
| Pull request (open / closed / merged), conversation comments, reviews, inline review comments | `.forkmesh/pulls/<n>/` on the `forkmesh/pulls` ledger branch: `pull.md`, `changes.patch` and `commits.mbox` for open pulls, and `NNNN-comment.md` / `NNNN-review.md` / `NNNN-line-comment.md`. (Native clients also write `NNNN-thread-comment.md`, `NNNN-thread-reply.md`, `NNNN-thread-state.md` and `NNNN-suggestion-state.md`; inline events may carry a signed patchset anchor, see [Review threads across patchsets](design/pull-review-threads.md).) |

- **Signatures.** ForkMesh rejects unsigned events, so every imported event
  is signed by the bridge key with the same canonical strings the desktop
  uses. The signing public key is the record's `author`. The GitHub account
  is kept as display credit in `authorName` with a `github:` prefix (for
  example `github:alice`). That prefix can never match a ForkMesh account
  name, so an imported comment cannot pass as a native user's.
- **Numbers.** GitHub numbers are kept, so `#12` references still resolve.
  If a native ForkMesh record already owns a number, the GitHub item gets the
  next free number and the job summary reports the remapping. The mapping is
  stored in `.forkmesh/github-sync.json`.
- **Idempotence.** Event ids are derived from GitHub ids (`github-…`),
  timestamps come from GitHub, and Ed25519 signatures are deterministic.
  Re-running on an unchanged item therefore rewrites nothing. Issues and pull
  requests whose `updated_at` has not moved are skipped without fetching
  their comments.
- **Edits on ForkMesh are kept.** The bridge only regenerates the `github-*`
  events it owns. A comment, priority, or status change made on ForkMesh on an
  imported item stays, merged in timestamp order. GitHub is authoritative for
  an imported item's open/closed state.
- **Pull request payloads.** For an open pull, the head is fetched from
  `refs/pull/<n>/head` as data only and written as
  `git diff --binary base...head` and `git format-patch --binary --stdout base..head`,
  matching what the desktop derives. Pull request code is never checked out
  or executed, which is what makes `pull_request_target` safe here. A payload
  over 8 MiB is skipped with a warning.

## Limits

- This bridge imports collaboration records GitHub → ForkMesh only. For issues
  and comments in both directions, use [Two-way forge sync](forge-sync.md).
  Pull requests created on ForkMesh stay on ForkMesh, but their commits reach
  GitHub through the code sync.
- Branch deletions are not propagated. A branch deleted on one side is
  recreated from the other on the next run.
- Attachments and images in GitHub bodies stay links to GitHub.
- Review events from fork pull requests run without secrets, so they are
  imported by the next scheduled run instead.
- A repository whose ForkMesh owner node republishes history that GitHub does
  not contain appears as *diverged*. The bridge never picks a winner.

## Running pieces by hand

```bash
# Two-way ref sync only
python3 tools/github_forkmesh_bridge.py git-sync --forkmesh-remote ssh://git@ssh.forkmesh.com/octo/app.git

# Convert records into a checkout without committing (pulls into a ledger worktree)
GITHUB_TOKEN=… FORKMESH_BRIDGE_SIGNING_KEY="$(cat key.pem)" \
  python3 tools/github_forkmesh_bridge.py export --github octo/app --pulls-root ../pulls-ledger

# Everything the workflow does, without pushing
python3 tools/github_forkmesh_bridge.py run --github octo/app --dry-run
```

The contracts are covered by
[`app/tests/test_github_forkmesh_bridge.py`](../../app/tests/test_github_forkmesh_bridge.py).

pages.title: Protocol and ecosystem governance
pages.description: Charter version: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Status: proposed (issue #513). The charter is itself the first proposal, FMP-0001, and follows the process it describes.
pages.markdown:
# Protocol and ecosystem governance

Charter version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Status: **proposed** (issue #513). The charter
is itself the first proposal,
[FMP-0001](decision-register.md#fmp-0001), and follows the process it
describes.

The machine-readable charter is
[`conformance/governance/v1/charter.json`](../../../conformance/governance/v1/charter.json).
Every proposal, security decision, and appeal is a JSON record in
[`conformance/governance/v1/records/`](../../../conformance/governance/v1/records/).
Participants, seat holders, and conflict and funding disclosures are in
[`participants.json`](../../../conformance/governance/v1/participants.json).
The public [decision register](decision-register.md) and the searchable
`/docs/governance/register.json` are generated from those files. A hand edit
to either output fails CI.

This charter governs the ForkMesh protocol suite, certification program,
compatibility commitments, and the moderation baseline. It does not govern an
individual repository. Repository authority still comes only from that
repository's policy document, as the
[collaboration protocol](../design/conflict-safe-collaboration.md) requires.

## Roles

| Body | Decides | Seats |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol council | Protocol, compatibility, deprecation, certification, moderation baseline, the charter | 2 ForkMesh maintainers, 2 independent implementers, 2 community operators |
| Security response team | Security decisions | 1 ForkMesh maintainer, 1 independent implementer, 1 community operator |
| Appeals panel | Appeals | 1 independent implementer, 1 community operator, 1 community member |

Constituencies:

- **ForkMesh maintainer:** has write access to `main`, or is paid by the
  operator of forkmesh.com.
- **Independent implementer:** maintains a client, relay, mirror, index, or
  verifier that is not ForkMesh code, has a public https source, and holds or
  is pursuing a [certification badge](../protocol/certification.md). Is not
  paid by the operator of forkmesh.com.
- **Community operator:** operates a public mirror, relay, gateway, or
  moderation service that other people use. Is not paid by the operator of
  forkmesh.com.
- **Community member:** has an active ForkMesh identity with signed
  contribution history and holds no other seat.

Seats are held by people, not groups. A person holds at most one seat in each
body.

### Quorum

A decision counts only when:

- enough seat holders vote: 4 for the council, 2 for the security team, and 3
  for the appeals panel;
- the required constituencies vote: independent implementers and community
  operators on the council and appeals panel, and an independent implementer
  on the security team;
- no single employer or funder casts more than half of the votes, or more than
  a third on the appeals panel.

ForkMesh maintainers cannot decide anything alone, because an empty
independent seat blocks quorum and no other constituency can fill it. While
the independent seats are vacant, proposals can be opened and reviewed, but
none can be decided.

## Proposals

1. **Draft.** Open a record `FMP-NNNN` naming the affected requirements,
   threats, protected rights, and disclosures. Normative protocol changes
   still follow the suite's [change process](../protocol/README.md#change-process).
2. **Review:** at least 14 days, or 30 days for a breaking change. Anyone may
   comment. The record sets `dissentSolicited: true`.
3. **Last call:** at least 7 days after review closes.
4. **Decision:** due within 14 days after last call. Each vote names the seat
   and a rationale. A `no` vote without a recorded dissent statement fails
   validation. Dissent from anyone, not only seat holders, is recorded with a
   date.
5. **Implemented**, or **withdrawn** at any stage.

## Security decisions

Report privately as described in [SECURITY.md](../../../SECURITY.md).

- Acknowledge within 3 days.
- The embargo lasts at most 90 days.
- A public `FMS-NNNN` record is published within 7 days of disclosure.
- The security response team ratifies the decision within 30 days of
  disclosure.

A fix may ship under embargo before ratification. The record then shows who
decided, when, and any dissent. Outcomes are `mitigated`, `accepted` (with a
threat-register entry naming reviewer, date, and rationale), `rejected`, or
`deferred`.

## Appeals

Anyone affected by a decision may appeal it within 30 days by opening
`FMA-NNNN`. The appeals panel decides within 30 days of filing. Nobody who
wrote or voted on the original decision may vote on the appeal. Outcomes are
`upheld`, `overturned`, or `remanded`. Certification appeals follow the same
timeline; see [appeals and revocation](../protocol/certification.md#appeals-and-revocation).

## Deprecation and compatibility

- Wire version identifiers name frozen bytes and never change meaning.
- Only a major suite version removes acceptance of a wire identifier. The
  removal is announced at least one minor release and 180 days ahead, and
  ships with a migration path.
- Details are in the [compatibility policy](../protocol/README.md#compatibility-policy).

## Conflicts and funding

- Every author and voter on a record must link a disclosure in that record.
  Validation rejects a record without one.
- A disclosure lists conflicts and every funding source by kind: membership,
  donation, grant, contract, investment, reward pool, employment, or none.
- A disclosure is current for 180 days.
- A funding entry without a published amount is shown as "not published" and
  keeps the closure criterion open.
- The register lists, for each disclosure, every record it is linked to.

## Protected rights

No plan, token, hosted-service setting, or funder can remove these rights:

| Right | Guarantee | Business-model commitments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free protocol | Implementing, running, and certifying the protocol requires no payment, plan, or ForkMesh account | `protocolUseRequiresPayment`, `selfHostingRequiresPayment`, `independentImplementationsAllowed` |
| Portable identity | Identities and signed history export and recover without operator permission | `portableSignedCollaborationRequiresPaidPlan` |
| Portable repositories | Git data and signed records can be read, cloned, and moved off any host | `publicReadAndCloneRequirePaidPlan`, `portableGitDataRequiresPaidPlan` |
| Token-free governance | No asset, payment, plan, or funding amount grants a seat, vote, standing, or weight | `governanceRequiresPaidPlan`, `tokenOrBlockchainRequired`, `incentivesAffectIdentityPermissionsRankingModerationOrGovernance` |

Validation fails if any cited
[business-model](../business-model.md) commitment no longer holds. A proposal
that narrows a protected right must be breaking. It needs a two-thirds vote,
including a yes from every filled independent seat. See also
[incentive independence](../incentive-independence.md).

## Moderation baseline

- Every moderation action on a signed record is itself a signed record that
  names the moderator key and the rule applied.
- Hiding content never deletes the underlying signed record. Another host may
  serve it under its own policy.
- A person whose content or account is actioned is told the rule applied and
  may appeal.
- Operators publish their own policy. The baseline is a floor for every host,
  and no operator's policy binds another operator's host.

## Implementation-neutral participation

- Participation needs no ForkMesh client, hosted account, or plan. Proposals,
  comments, and dissent may arrive through any forge mirror of this repository
  or by email, and a maintainer records them with attribution.
- Certification evidence, not the choice of implementation, qualifies an
  independent-implementer seat.

## Succession

- A vacant seat is filled within 60 days. Until then it counts as absent.
- If the operator of forkmesh.com stops operating, the protocol council holds
  the suite, vectors, and certification registry. Anyone may republish them
  under the MIT license.
- Organization-level succession is described in
  [organization succession](../operations/organization-succession.md).

## Running the ledger

```bash
python3 tools/protocol_governance.py validate      # charter, disclosures, records
python3 tools/protocol_governance.py render        # regenerate the register
python3 tools/protocol_governance.py gate          # validate + render --check (CI)
python3 tools/protocol_governance.py status        # deadlines, stale disclosures, blockers
python3 tools/protocol_governance.py closure       # non-zero until #513 can close
```

`gate` never reads today's date, so it cannot fail on the calendar.
`status` and `closure` accept `--as-of YYYY-MM-DD`.

## Failure, rollback, and recovery

- **A record breaks the charter** (short review window, missing disclosure,
  undocumented `no`, missing quorum): `validate` fails and the
  `protocol-governance` quality gate blocks the change. Fix the record. Do not
  waive the gate.
- **A decision is overturned on appeal:** revert the implementing change and
  mark the original record with the appeal outcome. The record is never
  deleted.
- **A deadline passes:** `status` lists the record under `overdue` and
  `closure` fails with `timelines-met`. Record a decision, an extension as a
  new dated note, or a withdrawal.
- **The register is stale or hand-edited:** run `render` and commit the result.

## Measures

`status` reports, and each monthly [outcome review](../outcome-review.md)
records:

- proposal participation: comments and dissent entries per record;
- decision latency: days from `opened` to `decided`;
- appeals filed and their outcomes;
- independent representation: filled independent seats, and independent votes
  per decision;
- policy compliance: overdue records and stale disclosures. The target is zero.

## Closure criteria for issue #513

`closure` exits non-zero until every item holds. At charter adoption, all of
them are open:

- **proposal-completed:** a proposal adopted under the charter is decided with
  a quorum, full timeline, and solicited dissent.
- **security-decision-completed:** a security decision adopted under the
  charter is decided and ratified with a quorum.
- **independent-roles:** the council has independent-implementer and
  community-operator seat holders who voted in a completed decision.
- **disclosures-current:** every active participant has a current disclosure,
  and every funding amount is published.
- **timelines-met:** nothing is overdue.

The two pre-charter records, [FMP-0000](decision-register.md#fmp-0000) and
[FMS-0001](decision-register.md#fms-0001), are kept for public history. They
do not count toward closure.

## Linked automated evidence

- Charter, disclosure, timeline, quorum, dissent, protected-right, and
  register checks: `app/tests/test_protocol_governance.py`
- Quality gate: `protocol-governance` in
  [`quality-gates.json`](../engineering/quality-gates.json), in the `core` and
  `release` profiles
- CI: `.github/workflows/collaboration-conformance.yml` runs `gate` on Linux,
  macOS, and Windows.

Automated checks do not replace the seated independent reviewers, the real
decisions, or the published funding amounts that closure requires.

A record marked *pre-charter* was made before the charter existed. It is kept for the public

pages.title: Hackathon
pages.description: How a ForkMesh hackathon campaign works, what earns what, and which guarantees the code enforces rather than merely documents.
pages.markdown:
# Hackathon

How a ForkMesh hackathon campaign works, what earns what, and which
guarantees the code enforces rather than merely documents.

The design goal is the one the growth plan set: taking part in the contest
should itself be the marketing, so that a participant has both a reason and a
one-tap way to bring the next one. The constraint that shapes every decision
below is that this must not become a spam machine or a lottery. So anything
worth money is gated on the referral ledger that already protects the public
referral programme, every reward is a fixed threshold, and pressing a share
button is worth nothing.

Code:

| Area | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Pure policy: points, missions, milestones, share copy, challenges, rewards, submissions, judging, growth funnel, config validation | `app/src/hackathon.py` |
| Routes, D1 access, hooks, personal pages, admin page | `app/src/hackathon_runtime.py` |
| Share cards | `app/src/og_card.py` (`render_hackathon_card`) |
| Participant HQ | `app/public/dashboard/partials/views/hackathon.html`, `app/public/dashboard/js/09-hackathon.js` |
| Landing page (main's) | `www/public/hackathon.html`, `www/public/assets/hackathon/` |
| Leaderboard, gallery, rules | `www/public/hackathon/{leaderboard,projects,rules}.html`, `www/public/hackathon.{css,js}` |
| Schema | `app/migrations/0182_hackathon.sql` (and its `down/` reversal) |
| Tests | `app/tests/test_hackathon*.py` |

## Lifecycle

A campaign is one row in `hackathons`, keyed by slug, with a status:

| Status | Public pages | Joinable | Submissions | Judging |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `draft` | 404 | no | no | no |
| `registration` | yes | yes | no | no |
| `live` | yes | yes | until `ends_at` | after `ends_at` |
| `judging` | yes | no | no | yes |
| `closed` | yes | no | no | no |

**`draft` is what makes this safe to ship.** Every push to this repository
deploys, so the feature has to be able to sit in production unfinished. A
draft campaign 404s on every personal page and every participant API, and
`GET /api/hackathon` returns `campaign: null`. A relay whose migration has not
run yet reports no campaign the same way instead of failing. Only an
administrator can advance a status, never a deploy.

With no slug, `_campaign()` resolves *the current campaign*: the newest one
that is not a draft. Every table is keyed by slug, so a second campaign needs
no migration.

## Points

`hackathon_points` is append-only, with primary key
`(hackathon_slug, account_bi, kind, ref)`. That key **is** the anti-double-pay
rule. A once-per-participant kind collapses its reference to the empty string,
so a second award is rejected by the key itself. A repeatable kind carries the
event's own reference, so one event pays exactly once however often its hook
fires. `hackathon_participants.points` caches the sum and only moves with a
write that landed.

| Kind | Points | Written when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `joined` | 50 | the participant row is created |
| `verified` | 150 | their email is verified |
| `referral_joined` | 100 | somebody they invited verifies their email |
| `referral_qualified` | 200 | the referral ledger **credits** that referral |
| `first_mirror` | 300 | their first repository is published to the catalog |
| `pull_accepted` | 150 | a pull they authored is accepted |
| `submission` | 500 | their team submits a project (each member, once per submission) |
| `referral_post` | 100 | the microjob verifier confirms a public post |

A submission is worth more than a qualified referral on purpose, so the
Builders board cannot be won by recruiting alone.

**No point kind is client-reportable.** `CLIENT_REPORTABLE_POINT_KINDS` is the
empty set and a test pins it there.

## Joined versus qualified

Two different numbers, never merged.

* **Joined**: the invited person verified their email. This moves progress
  bars, the onboarding nudge, squad membership and `referral_joined` points,
  immediately.
* **Qualified**: `referral_attributions.decision` became `credited`, which
  takes email verification, seven days of membership, sustained use from a
  proved desktop device, and the burst, network and risk rules the public
  referral board enforces.

Anything of value reads *qualified*. The hackathon never re-decides a
referral: `on_referral_credited` is called from inside
`_finalize_referral_signup`, so its gate is that function's gate.

## Rewards

### What a reward can be

Missions and milestones award `pro_months`, `supporter_months`, a `badge`, or
nothing. Two kinds are deliberately impossible:

* **Cash** follows the judged tracks only. Nothing reachable from a mission,
  a milestone or recruiting can pay it.
* **Points** come only from the events in the table above. A mission is
  derived from those same events, so a points reward on it would pay each
  event twice. The validator refuses one.

Every reward is a fixed threshold. There are no entries, tickets or random
draws anywhere, which is what keeps this a contest of skill rather than a
sweepstakes. `validate_config` refuses, rather than clamps, an unknown reward
kind, an unknown metric or an out-of-range threshold or month count.

### How memberships are granted

Every reward is first claimed in `hackathon_reward_grants`, keyed by
`(slug, account, reward_key, kind)`, with one
`INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING … RETURNING`. A reward whose event is observed
twice is granted exactly once.

Months are then projected into `role_grants` under
**`scope_type='promotion'`**, never the platform scope. Patreon revokes
platform-scope membership rows on every webhook, without even filtering by
scope, so a prize written there would vanish at the next subscription
renewal. A test replays a provider revoke against a granted prize.

* **Months stack.** One upsert computes `MAX(live expiry, now) + months`
  inside the database, so rewards landing together both count, and a lapsed
  promotion restarts from now. A month is thirty days.
* **Pro includes Supporter**, as every other tier table here does, which is
  what makes the World outfit perk follow a Pro prize.
* The plan surface (`/api/plans/usage`) reports an earned membership in its
  own `promotion` field, beside the paid `membership`. It is never folded
  into the paid one; otherwise the pricing page would stop offering
  membership to somebody whose free months are about to end.

### When rewards happen

| Source | Granted when |
| --- | --- |
| Missions | the moment a counter they read reaches the threshold: a friend verifying, a referral credited, a first mirror, a landed pull, a squad growing |
| Squad goals | every member of the squad that reached the goal, once; later arrivals are evaluated on joining |
| Prize table | when an administrator finalizes results |

The default missions pay memberships only for recruiting (3 qualified: 3
months; 10 qualified: 6 months and the Connector badge) and for a squad of
25 (3 months each). "Submit your project" is progress only. The Pro months
and Builder badge for a valid submission are the published prize, paid at
finalization and only once a project is confirmed valid. Paying the mission
too would reward the same entry twice, and before anyone had checked it.

## Squads and teams

A **squad** is an invite tree, not a chosen team. It is created the first time
a participant's link brings somebody in, and everyone who later arrives
through them joins it. `/hackathon/squad/<code>` is that participant's own
microsite, with their name, their meter and their reward. This is the
"let people run their own mini-contest" idea, with nothing to set up.

A **team** is the submission unit: up to five people, one project per track,
joined with an eight-character invite code. A participant is on one team per
campaign, enforced by the member table's key. The captaincy passes on when
the captain leaves, and the last member cannot leave while the team has a live
submission. The two words are never interchanged.

## Challenge links

"Alex has 1,240 points. Can you beat that?" A participant sends a link from
their HQ; `/hackathon/challenge/<token>` shows who dared you, the number to
pass, and how many people accepted and won.

* **The target is fixed when the link is sent**, as the number the page
  shows, so a challenge never moves under somebody chasing it.
* **Strictly more beats it.** A tie beats nobody. A beat is claimed with one
  `UPDATE … RETURNING` and announced to both people exactly once.
* **Beating one pays no points**, or two friends could mint points by
  challenging each other in a loop.
* **Accepting is not a referral.** It joins the campaign if needed but records
  no referrer and no squad, so the challenger earns nothing the referral
  ledger didn't decide. A newcomer gets a second button through `/r/<name>`.
* One link serves a group chat of up to fifty; a participant can have twenty
  open; a link closes after `challengeHours` (default 72). Pages are noindex.

Accepting happens on the HQ at `/hackathon/me?accept=<token>`, where the
session lives. The log-in link keeps the token, and the HQ removes it from the
address once used.

## Submissions, gallery and judging

**Submitting.** A team names a repository as `owner/name`. Each save checks
the catalog: public, not private, and first hosted inside the campaign window
with a week's grace. Anything unconfirmed becomes a **review flag, not a
rejection**. A false rejection costs a builder their entry, while a false flag
costs a judge one look. Posting again for the same track edits the submission
until the deadline, and an administrator's `invalid` survives an edit.

**Gallery.** Only `valid` projects are public, at `/hackathon/projects` and
`/hackathon/projects/<id>`. A flagged project appears the moment it is
cleared. Everything a submitter wrote is escaped, and outbound links are
`https` only and marked `nofollow ugc`.

**Community Choice.** One vote per verified participant per track, which can
be moved, never for their own team. It opens when the `community_choice`
milestone unlocks and closes after judging. Counts are recomputed from the
votes, so a moved vote moves the count.

**Judging.** Administrators name judges. A judge scores 1–5 on four criteria
(fits the track, working software, portable and self-hostable, craft), can
revise a score, and cannot score their own team. Scoring opens when
submissions close.

**Results.** Finalizing ranks each track by average judge score, then more
judges, then earlier submission; an unscored project cannot place. It writes
1st and 2nd, closes the campaign and grants the prize table through the
reward ledger. Running it again changes nothing.

## Community milestones

A milestone unlocks where the counter it watches moves: a join, a
verification, a new squad, a submission, or an administrator saving new
thresholds. That makes an unlock immediate for two small reads, without a
scheduler slot. The unlock is claimed with `UPDATE … WHERE unlocked_at=0
RETURNING`, so it happens once, and it never re-locks when a withdrawal moves
a counter down. The HQ's milestone panel is the in-product announcement.

## Sharing

The share kit offers copy, X, Mastodon, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Reddit, Hacker
News, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp, email, SMS on phones, the native share
sheet, a QR code, and a **story image**. Every channel opens the participant's
own client with editable text.

The story image is a 1080×1920 PNG drawn in the browser, carrying the
participant's rank, points and invite QR. On a phone it goes to the share
sheet, elsewhere it downloads, and it costs the Worker nothing.

* **Nothing is sent on anyone's behalf.** No contact list, no recipient
  column, no message to a third party.
* **A share press is measured, not paid.** It is the K-factor numerator and
  worth zero points; a mission on `shares` may award nothing.
* **Presses are deduped per channel per minute.**

## Ambassadors

A verified participant applies with a short pitch; an administrator approves
or rejects, and a rejected applicant may apply again. Approval awards the
Hackathon Ambassador badge. An approved ambassador's HQ shows their own funnel
since the campaign opened, using the referral click audit's accepted rows so
duplicates and crawlers are already excluded. It also offers a printable
poster with their QR code, marked "post only where you have permission".

## Administration

`/admin/hackathon` is gated like `/admin/acquisition` (account session plus
`is_admin`, checked live), has no script and a `default-src 'none'` CSP. It is
the Hackathon section of the unified admin, drawn inside the shared admin
shell, with a campaign switcher and one tab (`?tab=`) per area:

* **Growth**: K-factor, invitations per participant, invitation
  conversion; the viral funnel; share presses by channel; joins per UTC day;
  and recruiters with credited, pending and rejected referrals.
* **Campaign**: slug, title, status, UTC dates and the JSON
  config, validated before anything is written.
* **Judges & results** (adding and removing judges, finalize results),
  **Submissions** (review) and **Ambassadors** (decisions).

Forms post back and redirect to the tab they came from, so a refresh never
repeats an action, and a
cross-origin form is refused. The page and `POST /api/admin/hackathon` call
the same functions.

**The K-factor.** ForkMesh never sees a message being sent, so "invitations"
are share presses and are labelled as intent. K therefore equals referred
joins per participant. The funnel shows a share of the previous stage only
where a stage is a subset of it; presses and "built something" are not.

## Routes

| URL | Served by | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/hackathon` | www static asset | Main's landing page; observed by acquisition attribution. |
| `/hackathon/leaderboard` | www static asset | Builders, Recruiters, Squads. |
| `/hackathon/projects` | www static asset | Project gallery. |
| `/hackathon/rules` | www static asset | Official rules. |
| `/hackathon/join/<name>` | App, **proxied** by www | Personalised invitation. |
| `/hackathon/squad/<code>` | App, **proxied** by www | Squad microsite. |
| `/hackathon/challenge/<token>` | App, **proxied** by www | Challenge page; noindex. |
| `/hackathon/projects/<id>` | App, **proxied** by www | One valid project. |
| `/hackathon/me` | composed dashboard page | Participant HQ. |
| `/admin/hackathon` | App, `is_admin` | Administrator page. |
| `/api/hackathon[/…]` | App | Campaign, join, me, share, challenges, teams, submissions, projects, votes, judging, ambassadors, boards, squads, cards. |
| `/api/admin/hackathon` | App, `is_admin` | JSON equivalent of the administrator page. |

Personal pages are **proxied, not redirected**, so a shared link keeps the apex
URL it was shared as. This matters twice: the microjob verifier looks for
`forkmesh.com/r/<name>` in a posted page, and an unfurl should show the link
actually posted. They are matched before the two-segment repository shortcut,
like `/r/<name>`, so they never read as `owner/repo`.

## Read budget

D1 bills rows read, and the Worker was near half its daily free allowance
before this feature. So public reads are edge-cached (60 s) and bounded to
fifty rows (two hundred for the gallery). Campaign counters are denormalised
and moved by the writes that change them, so neither the meter nor a board
runs `COUNT(*)`. A participant's own rank is one indexed count on their own
page.

## Share cards

`render_hackathon_card` draws the same 1200×630 PNG family as the repository
and referral cards, in-process with the standard library and edge-cached per
colo. Kinds: `invite`, `rank`, `squad`, `challenge`, `project`.

## Privacy

* No contact of any kind is collected, stored or transmitted.
* Share events store a channel and a surface only.
* Public pages show public ForkMesh usernames only, the same trust level as
  the referral board and `badge_awards`.
* Notifications go only to the person concerned, about their own standing or
  reward.

## Done by people, not code

* Deciding the dates, the cash amount per track, the tracks, the milestone
  ladder, eligibility and who judges.
* Paying cash, running the guaranteed interview, and making featured
  placements on the homepage and the Marketplace after results.
* Recruiting ambassadors and anybody else. Nothing here contacts anyone.
* Having the official rules reviewed before the cash figure is announced.

## Deliberately not built

* **The physical QR scavenger hunt.** It only works with a venue and
  permission to place codes. Ambassadors' posters already cover the
  permission-based part.
* **Mass notifications on a milestone unlock.** One maintenance phase cannot
  notify every participant within its subrequest budget; the HQ panel and the
  landing meter carry the unlock instead.
* **Generated video for Stories.** The story image covers the channel at no
  Worker cost.
* **Random draws of any kind**, for the reason above.
