pages.markdown:
# Integration contract (v1)

ForkMesh publishes a versioned contract for tools that migrate, automate,
discover, deploy, analyze, or moderate repositories without scraping the
website or desktop UI. The contract has four parts:

- **HTTP resources** on the hosted API and on a self-hosted mirror node.
- **An event stream** of `forkmesh-event-v1` records.
- **Command-line output**, both the integration tool's and `forkmesh-mirror-node`'s.
- **Signed webhook delivery**.

| Artifact | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Machine-readable contract | [`conformance/integrations/v1/contract.json`](../../conformance/integrations/v1/contract.json) |
| SDK-light client, contract runner, watcher, webhook sender, offline fixture | [`tools/forkmesh_integration.py`](../../tools/forkmesh_integration.py) (one file, Python 3.10+ standard library) |
| Maintained examples | [`conformance/integrations/v1/examples/`](../../conformance/integrations/v1/examples/) |
| Contract tests | [`app/tests/test_integration_contract.py`](../../app/tests/test_integration_contract.py) |

The file `contract.json` is the source of truth. This page explains it. If the two
disagree, the JSON wins and the disagreement is a bug.

## Quick start

Download `forkmesh_integration.py` and `contract.json` into one directory.
The tool finds `contract.json` next to itself. Then run:

```sh
python3 forkmesh_integration.py discover --target hosted
python3 forkmesh_integration.py contract --target hosted --output report.json
python3 forkmesh_integration.py contract --target self-hosted --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8791
python3 forkmesh_integration.py contract --target hosted --fixture next   # offline, no network
```

`discover` prints one line with a capability map and a version-skew verdict.
`contract` checks every resource for its target and prints a
`forkmesh-integration-contract-report-v1` report. The report records the
status codes, required fields, headers, attempts, latency, additional
(unknown) field counts, and the service version. Reports hold no credentials:
base URLs are stripped of userinfo and query strings.

## Services and authentication

| Service | Default base URL | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hosted` | `https://app.forkmesh.com` | The hosted application API |
| `self-hosted` | `http://127.0.0.1:8791` | The `forkmesh-mirror-node` daemon's loopback control API |

Every HTTP resource names exactly one authentication scheme:

- `anonymous`: public reads. No credentials; responses may be edge cached.
- `loopback-operator`: the daemon binds `127.0.0.1` only, so reaching the
  socket is the authorization. Never publish that port.
- `catalog-view-token`: an owner signs a short-lived
  `forkmesh-catalog-view-v1` token and passes `viewer`, `ts`, and `sig`. This
  adds the viewer's private and shared repositories to `GET /api/repositories`.
  Those responses are `no-store` and carry a weak `ETag`, so revalidate with
  `If-None-Match`.
- `account-bearer`: a bearer token from `POST /api/accounts/login`, sent as
  `Authorization: Bearer …`. Never put it in a URL.
- `webhook-capability-url`: an inbound chat webhook URL contains a random
  256-bit token, and the URL itself is the credential. Rotate the webhook to
  revoke it.
- `webhook-hmac`: outbound deliveries are signed with a shared secret (see
  [Signatures](#signatures)).

## HTTP resources

| Service | Method and path | Required fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| hosted | `GET /api/version` | `ok`, `rev`, `worker`, `version`, `now` |
| hosted | `GET /api/openapi.json` | `openapi`, `info`, `paths` |
| hosted | `GET /api/metrics/endpoints` | `ok`, `endpoints[].method`, `endpoints[].template` |
| hosted | `GET /api/repositories` | `ok`, `repositories[].owner`, `.name`, `.visibility` |
| hosted | `GET /api/repositories/search` (beta) | `ok`, `total`, `results[].owner`, `.name`, `.clone` |
| hosted | `GET /api/status` | `ok`, `now`, `systems[].id`, `systems[].status` |
| hosted | `GET /api/mirrors/https` | `ok`, `protocol`, `registration` |
| hosted | `POST /api/chat/webhooks/{token}` | inbound webhook, `202 {"ok", "messageId"}` |
| self-hosted | `GET /healthz` | `ok`, `node` |
| self-hosted | `GET /readyz` (200 or 503) | `ok`, `ready`, `version` |
| self-hosted | `GET /v1/status` | `ok`, `ready`, `node`, `version`, `uptimeSeconds`, `repositories`, `lastSyncOk`, `syncCount` |
| self-hosted | `POST /v1/control/sync` | `202 {"ok", "queued"}` |

Use `GET /api/openapi.json` or `GET /api/metrics/endpoints` for discovery.
They enumerate every route the Worker serves. Only the routes above are part
of the stable contract. Other routes may change without notice.

## Pagination

Contract collections are bounded rather than paged. `GET /api/repositories`
returns at most 200 records, newest `updatedAt` first. Feeds ordered by time
resume with a `since` cursor set to the previous response's `latestTs`.
Entries exactly at that boundary can repeat, so deduplicate them.

`GET /api/repositories/search` is the one keyset-paged collection. Pass
its `nextCursor` back as `cursor` with the same filters until `nextCursor` is
`null`; each match is returned exactly once. See
[Searchable repository index](repository-index.md).

## Filtering

Contract collections have no server-side filters, except
`GET /api/repositories/search` (`q`, `view`, `language`, `topic`, `owner`,
`cloneable`). Otherwise filter on the client using
documented fields: `owner`, `name`, `visibility`, `liveHost`, `cloneOnline`,
`termsFlagged`. Query parameters not listed in the contract are not part of
it.

## Idempotency

- `GET` and `HEAD` are always safe to repeat.
- `POST /v1/control/sync` is idempotent. Repeating it while a sync is pending
  returns `202` with `"queued": false`.
- Inbound chat webhook POSTs are **not** deduplicated. Every accepted POST
  becomes a message, so a sender should retry only when no response arrived.
- Every outbound event has a stable `id`. Receivers use it as the idempotency
  key and answer `2xx` for duplicates.

## Ordering and the event stream

`watch` polls stable resources and prints one `forkmesh-event-v1` JSON object
per change:

```json
{"schema":"forkmesh-event-v1","id":"4c1f…","type":"repository.changed",
 "subject":"forkmesh/forkmesh","sequence":7,"digest":"9a0e…",
 "occurredAt":1789347378245,"source":"https://app.forkmesh.com",
 "data":{"owner":"forkmesh","name":"forkmesh","commit":"…","termsFlagged":false}}
```

| Type | Service | Subject | Producer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repository.changed`, `repository.removed` | hosted | lowercase `owner/name` | `watch` |
| `repository.push`, `branch.push` | hosted | lowercase `owner/name` | relay |
| `pull.merged`, `release.published` | hosted | lowercase `owner/name` | relay |
| `mirror.node.changed` | self-hosted | `node:<name>` | `watch` |
| `mirror.repository.changed`, `mirror.repository.removed` | self-hosted | the daemon's repository key | `watch` |

The `watch` types are produced by polling the public catalog. The four relay
types are produced by the relay itself and are only ever delivered to a
[registered repository webhook](#repository-webhooks).

```sh
python3 forkmesh_integration.py watch --target hosted --state watch-state.json --interval 60
```

Guarantees:

- **At-least-once.** State is saved *after* events are printed. A crash in
  between re-emits the same ids on restart; nothing is lost.
- **Per-subject order.** `sequence` increases by exactly one for each observed
  change to a subject. There is no global order across subjects.
- **Full state.** Every `changed` event carries the subject's complete current
  `data`. A consumer that gives up on a gap still converges.
- Volatile telemetry (CPU, memory, disk) is excluded from `data`, so idle
  repositories stay quiet.

### Recovering from duplicate, delayed, missing, and out-of-order delivery

`EventLedger` (in the tool) implements the consumer rules. Use it as it is,
or port these five rules:

1. **Duplicate**: an already-seen `id` is acknowledged and ignored.
2. **Out of order (stale)**: a `sequence` at or below the last applied one for
   that subject is ignored.
3. **Delayed**: a `sequence` more than one ahead is buffered until the gap
   fills. It is then applied in order.
4. **Missing**: once a gap has waited `gapTimeoutSeconds` (120), the ledger
   emits `resync` with the missing range. It then applies the lowest buffered
   event. Re-read the resource over HTTP if the skipped transitions matter.
5. **Baseline**: the first event seen for a subject is applied whatever its
   sequence. A late-joining consumer does not wait for history.

```python
import forkmesh_integration as fm
ledger = fm.EventLedger()
for action, payload in ledger.accept(event) + ledger.expire():
    if action == "apply":
        handle(payload["subject"], payload.get("data"))
    elif action == "resync":
        refetch(payload["subject"])
```

The relay's owner WebSocket (`{"type":"event","topic","repo","state","generation"}`)
is an internal, owner-signed doorbell for an account's own nodes. It is not a
third-party interface.

## Webhooks

### Outbound (`forkmesh-webhook-v1`)

```sh
export FORKMESH_WEBHOOK_SECRET=…            # never on the command line
python3 forkmesh_integration.py watch --target hosted --state s.json \
  | python3 forkmesh_integration.py deliver --url https://hooks.example/forkmesh \
      --dead-letter dead.ndjson
```

Each delivery is a `POST` whose body is one event serialized as canonical JSON
(sorted keys, no spaces). It carries these headers:

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `ForkMesh-Webhook-Id` | the event `id` (idempotency key) |
| `ForkMesh-Webhook-Timestamp` | Unix seconds, taken again on every attempt |
| `ForkMesh-Webhook-Signature` | `v1=<hex>`; during rotation, several comma-separated values |
| `ForkMesh-Webhook-Attempt` | `1`, `2`, … |
| `ForkMesh-Event-Type` | the event `type` |

The receiver's response decides what happens next:

- `2xx` acknowledges the event.
- `410 Gone` stops delivery for that event.
- `408`, `425`, `429`, `5xx`, and network errors are retried (see [Retries](#retries)).
- Any other `4xx`, or running out of retries, writes the event to the
  dead-letter file.

To replay, run `deliver --input dead.ndjson --dead-letter dead.ndjson`. The
file is rewritten to hold only the events that still fail.

### Signatures

The signed message and signature are:

```text
message   = "forkmesh-webhook-v1\n" + timestamp + "\n" + id + "\n" + raw_body
signature = "v1=" + hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, message))
```

A receiver can verify a delivery without the tool:

```python
import hashlib, hmac, time

def verify(secret: bytes, headers, body: bytes, tolerance=300):
    ts = int(headers["ForkMesh-Webhook-Timestamp"])
    if abs(time.time() - ts) > tolerance:
        raise ValueError("stale")
    msg = b"forkmesh-webhook-v1\n%d\n%s\n" % (ts, headers["ForkMesh-Webhook-Id"].encode()) + body
    expected = "v1=" + hmac.new(secret, msg, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    if not any(hmac.compare_digest(expected, part.strip())
               for part in headers["ForkMesh-Webhook-Signature"].split(",")):
        raise ValueError("bad signature")
```

Reject timestamps more than 300 seconds from now. Deduplicate by
`ForkMesh-Webhook-Id` so a captured request cannot be replayed within that
window.

Repository, issue, and pull records keep their own Ed25519 signatures over
`forkmesh-<kind>-v1` canonical strings. Node-to-relay requests carry
`X-ForkMesh-Signature`. Neither involves the webhook secret.

### Repository webhooks

A repository owner registers endpoints on the repository's **Settings** tab in
the dashboard (`POST /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/webhooks`, session-authenticated,
owner only). ForkMesh then delivers the events below with the same
`forkmesh-webhook-v1` envelope the `deliver` command uses — no watcher process
to run, and the signing secret is generated by the relay and shown once.

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `repository.push` | Any ref (branch or tag) moved: an owner-signed catalog publication, or a plain-git push to a repository ForkMesh hosts. |
| `branch.push` | A signed publication also moved the default branch tip. A hosted repository's plain-git push does not raise this, because that path pins a refs digest without a branch tip. |
| `pull.merged` | A merge completed *and* the node reported the result published. |
| `release.published` | A signed release manifest was published for a tag. |

Notes that matter when wiring a CI provider:

- A push produces `repository.push`, and additionally `branch.push` when the
  default branch moved, so a provider that should build only on the default
  branch subscribes to `branch.push` alone.
- Only public repositories emit these events.
- Destinations must be public `https`. Loopback, link-local, private-range and
  `forkmesh.com` addresses are refused when the webhook is saved.
- Deliveries are queued and drained out of band, so a slow endpoint never slows
  a push, a merge or a release down. Retries follow [Retries](#retries) and stop
  after 6 attempts; the Settings tab shows the last outcome per endpoint.
- `sequence` counts that endpoint's own deliveries and increases by exactly
  one per event it receives, so the consumer rules above apply unchanged. Two
  endpoints subscribed to the same event agree on its `id` but keep their own
  sequence, and a delivery test consumes one.

### Inbound chat webhooks

`POST /api/chat/webhooks/{token}` with a body of `{"text": "…"}` (`content`
or `message` also work) posts to a public channel and answers `202`. Errors:

| Status | `error` |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `empty_webhook` |
| 404 | `not_found` |
| 405 | `method_not_allowed` (with `Allow: POST`) |
| 409 | `public_channel_required` |

## Retries

Retry idempotent requests on transport errors and on `408`, `425`, `429`,
`500`, `502`, `503`, and `504`:

- Make at most 6 attempts, with exponential backoff starting at 0.5 s, capped
  at 30 s, with jitter.
- `Retry-After` (seconds or an HTTP date) or a `retryAfterMs` body field
  replaces the computed delay.
- Non-idempotent requests retry only on `429`.
- Never retry any other `4xx`.

`Client` in the tool implements this and counts retries in its telemetry.

## Rate limits

Throttled requests answer `429` with `Retry-After` and usually
`{"error":"rate_limited","retryAfterMs":…}`. Hosted public reads are edge
cached (the catalog for 30 s). Polling faster returns the same bytes and
spends the shared daily request budget. `watch` enforces a minimum poll
interval of 30 s for hosted and 5 s for self-hosted.

## Errors

- Hosted errors are JSON objects with a stable snake_case code, for example
  `{"error":"invalid_json"}`.
- The daemon answers `{"ok":false,"error":"<message>"}`.
- Branch on the HTTP status class first and the `error` code second. Treat an
  unknown code by its status class.
- New error codes are additive and may appear at any time.

## Command-line output

Every line written to stdout is one JSON object:

- Command results carry `"schema":"forkmesh-cli-v1"` and `"command"`.
- `watch` lines are `forkmesh-event-v1` events.
- Diagnostics go to stderr.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | success |
| 1 | contract failure or undeliverable events |
| 2 | usage or configuration error |
| 3 | unsupported service version skew |

Commands: `validate`, `discover`, `contract`, `watch`, `deliver`, `fixture`.

`forkmesh-mirror-node` has a smaller contract: the flags `-config`, `-init`,
`-check`, `-public-key`, `-set-version`, `-register-link-code`, and
`-version`. It exits `0` on success and `1` on failure, with the reason on
stderr. On success it prints these exact lines:

| Flag | stdout |
| --- | --- |
| `-check` | `mirror-node configuration OK` |
| `-set-version` | `mirror-node version updated` |
| `-register-link-code` | `node account registered` |

## Deprecation

To deprecate a contract entry:

1. Mark it `"stability": "deprecated"`.
2. List it under `deprecations` with `announced`, `sunset`, and `replacement`.
   The sunset must be at least **180 days** after the announcement.

A deprecated entry keeps working until its sunset, and contract reports warn
while it is in use. Removal requires the next contract major (v2). No entries
are deprecated in v1.0.0.

## Version skew

- Within v1, services only add things: fields, resources, event types, and
  error codes. Consumers **must ignore unknown fields**.
- A service reporting a version below `serviceMinimum` (`0.8.0`) is
  `unsupported`, and the tools exit with code 3.
- A version that cannot be parsed, such as a `dev` build, is `unknown`. It is
  reported, not failed.
- The fixture serves three skew profiles: `previous` (0.8.0, without
  `deployFingerprint`), `current`, and `next` (0.9.0, with extra fields). The
  contract tests run every profile against both services. The `broken` and
  `unsupported` profiles prove that failures are detected.

## Examples

Each example uses only the resources and rules on this page, plus
`forkmesh_integration.py` placed next to it (or pointed to by
`FORKMESH_INTEGRATION_TOOL`). The contract tests run all of them against the
offline fixture.

| Category | Example | Run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discovery, analytics | [`discovery_catalog.py`](../../conformance/integrations/v1/examples/discovery_catalog.py) | `python3 discovery_catalog.py --query mesh --live-only` |
| Migration | [`migration_export.py`](../../conformance/integrations/v1/examples/migration_export.py) | `python3 migration_export.py --output ./export` (rerun to resume) |
| Automation, moderation | [`webhook_moderation.py`](../../conformance/integrations/v1/examples/webhook_moderation.py) | `FORKMESH_WEBHOOK_SECRET=… python3 webhook_moderation.py --port 8787 --state ledger.json` |
| Deployment | [`deployment_gate.py`](../../conformance/integrations/v1/examples/deployment_gate.py) | `python3 deployment_gate.py --expect-version 0.8.8 --timeout 300` |

With `--stop-after`, `webhook_moderation.py` stops only after it has written
the last acknowledgement. If it stopped first, the server's handler threads
(which are daemon threads) could die with the process between the response
headers and the body. The sender would then get `IncompleteRead` on its final
delivery.

## Contract tests and telemetry

- `app/tests/test_integration_contract.py` checks each contract entry against
  the source that serves it: Worker routes and response fields, daemon routes
  and status JSON tags, and `forkmesh-mirror-node` flags and output. It then
  runs the contract against the fixture for both services and every skew
  profile, checks retry, ledger, and webhook recovery properties, and runs
  every example.
- CI runs the same contract offline for both services and every profile.
  Against production, run
  `contract --target hosted` (and `--target self-hosted` on a node).
- Each report's `telemetry` block records requests, retries, transport errors,
  status classes, and total latency, which is enough to track contract pass
  rate, API errors, and upgrade breakage per service version.
- Hosted per-route traffic and error rates are visible live in the desktop's
  Network → Web Requests tab, counted from the Worker log tail (they are not
  stored server-side).

pages.title: Lemmy-compatible threaded collaboration
pages.description: ForkMesh accepts public ActivityPub replies to public, federated issue, pull-request, and discussion objects. Lemmy Create activities containing a Note, Page, or Article use the…
pages.markdown:
# Lemmy-compatible threaded collaboration

ForkMesh accepts public ActivityPub replies to public, federated issue,
pull-request, and discussion objects. Lemmy `Create` activities containing a
`Note`, `Page`, or `Article` use the same normalization boundary as compatible
Mastodon replies. Nested replies may target either the original ForkMesh
ActivityPub object or another verified remote reply.

## Trust boundary

Remote replies are stored in `ap_comments` using the
`forkmesh-federated-thread-v1` encrypted record schema and the
`federatedReplies` storage namespace. They are never written to:

- `.forkmesh/issues`;
- `pulls`;
- `.forkmesh/discussions`; or
- any ForkMesh Ed25519-signed event stream.

An ActivityPub HTTP signature authenticates delivery by a remote actor. It
does not make the reply a ForkMesh native event. API projections therefore always
include `federated: true`, `nativeEvent: false`, remote provenance, and a
separation notice. Clients show the remote instance and canonical HTTPS
backlink alongside that notice.

A remote object cannot select a ForkMesh context. A top-level reply inherits
the context of the local `/ap/o/{id}` object it targets. A nested reply inherits
the encrypted context of its already-stored parent. Unresolved targets are
acknowledged and discarded.

## Lifecycle and deduplication

The remote object’s HTTPS `id` receives a stable blind index and SHA-256
deduplication key.

- `Create` inserts once; repeated delivery is idempotent.
- `Update` replaces only the public projection body and records `edited`.
  The author must match the verified original author.
- `Delete` erases the projected body and leaves a `tombstoned` placeholder so
  nested thread structure and the remote backlink remain understandable.
- `Remove` erases the projected body and records `moderated`. It is accepted
  only from a verified actor on the same remote instance.
- `Undo(Remove)` makes a record await safe redelivery rather than resurrecting
  moderation-hidden content from a local cache.

Tombstone and moderation placeholders never expose removed bodies.

## Instance blocks and privacy

The existing ActivityPub instance block list is checked before signature
verification and persistence. The read projection checks it again so a newly
blocked instance disappears immediately without waiting for encrypted-row
cleanup. Subdomains of a blocked domain are blocked as well.

Only public repository threads federate. Private repository visibility checks
run before the comments endpoint, and a remote activity cannot discover or
attach itself to an encrypted private repository.

## Client API

All clients read:

```text
GET /api/repo/{owner}/{repo}/fedi-comments?kind={issue|pull|discussion}&number={n}
```

The ordered `comments` array contains nesting depth, lifecycle, author,
instance/software provenance, plain-text body, canonical backlink, and the
non-native marker. The Web dashboard, Qt client, iOS and Android apps, and World use
this projection and render it in a distinct “Fediverse thread” area below or
beside the native collaboration timeline.

Clients must render bodies as plain text, accept backlinks only when they are
HTTPS URLs, cap visible nesting depth, and label edited, tombstoned, and
moderated records. No client may deserialize these records into a native event
class.

## Fixtures

Interoperability fixtures live under:

```text
app/tests/fixtures/activitypub/lemmy/
```

They cover issue create/update, pull-comment tombstones, nested discussion
replies, moderation, duplicate delivery, author mismatch, and instance blocks.

pages.markdown:
# Offline and low-bandwidth sync

Use this guide when a repository has to keep moving without a dependable
connection: a link that drops every few minutes, a metered data plan, a
community network with no internet uplink, or an air gap crossed on a USB
stick.

`tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py` does four things:

1. **Export** refs and collaboration history to a directory, signed with your
   Ed25519 key. The export can be full or limited: some branches, some paths,
   metadata only, or leaving large files for later.
2. **Fetch** that directory from removable media or any static HTTP host. The
   fetch works in verified chunks, resumes after disconnects, crashes, and
   cancellation, and respects a data budget, a rate limit, and time windows.
3. **Import** it into a repository. Import checks the signature, the digests,
   and any missing objects before it changes anything. Refs then update in one
   transaction; diverged work is kept aside for review, never overwritten.
4. **Roll back** any import.

Issues, pull requests, discussions, and releases live as signed records under
`.forkmesh/` in the repository's branches (for example `forkmesh/pulls`).
Exporting the refs therefore carries the collaboration history with them.

The manifest is `forkmesh-offline-media-v1`, wrapped in the signed envelope
`forkmesh-offline-media-signed-v1`. A transfer checkpoint is
`forkmesh-offline-transfer-checkpoint-v1`, an import journal is
`forkmesh-offline-import-journal-v1`, and a replica advertisement is
`forkmesh-replica-scope-v1`.

## Start here: carry a repository on a USB stick

On the connected machine:

```sh
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py keygen ~/.forkmesh-offline.key   # prints your public key
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py export ~/src/project /media/usb/project-2026-09-14 \
  --signing-key ~/.forkmesh-offline.key --repository alice/project
```

Send the printed public key to the other side over any channel you trust
(read it aloud, put it on paper, or use a signed message). On the disconnected
machine:

```sh
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py verify /media/usb/project-2026-09-14 --trusted-key <public key>
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py import /media/usb/project-2026-09-14 ~/src/project \
  --trusted-key <public key>
```

Carry changes back the same way with that machine's own key. Next time, export
only what is new:

```sh
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py export ~/src/project /media/usb/project-2026-09-21 \
  --signing-key ~/.forkmesh-offline.key --since /media/usb/project-2026-09-14
```

An incremental export lists its `prerequisites` and the digest of the export
it builds on (`previousExport`). Import refuses it, and reports the missing
prerequisite commits, until the earlier export has been imported. If nothing
changed, `export --since` writes nothing.

## Fetch over a link that keeps dropping

Put the export directory on any static HTTP host that honours `Range`
requests, then fetch it:

```sh
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py fetch https://files.example.org/project-2026-09-14/ ./incoming \
  --rate 64k --budget 20M --schedule 22:00-06:00 --trusted-key <public key>
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py status ./incoming
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py import ./incoming ~/src/project --trusted-key <public key>
```

`SOURCE` can also be a local directory, such as a mounted share or a flaky
card reader. Read errors on local media are treated as disconnects.

How a fetch stays correct:

- **The manifest is fetched and verified first,** exactly once per transfer.
  It is stored next to the checkpoint and never requested again, so a metered
  link does not pay for it every session.
- **Chunks resume from the byte they stopped at.** Bytes are appended to
  `.forkmesh-transfer/chunks/NNNNNNNN.part` as they arrive. After a disconnect
  the next request starts at the first missing byte, so no byte is transferred
  twice.
- **A chunk counts only after its SHA-256 matches the signed manifest.** Only
  then is it renamed to `.done` and recorded in `checkpoint.json` (written
  atomically). If a digest is wrong, the whole chunk is fetched again; after 3
  failures on one chunk the fetch stops with `failed` / `integrity`. Every
  resume re-checks finished chunks on disk, so a checkpoint lost in a crash, or
  a chunk damaged on disk, costs at most that one chunk.
- **The bundle is assembled only when every chunk is verified,** and its
  whole-file digest must match before `repository.bundle` and the manifest
  appear in `DEST`. A partial directory can never be imported.
- **Retries back off** (0.5 s doubling to 30 s). Progress resets the retry
  count. `--retries N` consecutive failures with no progress pause the fetch
  with `link_down`; run the same command again later.
- **Cancel with Ctrl-C.** The current block is written, the checkpoint is saved,
  and the fetch exits paused with `cancelled`.
- `--restart` discards the checkpoint, for example when the source directory
  was replaced by a different export.

### Data budgets, rate, and schedules

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--budget SIZE` | Transfer at most SIZE bytes this run, then pause with `budget_exhausted`. The request is trimmed to the budget, so it never overshoots. |
| `--rate SIZE` | Average at most SIZE bytes per second. |
| `--schedule HH:MM-HH:MM` | Transfer only inside local-time windows. Windows may cross midnight, and the option may repeat. Outside a window the fetch pauses with `outside_schedule` before any request, and reports `nextWindowAt`. |
| `--wait` | Sleep until the next window instead of exiting. |

Sizes accept bytes or binary `k`, `M`, `G` suffixes (`64k`, `20M`, `1GiB`).

### Estimates and checkpoints

`status DEST` reads only the local checkpoint. It never contacts the source.
It reports `totalBytes`, `bytesOnDisk`, `remainingBytes`, chunk counts, percent
complete, and `etaSeconds` at the last session's measured rate. `fetch --json`
also returns `counters`:

| Counter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sessions`, `resumes` | Runs of this transfer, and runs that continued earlier progress. |
| `disconnects` | Reads that ended early. |
| `bytesTransferred` | Bundle bytes received over the link. With no integrity failures this equals the bundle size, however many disconnects happened. |
| `bytesResumed` | Bytes already on disk when a session started, which did not need fetching again. |
| `integrityFailures`, `retransferredBytes` | Chunks that failed their digest, and the bytes discarded with them. |
| `manifestBytes` | The one-time manifest download. |

## Limited exports and what they may claim

| Export option | Limitation code | What is left out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--metadata-only` | `metadata_only` | File contents, except collaboration records under `.forkmesh/`. Commits, trees, and refs travel. |
| `--path PATH` (repeatable) | `path_filter` | File contents outside PATH. `.forkmesh/` is always kept. |
| `--defer-blobs-over SIZE` | `deferred_large_objects` | File contents larger than SIZE. |
| `--ref GLOB` (repeatable) | `branch_filter` | Refs that match no glob. |
| _(detected on import)_ | `missing_objects` | Objects the repository references but does not hold. |

Every manifest carries a `replica` advertisement, derived only from the
selection:

- **`full`** — no limitation. Only a full replica sets `claimsFullAvailability: true`.
- **`filtered`** — at least one limitation, but not metadata-only.
- **`metadata-only`** — metadata only, possibly with other limitations.

The advertisement is part of the signed manifest, and `verify` recomputes it
from the selection. An export that claims more than its selection allows fails
verification, even when it is correctly signed.

Import refuses a limited export unless you pass `--allow-limited`. Before
recording any ref, it checks that no commit or tree object is missing. Left-out
file contents are stored as a Git partial clone: the pack is marked
`.promisor`, and `extensions.partialClone` is set to `forkmesh-offline`. Reading
a left-out file fails with Git's missing-object error rather than showing wrong
content.

```sh
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py replica ~/src/project --json
```

`replica REPO` prints what the repository may advertise. It combines the
recorded limitations with a live count of missing objects. A limited
repository keeps advertising its limitations until a complete full export (one
with no `--since`) is imported and no objects are missing.

When a copy reports that scope as `replicaScope` in the mirrors payload, the
[availability proof](availability-proof.md) classifies it as `observed` with
`limited_replica`, however fresh its evidence. It never counts toward a
quorum.

## Import, reconciliation, and rollback

Import verifies, in order: the envelope signature and the trusted key, the
manifest shape and replica advertisement, every chunk digest and the bundle
digest, the scope (`--allow-limited`), the object format, and the
prerequisites. Any failure exits `3` before any ref is written. It then
unpacks the objects with `git bundle unbundle` and checks that every commit and
tree the refs need is present. For a full export, every file's contents must be
present too. Only then does it decide each ref:

| Decision | When | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create` | The ref does not exist locally. | Created. |
| `fast_forward` | The local ref is an ancestor of the incoming one. | Moved forward. |
| `unchanged` | Same object. | Nothing. |
| `local_ahead` | The incoming ref is an ancestor of the local one. | Local kept. |
| `conflict` | History diverged, or a tag points elsewhere. | Local kept; incoming saved at `refs/forkmesh-offline/conflicts/<exportId>/…`. |
| `checked_out` | A fast-forward of the branch checked out in a working tree. | Local kept; incoming saved aside so you can `git merge --ff-only` it. |

Refs missing from the export are never deleted. Every change, including the
refs saved aside, is applied in one `git update-ref --stdin` transaction. A
journal is written first to
`<git-dir>/forkmesh-offline/imports/<importId>.json`. The journal records the
signer, the manifest digest, every decision, and each old and new value.
Import exits `5` when anything was saved aside.

```sh
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py rollback ~/src/project <importId>
```

Rollback reverses the transaction, verifying each ref still holds the value the
import wrote. If anything moved since, it changes nothing and exits `3`.
Rolling back twice is a no-op. Objects that were unpacked stay in the object
store; they are unreferenced and harmless.

## Provenance and trust

- Manifests are canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace). The signature is
  Ed25519 over `forkmesh-offline-media-v1\n` followed by the manifest's SHA-256
  hex. Signing uses `cryptography` when it is installed, otherwise a pure-Python
  RFC 8032 implementation. Verification is pure Python, so it needs no
  dependencies on an air-gapped machine.
- `verify` and `import` report the signer's public key and whether it matched a
  `--trusted-key`. Import accepts an unpinned signature only with
  `--allow-unpinned`, which still requires a valid signature.
- `fetch` checks the signature before it downloads any bundle bytes. With
  `--trusted-key` it also refuses an untrusted signer.
- The signing key file is a base64url 32-byte seed, created with mode `0600`.
  Keep it off the removable media.

## Telemetry

`export`, `fetch`, `import`, and `rollback` take `--telemetry FILE` and append
one `forkmesh-offline-telemetry-v1` JSON line per run. The line holds the
outcome, the pause reason, the counters above, conflict and changed-ref counts,
omitted bytes, and scope. It never holds repository names, URLs, ref names, or
keys. Nothing is sent anywhere. These lines are the evidence for resume
success, bytes saved (`bytesResumed` plus export `omittedBytes`), integrity
failures, and reconciliation conflicts.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Done. |
| `2` | Usage error or unreadable input. |
| `3` | Verification, integrity, or missing-object failure; nothing was changed. |
| `4` | Paused with the checkpoint kept (`budget_exhausted`, `outside_schedule`, `cancelled`, `link_down`); run the same command to resume. |
| `5` | Imported, with conflicts saved aside for review. |

## Failure paths and recovery

| Situation | Result | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Link drops mid-chunk, repeatedly | Resumes from the next missing byte | Automatic |
| Link down longer than `--retries` | `4` / `link_down` | Re-run `fetch` |
| Corrupted bytes on the link | Chunk re-fetched, `integrityFailures` counted | Automatic |
| Source export replaced or persistently corrupt | `failed` / `integrity` | `fetch --restart` |
| Crash or power loss during fetch | Checkpoint and chunks re-checked on the next run | Re-run `fetch` |
| Host ignores `Range` | `3`, no bundle bytes accepted | Use a host with `Range` support, or copy the directory |
| Tampered manifest, bundle, or wrong signer | `3`, repository untouched | Obtain a fresh export and confirm the key |
| Incremental export without its base | `3`, prerequisites listed | Import the earlier export first |
| Diverged branches or moved tags | `5`, local kept, incoming aside | Review and merge from `refs/forkmesh-offline/conflicts/…` |
| Wrong import | — | `rollback REPO IMPORT_ID` |

## Not covered yet

- Hosts do not yet publish `replicaScope` in their catalog records. The Worker
  passes it through and the availability proof honours it when present.
- Ref deletions are not propagated.
- Discovering other hosts on a local network is handled by the desktop app's
  LAN mesh. This tool moves data between them once you know where they are.
- The desktop and mobile apps do not yet expose these commands.

## Evidence

- `app/tests/test_offline_sync.py` runs against real Git repositories and a
  fault-injecting HTTP host. It covers repeated disconnects with byte-exact
  no-duplicate accounting, restarts under data budgets, lost checkpoints,
  corrupted link bytes, a link that stays down, hosts that ignore `Range`,
  cancellation, schedules, rate limits, all four limited modes and their
  advertisements, incremental prerequisites, conflicts, checked-out branches,
  rollback refusal, exit codes, and count-only telemetry.
- The suite runs in the `offline-sync-conformance` quality gate and in the
  `Collaboration conformance` workflow on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
- `conformance/availability-proof/v1/fixture.json` case
  `limited-replicas-never-verified` pins the availability-proof behaviour.

pages.description: ForkMesh makes roadmap and investment decisions from the KPIs in the versioned outcome metric dictionary. The dictionary names every KPI's numerator, denominator, window, owner…
pages.markdown:
# Monthly outcome review

ForkMesh makes roadmap and investment decisions from the KPIs in the
[versioned outcome metric dictionary](outcome-metrics.json). The dictionary
names every KPI's numerator, denominator, window, owner, privacy class,
collection method, consent basis, opt-out, retention, minimum cell size,
freshness limit, coverage, baseline, target, and source. This page is the
monthly record template. It never creates a second definition for a metric.

The [weekly activation-to-revenue scorecard](activation-revenue-scorecard.md)
covers the `weekly` metrics. This review covers every metric, including the
`monthly` community, migration, availability, and hosted-adoption KPIs.

## Decision cadence

| Cadence | Forum | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weekly | Activation-to-revenue scorecard | One action for the next week. Definitions do not change mid-period. |
| Monthly | This review, after the UTC month is complete | Every KPI with freshness and confidence, plus decisions, experiments, and roadmap changes. |
| Quarterly | The monthly review that closes a quarter | Adopt, keep, or retire targets. Publish any dictionary version change. |

A baseline is `unmeasured` until a recorded review reports a `COMPLETE` value
for it. A target stays `to-be-set` until a review adopts it and the dictionary
names that review as its `source`. The dictionary validator rejects an invented
baseline or target.

## Privacy rules

Measurement must never become required surveillance.

- **Consent.** Product analytics is opt-in and off by default. Attribution sets
  no cookie for DNT/GPC visitors or configured skip countries. Every other KPI
  uses records the service already keeps to operate, closed accounting
  ledgers, synthetic probes, or voluntary operator registrations.
- **Self-hosting stays invisible.** A self-hosted node never has to report
  anything. Operator-reported and hosted-only KPIs have `lower-bound`
  coverage; they are never backfilled or inferred for nodes that stay silent.
- **Minimization.** Observation files carry counts, totals, coverage, and
  segment labels only. `tools/outcome_metrics.py review` rejects email, IP,
  account, user, owner, author, actor, session, customer, subscription,
  repository, path, URL, referrer, and name fields, and any email or IPv4
  value.
- **Aggregation.** When a segment is smaller than the metric's
  `minimumCellSize`, it is suppressed. If only one segment is suppressed, the
  next smallest is suppressed too, so the other segments cannot be subtracted
  from the total to reveal it. A value computed over a population smaller than
  the minimum is `publishable: false` and stays in the internal record.
- **Retention.** Raw sources keep the retention named on each metric. Daily
  and boundary exports that exist only to build a monthly KPI are deleted once
  the month's review is recorded. The review record holds aggregates only.
- **Opt-out.** Each metric names its opt-out. Removing an attribution session,
  withdrawing analytics consent, self-hosting a repository, or merging on your
  own node never degrades the product.
- **No deanonymization.** A record never quotes a person, repository, pull,
  ticket, or customer. It also never cross-tabulates small segments to
  explain a change. Interview and support evidence is linked by sanitized
  reference only.

## Prepare the review

1. Validate the dictionary the review will cite:

   ```sh
   python3 tools/outcome_metrics.py validate-dictionary
   ```

2. Build one aggregate observation file for the month. Collect every source to
   exhaustion. Record the source total beside the collected total, and set
   `continuationExhausted` only after the last page:

   ```json
   {
     "schema": "forkmesh-outcome-observations-v1",
     "dictionarySchema": "forkmesh-outcome-metric-dictionary-v2",
     "dictionaryVersion": 2,
     "cadence": "monthly",
     "periodStart": "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z",
     "periodEnd": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z",
     "generatedAt": "2026-10-03T09:00:00Z",
     "observations": [
       {
         "metric": "repository_availability",
         "numerator": 1293120,
         "denominator": 1296000,
         "sourceTotal": 30,
         "collectedTotal": 30,
         "continuationExhausted": true,
         "coverage": 1.0,
         "dataCutAt": "2026-10-01T01:00:00Z",
         "segments": [{ "label": "clone", "value": 646560 }]
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

3. Produce the report:

   ```sh
   python3 tools/outcome_metrics.py review --input /path/to/month.json
   ```

   Every metric in scope appears in the report. A metric without an
   observation is `UNKNOWN`, never zero. Freshness is `stale` when the data
   cut is older than the metric's `freshnessHours`. Confidence follows the
   dictionary's `confidencePolicy`:

   | Confidence | Meaning |
   | --- | --- |
   | `high` | Reconciled, exhausted, fresh, measured coverage at least 0.95, and full coverage class |
   | `medium` | Reconciled and fresh, but partial coverage or a partial/lower-bound class |
   | `low` | Reconciled but stale, or measured coverage below 0.5 (`PARTIAL`) |
   | `unknown` | Missing, unreconciled, not exhausted, or cut before the window ended (`UNKNOWN`) |

## Reconcile with billing and operations samples

Before the review is circulated, sample at least one source row family per
collection method and record the result:

- **Billing.** Reconcile `paid_conversion`, `retention`, and `gross_margin` to
  the provider ledger and invoices with `python3 tools/unit_economics.py report
  --input /path/to/period.json`. A missing invoice is a blocker, not a zero.
- **Operations.** Compare one day of `repository_availability` with the
  `/status` history and the status alert log. Compare one day of
  `independent_mirror_nodes` with the `/status` mirror roster. Compare
  `successful_migration` with a `finished_at`-bounded row count. The
  authenticated migration-metrics view only shows the latest 1,000 runs and is
  not a monthly population.
- **Synthetic.** Attach the latest stock Git conformance report for the same
  month.

A failed sample turns the affected metric `UNKNOWN` for the month. Record the
reason; do not adjust the value by hand.

## Copy for each month

Store completed records as `www/docs/strategy/outcome-reviews/YYYY-MM.md`.
Record only aggregate values.

```text
Month: YYYY-MM (YYYY-MM-01T00:00:00Z through YYYY-MM-01T00:00:00Z)
Generated at: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ
Dictionary: forkmesh-outcome-metric-dictionary-v2 / version 2
Owner sign-off: Growth=<name>; Product=<name>; Community=<name>; Infrastructure=<name>; Finance=<name>; Support=<name>; Privacy=<name>
Data cuts: hosted=<timestamp>; analytics=<timestamp>; finance=<timestamp>; synthetic=<timestamp>
Reconciliation samples: billing=<pass|fail + reference>; operations=<pass|fail + reference>; synthetic=<report reference>
Quality state: COMPLETE | PARTIAL | UNKNOWN
```

| Stage | Metric id | Value | Baseline | Target | Freshness | Confidence | Coverage | Note |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Acquisition | `landing_activation` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `anonymous_clone` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `signup` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `first_mirror` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `contribution` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `managed_service_qualification` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `paid_conversion` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `retention` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Product | `feature_adoption` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `support_load` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `infrastructure_cost` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `gross_margin` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `successful_migration` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Community | `first_contribution` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Community | `active_maintainers` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Product | `hosted_service_adoption` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Availability | `repository_availability` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Availability | `independent_mirror_nodes` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

```text
Decisions:
- <decision> — evidence: <metric ids> — owner: <role> — revisit: YYYY-MM
Experiments:
- <hypothesis> — metric: <id> — guardrail: <id> — start/stop: YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD — result: <pending|kept|reverted>
Roadmap changes:
- <issue or milestone> — change: <added|reprioritized|dropped> — because: <metric ids>
Definition changes proposed for the next dictionary version:
- <metric id> — change — reason
Exports deleted after this review: <list of export references>
```

## Changing a definition

Definitions change only between periods. A change updates
`www/docs/outcome-metrics.json`, increments `version`, appends a `changelog`
entry, and updates the dictionary line in both templates. It does not rewrite
earlier records. An earlier record keeps the version it cites, and a
comparison across versions is labelled as not comparable.

## Failure and recovery

- **A source is unavailable or unreconciled.** The metric is `UNKNOWN` for the
  period. Record the reason, and do not carry the prior value forward.
- **A data cut is stale.** Re-cut the source and regenerate the report. If a
  fresh cut cannot be produced, publish at `low` confidence as `PARTIAL`.
- **An export or record contains an identifier.** Delete it, regenerate it
  from the aggregate observation file, and log the incident for privacy
  review. The review tool refuses such input, so a record with an identifier
  was assembled by hand.
- **A dictionary version is wrong.** Revert the JSON change, re-run
  `validate-dictionary`, and regenerate any record that cited the bad version.
- **A daily or boundary export was missed.** The affected monthly KPI
  (`first_contribution`, `active_maintainers`, `hosted_service_adoption`,
  `independent_mirror_nodes`, or availability days beyond the 30-day status
  retention) is `UNKNOWN` for the month. Resume exports the next day; do not
  reconstruct history from cumulative tables.

## Linked automated evidence

- Dictionary validation, consent/coverage rules, baseline/target honesty,
  freshness, confidence, suppression, identifier rejection, and CLI failure
  paths: `app/tests/test_outcome_metrics.py`
- Weekly scorecard rows, source locators, and pagination to exhaustion:
  `app/tests/test_activation_revenue_scorecard.py` and
  `app/tests/test_attribution.py`
- Closed-period revenue, cost, and margin: `app/tests/test_unit_economics.py`
- Consent-gated product analytics: `app/tests/test_first_party_analytics.py`
- Migration completion and setup percentiles:
  `app/tests/test_repository_migration.py`
- Status samples and history: `app/tests/test_status_page.py`

Automated checks prove the contract and the report arithmetic. They do not
replace a recorded month with real data cuts, billing and operations samples,
owner sign-off, or privacy review.

pages.markdown:
# Planned plugins

These pages list the features we plan to move out of the ForkMesh core and
into optional Marketplace packages. They come from the repo-wide plugin
decomposition audit in issue #677, which looked at 1,742 tracked code files
(686 of them tests). Nothing here is shipped yet. Each package family gets its
own issue once it is scheduled.

Here, **plugin** means a `.fmpkg` package with a manifest: it declares its
entrypoints and permissions, owns its own state, removes everything when
uninstalled, and has migrations that can be rolled back. It does not mean a
library loaded at runtime.

The audit comes in two modes:

| Mode | Page | What it answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stingy | [Plugin shortlist](shortlist.md) | What we recommend building: 12 package families and 10 host socket families, plus the test a candidate must pass, when to stop, and the boundaries that stay in core. |
| Generous | [Plugin opportunity inventory](opportunities.md) | What could be built: 316 candidate packages across desktop, App, World, mobile, mirror, CLI/MCP/operations, web, content, and portable skills, plus the 15 package boundaries that already exist and 44 proposed host sockets. |

Use the shortlist to choose what to build next. Use the inventory to check
whether an idea has already been considered, and which host socket it would
need.

## Next step

Start with one family. The World element trio is the cheapest. Land its socket
with install, activate, uninstall, upgrade, rollback, and crash-restart tests
before building a general version.

The Marketplace package format and lifecycle are described in
[`marketplace/README.md`](../../../marketplace/README.md). The per-candidate
keep-or-extract review from issue #653 is
[`docs/marketplace-extraction-inventory.md`](../../../docs/marketplace-extraction-inventory.md).

pages.markdown:
# Planned plugins: opportunity inventory

> **Planned, not shipped.** This page is the generous mode of the plugin
> decomposition audit tracked in issue #677. Rows are candidates, not
> commitments; see [Planned plugins](README.md) for both modes.

This is a deliberately generous inventory of code and content that could move
into ForkMesh Marketplace packages. It is not a promise that every row should
be extracted. The list includes both small, independently useful packages and
larger alternative bundles so product and creator experiments are not ruled out
too early.

For the conservative recommendation, see the
[stingy plugin shortlist](shortlist.md).

The tables contain 316 candidate package rows, plus 15 package boundaries that
already exist and 44 proposed host sockets. Bundle rows deliberately overlap
their smaller components.

In this document, **plugin** means a manifest-backed ForkMesh `.fmpkg`, not a
random dynamically loaded library. A real extraction must keep the Marketplace
lifecycle contract: explicit entrypoints and permissions, validated content,
package-owned state, complete teardown, and reversible migrations.

## Audit coverage

The 2026-09-01 audit mechanically inventoried all 4,926 tracked repository
files, including 1,742 code-like files and 686 tests. It reviewed the functional
boundaries under `app/`, `desktop/`, `marketplace/`, `mobile/`, `server/`,
`tools/`, `world/`, `www/`, and the portable `.forkmesh/` skills and shortcuts.
Generated assets and test fixtures informed the inventory but are not proposed
as standalone plugins merely because they are separate files.

The strongest evidence is already in the source layout:

- Desktop product surfaces are split across `MainWindow*.cpp` files and focused
  stores/runtimes, but most still compile into the core application.
- App features are split into route modules such as `notes.py`, `calendar_api.py`,
  `activitypub.py`, `security_scan_ingest.py`, and `repository_migration.py`.
- World features already have separable backend modules, front-end modules, and
  self-contained element implementations.
- Mobile services and screens are separated, and the owned Git engine is
  already its own module in each native app (`FMGit` on iOS, the
  `nativeapp.git` package on Android).
- Headless operations are mostly one-purpose Python tools or focused Go server
  modules.
- The test suite names many coherent capabilities that are less obvious from
  navigation alone: direct messages, repository migrations, referral controls,
  reward scheduling, workshops, QA boards, satellites, private mirrors, and
  provider-specific agent transports.

Readiness labels used below:

- **Now** — an existing host socket or package adapter is close to sufficient.
- **Socket** — a good package boundary, but the host needs a neutral extension
  socket before extraction.
- **Content** — primarily declarative content, a theme, an agent/skill, or a
  World object; it should need little or no privileged runtime code.
- **Guarded** — plausible only as a signed first-party or administrator-approved
  package with narrow capabilities and fail-closed host policy.
- **Bundle** — a useful collection of smaller candidates; it intentionally
  overlaps atomic rows.

## Already represented by packages: finish and preserve the boundary

These are not future ideas: their manifests or content already live under
`marketplace/packages/`. They should be treated as reference extractions and
expanded without adding package-id branches back to the hosts.

| Package | Current package surface | Generous follow-on variants |
