## Portable skills, shortcuts, policies, and templates

The checked-in `.forkmesh/skills` and `.forkmesh/shortcuts` are natural package
content. They should remain reviewable text with declared capabilities; a skill
must never silently acquire more authority than the installing user or agent.

| Candidate | Package content | Readiness |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CFO payout operations | Existing guarded payout skill, workflow references, and audit checklist | Content |
| Discord quality intake | Existing bug-intake skill, dedupe policy, reporter credit, and result schema | Content |
| Code-review skill pack | Review shortcut, security checks, severity rubric, and report template | Content |
| Bug-triage skill pack | Bug-report checks, reproduction template, dedupe, and issue creation | Content |
| UI-stall remediation | Stall evidence collection, Qt diagnostics, profiling, and safe fixes | Content |
| Qt performance pack | Performance budgets, measurement shortcut, and regression checklist | Content |
| Documentation maintainer | Docs refresh, link validation, changelog/blog generation, and ownership map | Content |
| Release-readiness pack | Critical tests, packaging, app-store checklist, signatures, and rollout | Content |
| Mobile release pack | Existing mobile advance shortcut plus Android/iOS validation workflows | Content |
| Security response pack | Report triage, disclosure workflow, scan evidence, and escalation policy | Content |
| Feature-removal pack | Usage evidence, dependency audit, migration, deprecation, and cleanup checklist | Content |
| Repository cleanup pack | Redundant code, stale comments, temporary files, and verification shortcuts | Content |
| YC/news launch pack | Existing launch-readiness shortcut, evidence checklist, and campaign templates | Content |
| Contributor reward pack | Reward validation, reconciliation, public receipt, and non-custody policy | Content |
| Mirror operator skill pack | Provision, health check, failover proof, recovery, and incident templates | Content |
| Project template pack | Portable issue, pull, discussion, project, release, and workflow templates | Content |
| Organization operating pack | Roles, team structure, recurring tasks, calendars, notes, and dashboards | Content |
| Agent persona pack | Teammate definition, model routing, skills, schedule, and collaboration policy | Content |

## Host sockets needed to unlock the inventory

Creating these neutral sockets is higher leverage than adding more
`builtin:<feature>` branches. Socket names are proposals, not schema commitments.

| Proposed socket | Capability exposed by the host | Unlocks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `desktop.page` | Lifecycle-owned native page with declarative navigation | Most desktop feature pages |
| `desktop.repo-panel` | Bounded repository context and embedded panel | Stats, security, pulls, project and release panels |
| `desktop.repo-action` | Explicit user-triggered repository action with scoped inputs | Import, migration, sync, review, publish |
| `desktop.log-source` | Register category, poll/push records, filter page, teardown | Sentry-style observability providers |
| `desktop.chat-provider` | Channels, messages, sends, presence, credentials, teardown | Discord, Slack, Matrix, custom chat |
| `desktop.agent-provider` | Models, session start/resume/steer, usage, transcript events | Codex, Claude, Ollama, remote agents |
| `desktop.scm-provider` | Read status/diffs and execute approved SCM operations | Git workflows and future SCM backends |
| `desktop.composer-tool` | Add bounded attachments or transformations after user action | Capture, OCR, voice, templates |
| `desktop.status-widget` | Small status/health/usage surface | Mirrors, deployments, agents, budgets |
| `desktop.control-panel` | Administrator-gated service configuration and actions | Node, mirror, tunnel, server packages |
| `dashboard.repo-panel` | Repository-scoped web panel and safe API | Security, analytics, releases, imports |
| `dashboard.profile-panel` | Account/profile-scoped web panel | Badges, contributions, memberships |
| `worker.cron` | Named scheduled callback with time/resource budget | Digests, reminders, monitors, sync jobs |
| `worker.event` | Typed internal event subscription | Notifications, badges, analytics, bots |
| `worker.webhook` | Verified provider webhook with package-specific secret handle | Payments, chat, email, CI providers |
| `worker.queue` | Bounded asynchronous job consumer with retries and dead-letter state | Imports, migrations, scans, agent jobs |
| `worker.websocket` | Scoped realtime endpoint without arbitrary namespace access | Chat providers, meetings, live status |
| `worker.durable-object` | Explicit class/binding allocation and migration lifecycle | Rooms, sessions, rate limits, coordination |
| `worker.outbound` | Existing exact-origin outbound adapter made consistently available | Provider connectors and public feeds |
| `worker.notification` | Provider-neutral delivery request | APNS, web push, email, chat notifications |
| `worker.payment-provider` | Read/verify/entitlement contract without private-key custody | Patreon, chain indexers |
| `worker.audit-sink` | Redacted typed audit events | SIEM and compliance packages |
| `world.object` | Bounded scene object with placement and teardown | Existing elements and virtual goods |
| `world.panel` | Safe 2D/3D panel with data access and click handling | Chat, Discord, notes, status boards |
| `world.activity` | Enter/exit/update lifecycle for rides, games, meetings, workshops | Campfire, gym, swings, events |
| `world.building` | Bounded geometry, surfaces, portals, floors, and access rules | Offices, venues, repository districts |
| `world.avatar-part` | Faces, clothing, accessories, material and compatibility metadata | Avatar creator economy |
| `world.animation` | Named clips, state transitions, accessibility metadata | Avatar and object animations |
| `world.audio` | Licensed audio assets and bounded spatial playback | Ambience, radio, sound packs |
| `world.data-source` | Privacy-filtered snapshot subscription | Feeds, mirror state, repo graphs, events |
| `world.admin-tool` | Role-gated diagnostics/moderation action | Infrastructure and moderation consoles |
| `mobile.tab` | Lifecycle-owned tab/screen with route/deep-link contract | Chat, agents, orgs, local repos |
| `mobile.repo-action` | Explicit repository operation in an isolate with cancellation | Clone, commit, publish, PR |
| `mobile.share-target` | Approved external share payload to a selected composer | Issues, notes, chat, agents |
| `mobile.agent-provider` | Provider-neutral mobile session contract | Local and hosted agent adapters |
| `mirror.sync-adapter` | Fetch/catalog source and integrity proof contract | Alternative repository sources |
| `mirror.transport` | Direct endpoint lifecycle and health contract | HTTPS, SSH, tunnel transports |
| `mirror.repository-hook` | Bounded push/fetch/collaboration event | Refresh, indexing, notifications |
| `cli.command` | Namespaced subcommand with explicit files/network permissions | Maintainer and operator tools |
| `mcp.toolset` | Independently grantable MCP tools and resources | Code, notes, chat, issue, release tools |
| `release.publisher` | Artifact read, sign request, upload, and publication receipt | Hosting/provider release adapters |
| `content.skill` | Reviewable agent instructions plus required capability declarations | Skill packs and teammate behaviors |
| `content.shortcut` | Parameterized prompt/workflow/command with safe host substitution | Maintainer shortcuts |
| `content.template` | Repository/org/project templates with preview and merge policy | Project and organization packs |

## Boundaries that should stay in the trusted host

Being generous about candidates does not mean turning the application into an
unbounded native-code loader. The following enforcement points should remain
host-owned even when a package supplies UI, policy, or provider behavior:

- Manifest, signature, digest, provenance, permission, and dependency
  validation.
- Install/uninstall transactions, quarantine, migration ledger, export, purge,
  and rollback.
- Secret storage and opaque credential handles; packages should never enumerate
  unrelated secrets.
- Account authentication, session validation, CSRF/CORS/origin enforcement,
  role checks, and audit-record integrity.
- Identity private keys, owner encryption keys, wallet private keys, and the
  final user-presence/arming step for signatures or payments.
- Git path validation, object-integrity checks, repository locks, worktree
  quarantine, command allowlists, and process sandbox enforcement.
- Route prefix allocation, exact outbound-origin enforcement, request/body
  limits, rate limits, and Worker/DO resource budgets.
- Native widget ownership, destruction, callback revocation, thread/process
  cancellation, and crash containment.
- World triangle/draw-call budgets, asset limits, collision bounds, interaction
  ownership, accessibility rules, and complete scene teardown.
- Mobile isolate/resource limits, secure storage, platform permission prompts,
  background-execution policy, and app-store disclosure enforcement.

## Suggested extraction order

1. Finish converting existing `builtin:*` packages to neutral contribution
   sockets and use them as contract tests.
2. Add `desktop.page`, `desktop.repo-panel`, `desktop.repo-action`,
   `desktop.agent-provider`, and `desktop.chat-provider`; then extract low-risk
   pages before runners, signers, or control planes.
3. Add Worker cron, event, webhook, queue, and notification sockets; extract
   provider adapters such as Patreon, APNS, Discord, and analytics.
4. Generalize the existing World element loader into object, panel, activity,
   building, avatar, animation, and audio sockets; move the three checked-in
   elements first.
5. Add mobile tab/repository-action/provider sockets only after lifecycle,
   app-store disclosure, secure-storage, and background-task policies are
   enforceable by the host.
6. Package standalone tools and portable skills early, because their inputs,
   outputs, and permissions are easier to review than arbitrary in-process
   native extensions.
7. Leave identity, authentication, signature arming, migration enforcement,
   sandboxing, route allocation, and integrity checks in the host permanently.

pages.title: Planned plugins: stingy shortlist
pages.description: Planned, not shipped. This page is the conservative mode of the plugin decomposition audit tracked in issue #677. Each family becomes its own issue when it is scheduled; until…
pages.markdown:
# Planned plugins: stingy shortlist

> **Planned, not shipped.** This page is the conservative mode of the plugin
> decomposition audit tracked in issue #677. Each family becomes its own issue
> when it is scheduled; until then the code stays where it is. See
> [Planned plugins](README.md) for both modes.

This is the stingy counterpart to the deliberately broad
[plugin opportunity inventory](opportunities.md). It recommends only
package boundaries that are optional to the core ForkMesh promise, cohesive,
independently useful, removable without damaging repository state, and
realistic to expose through a narrow host capability.

The shortlist contains 12 package families. Some families can publish more
than one artifact, but they should share one host contract rather than cause a
new socket for every implementation.

## Admission test

A candidate belongs here only when every answer is **yes**:

1. Can ForkMesh still browse, collaborate on, mirror, and preserve repositories
   when the package is absent?
2. Does the code have one clear owner, lifecycle, configuration surface, and
   reason to version independently?
3. Can install and uninstall be tested without rewriting or orphaning user Git
   history, identity, collaboration records, or security state?
4. Can the host expose a narrow capability instead of arbitrary filesystem,
   process, network, database, or secret access?
5. Is there a credible second implementation, provider, content pack, or user
   group that benefits from choosing whether to install it?

If any answer becomes “no” during implementation, keep the feature in core.

## The shortlist

| Priority | Package family | Existing code to move | Why it passes the high bar | Required host boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | World element trio | `world/public/world/elements/status-obelisk.js`, `aurora-beacon.js`, and `orbit-sculpture.js` | They already implement self-contained manifests/builders, are cosmetic, and can disappear without affecting protocol state. Publish separately if creator ownership or pricing differs. | Existing World entrypoint generalized as `world.object` |
| 2 | Portable operations skills | `.forkmesh/skills/*.skill` and the review, bug, docs, performance, release, and mirror shortcuts under `.forkmesh/shortcuts/` | Reviewable text content has a small attack surface, versions independently, and is useful only to selected teams or agents. | `content.skill` and `content.shortcut`; capabilities remain host-enforced |
| 3 | Analytics (extracted: `marketplace/packages/analytics`) | `www/public/analytics.js` and its consent/event tests | Analytics is optional and should uninstall to zero collection; the first-party package replaced the third-party provider. | `web.analytics-provider` with an event allowlist, consent state, exact origin, and teardown |
| 4 | Patreon membership adapter | `app/src/patreon.py`, `app/src/patreon_handler.py`, related dashboard UI, migrations, and tests | OAuth, webhooks, reconciliation, and provider-owned records form one replaceable integration; ForkMesh membership semantics remain host-owned. | `worker.webhook` plus a narrow `membership.provider` contract and opaque secret handles |
| 5 | APNS notification adapter | `app/src/apns.py`, mobile push/deep-link services, device-token delivery code, and tests | Apple delivery is platform/provider-specific; notification creation, preferences, and unread state can remain core. | `worker.notification-provider` with opaque credentials, bounded payloads, receipts, and token purge |
| 6 | Codex agent adapter | `CodexAppServerSession`, Codex transcript styling, model discovery, usage reporting, and provider protocol | Provider behavior changes independently and users may choose another agent. Worktrees, sandboxing, approvals, and repository mutation stay in the desktop host. | `desktop.agent-provider`; no raw shell or unrestricted worktree handle |
| 7 | Claude Code agent adapter | `ClaudeStreamSession`, `ClaudeSessionScan`, resume identity, transcript view, and IDE bridge | It is a second implementation of the same provider contract and has provider-specific transport/transcript behavior. | The same `desktop.agent-provider` socket used by Codex |
| 8 | Repository statistics panel | `RepoStatsStore`, size/language/activity views, and their tests | It is read-mostly, nonessential, computationally bounded, and naturally competes with other analytics panels. | `desktop.repo-panel` with immutable repository snapshots and cache quota |
| 9 | Developer diagnostics panel | `NodeDiagnostics`, `SystemStats`, `StartupTrace`, `RestartTiming`, runtime diagnostics, and performance tests | Operators and developers need it; ordinary users do not. It reads bounded telemetry and can be removed without losing product data. | `desktop.diagnostics-panel`; crash uploads and destructive actions are excluded |
| 10 | Git conformance toolkit | `tools/git_conformance.py`, conformance fixtures, generated compatibility report logic, and focused tests | It is a standalone verifier with explicit inputs/outputs, useful to mirror operators and Git implementers but unnecessary at runtime. | `cli.command` with disposable-directory, process, time, and output limits |
| 11 | Live sky and satellites | `world/src/world_satellites.py`, `world/public/world/world-sky.js`, satellite snapshot migration, assets, and tests | This is an optional visual/data experience with clear resource budgets and no role in repository correctness. Split sky styling from live satellite data only if each remains useful alone. | `world.object` plus read-only `world.data-source` with draw-call, triangle, request, and update-rate budgets |

## Finish the boundaries already started

Do this before inventing more package types. These are existing packages, not
new shortlist entries:

- Move Calendar, Notes, and Tasks package-specific Worker behavior out of
  `builtin:*` paths and behind the same neutral contribution discovery used by
  package-owned Worker modules.
- Keep CRM, Marketing, and Competitor data schemas, exports, purges, navigation,
  and API routes entirely package-owned.
- Consolidate desktop, organization OAuth, bug-intake, and World-panel Discord
  behavior behind the existing Discord package instead of creating parallel
  core and package implementations.
- Keep Sentry as the contract test for an uninstallable desktop log provider;
  do not add another observability vendor until it uses the same neutral socket.
- Keep X and Reddit boards as the contract tests for World package placement,
  bounded data snapshots, click permissions, and complete scene teardown.
- Replace package-specific `builtin:<feature>` checks with contribution sockets;
  a package manifest must be sufficient for discovery.

## Only ten new socket families

The broad inventory proposes many possible sockets. The stingy plan adds only
the following, and only when the first package using each is ready:

| Socket | Minimum contract |
| --- | --- |
| `world.object` | Package-owned build, placement, bounds, budget declaration, interaction registration, and teardown |
| `world.data-source` | Read-only normalized snapshots, exact origins, size/update limits, backoff, and cache purge |
| `content.skill` / `content.shortcut` | Reviewable content, declared required capabilities, parameters, provenance, and no authority escalation |
| `web.analytics-provider` | Consent gate, fixed event schema, exact origin, no repository content, and uninstall disablement |
| `worker.webhook` | Provider signature verification, bounded body, event allowlist, idempotency, secret handle, and delivery audit |
| `membership.provider` | External-customer mapping and entitlement evidence; plan policy and authorization remain core |
| `worker.notification-provider` | Bounded notification request, opaque provider credential, delivery receipt, token lifecycle, and rate limit |
| `desktop.agent-provider` | Model/session/transcript/usage protocol; host owns approvals, sandbox, worktree, Git, cancellation, and secrets |
| `desktop.repo-panel` / `desktop.diagnostics-panel` | Read-only bounded snapshots, navigation lifecycle, cache quota, refresh, and widget teardown |
| `cli.command` | Explicit executable, arguments, input roots, output schema, timeout, process policy, and disposable workspace |

The paired names in two rows are related specializations of one underlying
host mechanism; they do not justify separate arbitrary-code runtimes.

## Keep these in core

The following broad-inventory ideas fail the stingy admission test or sit below
an enforcement boundary. They may expose data or actions to packages, but their
authoritative implementation should remain host-owned:

- Account authentication, sessions, password recovery, portable identity,
  device trust, private keys, room keys, and signature arming.
- Git object parsing, repository locks, ref validation, worktree quarantine,
  clone/fetch/push correctness, and the mobile owned Git engine.
- Mirror eligibility, signed health, source authority, integrity matching,
  stable clone routing, the direct HTTPS gateway, and the SSH authorization
  broker.
- Issue, discussion, pull, review, merge, project, release, and portable record
  semantics. Optional panels can extend them, but packages must not redefine
  their source-of-truth format.
- Permission evaluation, organization roles, security restrictions, audit-log
  integrity, moderation enforcement, and abuse/rate-limit policy.
- Marketplace manifest/signature verification, dependency resolution,
  installation transactions, migration ledger, quarantine, export, purge,
  rollback, and route allocation.
- Wallet custody, payout arming, transaction signing, reward settlement, and
  financial authorization. A package may display public data or submit a
  narrowly scoped request, never control the trust boundary.
- Native process sandboxing, agent worktree ownership, VM isolation, command
  allowlists, and final approval for repository mutations.
- Core chat encryption and membership enforcement. Provider packages may bridge
  messages only through a scoped, auditable host API.
- World renderer ownership, movement/collision rules, frame and triangle
  budgets, accessibility policy, and asset teardown enforcement.
- The base repository explorer, source-control workspace, issue tracker, pull
  review, chat, notifications, settings, and onboarding. They are central
  product surfaces, not optional Marketplace purchases.

## Stop rules

Do not add a candidate from the broad inventory to this shortlist until all of
the following exist in the same change or an accepted prerequisite:

- A second plausible implementation or a clear group of users who want the
  feature absent.
- A neutral socket with no package IDs or provider names in host code.
- A permission list that does not collapse to “arbitrary code,” “all network,”
  “all repositories,” or “all secrets.”
- Install, activate, deactivate, uninstall, reinstall, upgrade, rollback, and
  crash/restart tests.
- Package-owned settings/cache/data plus tested export and purge behavior.
- Resource budgets and cancellation for network, process, database, rendering,
  or model work.
- A documented degraded state when the provider, package, or external service
  is unavailable.

This smaller plan intentionally leaves most of the broad inventory in core
until real demand and a reusable capability boundary prove otherwise.

pages.title: ForkMesh protocol suite
pages.description: Suite version: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Status: candidate — not yet stable; see Stable release gate.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh protocol suite

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Status: **candidate** — not yet stable; see
[Stable release gate](#stable-release-gate).

This suite is the normative description of ForkMesh wire behavior. An
independent implementation should be able to derive every identifier, produce
and verify every signature, and fold collaboration state from these documents
and their vectors without reading ForkMesh source. The hosted
[protocol reference](https://forkmesh.com/docs/protocol/) remains the
narrative guide to HTTP routes and deployment; where the two disagree, this
suite wins and the disagreement is a bug.

| Document | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Encoding and identifiers](encoding-and-identifiers.md) | Canonical JSON, base64url, canonical strings, repository/policy/object/event/refs/migration identifiers |
| [Signatures and authentication](signatures-and-authentication.md) | Strict Ed25519, domain separation, envelope verification order, request tokens, push authorization, portable sessions, catalog publication |
| [Relay, synchronization, and migration](relay-sync-and-migration.md) | Integrity-gated clone routing, NDJSON log exchange, deterministic folding, migration receipts, rollback |
| [Version negotiation](version-negotiation.md) | Version identifiers, rejection of unknown versions, downgrade resistance, rollout order |
| [Conflict-safe collaboration](../design/conflict-safe-collaboration.md) | Collaboration event families, fold rules, moderation lineage |
| [Threat model](threat-model.md) | Trust boundaries, attackers, threat register, release blockers |
| [Certification program](certification.md) | Profiles, adapter protocol, detection classes, expiring badges, independence, governance, appeals, trademark use; current badges in the [registry](certification-registry.md) |

## Conformance language

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY are to be interpreted
as described in BCP 14 (RFC 2119, RFC 8174) when, and only when, they appear in
a numbered requirement. A requirement is written as a bold identifier followed
by its level, in the form `**FM-AREA-NNN** MUST`. Identifiers are never reused;
a withdrawn requirement keeps its number with the text "Withdrawn".

Everything outside a numbered requirement is informative.

## Suite requirements

- **FM-SUITE-001** MUST — The documents, schemas, vectors, and threat register
  of one suite version are released together. The manifest
  (`conformance/protocol/v1/manifest.json`) records the SHA-256 of each file
  and maps every requirement to its evidence. A verifier MUST reject the suite
  when any digest, version string, requirement identifier, requirement level,
  vector citation, or threat severity/status disagrees.
- **FM-SUITE-002** MUST — An implementation that claims a vector set passes
  every case in it: valid cases produce exactly the listed values, and invalid
  cases are rejected.
- **FM-SUITE-003** SHOULD — A rejection reports the listed error code.
  Validity is normative; codes are the stable vocabulary for audit telemetry
  and interop debugging. An implementation's known code deviations are
  recorded in the manifest (`codeDeviations`) and tested for exact equality,
  so a new deviation fails like any other inconsistency.

## Vectors

Vector files live in `conformance/protocol/v1/vectors/`:

| File | Content | Implementations passing it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `canonical-json.json` | Parse and encode cases, including every rejection class | reference Python, WebCrypto JavaScript, clean-room Python |
| `identifiers.json` | Repository, policy, object, refs-state, and migration identifiers | reference Python, clean-room Python; JavaScript for repository/policy/object |
| `signatures.json` | RFC 8032 and strictness cases, canonical-string schemes, push-message normalization, freshness windows | reference Python, clean-room Python |
| `events.json` | Signed collaboration envelopes and each verification failure | reference Python, WebCrypto JavaScript, clean-room Python |
| `fold.json` | Folded NDJSON logs with state digests and telemetry | reference Python, WebCrypto JavaScript |
| `sessions.json` | Portable session tokens | reference Python, clean-room Python |

Byte-exact inputs are given as `rawHex`; `rawText` is informative. Keys and
signatures come from deterministic test identities and MUST NOT be used
outside tests.

Run the suite:

```bash
python3 conformance/protocol/v1/verify_suite.py          # clean-room verifier + consistency
python3 conformance/protocol/v1/generate_vectors.py --check
python3 -m pytest -q app/tests/test_protocol_suite.py
```

`verify_suite.py` uses only the Python standard library and was written from
these documents. It does not yet fold collaboration logs, so `fold.json` is
evidenced by the two reference implementations only.

## Compatibility policy

Wire version identifiers and the suite version are separate:

- A **wire version identifier** (for example `forkmesh-collaboration-event-v1`
  or the `v1.` session-token prefix) names frozen bytes. Its meaning never
  changes; see [Version negotiation](version-negotiation.md).
- The **suite version** uses semantic versioning. A patch release fixes
  wording or adds vectors for existing behavior. A minor release adds
  requirements, vectors, or wire identifiers without changing what an existing
  conforming implementation accepts. A major release removes acceptance of a
  wire identifier; it is announced one minor release in advance and ships
  with a migration path.

## Change process

Changes are decided under the [governance charter](../governance/README.md).
Steps 1–5 are the technical part of a proposal record (`FMP-NNNN`). Review
windows, quorum, dissent, and appeals follow the charter.

1. Open an issue that names the requirement identifiers and threats affected.
2. Change the normative text, the reference implementations, and the
   generator expectations in one change. The generator compares every vector
   with an expectation written in `generate_vectors.py`, so a behavior change
   that is not also a documented expectation fails generation.
3. Update `threats.json` and the [threat model](threat-model.md) table
   together when a control or residual risk changes.
4. Regenerate: `python3 conformance/protocol/v1/generate_vectors.py`. This
   rewrites vectors and manifest digests; `--check` fails CI on anything stale.
5. Review requires one maintainer for informative or vector-only changes and a
   security reviewer for any requirement, wire identifier, or threat status
   change.

## Stable release gate

The suite may be marked `stable` only when no `critical` or `high` threat in
the register is `open`. Each must be `mitigated` by a numbered requirement or
`accepted` with a reviewer, date, and rationale. The verifier enforces this and
reports the current blockers as `stableReleaseBlockers`.

Before the umbrella epic can close, more evidence is needed:

- a clean-room collaboration fold;
- a second-language clean-room verifier;
- stock-Git clone interoperability against an independently written relay;
- the platform matrix.

The [certification program](certification.md) packages these vectors into
profiles any implementation can run through a language-neutral adapter. Its
closure gate is an independent implementation holding a current `core`
badge.

The [Git conformance suite](../operations/git-conformance.md) already covers
stock clients.

# Protocol certification registry

Evaluated as of 2026-09-14 against suite `1.0.0-rc.1` · badges stay valid for 90 days after testing · [Program and governance](certification.md)

Closure gate **not met**: no independent implementation holds a current `core` badge yet.

| Implementation | Independent | Profile | Status | Tested | Expires | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ForkMesh clean-room Python verifier (`forkmesh-clean-room-python`) | no | `core` | certified | 2026-09-14 | 2026-12-13 | [0f463340bf4d3c03](https://forkmesh.com/docs/certification/evidence/0f463340bf4d3c03.json) |
| ForkMesh WebCrypto JavaScript collaboration library (`forkmesh-webcrypto-javascript`) | no | `collaboration-fold` | certified | 2026-09-14 | 2026-12-13 | [47ee8e5f355c09c9](https://forkmesh.com/docs/certification/evidence/47ee8e5f355c09c9.json) |

The hosted badge re-checks expiry on every request, so an embedded badge turns `expired` on its own.

## Embedding a badge

`forkmesh-clean-room-python` · `core` — reproduce with `python3 tools/protocol_certification.py run --implementation forkmesh-clean-room-python --profile core`

```markdown
[![ForkMesh core certification](https://forkmesh.com/docs/certification/badges/forkmesh-clean-room-python/core.svg)](https://forkmesh.com/docs/certification/badges/forkmesh-clean-room-python/core)
```

`forkmesh-webcrypto-javascript` · `collaboration-fold` — reproduce with `python3 tools/protocol_certification.py run --implementation forkmesh-webcrypto-javascript --profile collaboration-fold`

```markdown
[![ForkMesh collaboration-fold certification](https://forkmesh.com/docs/certification/badges/forkmesh-webcrypto-javascript/collaboration-fold.svg)](https://forkmesh.com/docs/certification/badges/forkmesh-webcrypto-javascript/collaboration-fold)
```

## Detection coverage

| Profile | Class | Cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `core` | malformed-signature | 13 |
| `core` | divergence | 7 |
| `core` | downgrade | 2 |
| `core` | replay | 6 |
| `core` | data-loss | 5 |
| `core` | incompatible-version | 5 |
| `collaboration-fold` | malformed-signature | 3 |
| `collaboration-fold` | divergence | 8 |
| `collaboration-fold` | replay | 1 |
| `collaboration-fold` | data-loss | 4 |
| `collaboration-fold` | incompatible-version | 3 |

pages.description: Program version: 1.0.0 · Protocol suite: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Part of the ForkMesh protocol suite · Current badges: certification registry
pages.markdown:
# Protocol certification program

Program version: `1.0.0` · Protocol suite: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Part of the
[ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md) · Current badges:
[certification registry](certification-registry.md)

Independent clients, relays, indexes, and providers prove compatibility by
running the published suite through a small adapter and publishing the
report. A badge says exactly one thing: *this implementation, at this version,
passed every case of this profile, against these vectors, within the last 90
days, on these platforms*. Nothing is certified by assertion; badges are
derived from retained reports only.

Sources, all versioned together:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `conformance/certification/v1/program.json` | Profiles, detection classes, performance budgets, freshness window, closure gate |
| `conformance/certification/v1/implementations.json` | Registered implementations, adapter commands, claimed profiles and platforms, independence review |
| `conformance/certification/v1/evidence/<run>.json` | Retained reports, named by content address |
| `conformance/certification/v1/results.json` | Index of retained reports, recomputed from evidence on `validate` |
| `tools/protocol_certification.py` | Harness, attestation, badge derivation, and generated outputs |

Generated outputs, never edited by hand: [certification-registry.md](certification-registry.md),
`/docs/certification/badges.json`, and `/docs/certification/evidence/<run>.json`.

## Profiles

A profile is a list of vector groups plus the defect classes the profile must
detect. The program refuses a profile that names a class with no case in its
groups.

| Profile | For | Vector groups | Must detect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `core` | clients, relays, indexes, providers | canonical JSON parse and encode; repository, policy, object, refs-state, and migration identifiers; Ed25519 strictness, canonical strings, git-push messages, freshness; signed events; portable sessions | malformed signatures, divergence, downgrade, replay, data loss, incompatible versions |
| `collaboration-fold` | clients and relays that fold collaboration logs | canonical JSON; repository, policy, and object identifiers; signed events; log folding | malformed signatures, divergence, replay, data loss, incompatible versions |

Every case is **positive** (valid input, exact value) or **negative**
(rejected input). Detection classes group the adversarial and version-skew
cases that matter most:

| Class | A failing implementation … | Example cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `malformed-signature` | accepts a non-canonical scalar, a small-order key, a tampered payload, or an alternate signature spelling | `signatures:ed25519-order-2-public-key`, `events:event-tampered-payload` |
| `divergence` | derives a different identifier or folded state from the same input | `identifiers:repository-decomposed-root-normalizes`, `fold:concurrent-scalar-conflict` |
| `downgrade` | verifies a signature under an older version or another scheme | `signatures:cross-version-view-signature` |
| `replay` | accepts a stale request, an expired or future session, or re-applies a redelivered event | `signatures:stale-past`, `sessions:session-expired` |
| `data-loss` | drops a ref, rounds an integer, or silently discards a pending or rejected record | `identifiers:refs-bytewise-refname-order`, `fold:missing-parent-pending` |
| `incompatible-version` | parses an unknown or future version identifier instead of rejecting it | `events:event-future-schema`, `sessions:session-future-token-prefix` |

The suite's own tests prove each class is detected. The clean-room adapter
accepts `--fault` modes that break one property at a time (lenient Ed25519,
skipped normalization, version downgrade on failure, ignored expiry, dropped
refs, accepted future versions), and `app/tests/test_protocol_certification.py`
requires every fault to fail its class. A faulted run records a different
adapter command, so it can never be attested.

**Performance.** Each case must answer within 2,000 ms and a profile within
120 s on the runner. A slower run fails; the report records the slowest case.

**Error codes.** Validity and values are normative. When a rejection uses a
different stable code than the vector lists, the case still passes and the
report records `expectedError`/`actualError` as a code deviation (FM-SUITE-003).

## Adapter protocol

`forkmesh-conformance-adapter-v1` is newline-delimited JSON over the
adapter's standard input and output, one request and one response per line,
so any language can take part without linking ForkMesh code. The harness runs
the adapter with the repository root as its working directory; the vectors
arrive inside the requests.

1. The harness sends
   `{"type":"hello","protocol":"forkmesh-conformance-adapter-v1","suite":"forkmesh-protocol","suiteVersion":"1.0.0-rc.1"}`.
2. The adapter answers
   `{"type":"hello","protocol":"forkmesh-conformance-adapter-v1","implementation":{"name":"…","version":"…"},"suiteVersions":["1.0.0-rc.1"]}`.
   If the protocol differs or `suiteVersions` lacks the harness's suite
   version, the run is recorded as `incompatible` and every case fails. That
   is how version skew between an implementation and the suite shows up.
3. For each case the harness sends
   `{"type":"case","id":"<set>:<case>","operation":"…","input":{…}}` and the
   adapter answers `{"id":"<same>","valid":true,"value":…}`,
   `{"id":"<same>","valid":false,"error":"<code>"}`, or
   `{"id":"<same>","unsupported":true}`.

A missing, late, or mismatched response fails that case. An adapter that exits
or hangs fails the case in flight and every later case, and the run still
produces a report.

| Operation | Input | Valid response value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `canonical.parse` | `rawHex` | ignored |
| `canonical.encode` | `value` | canonical text |
| `identifier.repository` | `verifiedRoot` | repository identifier |
| `identifier.policy` | `policy` | policy identifier |
| `identifier.object` | `repository`, `family`, `creator`, `objectKey`, `references` | object identifier |
| `identifier.refs-state` | `advertisementHex` | `{"canonicalText","stateHash"}` |
| `identifier.migration` | `operation` plus its fields | identifier or hash string |
| `signature.ed25519` | `publicKeyHex`, `messageHex`, `signatureHex` | ignored (validity is the verdict) |
| `signature.canonical-string` | `messageText`, `publicKey`, `signature`, optional `scheme`/`fields`, `catalogV2Record` | ignored |
| `signature.git-push-message` | `owner`, `repo`, `method`, `ts`, `bodySha256` | message text |
| `request.freshness` | `ts`, `nowMs` | ignored (valid means fresh) |
| `event.verify` | `rawHex`, `policy`, `context` (ancestor envelopes as hex) | event identifier |
| `session.parse` | `token`, `nowMs`, `routerPublicKey` | claim object |
| `log.fold` | `ndjson`, `policy` | `{"stateDigest","telemetry","rejectionReasons"}` |

Each vector file's `procedure` and the protocol documents define what an
operation must do. The adapters in `conformance/certification/v1/adapters/`
are working examples in Python and JavaScript.

## Running and publishing

```sh
# Any implementation, registered or not
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py run --profile core \
  --implementation acme-relay --command "cargo run --release --bin fm-adapter" \
  --output artifacts/acme-relay-core.json

# A registered implementation uses its registered adapter command
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py run --profile core \
  --implementation forkmesh-clean-room-python

python3 tools/protocol_certification.py attest artifacts/*.json   # retain + regenerate
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py validate
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py render --check
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py status --as-of 2026-12-31
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py gate
```

`attest` accepts passing and failing reports. It rejects a report that does
not match its registered implementation, profile, platform, or adapter
command. It also rejects a summary or detection table that disagrees with its
cases, a case list trimmed from the current profile, and any local path, file
URL, or loopback address. The newest report for each implementation, profile,
and platform replaces older ones, and an older report never replaces a newer
one. Editing evidence or the results index fails `validate`.

`gate` is part of the `core` and `release` quality-gate profiles. It validates
everything, checks the generated outputs, and re-runs every in-repository
adapter on the current machine, so it never fails just because the date
changed. It also prints the closure gate status.

## Badges

**Scope.** One implementation, one profile. A badge covers only the vector
groups of that profile and the platforms the registry lists for the
implementation. It says nothing about features outside the profile, hosted
availability, security audits, or product quality.

**Version.** Each report binds the program version, a digest of the profile
definition (groups, detection cases, and budgets), the suite version, and a
digest of every vector file. The implementation's own name and version come
from the adapter handshake.

**Statuses**, derived in this order:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `revoked` | Withdrawn by a governance decision recorded in the registry |
| `unverified` | No retained run on at least one listed platform |
| `failing` | The newest run on some platform failed |
| `expired` | The suite vectors, suite version, program version, or profile changed after testing, or the oldest platform run is older than 90 days |
| `certified` | Every listed platform passed, bound to the current suite and profile, within 90 days; `expiresAt` is the last valid day |

**Expiry and retesting.** Expiry is automatic in two places. First, a vector,
profile, or suite-version change changes the badge data, so
`render --check` fails in CI until the registry is regenerated with those
badges marked `expired`. Second, the hosted SVG at
`/docs/certification/badges/<implementation>/<profile>.svg` compares
`expiresAt` with the time of each request, so an embedded badge shows
`expired` the day after the window closes, with no redeploy. To renew,
re-run the profile and attest the report. The same rules apply to a retest:
there is no grace period, and a failing retest replaces a passing one.

**Links.** `/docs/certification/badges/<implementation>/<profile>` redirects
to the raw evidence report of the badge's current run. The registry page
lists the reproduction command for every badge. Embed a badge as:

```markdown
[![ForkMesh core certification](https://forkmesh.com/docs/certification/badges/<implementation>/core.svg)](https://forkmesh.com/docs/certification/badges/<implementation>/core)
```

## Independence

The issue this program serves closes only when a **non-ForkMesh**
implementation holds a current `core` badge (`closureGate` in the program). An
implementation counts as independent when all of the following hold:

- its source is published at a public `https://` URL outside ForkMesh-controlled repositories;
- it was written by people who are not ForkMesh maintainers, from the protocol
  documents and vectors, without copying ForkMesh source;
- a reviewer who does not maintain it records the review in the registry's
  `independence` block (`reviewer`, `date`, `statement`).

The two registered in-repository implementations are marked `independent:
false` and do not count, even though the Python verifier is clean-room.

## Governance

Certification decisions belong to the protocol council under the
[governance charter](../governance/README.md). Appeals go to its appeals panel
on the timeline below. Until independent seats are filled, the stewards below
act under the charter, and their decisions are recorded in the
[decision register](../governance/decision-register.md).

- **Stewards.** Two ForkMesh maintainers act as certification stewards for each
  program minor version. At least one of them must not work on the
  implementation under review. Stewards review registry entries, independence
  statements, and appeals.
- **Registration.** An implementer opens a pull request that adds a registry
  entry and one attested report. The entry includes a runnable adapter command,
  so a reviewer can reproduce the run with the command on the registry page.
  A steward reruns the report on at least one listed platform before merging.
- **Program changes.** They follow the protocol suite's
  [change process](README.md#change-process). A change that removes or narrows
  what a profile accepts is a major program version. Adding cases or classes to
  a profile is a minor version and expires existing badges, which is intended:
  they must be retested against the new cases. Wording changes are patch
  versions and leave badges valid.
- **Conflicts of interest.** A steward who maintains, or is paid by the
  maintainer of, an implementation does not review its registration, appeal,
  or revocation.
- **Transparency.** Every decision lands as a commit to the registry. A
  revocation carries its date and reason, and the registry page shows both.

## Appeals and revocation

- **Disputing a vector.** An implementer who believes a vector or expectation
  is wrong opens an issue naming the case identifiers and the requirement
  text. If the stewards agree, the vector is fixed through the change process,
  and every badge for the affected profile expires and is retested. No
  implementation receives an exemption.
- **Appealing a decision.** A registration refusal or revocation can be
  appealed within 30 days. Two stewards who took no part in the original
  decision hear it and publish their written decision within 30 days.
- **Revocation.** A badge is revoked when its evidence cannot be reproduced
  from the registered adapter, the independence statement proves false, or the
  badge is used outside its scope. Revocation adds an entry to the
  implementation's `revocations` list. It is lifted by a steward decision and
  a fresh attested run.

## Trademark use

"ForkMesh" and the badge artwork identify the project. A certified
implementation may:

- embed the hosted badge, linked as shown above;
- say "passes the ForkMesh `<profile>` profile, suite `<version>`" while the
  badge is `certified`.

It may not:

- say "ForkMesh certified" without naming the profile;
- use a copied or self-hosted badge image, since only the hosted badge expires;
- use the ForkMesh name as part of the product name;
- imply endorsement, hosting, or security review by ForkMesh.

After a badge expires or is revoked, the claim must be removed or qualified
with the date it last held.

## Interoperability events

The stewards announce public interoperability events on the project chat and
the protocol issue tracker at least four weeks ahead. Each event pins a program
and suite version.

- Participants bring an adapter. During the event every participant runs every
  profile, and the stewards attest the reports the same day, passing or failing.
- Cross-implementation pairs also exchange live NDJSON logs and compare folded
  state digests. Any mismatch is filed as an issue against the vector or the
  implementation.
- Event notes list the participants, reports, failures found, and each
  failure's time to retest. They are published as a note linked from the
  registry page.

## Contributing tests

Independent implementers are encouraged to contribute cases, especially
adversarial and version-skew inputs that caught a real bug.

1. Open an issue naming the requirement identifiers the case exercises and the
   detection class it belongs to.
2. Add the expectation to `conformance/protocol/v1/generate_vectors.py`,
   regenerate the vectors, and list the new case under its class in
   `program.json`.
3. Include one run of the reference implementation that passes and, where
   possible, a fault or an implementation that the case catches.

A contributed case is reviewed like any vector change. Once merged, it expires
the badges of every profile that includes it, so all implementations are
retested against it.

pages.markdown:
# Encoding and identifiers

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Vectors: `canonical-json.json`,
`identifiers.json` · Part of the [ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md)

## Canonical JSON

ForkMesh hashes and signs a deliberately small JSON subset. It is chosen so
that Python `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True,
separators=(",", ":"))` and ECMAScript `JSON.stringify` with sorted keys emit
identical bytes for every admitted value.

- **FM-ENC-001** MUST — A canonical document is UTF-8 without a byte-order
  mark, without insignificant whitespace, and without a trailing newline. A
  signed document's top level is an object. Object keys match
  `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,256}$` and appear in ascending code-point order.
- **FM-ENC-002** MUST — Values are objects, arrays, strings, `true`, `false`,
  `null`, or integers whose magnitude is at most 2^53−1. Integers are written
  in shortest decimal form: no fraction, exponent, leading zero, or negative
  zero. `NaN` and infinities are not JSON and are rejected. Individual fields
  can narrow the range further; envelope counters, for example, are
  non-negative.
- **FM-ENC-003** MUST — Strings are Unicode NFC and contain no unpaired
  surrogate. An encoder normalizes strings to NFC before hashing. Within a
  string, `"` and `\` are written `\"` and `\\`; U+0008, U+000C, U+000A,
  U+000D, and U+0009 use `\b \f \n \r \t`; all other code points below U+0020
  use `\u00XX` with lowercase hex. Every other code point, including U+007F,
  U+2028, U+2029, `/`, and characters outside the BMP, is written literally.
- **FM-ENC-004** MUST — A receiver parses with duplicate-key detection,
  re-encodes the parsed value under FM-ENC-001..003, and rejects the input
  unless the result is byte-for-byte identical. An alternate spelling of the
  same value — whitespace, escapes, key order, or a non-NFC string — is a
  different, invalid input, not an equivalent one.
- **FM-ENC-005** MUST — A signed document is at most 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes)
  and non-empty. Nesting depth is at most 32, counting the top-level object as
  depth 0 and each nested array or object as one more.

Some integrity receipts use variants that differ from signed collaboration
documents. The portable session claim (FM-AUTH-003) and the catalog v2 record
hash (FM-AUTH-004) serialize with ASCII escaping: every code point above
U+007E is written as lowercase `\uXXXX`, using surrogate pairs outside the
BMP. Migration state receipts (FM-ID-006) use the literal form without NFC
normalization. Each variant is pinned by vectors.

Rejection codes, in the order a parser meets them: `invalid_event_size`,
`invalid_json`, `invalid_number`, `floating_point_forbidden`, `duplicate_key`,
`event_not_object`, `json_too_deep`, `invalid_key`, `unsafe_integer`,
`invalid_unicode`, `noncanonical_encoding`.

## Binary encodings

- **FM-ENC-006** MUST — Keys, signatures, and object keys are base64url
  (RFC 4648 §5) without padding. A decoder rejects padding, characters outside
  the alphabet, the wrong decoded length, and any spelling that does not
  re-encode identically. The last check catches non-zero unused trailing bits:
  two textual signatures for the same bytes would otherwise produce two
  distinct envelopes. Ed25519 public keys decode to 32 bytes, signatures to
  64, and collaboration object keys to 16.

Digest identifiers are written `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits,
except where a field is specified as bare hex.

## Canonical strings

Older signed actions sign newline-joined strings rather than JSON.

- **FM-ENC-007** MUST — A canonical string is the UTF-8 encoding of a frozen
  scheme prefix `forkmesh-<scheme>-v<N>`, then each field in the order the
  scheme lists, joined by a single LF (0x0A) with no trailing LF. Timestamps
  are decimal milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Senders write them without
  sign or leading zeros; verifiers sign-check the field text exactly as
  transmitted. Variable-length content is bound as a lowercase hex SHA-256
  field, never inline.

The scheme field lists live in [Signatures and
authentication](signatures-and-authentication.md#canonical-string-schemes).

## Identifiers

- **FM-ID-001** MUST — A repository identity is
  `urn:forkmesh:repository:sha256:` followed by
  `hex(SHA-256("forkmesh-repository-identity-v1\n" || NFC(verified root)))`.
  The verified root is established out of band, for example by a signed
  repository manifest. Display names, organization aliases, and URLs are
  routing hints, never identities.
- **FM-ID-002** MUST — A collaboration policy document has exactly the keys
  `schema` (`forkmesh-collaboration-policy-v1`), `repository`, `maintainers`,
  `moderators`, and `notifiers`. Each role is a sorted, duplicate-free list of
  32-byte base64url Ed25519 keys. Its identity is
  `sha256:` + `hex(SHA-256(canonical JSON))`, with no domain prefix because
  the schema value is inside the hashed bytes. A document that is not already
  in this form is rejected, never repaired.
- **FM-ID-003** MUST — A collaboration object identity is
  `urn:forkmesh:collaboration:<family>:sha256:` followed by
  `hex(SHA-256("forkmesh-collaboration-object-v1\n" || canonical JSON of
  {repository, family, creator, objectKey, references}))`. `references` is
  the validated, sorted list of `{relation, family, object}` triples that the
  object's first event carries.
- **FM-ID-004** MUST — A collaboration event identity is
  `sha256:` + `hex(SHA-256(signingBytes || 0x00 || rawSignature))`. Here
  `signingBytes` is defined by FM-SIG-003 and `rawSignature` is the 64 decoded
  signature bytes. A receiver recomputes it and rejects a mismatch
  (`event_id_mismatch`).
- **FM-ID-005** MUST — A repository state digest is taken over the refs a node
  serves. From a protocol-v0 `upload-pack --advertise-refs` pkt-line stream,
  keep only `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*`. Drop `HEAD`, peeled `^{}` lines,
  and every other namespace, including `refs/pull/` and `refs/forkmesh/`.
  Strip capabilities after the first NUL, and sort by refname in byte order.
  The canonical text joins `<object-id> <refname>` lines with LF and has no
  trailing LF. `stateHash` is its lowercase hex SHA-256; an empty
  advertisement hashes the empty string.
- **FM-ID-006** MUST — Migration identifiers are domain-separated SHA-256 over
  LF-joined parts: `hex(SHA-256(domain || "\n" || join("\n", parts)))`.
  A job is `mig_` followed by the first 24 hex digits for the domain
  `forkmesh-migration-job-v1`. An object key uses
  `forkmesh-migration-object-v1` with parts object type and source id. A
  state receipt is `sha256:` + hex SHA-256 of the literal-form canonical JSON
  (see above) of the state document.

pages.markdown:
# Relay, synchronization, and migration

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Vectors: `fold.json`, `identifiers.json` ·
Part of the [ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md)

## Roles

- A **source of truth** is a node holding the owner's working repository. It
  signs catalog records and `forkmesh-repostate-v1` attestations.
- A **mirror** is an independently operated HTTPS origin serving a copy. Its
  own attestations prove what it serves, not what the owner published.
- The **relay** (mainnode) routes reads to mirrors, verifies signed
  submissions, and indexes metadata. It never stores repository bytes and is
  never authoritative for collaboration meaning.

## Clone and fetch routing

- **FM-REL-001** MUST — A relay serves a public clone or fetch only from a
  mirror that passes three checks. The mirror has a fresh signed health
  result. Its live advertised refs hash (FM-ID-005) to a state that a source
  of truth in the repository's logical group attested with
  `forkmesh-repostate-v1`. Mirrors are grouped by root commit, falling back to
  name. A source is checked against its current pin plus bounded recent
  history. A mirror's self-attestation never activates a repository. When the
  group has no source-signed pin, routing fails closed.
- **FM-REL-002** MUST — The two requests of a smart-HTTP clone (`info/refs`,
  then `git-upload-pack`) reach the same accepted origin. A relay may retry
  another integrity-matching origin only before any response byte is sent. It
  never splices responses from different origins and never rewrites pack
  data.
- **FM-REL-003** MUST — Receive-pack is refused before any request body is
  read unless FM-AUTH-002 authorizes the request. Both upload-pack and
  receive-pack hide the `refs/forkmesh/` namespace, which holds merge
  anchors and staging refs, and reject wants for object ids that no
  advertised ref reaches.

Protocol negotiation inside Git (protocol v0 or v2) is left to stock Git
clients and servers. The refs digest is always computed from a protocol-v0
advertisement generated for attestation.

## Collaboration log exchange

- **FM-SYNC-001** MUST — A collaboration log is exchanged as one canonical
  envelope per line, separated by LF. A reader splits only on LF and retains
  a stray CR in the record, where it fails as `noncanonical_encoding` rather
  than being normalized into a valid envelope. An importer verifies every
  record and recomputes state; it never trusts an exported snapshot. Export
  sorts unique raw records by SHA-256 of their bytes.
- **FM-SYNC-002** MUST — Folding is a pure function of the policy and the set
  of unique raw records. Permutation, duplication, and delay never change the
  result. The state digest is `sha256:` + hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON
  state document (`forkmesh-collaboration-state-v1`). Duplicate deliveries are
  counted, not re-applied.
- **FM-SYNC-003** MUST — Beyond FM-SIG-004, a fold enforces six rules:
  - An event whose parents are not all present stays **pending**, with its
    raw bytes retained.
  - A descendant of a rejected event is rejected.
  - The Lamport `clock` is 0 without parents and otherwise one more than the
    greatest parent clock.
  - Two different events signed by one key in the same `sequence` slot are
    **equivocation**; both are excluded and counted.
  - Role authorization follows the pinned policy. Unauthorized events are
    audited but never folded.
  - Concurrent differing scalar writes produce an explicit conflict rather
    than a winner chosen by time, author, or arrival order.

  The complete family rules are normative in
  [Conflict-safe collaboration](../design/conflict-safe-collaboration.md).

A fold over an incomplete set cannot detect omission. A relay that withholds
events is an open threat (TM-008), not a property this suite guarantees.

## Migration and rollback

- **FM-MIG-001** MUST — A repository migration state receipt (FM-ID-006)
  excludes run timestamps, attempt counters, and credentials. Re-running an
  import over unchanged provider data yields the same receipt, and source
  deletions are pruned, not retained as stale objects.
- **FM-MIG-002** MUST — Each legacy collaboration record migrates through an
  importer-signed `create` or `decide` event. That event binds the exact
  legacy record digest and records whether the legacy signature is `valid`,
  `invalid`, or `unavailable`. It never presents the importer's signature as
  the legacy author's. The original bytes are kept alongside the new log.
- **FM-MIG-003** MUST — Rollback proceeds in a fixed order: stop writers
  emitting the newer version first, then roll back readers. Readers keep
  accepting and preserving newer raw envelopes they already hold. No
  implementation down-converts or deletes signed events, because that loses
  causality. Recovery restores policy and NDJSON, re-verifies, and compares
  state digests; corrupt lines stay quarantined while valid objects keep
  folding.

pages.markdown:
# Signatures and authentication

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Vectors: `signatures.json`, `events.json`,
`sessions.json` · Part of the [ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md)

## Ed25519

- **FM-SIG-001** MUST — Signatures are Ed25519 (RFC 8032, PureEdDSA, no
  context) verified with the cofactorless equation `[S]B = R + [k]A`, where
  `k = SHA-512(R || A || M) mod L`. A verifier rejects:
  - a signature that is not exactly 64 bytes;
  - a scalar `S ≥ L`, so no `S + L` malleability;
  - a point encoding with `y ≥ p`, no square root, or `x = 0` with the sign
    bit set;
  - the identity as the public key;
  - any public key outside the prime-order subgroup (`[L]A ≠ identity`), which
    excludes all small-order and mixed-order keys.

Implementations that wrap a platform verifier (for example WebCrypto) MUST add
the checks their platform omits.

## Domain separation

- **FM-SIG-002** MUST — Every signed message begins with a frozen,
  scheme-specific prefix, and a verifier builds the message itself from the
  fields it will act on. A client-supplied message is never accepted. A
  signature valid under one prefix therefore never verifies under another
  scheme, another version, or a substituted field such as a different HTTP
  method.

### Canonical-string schemes

These follow FM-ENC-007. The fields below come after the prefix line.

| Prefix | Fields | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `forkmesh-catalog-v1` | owner, name, updatedAt | relay, catalog publish (public records only) |
| `forkmesh-catalog-v2` | recordSha256 | relay, catalog publish |
| `forkmesh-repostate-v1` | owner, repo, stateHash (FM-ID-005), updatedAt | relay, catalog publish and mirror attestations |
| `forkmesh-private-manifest-v1` | owner, name, opaqueRepoId, keyEpoch, manifestHash, updatedAt | relay, private catalog publish |
| `forkmesh-view-v1` | owner, repo, ts | relay, private browse and clone |
| `forkmesh-rotate-v1` | oldPubkey, newPubkey, ts | relay, account key rotation (signed by the old key) |
| `forkmesh-git-push-v1` | owner, repo, method, ts, bodySha256 | relay and mirror gateway, HTTPS receive-pack |

For `forkmesh-catalog-v2`, `recordSha256` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the
normalized catalog record minus its descriptive `signature` field. The record
is serialized with sorted keys, no whitespace, and ASCII escaping. The
[published protocol reference](https://forkmesh.com/docs/protocol/#signature-schemes)
lists the remaining legacy schemes (issue, discussion, pull, release, room,
node link). Their field layout is informative until they receive vectors; see
TM-004 in the [threat model](threat-model.md).

## Collaboration envelopes

- **FM-SIG-003** MUST — A collaboration event's signing bytes are
  `"forkmesh-collaboration-event-v1\n"` followed by the canonical JSON of the
  unsigned envelope. The unsigned envelope is the event without `signature`
  and `eventId`, with exactly the keys `schema`, `repository`, `policy`,
  `family`, `object`, `action`, `author`, `sequence`, `clock`, `issuedAt`,
  `parents`, `references`, and `payload`. The author's key signs those bytes.
- **FM-SIG-004** MUST — A receiver rejects an event at the first failing step
  and never lets it influence causality, authorization, or state:
  1. size and canonical parse (FM-ENC-004, FM-ENC-005);
  2. exact key set (`invalid_envelope_keys`), then schema identifier
     (`unsupported_schema`);
  3. field shapes: repository URN, policy digest, known family and action,
     object URN of that family, author and signature encodings, non-negative
     safe integers, sorted duplicate-free `parents` (at most 64), references,
     and payload structure;
  4. event identity (`event_id_mismatch`, FM-ID-004);
  5. for `create` and `decide`, object identity (`object_id_mismatch`,
     FM-ID-003);
  6. repository binding (`wrong_repository`) and policy binding
     (`unknown_policy`) against the pinned policy;
  7. the Ed25519 signature (`invalid_signature`).

  Binding is checked before the signature. A replay into another repository
  is therefore classified as a replay even when its signature is also invalid.

Causality, sequence, equivocation, and authorization rules follow in
[Relay, synchronization, and migration](relay-sync-and-migration.md#collaboration-log-exchange).

## Request authentication

- **FM-AUTH-001** MUST — A time-bound request proof (`view`, `rotate`, and
  `git-push` schemes) is accepted only when its timestamp field is within
  300,000 ms of the verifier's clock in either direction, inclusive. Senders
  write the timestamp as ASCII decimal digits. A verifier rejects a timestamp
  that is not a base-10 integer, and it signs-checks the field text as sent
  (FM-ENC-007). The window limits replay but does not prevent it; see TM-012.
- **FM-AUTH-002** MUST — An HTTPS push is authorized by a signature over
  `forkmesh-git-push-v1`. Before signing and verifying, the owner is trimmed and
  lowercased, the repository trimmed, the method trimmed and uppercased, and
  the body digest trimmed and lowercased. Anything else is rejected: an owner
  that is not a valid account name, a repository that is not a single safe
  path segment, a method other than `GET` or `POST`, a timestamp that is not
  1–16 digits, or a body digest that is not 64 hex digits. The ref
  advertisement `GET` signs the digest of the empty body. When the relay
  streams a pack it has not buffered, it forwards the signed digest, and the
  gateway MUST check the received bytes against it before running
  receive-pack.
- **FM-AUTH-003** MUST — A portable session token is
  `v1.<claim>.<signature>`. `<claim>` is 80–1024 base64url characters of
  ASCII-escaped canonical JSON. `<signature>` is 86 characters and signs
  `"forkmesh-portable-session-v1\n" || <claim>` with the router key. The claim
  has exactly the keys:
  - `type` = `forkmesh.portable-session`;
  - `aud` = `forkmesh-mirror-dashboard`;
  - `v` = 1;
  - integer `iat` and `exp`;
  - `sub`: 32–128 lowercase hex;
  - `name`: an account name;
  - `sid` and `jti`: opaque 16–128 base64url-alphabet strings.

  A verifier rejects, in order: framing (`token_invalid`), encodings
  (`encoding_invalid`), claim shape (`claim_invalid`), time (`not_current`:
  `iat ≤ 0`, `exp ≤ iat`, lifetime over 12 hours, `iat` more than 60 s ahead,
  or `exp` more than 60 s past), a non-canonical claim
  (`claim_noncanonical`), and the signature (`signature_invalid`).
- **FM-AUTH-004** MUST — A catalog publication is signed by a key registered
  to the owner account.
  - When `catalogSigVersion` is 2, `catalogSig` MUST verify
    `forkmesh-catalog-v2`.
  - Otherwise it MUST verify `forkmesh-catalog-v1`, and only for a record
    whose visibility is `public`. Any other visibility is refused with HTTP 426
    `client_upgrade_required` and `requiredCatalogSigVersion: 2` before any
    confidential field is stored.
  - A present `stateSig` MUST verify `forkmesh-repostate-v1`, and a present but
    invalid attestation rejects the whole write.
  - A record whose `updatedAt` is older than the stored record is rejected as
    a rollback.

Inbox submissions (issues, pulls, discussions) prove only that a record was
not altered after signing. They carry no authority. The repository owner's
review and push is the authorization step.

pages.description: Suite version: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Register: conformance/protocol/v1/threats.json · Part of the ForkMesh protocol suite
pages.markdown:
# Threat model

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Register: `conformance/protocol/v1/threats.json`
· Part of the [ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md)

This model covers the wire protocol in this suite. Endpoint compromise,
Cloudflare platform compromise, and supply-chain attacks against clients
belong to [SECURITY.md](../../../SECURITY.md) and the [dependency
audit](../security/dependency-security-audit.md). The register file is
authoritative. The table below MUST match its severity and status, and the
suite verifier fails if they differ.

## Assets

- Private keys: device, account, router, and importer keys.
- Repository history and the integrity of refs.
- Signed collaboration history: issues, pulls, reviews, moderation.
- Private repository names, contents, and collaborator lists.
- Session and request authorizations.
- Availability of clone and collaboration flows.

## Trust boundaries

| ID | Boundary |
| --- | --- |
| B1 | Client device and its key store |
| B2 | Client ↔ relay (Worker HTTPS and WebSocket) |
| B3 | Relay ↔ mirror origin |
| B4 | Mirror ↔ source-of-truth node |
| B5 | Relay storage (D1, Durable Objects, KV) |
| B6 | External provider ↔ migration importer |
| B7 | Portable session ↔ independent mirror dashboard |

## Attacker capabilities

| ID | Attacker | Can | Cannot (assumed) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | Network attacker | Observe timing and sizes; drop or delay traffic | Break TLS 1.2+ or Ed25519/SHA-256 |
| A2 | Malicious or compromised relay operator | Read and rewrite anything the relay receives; withhold, reorder, or replay messages; read relay-layer room traffic | Forge user signatures |
| A3 | Malicious mirror operator | Serve any bytes; lie in its own attestations; log requests | Forge a source-of-truth attestation |
| A4 | Malicious registered user | Sign any content with its own keys; equivocate; craft malformed input | Sign with another user's key |
| A5 | Holder of a stolen device key | Everything that key authorizes until rotation or revocation | Use the account password or TOTP |
| A6 | Malicious migration provider | Return inconsistent, oversized, or hostile API data | Access ForkMesh keys |
| A7 | Resource-exhaustion attacker | Send many or large requests within platform limits | Exceed Cloudflare edge limits |

## Register

| ID | Threat | Boundaries | Attackers | Severity | Status | Controls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TM-001 | Forged authorship of signed objects | B2, B5 | A2, A4 | high | mitigated | FM-SIG-001, FM-SIG-003, FM-SIG-004 |
| TM-002 | Signature or encoding malleability that aliases event identities | B2 | A2, A4 | high | mitigated | FM-SIG-001, FM-ENC-004, FM-ENC-006, FM-ID-004 |
| TM-003 | Replay of collaboration events into another repository or policy epoch | B2, B5 | A2, A4 | high | mitigated | FM-ID-003, FM-SIG-004 |
| TM-004 | Replay of legacy issue/discussion/pull records whose canonical strings omit owner and repository | B2 | A2, A4 | high | open | FM-SIG-002, FM-MIG-002 |
| TM-005 | Cross-scheme or cross-version signature confusion | B2 | A2 | high | mitigated | FM-SIG-002, FM-VER-001, FM-VER-002 |
| TM-006 | Catalog v1 signatures, which do not bind visibility or descriptive fields, replayed for public records | B2, B5 | A2 | high | open | FM-AUTH-004, FM-VER-002 |
| TM-007 | Tampered or rolled-back history served to cloners | B3, B4 | A3 | high | mitigated | FM-REL-001, FM-REL-002, FM-ID-005 |
| TM-008 | Relay or mirror withholds collaboration events | B2, B3 | A2, A3 | high | open | FM-SYNC-003 |
| TM-009 | Signing-key equivocation | B2 | A4, A5 | high | mitigated | FM-SYNC-003 |
| TM-010 | Clock or timestamp manipulation to win conflicts or extend tokens | B2 | A4 | medium | mitigated | FM-SYNC-002, FM-SYNC-003, FM-AUTH-001, FM-AUTH-003 |
| TM-011 | Unauthorized moderation or role escalation | B2, B5 | A4 | high | mitigated | FM-ID-002, FM-SYNC-003 |
| TM-012 | Replay of view, rotate, or push proofs within the freshness window | B2 | A1, A2 | medium | open | FM-AUTH-001, FM-AUTH-002 |
| TM-013 | Theft and replay of portable session bearer tokens | B7 | A1, A3 | medium | open | FM-AUTH-003 |
| TM-014 | Tunnelled node traffic trusts the relay as an authenticated intermediary | B2, B3 | A2 | high | open | FM-SIG-002 |
| TM-015 | Relay operator reads the outer room layer, including public channel plaintext and presence | B2, B5 | A2 | medium | open | FM-SIG-002 |
| TM-016 | Metadata leakage through the catalog, presence, routing, and timing | B2, B5 | A1, A2 | medium | open | FM-REL-001 |
| TM-017 | Parser, verifier, or fold resource exhaustion | B2 | A7, A4 | medium | mitigated | FM-ENC-005, FM-SIG-004 |
| TM-018 | Account key compromise or loss without a specified recovery protocol | B1 | A5 | high | open | FM-AUTH-004 |
| TM-019 | Data loss through lossy migration, down-conversion, or snapshot trust | B5, B6 | A2, A6 | high | mitigated | FM-MIG-001, FM-MIG-002, FM-MIG-003, FM-SYNC-001 |
| TM-020 | Substituting the pack body of an authorized HTTPS push | B2, B3 | A2 | high | mitigated | FM-AUTH-002, FM-REL-003 |

Open high-severity threats — TM-004, TM-006, TM-008, TM-014, and TM-018 — block
a stable suite release until they are mitigated or explicitly accepted.

## Discussion by class

**Replay.** Collaboration v1 binds repository, object, and policy inside the
signed bytes (TM-003). The legacy `forkmesh-issue-event-v1` family binds only
type, number, author, timestamp, and a content hash. The same signed record can
therefore be presented to another repository that has a matching issue number
(TM-004). The mitigation path is FM-MIG-002 migration to collaboration v1 plus
a relay rule that stops accepting legacy inbox records after the migration
window. Request proofs carry no nonce, so capture inside the five-minute window
permits replay (TM-012). Push proofs bind the method and body digest, so a
replay can only resubmit the identical pack.

**Downgrade.** Exact identifier matching and distinct prefixes defeat
cross-version confusion (TM-005). `forkmesh-catalog-v1` is still accepted for
public records. Descriptive fields and visibility are not signed under v1, and
the rollback check permits an equal `updatedAt`. A relay-level replayer could
therefore reissue an old public record (TM-006). Removing v1 acceptance is a
major suite change (see the compatibility policy).

**Equivocation.** A key signing two events in one sequence slot loses both
(TM-009). Detection needs both events in the same fold, so equivocation hidden
by withholding reduces to TM-008.

**Omission and availability.** No fold detects missing events (TM-008).
Closing it requires availability receipts or peer exchange that cross-checks
relay-delivered logs. Clone availability degrades to fail-closed, never to
unverified bytes (TM-007).

**Metadata leakage.** The relay learns public repository names, sizes, node
versions, presence, and request timing (TM-016). Private repository names never
enter the public routing index; private reads use opaque handles and ciphertext
([private repository
confidentiality](../security/private-repository-confidentiality.md)). By
design, default rooms use a relay-derivable key; private channels add a
recipient layer (TM-015, [sealed chat](../security/sealed-chat.md)). Telemetry
exports counts only.

**Abuse.** Size and depth limits bound parsing (TM-017). Verification caches
key on fixed-size digests. Catalog publication is rate-limited per owner.
Inbox signatures prove integrity, not reputation, and owner review gates every
merge.

**Recovery and data loss.** Signed raw bytes are the source of truth, and
snapshots are disposable (TM-019). Account key rotation requires the old key
(`forkmesh-rotate-v1`). Recovering from a lost or stolen key currently relies
on account credentials and the procedures in [portable
identities](../portable-identities.md). There is no normative, independently
verifiable recovery protocol yet (TM-018).

## Review

A security reviewer changes a threat's status only by editing `threats.json`
and this table together. The reviewer cites the requirement or test that closes
it, or records `acceptance` with reviewer, date, and rationale. The 2026-07
security audit is the origin of TM-004 and TM-014. This register does not
record any acceptance until a named reviewer signs one.

pages.description: Suite version: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Vectors: events.json, identifiers.json, signatures.json, sessions.json · Part of the ForkMesh protocol suite
pages.markdown:
# Version negotiation

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Vectors: `events.json`, `identifiers.json`,
`signatures.json`, `sessions.json` · Part of the [ForkMesh protocol
suite](README.md)

ForkMesh has no interactive handshake. Every signed or hashed structure
carries an explicit version identifier, and each receiver selects exactly one
verifier from it:

| Structure | Identifier | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Collaboration event | `forkmesh-collaboration-event-v1` | `schema` field and signing domain |
| Collaboration policy | `forkmesh-collaboration-policy-v1` | `schema` field |
| Collaboration state | `forkmesh-collaboration-state-v1` | `schema` field |
| Canonical-string schemes | `forkmesh-<scheme>-v<N>` | first line of the signed message |
| Catalog publication | `catalogSigVersion` 1 or 2 | request field; selects the scheme |
| Portable session | `v1.` token prefix and claim `v: 1` | token framing and claim |
| Repository migration | `forkmesh-repository-migration-v1`, `forkmesh-repository-migration-state-v1` | job and receipt `schema` |
| Room key proof | `forkmesh-room-key-v2` (v1 only for the compatibility room) | first line of the signed message |

The only advertised negotiation is the catalog upgrade response: HTTP 426
with `{"error": "client_upgrade_required", "requiredCatalogSigVersion": 2}`.
Git protocol v0/v2 negotiation belongs to stock Git.

- **FM-VER-001** MUST — Receivers match version identifiers exactly. They
  reject an unknown or future identifier with the structure's stable code
  (`unsupported_schema`, `invalid_policy`, `token_invalid`, `claim_invalid`),
  never parse it heuristically, and never ignore unknown fields in a signed
  structure.
- **FM-VER-002** MUST NOT — A receiver MUST NOT downgrade. A message that
  fails verification under its declared version is never retried under an
  older version's rules. An older version stays accepted only within its
  published scope: `forkmesh-catalog-v1` only for public records, and
  `forkmesh-room-key-v1` only for the public compatibility room. Because
  prefixes differ, a signature over one version never verifies as another.
- **FM-VER-003** MUST — The bytes an identifier covers are frozen. Any change
  to signed or hashed bytes, field order, normalization, or meaning requires a
  new identifier, and the committed vectors for the existing identifier stay
  unchanged.
- **FM-VER-004** MUST — A new identifier rolls out in a fixed order. First,
  readers that verify and preserve the new identifier deploy. Then writers
  begin emitting it. Readers keep accepting the previous identifier for as
  long as retained history contains it. Rollback reverses the order
  (FM-MIG-003).
