pages.description: Checked against main on 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-23 (Cloudflare stack), and again on 2026-09-27 after the move to self-hosted core nodes (issue #709).
pages.markdown:
# Relay data retention and deletion

Checked against main on **2026-09-16** and **2026-09-23** (Cloudflare stack),
and again on **2026-09-27** after the move to self-hosted core nodes (issue
#709).

This page covers the hosted relay behind `forkmesh.com`, `app.forkmesh.com`, and
`world.forkmesh.com`. For each store, backup, and outside processor it says what
the data is, how long it lasts, and what deletes it. Git objects and refs in
repositories published from desktops and mirror nodes are not relay data. The
relay cannot delete them (see [Copies the relay cannot
reach](#copies-the-relay-cannot-reach)).

Every row is **repository evidence** from the named source unless it is marked
**platform default** (a vendor or software default this repository does not
configure) or **missing proof**. "Until deleted" means no automatic limit
exists.

## Where the relay runs

On 2026-09-24 the relay moved off Cloudflare Workers. The same application code
(`app/src/`) now runs under `app/host/` on three core nodes, `fmnext-n1` to
`fmnext-n3`, rented from Vultr in the `ewr` (New Jersey, United States) region
(`deploy/fleet.toml`). The Cloudflare D1 database was deleted on 2026-09-27.
The `forkmesh-app` and `forkmesh-world` Workers were deleted the same day,
together with their Durable Object namespaces, the KV namespace, and the queue
([cutover record](../../docs/CUTOVER.md)).

- `app.forkmesh.com` and `world.forkmesh.com` resolve straight to the core
  nodes. Their DNS records at Cloudflare are not proxied.
- `forkmesh.com` and `www.forkmesh.com` are still served by the Cloudflare
  Worker `forkmesh-www`. It fetches pages from the core nodes and forwards the
  visitor's IP address and country in a signed header.

## Live stores

The application still declares its bindings in `app/wrangler.toml`. On the core
nodes `app/host/forkmesh_host/env.py` maps each binding to a local
implementation.

| Store | Replaces | What it holds | Retention | Deletion path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| rqlite database (`DB`) | D1 `forkmesh` | Accounts, repository catalog, collaboration inboxes, chat backlog, health, status, analytics, memberships, package data, and Durable Object storage. See [Database tables](#database-tables-rqlite) | Per table below | Per table below. Every core node holds a full replicated copy in `/var/lib/forkmesh-next/rqlite` |
| KV `REPOSITORY_METADATA` | Cloudflare KV | Cached repository-page JSON, in a separate SQLite file on each core node (`kv-repository_metadata.sqlite`). Not replicated and not backed up | Until overwritten. Writes set no expiry (`app/src/entry.py`) | No delete call exists. **Missing proof:** deleting an account or repository does not remove its cached page JSON |
| KV `admission-override:*` keys | Cloudflare KV | Blind-indexed repository id plus a time window, on the core node that handled the admin request | 30 minutes by default, 6 hours at most | Unreadable once expired; the row itself is removed only when it is read again |
| Durable Objects `ForkMeshRoom`, `ForkMeshNoteRoom`, `ForkMeshWorld`, `ForkMeshOfficeRoom` | Durable Objects | Sockets and live presence, in memory on the core node that owns each object. Kept chat messages go to `chat_history` | Socket lifetime | Socket close |
| Durable Objects `ForkMeshNodes`, `ForkMeshCronWatchdog`, `ForkMeshCronRunner`, `ForkMeshDiscordGate` | Durable Objects | Node push sockets, the latest commit target per repository, cron progress, and Discord rate buckets. Their storage is the `do_storage` and `do_alarms` tables, so it is replicated and backed up | Overwritten on each push or tick; rate buckets expire | Overwritten or expired |
| Queue `forkmesh-notification-email` | Cloudflare Queues | A wake-up naming the recipient, held in the memory of one app process | Until delivered; at most 3 retries; lost on restart, when the per-minute cron picks the work up | Consumed |
| Response cache | Cloudflare edge cache | Public pages and API responses, at most 8 MiB in memory per core node | Their `Cache-Control` lifetimes | Account delete purges catalog entries on the node that ran it only; the others expire |
| Hosted Git repositories | New | Repositories created on the website, a full copy on every core node under `/var/lib/forkmesh/hosted/` ([hosted repositories](../../docs/HOSTED_REPOS.md)) | Until removed | Removal moves each copy to `.trash`. **Missing proof:** nothing ever deletes `.trash`; an operator empties it by hand |
| AI binding (`AI`) | Workers AI | Nothing. No AI provider is configured on the core nodes, so ForkBot and username moderation run without one | None | None needed |

No object store, analytics dataset, or vector index is configured.

## Database tables (rqlite)

Migrations are in `app/migrations/`; `app/src/schema.py` adds a few runtime
tables. Rows marked "account delete" are removed by the account deletion
described [below](#what-account-deletion-removes). Every deletion below also
stays in the [backups](#backups-and-copies) until they age out.

| Data family | Representative tables | Retention | Deletion path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts | `users`, `nodes`, `role_grants`, `owner_encryption_keys` | Until deleted | Account delete, by the user or an admin |
| Sessions | `account_sessions` | 5 years and 1 day; expired sessions, and revoked ones after 24 hours, are removed on the next login | Account delete; sign out; Settings revokes every device |
| Devices and keys | `account_devices`, `account_ssh_keys` | Stale devices 60 days | Account delete; removing the device or key |
| Push tokens | `apns_device_tokens` | 180 days without use | Token unregister. **Missing proof:** account delete leaves them |
| Sign-in throttles | `login_attempts`, `signup_rate`, `password_reset_rate`, `ai_ask_rate` | One rolling window each (15 minutes to 24 hours) | Overwritten when the window rolls; account delete removes `login_attempts` |
| Repository catalog and health | `repositories`, `repo_shares`, `repo_forks`, `repo_stars`, `repo_device_mirrors`, `mirror_repository_integrity`, `repo_security_scans` | Until deleted | Repository delete or account delete |
| Repository deletion tombstones | `repo_deletions` | 90 days | Expires on its own |
| Hosted repository records | `hosted_repos`, `hosted_repo_copies` | Marked deleted on removal, then dropped from replica exchange after 30 days | **Missing proof:** rows are never deleted, and account delete leaves them |
| Collaboration inboxes | `issue_inbox`, `pull_inbox`, `discussion_inbox` | Until drained or deleted | Repository delete or account delete. Records already committed to Git travel with the repository |
| Chat backlog | `chat_history` (encrypted envelopes) | 7 days, at most 500 messages and 16 MiB per room. A direct message is deleted as soon as the other person's device acknowledges it | Receipt from the recipient (direct messages); hourly sweep; message delete; room delete; account delete removes DMs and repository rooms |
| Notes and calendar | `notes`, `note_versions`, `calendar_events` | Until deleted | Per-item delete. **Missing proof:** account delete leaves them |
| World floor notes | `world_floor_notes`, `world_floor_note_replies` | Until deleted | Per-item delete; account delete |
| Organizations | `org_*`, `organization_task_*` | Until deleted | Organization delete or member removal |
| Notifications | `notifications` | 90 days, at most 500 per recipient | Account delete |
| Email delivery records | `mail_sends`, `mailtrap_email_sends`, `mailtrap_webhook_events` | 90 days | Expires on its own. Account delete removes `feedback_email_sends` only |
| Email suppressions | `mail_suppressions` (blind-indexed recipient and reason) | Until deleted | **Missing proof:** no delete path exists |
| Federation | `ap_outbox`, `ap_objects`, `ap_followers`, `ap_remote_actors` | Outbox row until delivered, refused, or 8 attempts; objects until deleted | Per-object delete sends a federated delete that peers may ignore |
| Security audit | `sensitive_audit_log` | 365 days | Expires on its own |
| Intrusion detection | `security_incidents`, `cluster_quarantine` ([IDS](../../docs/IDS.md)) | Until deleted | **Missing proof:** no delete path exists |
| Error and diagnostic logs | `error_log`, `install_diag`, `feedback` | Newest 5,000 rows each | Row cap; admin console delete |
| Bug reports | `bug_reports`, `discord_bug_reports` | Until deleted | **Missing proof:** no automatic or account delete found |
| Site analytics | `attribution_sessions`, `attribution_events` | 400 days (`ATTRIBUTION_RETENTION_DAYS`); IP digest 24 hours; `fm_attr` cookie 90 days | Delete button on the [privacy page](../public/privacy.html); daily sweep |
| Flagship read failures | `flagship_read_failure_minute` (a count per minute, no request data) | 24 hours | Expires on its own. `api_metrics_minute` was dropped by migration 0190 |
| Referrals | `referral_attributions`, `referral_click_seen`, `referral_stats` | Click records 35 days, click audit 180 days | Account delete |
| Presence and online counts | `account_presence`, `host_presence`, `online_hourly*`, `world_*` presence | 10 minutes to 30 days | Expires on its own; account delete |
| Status history | `system_status_minute`, `system_status_hourly`, `system_status_daily` | Minute rows 30 hours; hourly and daily 30 days | Expires on its own |
| Cron ticks | `cron_tick`, `host_cron_runs` | 6 hours and 24 hours | Expires on its own |
| Memberships | `patreon_*`, `plan_trials`, `role_grants` | Membership rows until deleted; webhook events 90 days | Account delete removes the Patreon link, trials, and grants. Migration 0189 dropped every `polar_*` table |
| Ledger and rewards | `funds_received`, `wallet_balances`, `reward_*`, `legacy_custody_*` | Until deleted | **Missing proof:** no documented deletion; financial records may need to be kept |
| Repository webhooks | `repo_webhooks` (encrypted URL and signing secret), `repo_webhook_outbox`, `repo_webhook_deliveries` | Outbox row until delivered or 6 attempts; newest 20 deliveries per webhook | Webhook delete; repository delete; account delete |
| GitHub and GitLab mirrors | `repo_provider_mirrors` (encrypted access token, remote name and settings), `repo_provider_mirror_links` (which issue numbers correspond), `repo_provider_mirror_outbox` (encrypted queued items) | Until the owner disconnects the mirror; outbox row until delivered or 6 attempts | Disconnect in repository settings; repository delete; account delete |
| Desktop commands | `desktop_commands` | 24 hours | Expires on its own |
| Runner tier | `runner_nodes`, `runner_job_leases`, `runner_login_sessions`, `runner_login_chunks` | Runners until removed; sign-in terminals deleted shortly after they end | Sweeps; runner removal |
| Third-party apps | `apps`, `app_installs`, `app_tokens`, `app_reviews`, `app_deliveries` | Until deleted | App delete. **Missing proof:** account delete leaves an account's installs, tokens, and reviews |
| Market ratings | `marketplace_reviews`, `marketplace_review_history`, `marketplace_review_reports` | Until deleted | **Missing proof:** account delete leaves them |
| Code challenges | `code_challenges`, `code_challenge_members` | Until deleted | Challenge delete; leaving. **Missing proof:** account delete leaves them |
| Ad network | `ad_network_ads`, `ad_network_reports`, `ad_network_reviews`, `ad_network_daily_stats` | Ads until deleted; click counts 400 days (`STATS_RETENTION_DAYS`) | Ad delete; account delete removes ads, reports, and counts. **Missing proof:** review records stay |
| Account-scoped packages | Calorie Counter `calories_*`, Password Vault `vault_*` (end-to-end encrypted items) | Until deleted | Per-account package uninstall; account delete runs each package's `purge_account_data` |
| Organization-scoped packages | CRM `crm_*`, Marketing `marketing_*`, Competitor `competitor_*` | Until deleted | Organization uninstall offers an export, purges that organization's rows, and drops the tables after the last uninstall; organization delete does the same (`app/src/plugin_data.py`) |
| Public snapshots | `public_catalog_snapshot`, `public_api_snapshots` | Replaced on republish | Account delete schedules a republish |
| Host secrets | `host_secrets` (application secrets encrypted under `DATA_KEY`, [vault](../../docs/VAULT.md)) | Until replaced | Operator vault sync. Not user data |

## What account deletion removes

Deleting an account from profile settings, or through the audited admin route
`POST /api/accounts/admin-delete`, runs `_delete_account_namespace` in
`app/src/entry.py`. The core nodes run the same code as the Cloudflare Worker
did. It removes:

- the account's repositories and every repository-scoped row, including inboxes,
  scans, mirrors, shares, forks, and repository chat rooms;
- `users` and `nodes` rows, sessions, devices, SSH keys, login lockout rows, and
  pending verifications;
- notifications, follows, referrals, contribution profile rows, stars, role
  grants, owner encryption keys, plan trials, the Patreon link, World and
  office participation rows, World floor notes and their replies, and
  organization task check-ins;
- the account's ads with their reports and click counts, and every
  account-scoped package's rows (Calorie Counter, Password Vault);
- channel memberships and direct conversations;
- cached catalog pages on the core node that ran the deletion, followed by a
  public catalog republish.

**Missing proof:** it leaves these rows keyed to the account or its content:
`notes`, `calendar_events`, `apns_device_tokens`, `org_members`,
`hosted_repos`, `app_installs`, `app_tokens`, `app_reviews`,
`marketplace_reviews`, `code_challenges`, `mail_suppressions`,
`mail_sends` and `mailtrap_email_sends` (removed after 90 days anyway),
`sensitive_audit_log` (365 days), `attribution_sessions` (400 days),
`error_log` actor fields (row cap), `ad_network_reviews`, federated `ap_*`
objects, bug reports, KV `REPOSITORY_METADATA` on every core node, and the
response caches of the other core nodes until they expire.

## Backups and copies

| Copy | What it holds | Retention | Deletion path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nightly rqlite backups | The whole database, taken from the Raft leader at 03:30 UTC, checked, and encrypted with age on the operator's machine (`tools/next_backup.py`) | The newest backup of each of the last 7 days and of each of the last 4 weeks | Ages out. Deleted rows stay in older backups for up to about 4 weeks, and a restore brings them back, so deletions must be replayed |
| rqlite files on each core node | Raft log, snapshots, and the SQLite write-ahead log | **Platform default:** rqlite's snapshot and log truncation; no secure-delete or vacuum step is configured | Overwritten over time |
| Final D1 export (2026-09-27) | Every row of the deleted Cloudflare database, as SQL and as an age-encrypted copy, on the operator's machine ([cutover record](../../docs/CUTOVER.md)) | **Missing proof:** no retention period. Backup pruning skips it | **Missing proof:** no deletion step. Accounts deleted later remain in it |
| Old-stack archive (2026-09-24) and retired Worker export (2026-09-27) | The D1 export taken at the cutover, Durable Object state, and every `REPOSITORY_METADATA` value, on the operator's machine | Kept as the rollback record | **Missing proof:** no deletion step |
| Manual D1 exports before the move | SQL files and SQLite snapshots used before migrations and audits ([cleanup plan](operations/d1-database-cleanup-plan.md), [legacy custody migration](operations/legacy-solana-custody-migration.md)) | **Missing proof:** no retention period and no storage location are documented | **Missing proof:** no deletion step |
| D1 Time Travel | Point-in-time history of the deleted `forkmesh` database | **Missing proof:** nothing records whether Cloudflare kept any history after the deletion | None from the relay |
| Hosted repository `.trash` | Removed hosted repositories on every core node | Until an operator empties it | By hand only |
| GitHub Actions artifacts | Disaster-recovery drill evidence, no user data | 30 days | Expires on its own |

## Logs

| Log | What it holds | Retention | Deletion path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Core node journal | App errors with tracebacks, per-route request counts, the text of each database statement without its values, and Postfix delivery lines with recipient addresses ([node logs](../../docs/NODE_LOGS.md)) | At most 64 MiB per node, split into files of up to one week (`deploy/core/templates/journald.conf`); no time limit | Rotated out by size |
| Caddy access log | Path, status, and timing, with client addresses masked to /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6), headers dropped, and credential query parameters replaced | In the core node journal, as above | Rotated out by size |
| Mail event spool | One file per delivery result, with the recipient address | 3 days | Pruned by the mail event agent |
| `forkmesh-www` Worker logs and traces | 5% sample of logs; every request traced and kept | **Platform default:** the Cloudflare plan's log and trace retention | Ages out; no relay delete |

## Outside processors

Details and sources for services outside the core nodes are in the [external
dependency map](external-dependency-map.md), which still describes the relay as
it ran on Cloudflare (see [Known gaps](#known-gaps)).

| Processor | Relay data it receives | Retention | Deletion path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vultr | Hosts the core nodes and their disks: every store above, the journal, and hosted repositories. Automatic Vultr backups are off | Until the instance is destroyed | Destroying the instance |
| Cloudflare | DNS for every name; Turnstile checks on signup and password reset; for `forkmesh.com` only, every request (IP, headers, path, timing) through the `forkmesh-www` Worker | Its plan's retention | Logs age out |
| Recipients' mail servers | Account email, sent directly by Postfix on the core nodes. Mailtrap is no longer used for sending | The receiver's | The receiver's operator |
| Sentry (optional) | Redacted route, status, and stack locations; no IP or query strings | Operator's Sentry organization | Sentry project settings |
| Patreon | Email, pledge or membership state, and membership webhooks | Vendor retention | Vendor account; unlinking |
| Polar and Mailtrap (retired) | Nothing new. Their own records of past subscriptions and sent mail remain | Vendor retention | Vendor account |
| AI coding providers used by the runner tier | Repository code and prompts of agent jobs that the account starts on the pool runner | Each provider's; runner session homes are removed 14 days after last use ([runners](../../docs/RUNNERS.md)) | Provider account |
| Repository webhook receivers | Event payloads for the repository, sent to URLs its owner configures | The receiver's | The receiver's operator |
| Open Food Facts, USDA FoodData Central | Barcodes and food search text from Calorie Counter, with no account identifier | Each service's | None needed |
| Apple Push Notification service | Device token and a fixed "New activity" alert with no sender or content | Apple's | Token unregister; pruned on permanent failure |
| Discord | Discord user id, the #bugs channel messages the bot reads and replies to, and bridged organization channel messages | Discord's | Discord |
| ActivityPub peers | Public federated posts | Each peer's | Federated delete, which peers may ignore |
| PostHog (opt-in only) | A coarse page category and fixed action names, never under Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control | Operator's PostHog project | PostHog project settings |

## Copies the relay cannot reach

- **Mirror nodes** hold Git bytes, including `.forkmesh` issue, pull, and
  discussion records. Removing a repository from the catalog does not delete a
  mirror's copy, and a mirror operator's own backups follow
  [node backup and recovery](operations/node-backup-and-recovery.md), whose
  example timer removes archives older than 14 days.
- **Desktops** keep sessions, identities, transcripts, logs, and mirrors
  locally. `www/public/uninstall.sh --purge` deletes them on that machine only
  and touches no relay data.
- **Git history** cannot be recalled once cloned.

## Known gaps

Each gap is **missing proof** that a launch reader can ask about:

1. There is no user data export API.
2. Account deletion leaves the rows listed [above](#what-account-deletion-removes).
3. KV `REPOSITORY_METADATA` entries never expire and are never deleted, on any
   core node.
4. Deleted rows stay in the nightly backups for about 4 weeks, and no step
   replays deletions after a restore.
5. The final D1 export, the old-stack archive, and the retired Worker export
   have no documented retention or deletion.
6. Removed hosted repositories stay in `.trash` on every core node until an
   operator deletes them by hand.
7. The [external dependency map](external-dependency-map.md) still lists D1,
   KV, Durable Objects, Queues, Workers AI, and Mailtrap as live, and has no
   entry for Vultr as the relay's host or for direct mail delivery.

Update this page with any change to `app/wrangler.toml` bindings,
`app/host/forkmesh_host/env.py`, the backup retention in `tools/next_backup.py`,
a new retention sweep, or a change to `_delete_account_namespace`.

pages.title: Searchable public repository index
pages.description: The public index lets anyone find an active, trustworthy project and clone it without an account and without already knowing its ForkMesh URL. This page is the published…
pages.markdown:
# Searchable public repository index

The public index lets anyone find an active, trustworthy project and clone it
without an account and without already knowing its ForkMesh URL. This page is
the published methodology: it describes exactly what
`app/src/repository_index.py` does, and changes to the ranking must update
this page in the same commit.

Tracking issue: #478.

## Endpoint

```
GET /api/repositories/search?q=<text>&view=<view>&limit=<1-50>&cursor=<token>
                            &language=<name>&topic=<name>&owner=<account>
                            &cloneable=1
```

No authentication. The response is public catalog data only (it never
includes private or shared repositories, even for a signed-in caller) and
may be cached for 30 seconds.

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `q` | Up to 8 words. Every word must match the name, owner, a topic, a language, or the description. |
| `view` | `relevance` (default when `q` is set), `updated` (default otherwise), `trending`, `new`, `discussions`. |
| `limit` | Page size, 1–50, default 20. |
| `cursor` | The previous page's `nextCursor`. A cursor is bound to its query; reusing it with different filters answers `400 cursor_query_mismatch`. |
| `language`, `topic` | Exact, case-insensitive facet filters. |
| `owner` | The publishing account or the organization that owns the repository. |
| `cloneable` | `1` keeps only repositories with a healthy clone endpoint right now. |

Malformed parameters answer `400` with one of `unknown_view`,
`relevance_requires_query`, `invalid_limit`, `invalid_cloneable`,
`invalid_cursor`, or `cursor_query_mismatch`. If no catalog can be read, the
endpoint answers `503 catalog_unavailable` rather than an empty result.

Every result carries:

- `identity` — the provider-independent repository identity
  (`urn:forkmesh:repository:sha256:…`, derived from the signed root commit),
  shared by every mirror and unchanged by renames or host moves. It is empty
  when the record has no root commit. See
  [dependency workflows](dependency-workflows.md).
- `clone.https` and `clone.command` — a copy-ready `git clone` of the
  repository's durable public address, with `clone.requiresAccount: false`.
  `clone.ssh` appears only when the SSH gateway is configured.
- `maintainer` — the publishing account, the owning organization when there
  is one, the maintainer's public key, and
  `verification: "account-key-signed-catalog-record"`.
- `availability` — `cloneOnline` (a fresh, healthy, integrity-verified mirror
  endpoint can serve it now), and the number of independent mirrors.
- `activity`, `freshness`, `duplicates`, and `ranking` — the exact inputs and
  sort key that placed it where it is.

The response also reports `total`, `facets` (language and topic counts over
all matches, plus how many are cloneable), `withheld` (how many catalog rows
each rule removed), `freshness`, and `budgets`.

## Budgets

| Budget | Value | How it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Freshness | 6 minutes | Results are ranked from the published catalog snapshot, which is republished when the catalog changes and expires after 6 minutes. `freshness.snapshotAgeMs` and `freshness.withinBudget` report the actual age on every response. An expired snapshot falls back to the live anonymous catalog (at most 30 seconds old). |
| Latency | 250 ms ranking | Ranking over a full 200-repository catalog is covered by an automated budget test. The route reads one D1 row; it never decrypts the repository table while a snapshot is current. |
| Page size | 50 | `limit` above 50 is rejected, not silently truncated. |

## Determinism and pagination

Results are sorted by a full key that always ends in the unique
`owner/name`, so equal scores never reorder between requests. Pagination is
keyset-based: `nextCursor` encodes the last result's sort key, and the next
page starts strictly after it. Walking every cursor over one snapshot returns
each match exactly once. When the snapshot changes between pages, results
that moved behind the cursor are not repeated. `nextCursor` is `null` on the
last page.

## Views

All scores are integers built only from signed repository facts.

- **relevance** — per word: name exact 100, name prefix 40, name contains 20;
  owner exact 30 or contains 10; topic exact 15; language exact 15;
  description contains 5. Ties sort by most recent activity.
- **updated** — most recent head-commit time, or the signed record time when
  the publisher did not report a commit time.
- **trending** — commits plus merges over the last 4 weekly buckets, each
  week capped at 50, plus 5 points per independent mirror (at most 8 mirrors
  count).
- **new** — the publisher's signed hosted-since time, newest first.
  Repositories without one are left out of this view.
- **discussions** — open discussions plus pull requests plus open issues,
  each capped at 500.

Trending and discussions leave out repositories whose signed record is older
than 14 days, and repositories with a zero score. Those repositories stay
searchable.

## Moderation and anti-manipulation rules

Before a row can appear:

1. It must be in the public catalog, which accepts only records signed by the
   account's key. Private records, records shared with a viewer, blocked
   identities, and repositories with an active Terms flag are withheld.
2. It must name an owner, a repository, and a maintainer key.

Deduplication and manipulation resistance:

- **One result per repository.** Mirror rows (a different machine or account
  serving the same repository) are never separate results. They only add to
  the canonical repository's mirror count.
- **Self-mirroring does not count.** Only mirrors run by a different account
  count as independent. Extra devices on the owner's own account, and accounts
  that republished the same content, add nothing.
- **Republished content is collapsed.** Two catalog records with the same
  head commit are byte-identical history. The earliest hosted publisher (then
  alphabetical) is the result, and the others are listed in `duplicates`.
- **Replay and bulk history are bounded.** The catalog rejects a record older
  than the one it already holds (`stale_update`), so an old signed record
  cannot be replayed to restore a past ranking. Weekly activity is capped, so
  generated or rewritten history cannot buy unlimited trending weight.
- **Heartbeats do not rank.** Republishing an unchanged record does not
  change any score, because scores ignore the record's publish timestamp in
  favour of commit time and activity buckets.
- **Self-reported traffic is not a signal.** Clone and page-view counters
  come from the serving node and could be inflated by cloning oneself, so no
  view ranks on them.
- **Clocks are bounded.** A hosted-since or commit time more than 5 minutes
  in the future is ignored.

Reports of spam or abuse go through the existing Terms flag process. An
active flag removes the repository from every view on the next snapshot.

## From result to clone

A result's `clone.command` works with stock Git and no ForkMesh account:

```
curl -s 'https://app.forkmesh.com/api/repositories/search?q=mesh&cloneable=1&limit=1' \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["results"][0]["clone"]["command"])'
```

The clone URL is the repository's public address, not a particular mirror,
so it keeps working after the machine that answered today goes away.

## Not covered yet

- The dashboard repository list still filters client-side. It does not call
  this endpoint yet.
- Privacy-safe `index_search` and `index_result_open` events are not emitted,
  so search-to-result conversion cannot be measured yet (see
  `docs/experiments/public-index-search-to-clone-2026-09.md`).
- Maintainer verification is key-based. There is no separate human identity
  check.

pages.title: Start your own instance from a settings file
pages.description: The Start your own instance page can be filled in from one zip file that holds your settings and your logo. Upload the zip (or drop it on the page) and every field is set…
pages.markdown:
# Start your own instance from a settings file

The [Start your own instance](https://app.forkmesh.com/start) page can be
filled in from one zip file that holds your settings and your logo. Upload
the zip (or drop it on the page) and every field is set: project name, logo,
server, address, admin account, organization owners and email. When nothing
is missing, the page shows **Start my instance now**, so the whole setup is
one click.

Download the example:
[start-config.example.zip](https://app.forkmesh.com/start-config.example.zip).
It holds two files:

- `forkmesh-instance.json`, the settings below;
- `logo.svg`, the logo.

Edit the settings, put your own logo in place of `logo.svg`, and zip the two
files again. The settings alone are also
[start-config.example.json](https://app.forkmesh.com/start-config.example.json),
and the page's **Copy example settings** button copies them to the clipboard.

## The zip

- It needs exactly one `.json` file: the settings.
- The logo is the image the settings name in `logo` (for example
  `"logo": "logo.svg"`). Without a name, the zip's only image is the logo.
  With several images, name the one to use.
- The logo is a PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG image of up to 200 KB; the zip is up
  to 1 MB.
- Files in a folder inside the zip are found too; `__MACOSX` folders and
  hidden files are skipped, so a zip made with Finder or Windows works.
- Zips with a password cannot be read.

You can still upload the `.json` file on its own; then the logo is not
included, and you can add it with the form's **Upload logo**.

## The file

```json
{
  "projectName": "Acme Code",
  "logo": "logo.svg",
  "host": "203.0.113.10",
  "sshUser": "root",
  "port": 22,
  "sshPassword": "change-me-ssh-password",
  "sshPrivateKey": "",
  "sshPassphrase": "",
  "hostKeyFingerprint": "",
  "domain": "code.example.com",
  "adminUsername": "ada",
  "adminEmail": "ada@example.com",
  "adminPassword": "change-me-admin-password",
  "ownerType": "org",
  "ownerName": "acme",
  "owners": [
    {
      "username": "grace",
      "email": "grace@example.com",
      "password": "change-me-grace-password"
    },
    {
      "username": "linus",
      "email": "linus@example.com",
      "password": "change-me-linus-password"
    }
  ],
  "mailProvider": "none",
  "mailApiKey": "",
  "mailFrom": "",
  "mailgunDomain": "",
  "mailgunRegion": "us",
  "ownWorld": true,
  "listOnHomepage": true
}
```

Every setting is optional in the file: anything left out keeps what the form
already has, and the page then points at the first field that still needs a
value. Keys that start with `_` or `$` (such as `"_docs"`) are notes and are
skipped. Any other key the page does not know is listed after the upload and
skipped.

| Setting | Form field | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `projectName` | Project name | Up to 40 letters, numbers, spaces and `._&+-` |
| `theme` | Colour theme | Optional; `crimson`, or empty for ForkMesh's default colours |
| `logo` | Logo | Optional; the name of the logo image in the zip, such as `logo.svg` (a `data:image/…;base64,…` URL also works) |
| `host` | Server IP address | The server's public IP address or host name |
| `sshUser` | SSH user | Default `root` |
| `port` | SSH port | 1 to 65535, default `22` |
| `sshPassword` | SSH password | Sign in with a password |
| `sshPrivateKey` | Private key | Sign in with a key instead; the whole key file as one string |
| `sshPassphrase` | Key passphrase | Only if the key has one |
| `hostKeyFingerprint` | Host key fingerprint | Optional, `SHA256:` followed by 43 characters |
| `domain` | Domain | Optional; empty starts on a free `sslip.io` address |
| `adminUsername` | Username | Lowercase letters, numbers and dashes, starting with a letter |
| `adminEmail` | Email | The admin's email address |
| `adminPassword` | Password | At least 10 characters |
| `ownerType` | Repository belongs to | `org` (an organization) or `user` (the admin) |
| `ownerName` | Organization name | Used when `ownerType` is `org`; must differ from the admin username |
| `owners` | Other owners | Optional, `org` only; up to 20 people who own the organization with the admin, each `{"username", "email", "password"}` |
| `mailProvider` | Email service | `none`, `mailtrap`, `sendgrid` or `mailgun` |
| `mailApiKey` | API key | Needed unless `mailProvider` is `none` |
| `mailFrom` | Send from | Optional, default `no-reply@<domain>` |
| `mailgunDomain` | Mailgun sending domain | Needed for Mailgun |
| `mailgunRegion` | Mailgun region | `us` or `eu` |
| `ownWorld` | Give my instance its own world | `true` (default) or `false`; a hexagon joined to the ForkMesh World with a small landmark and your logo |
| `listOnHomepage` | List my instance on forkmesh.com | `true` (default) or `false`; your name and logo in the homepage's list of instances |

### Other owners

The admin always owns the organization. Everyone listed in `owners` gets an
account on your instance and owns the organization too, with the same rights
as the admin there (they are not instance admins). Each needs:

- `username`: lowercase letters, numbers and dashes, starting with a letter;
  different from the admin, the organization and the other owners;
- `email`: an address of their own;
- `password`: at least 10 characters. Give it to them; they can change it
  after they sign in.

On the page they appear under **Other owners** in section 4, where you can
add more with **Add an owner** or remove them.

### Password or key

Give `sshPassword` or `sshPrivateKey`. When the file has a key, the page signs
in with the key. A key goes in as one JSON string with `\n` line breaks; to
turn a key file into that string:

```sh
python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps(open(sys.argv[1]).read()))' ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

You can also leave the key out of the file and upload it in the form's
**Private key** box after loading the settings.

## Keep the file private

The file holds your server's password or key, your admin password and the
other owners' passwords. The page reads it in your browser only: it is not uploaded on its own and not
kept. Only the settings sent with **Start my instance** go to ForkMesh, the
same as when you type them, and the secret fields are cleared once the setup
starts. Delete the file, or remove the passwords from it, when your instance
is running.

What happens after you press start, step by step, is on the page itself and
in `docs/INSTANCES.md` in the source.

pages.title: Synchronization status
pages.description: Every repository and collaboration object explains where it has reached, how many copies were verified, and whether what you see is current or conflicted. The web app, desktop…
pages.markdown:
# Synchronization status

Every repository and collaboration object explains where it has reached, how
many copies were verified, and whether what you see is current or conflicted.
The web app, desktop, mobile, the mirror node, the API, and the CLI all use one
state model, `forkmesh-sync-status-v1`, so the same evidence reads the same way
everywhere.

## States

| State | Severity | Current | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `queued` | info | no | A synchronization is waiting to start. |
| `syncing` | info | no | A synchronization is in flight and within its deadline. |
| `verified` | ok | yes | Every copy holds the latest state with a verified signature, confirmed within the last hour. |
| `degraded` | warning | yes | Enough copies are verified, but at least one is offline, behind, unverified, or rejected. |
| `stale` | warning | no | Nothing confirms the latest state recently: copies are offline, the sync missed its deadline, or the last confirmation is over an hour old. |
| `conflicted` | error | no | Copies disagree about the latest state and someone has to choose. |
| `paused` | info | no | An owner or operator paused synchronization. |
| `external-only` | info | no | The object so far exists only at an external provider (for example, a GitHub import that has not been mirrored yet). |
| `failed` | error | no | A copy rejected the update or synchronization reported an error. |

Only `verified` and `degraded` count as current. Nothing reports success
without a verified copy of the latest state, and a conflict always outranks
success.

## What each status contains

```json
{
  "schema": "forkmesh-sync-status-v1",
  "state": "degraded",
  "label": "Degraded",
  "severity": "warning",
  "current": true,
  "totalCopies": 3,
  "nodesReached": 2,
  "verifiedCopies": 2,
  "trustedMirrors": 1,
  "lastConfirmedAt": 1799999970000,
  "lagMs": 180000,
  "error": "unreachable",
  "action": "One or more copies could not be reached; check that the mirrors are online.",
  "summary": "Verified, but some copies are not current. 2 of 3 copies verified, 1 trusted mirror, 2 nodes reached. Last confirmed just now. 3 min behind the source. One or more copies could not be reached; check that the mirrors are online."
}
```

- **Nodes reached**: copies that answered, including ones that rejected the update.
- **Verified copies**: copies holding the latest state with a verified signed attestation.
- **Trusted mirrors**: verified copies admitted to serve clones.
- **Last confirmation**: the newest confirmation from a verified copy.
- **Lag**: how long ago the source changed, while not every copy has the change.
- **Error and action**: a code from a closed list, plus what to do about it.

## Privacy

A status is built only from counts, timestamps, and fixed wording. Node names,
peer addresses, private object names, and raw error messages in the evidence
are never repeated. An error code a client does not recognize is reported as
`unknown`, so the status is safe to show to anyone who can see that the object
exists. The shared fixture plants private strings in its evidence, and every
client's test fails if one of them appears in the output.

## Where it appears

| Client | Where | Implementation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API | `syncStatus` on `GET /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/mirrors` | `app/src/sync_status.py` |
| Web | Mirrors tab status line on the repository page | renders the API's `syncStatus` |
| Desktop | Mirror nodes summary (hover for the full explanation) | `desktop/src/SyncStatusModel.h` |
| iOS | Repository Mirrors tab | `native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMAccount/SyncStatus.swift` |
| Android | Repository Mirrors tab | `native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/api/SyncStatus.kt` |
| Mirror node | `syncStatus` in the loopback `/v1/status` and `/readyz` responses | `server/syncstatus.go` |
| CLI | `tools/forkmesh_sync_status.py` | reuses the API implementation |

The mirrors payload maps each row to one copy: an offline row is unreachable;
an online row with integrity `rejected` is rejected; `behind` or integrity
`healing` is behind; otherwise the row is current. It counts as verified when
integrity is `ok`, and as trusted when `cloneAvailable` or `endpointHealthy` is
true.

## CLI

```sh
tools/forkmesh_sync_status.py explain evidence.json           # Degraded: Verified, but ...
tools/forkmesh_sync_status.py explain --json evidence.json    # machine-readable status
curl -s https://app.forkmesh.com/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/mirrors \
  | tools/forkmesh_sync_status.py explain --mirrors -
tools/forkmesh_sync_status.py fixture                         # verify the shared fixture
```

`explain` exits 0 when the state is current, 3 when it is not, and 2 when the
input is unreadable. `fixture` exits 1 on any mismatch.

## Conformance

- `conformance/sync-status/v1/model.json` sets out the states, precedence, wording, and policy (`staleAfterMs` 1 hour, `syncDeadlineMs` 15 minutes).
- `conformance/sync-status/v1/fixture.json` holds evidence cases, offline, delayed, rejected, and conflict sequences that each end recovered, and mirrors-payload cases, all with their exact expected output.
- `conformance/sync-status/v1/generate_fixture.py` regenerates the expected output from the reference implementation. Every entry also records a hand-written expected state, so a reference change that moves a state fails loudly. Run it with `--check` in CI.

Every implementation compares its full output with the fixture:

| Suite | Command |
| --- | --- |
| API, CLI, web | `python -m pytest app/tests/test_sync_status.py` |
| Mirror node | `cd server && go test -run SyncStatus .` |
| Desktop | `forkmesh-control-tests` |
| iOS | `cd native/ios/ForkMeshCore && swift test --filter SyncStatusTests` |
| Android | `cd native/android && ./gradlew :core:coreTest -Pfilter=SyncStatus` |

To change the model, edit `model.json` and the reference implementation, run
`generate_fixture.py`, then update each client until its suite passes. Adding
`syncStatus` is additive, so older clients ignore it. Rolling back the Worker
removes the field, and the desktop and mobile clients keep deriving the status
from the mirror rows.

pages.markdown:
# Transports and anonymity postures

Use this guide to choose how a device reaches repositories and how much it may
reveal on the way. A transport can be the open internet, Tor or I2P, an overlay
network such as a WireGuard mesh, or only the local network. You might need
this because your address must stay private, because a network blocks direct
access, or because a team shares code only inside a building.

`tools/forkmesh_transports.py` does five things:

1. **Plans** a route for a repository URL from a profile. The profile lists the
   adapters this device has and one posture that decides which adapters may
   be used.
2. **Runs Git** over the first permitted route that answers. If that route
   fails, it moves to the next permitted one and never to a route the posture
   forbids.
3. **Traces** the Git process in the private postures. Any DNS query or
   connection outside the route marks the run `exposed`.
4. **Probes** every permitted route and reports one state: reachable,
   degraded, unreachable, anonymous, or exposed.
5. **Chooses which of this device's addresses** a posture lets peers learn, and
   says whether it can accept inbound connections behind NAT.

The profile is `forkmesh-transport-profile-v1`. A plan is
`forkmesh-transport-plan-v1`, a health report is
`forkmesh-transport-health-v1`, an advertisement is
`forkmesh-transport-advertisement-v1`, and a telemetry line is
`forkmesh-transport-telemetry-v1`. Route-planning vectors live in
`conformance/transports/v1/cases.json`; another implementation must produce
the same routes and the same codes in the same order.

## Start here: clone over Tor without leaking your address

Run Tor (its SOCKS port is `127.0.0.1:9050` by default) and write a profile:

```json
{
  "schema": "forkmesh-transport-profile-v1",
  "posture": "anonymous",
  "adapters": [
    {"id": "tor", "kind": "proxy", "network": "tor", "socks": "127.0.0.1:9050"}
  ]
}
```

Then check it, see the route, and clone:

```sh
tools/forkmesh_transports.py validate tor.json
tools/forkmesh_transports.py plan --profile tor.json https://git.example.org/team/app.git
tools/forkmesh_transports.py git --profile tor.json https://git.example.org/team/app.git \
  --trace required --report health.json -- clone @URL app
tools/forkmesh_transports.py status health.json
```

`--trace required` stops before sending anything if the tracer is missing.
Leave it at `auto` on systems where tracing is not available (see
[Supported platforms](#supported-platforms)).

## Adapters

| Kind | What it carries | How names are resolved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clearnet` | Direct connections over the open internet. | The operating system resolver, and only in the `standard` posture. Other postures accept only literal addresses. |
| `proxy` | A SOCKS5 proxy. `network` is `tor`, `i2p`, or `socks` (a VPN provider, SSH `-D`, or any other SOCKS5 server). | By the proxy (`socks5h`). The device never looks up the destination. The proxy itself must be a literal `IP:port`, so reaching it needs no lookup either. |
| `overlay` | Addresses inside the overlay's `cidrs` (default `100.64.0.0/10` and `fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48`). Also `200::/7` for Yggdrasil, or your WireGuard, ZeroTier, or Nebula range. | No lookups. Use literal addresses, or pin names with `hosts`. |
| `lan` | Loopback, RFC 1918, link-local, and unique-local addresses. This is the same rule the desktop local mesh uses. Carrier-grade NAT space (`100.64.0.0/10`) is not the LAN. | No lookups, except multicast DNS for `.local` names. `hosts` pins other names. |

Other adapter fields:

- `allowPlaintext` lets `http://` and `git://` run without transport
  authentication on this adapter. The default is off, and the route is refused
  with `peer_unauthenticated`. HTTPS, SSH, onion, and I2P destinations
  authenticate the peer on their own.
- `authenticatedNetwork` on an overlay says the overlay authenticates every
  peer (WireGuard keys, for example), so plaintext inside it is acceptable.
- `isolateStreams` on a proxy sends fresh SOCKS credentials on every run.
  Tor's `IsolateSOCKSAuth` then puts each run on its own circuit. It is on by
  default for `tor` and always on in the `anonymous` posture.
- `serviceAddress` on a proxy is an onion or I2P address this device serves.
  It is the only address the private postures advertise.
- `budgets.latencyMs` (default 2000) is the median connection time above which
  a route is `degraded`.

Profile validation stops at the first failing check, in this order:
`profile_schema`, `unknown_posture`, `adapters_missing`, `adapter_id_invalid`,
`adapter_id_duplicate`, `unknown_adapter_kind`, `proxy_endpoint_not_literal`,
`proxy_network_unknown`, `overlay_cidr_invalid`, `overlay_cidr_global`,
`pinned_host_invalid`, `budget_invalid`, `posture_has_no_adapter`,
`anonymous_requires_anonymity_network`.

## Postures

| Posture | Adapters | Name lookups | Falls back to a direct connection | Telemetry | Logs | Advertises |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `standard` | all, preferring `lan`, then `overlay`, then `clearnet`, then `proxy` | system | yes | counts | full | public, overlay, and LAN addresses |
| `private` | `proxy` (any network), in profile order | by the proxy | never | counts | redacted | nothing but a service address |
| `anonymous` | `proxy` on `tor` or `i2p`, in profile order | by the proxy | never | off | redacted | nothing but a service address |
| `overlay-only` | `overlay` | none | never | counts | redacted | overlay addresses |
| `lan-only` | `lan` | none (multicast DNS for `.local`) | never | counts | redacted | LAN addresses |

In every posture except `standard`, Git runs with a scrubbed environment and
without system or global Git configuration. Proxy variables, `NO_PROXY`,
`GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `GIT_PROXY_COMMAND`, `GIT_TRACE*`, and `GIT_CURL_VERBOSE`
cannot redirect traffic or print a destination. Credential helpers, prompts,
and HTTP redirects are also off. `git://` and `ssh://` go through this tool's
relay, which applies the same route rules as HTTP. OpenSSH runs with
`VerifyHostKeyDNS=no`, and in `private` and `anonymous` also with `-F none`,
so a `~/.ssh/config` `ProxyJump` or `HostName` cannot bypass the proxy. Load
keys through `ssh-agent`.

Before running, the tool reads the repository's own configuration. If
`url.*.insteadOf`, `http.*.proxy`, `core.gitProxy`, `core.sshCommand`,
`remote.*.proxy`, or an include is set, the run is refused with
`repository_config_overrides_route`, because it could send traffic around the
route. Nothing is sent.

## Route refusals

Each adapter is checked in this order, and the first refusal is recorded
against it:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `adapter_not_permitted` | The posture does not use this kind of adapter. |
| `proxy_network_not_permitted` | `anonymous` accepts only `tor` and `i2p` proxies. |
| `destination_requires_anonymity_network` | An onion or I2P destination on a direct adapter. |
| `onion_requires_tor` | An onion destination on a proxy that is not Tor. |
| `i2p_requires_i2p` | An I2P destination on a proxy that is not I2P. |
| `local_destination_via_proxy` | A LAN, loopback, `.local`, or carrier-grade NAT address sent to a proxy, which would reveal your network layout to it. |
| `destination_outside_overlay` | The address, or pinned address, is outside every overlay range. |
| `destination_outside_lan` | The destination is not a local address, a `.local` name, or a pinned local name. |
| `name_needs_dns` | A direct adapter was given a name in a posture that forbids lookups. |
| `plaintext_via_exit` | `http://` or `git://` to a clearnet host in `anonymous`. The exit relay could read or change it. |
| `peer_unauthenticated` | Plaintext without `allowPlaintext` or an authenticated overlay. |

When no adapter is left the plan fails with `no_permitted_route`. A URL is
refused before any adapter is considered with `invalid_url` or
`scheme_unsupported` (only `https`, `http`, `ssh`, and `git` are carried).

## States

A health report has one `state`, with a `label`, a `tone`, and an
`explanation` that clients show without rewording. Precedence is from top to
bottom:

| State | Label | Tone | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exposed` | Exposed | danger | The trace saw a DNS query or a connection outside the route. The address or destination may have been disclosed. This wins over every other state, even if Git succeeded. |
| `unreachable` | Unreachable | danger | No permitted route answered, or the transfer broke. Nothing was sent another way. |
| `degraded` | Degraded | warning | Reachable, but with a `reason`: `failed_over` (a later route carried it), `slow` (median latency over budget), `intermittent` (some probes failed), or `unauthenticated_peer` (plaintext by opt-in). |
| `anonymous` | Anonymous | success | `anonymous` posture, healthy, and no leak observed. |
| `protected` | Protected | success | `private`, `overlay-only`, or `lan-only`, healthy, and no leak observed. |
| `direct` | Direct | neutral | `standard` posture, healthy. No anonymity is claimed. |

`blockedAttempts` counts lookups and connections the in-process guard stopped
before they left the device. They do not make a run `exposed`. The `leakTrace`
field says whether the Git process was `traced`, whether tracing was
`unavailable`, or whether it was `not_required` (the `standard` posture).

## How leaks are prevented and detected

- **DNS.** Proxy routes pass names to the proxy (`socks5h`, SOCKS5 address type
  3), and the `lan`, `overlay`, and pinned routes dial literal addresses. The
  tool's own sockets run inside an audit-hook guard. The guard blocks any
  lookup, and any connection except to the route's endpoint.
- **Direct fallback.** A private posture has no direct adapter to fall back
  to. When every permitted proxy is down, Git does not run, and the report is
  `unreachable`.
- **The Git process.** On Linux, Git runs under `strace`. Connections to
  resolver sockets (nscd, systemd-resolved, Avahi) or to ports 53, 853, or
  5353 count as `dns_query`. Any other connection outside the route counts as
  `direct_connection`. Either one makes the run `exposed`, with exit code 5.
- **Logs.** In every posture except `standard`, Git's output, errors, and the
  saved report go through redaction. The destination, proxy endpoint, SOCKS
  credentials, URLs, onion and I2P names, and IP addresses become
  `<redacted>`.
- **Telemetry.** `--telemetry FILE` appends one line with only posture, state,
  reason, and counts. `anonymous` never writes it, and the report records
  `"telemetry": "suppressed"`.
- **Peer addresses.** `advertise` lists only the addresses the posture allows
  peers to learn. It also reports `nat` as `public`, `behind_nat`,
  `carrier_nat`, or `no_clearnet_address`, and `inbound` as `direct`,
  `needs_relay_or_overlay`, `overlay`, `local_network`, `onion_service`, or
  `outbound_only`.

## Commands

```sh
tools/forkmesh_transports.py validate PROFILE [--json]
tools/forkmesh_transports.py plan --profile PROFILE URL [--json]
tools/forkmesh_transports.py probe --profile PROFILE URL [--attempts N] [--timeout S] \
  [--report FILE] [--telemetry FILE] [--json]
tools/forkmesh_transports.py git --profile PROFILE URL [--repo DIR] [--trace auto|required|off] \
  [--report FILE] [--telemetry FILE] [--json] -- GIT_ARGS...
tools/forkmesh_transports.py status REPORT [--json]
tools/forkmesh_transports.py advertise --profile PROFILE --address IP... [--json]
```

`GIT_ARGS` name the remote as `@URL`, for example
`-- -C app fetch --atomic @URL main`. Pass `--repo` for commands that run
inside a repository, so its configuration is checked first. Use `--atomic` on
fetches: when a route breaks mid-transfer, Git keeps every ref as it was, and
you can repeat the same command once the route recovers.

Git's own failures, such as a missing repository or a rejected push, do not
cause failover, because another route would fail the same way.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Done. |
| `2` | Usage error, invalid profile, or `--trace required` without a tracer. |
| `3` | Refused by policy before anything was sent. |
| `4` | Unreachable: no permitted route answered, or the transfer broke. |
| `5` | Exposed: a prohibited DNS query or connection was observed. |
| `6` | Git failed on a reachable route. |

## Supported platforms

| Platform | Adapters and failover | `git://` and `ssh://` relay | Leak tracing of the Git process |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linux | covered by the CI workflow | covered by the CI workflow | covered by the CI workflow with `strace` |
| macOS | covered by the CI workflow | covered by the CI workflow | not available: `leakTrace` is `unavailable`; the in-process guard and Git configuration still apply |
| Windows | not yet tested | not yet tested | not available |

## Evidence

`app/tests/test_transports.py` is the `transport-conformance` quality gate. The
`Transport conformance` workflow runs it on Linux and macOS. It covers:

- common stream conformance for every adapter: 2 MiB round trip, throughput,
  latency, and unreachable detection;
- repository conformance for every adapter over smart HTTP and `git://`:
  `ls-remote`, clone, atomic fetch, and push;
- every planner vector and profile error;
- leak tests: hostile environment variables, dead proxies with no fallback, a
  simulated regression that drops the proxy (caught as `exposed`), repository
  configuration overrides, stream isolation, and log and telemetry disclosure;
- failover, a transfer dropped mid-fetch with refs unchanged and recovery
  afterwards, slow and intermittent routes, and address advertisement.

## Not built yet

- The desktop, mobile, and web clients do not yet show these states or edit
  profiles. They should read the health report and display `label`, `tone`,
  and `explanation` as written.
- Only Git traffic is carried. Relay chat, the Worker API, mirror sync, and the
  desktop local mesh do not yet read the profile, so a private posture here
  does not cover them.
- Tracing covers Linux only. macOS (`dtruss`, which needs SIP changes) and
  Windows (ETW) have no process-level leak evidence yet.
- A real Tor or I2P daemon, NAT traversal between two real networks, and
  bandwidth over real links are not part of CI. The tests use a local SOCKS5
  proxy that behaves like Tor's SOCKS port.

pages.description: A trust list is a signed list of people. Its owner vouches for them, or warns you about them, in a specific role and place. Examples
pages.markdown:
# Trust lists

A trust list is a signed list of people. Its owner vouches for them, or warns
you about them, in a specific role and place. Examples:

- the security researchers whose advisories a project's maintainers stand
  behind;
- the reviewers a maintainer relies on for one repository;
- the mirror operators an organization has worked with;
- the accounts a community's moderation group has flagged.

You choose which lists to follow. ForkMesh does not ship a global list and
follows nothing on your behalf. Trust is never universal: an entry always
names one role, such as `reviewer`, and one place, such as
`repo:forkmesh/app`, `org:forkmesh`, or `community:rust`. An organization
scope covers that organization's repositories. Nothing covers everything.

The protocol, verification order, and threat model are in
[Scoped community trust lists](design/scoped-trust-lists.md).

## What does not need a list

You never need to follow a list to read or clone a repository, sign in,
recover your identity, push, fork, or open an issue or pull request. Lists
only add information, such as review suggestions, badges, and moderation
queue hints. If you follow nothing, ForkMesh works exactly as it does
without trust lists.

## Following and narrowing

Following a list is local to your device. It is not published, and
ForkMesh's usage counts never include which lists you follow. When you
follow a list you can narrow it further: for example, only its `reviewer`
entries, and only for `repo:forkmesh/app`. Narrowing can only shrink what a
list says, never widen it.

Lists can include other lists, and an owner can hand part of a list to a
trusted maintainer until a date. Included entries only count inside the
overlap of every scope along the way. Composition stops after four lists and
ignores loops.

## When lists disagree

If one list you follow trusts a key as a security researcher for
`org:forkmesh` and another distrusts it, ForkMesh shows **conflict** and lists
both sources. It never picks a winner for you. To settle it on your device,
add a local override (`trust`, `distrust`, or `ignore`) for that key, role,
and place. Overrides stay on your device, and the conflict stays visible with
a note that you overrode it.

## Appeals

If a list distrusts you, you can sign an appeal with your own key, naming the
list version and entry. The appeal appears next to that entry for everyone
who follows the list. It shows as **resolved** once a newer version of the
list no longer distrusts you. The list owner decides what their list says,
and your appeal makes sure followers can see your side.

## List states

| State | What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Active | The list's newest version applies | Nothing |
| Recovered | Something went wrong with newer versions (a revocation, two conflicting copies of one version, or a rewritten history), so ForkMesh uses the last good version | Read the reason; if a successor list is shown, decide whether to follow it |
| Expired | The newest version's expiry passed; older versions are never revived | Wait for the owner to publish a new version, or unfollow |
| Revoked | The owner (or their recovery key) withdrew every version | Unfollow, or follow the successor if you trust it |
| Conflicted | Conflicting copies left no usable version | Unfollow until the owner publishes a clean successor |
| Missing | You follow a list but have no verified copy yet | Check your connection or mirror |

## Publishing a list safely

- Give every list at least one **recovery key**, kept offline and separate
  from the signing key. Recovery keys named in a version can revoke any
  later version, which is how you recover from a stolen signing key.
- Keep lists short-lived. A version can last at most 400 days. Publish
  regular updates rather than long-lived lists.
- Keep scope tight. A list cannot contain entries outside its own roles and
  places, and a client rejects the whole version if it tries.

## Drill: compromised list

Run this drill before relying on a list:

1. **Compromise.** A stolen signing key publishes a new version that
   distrusts a real maintainer and trusts the attacker. Followers who have
   not yet seen a revocation accept it, because the signature is valid.
2. **Revoke.** With a recovery key named in an earlier version, publish a
   revocation from the malicious version onward, with reason `compromised`.
   Point it at a successor list signed by a new key.
3. **Recover.** As soon as a follower has the revocation, their client shows
   the list as **Recovered** at the last good version. The malicious entries
   disappear, and the successor is offered but not followed automatically.

The shared vectors replay this drill on every client. Operators can replay it
with:

```bash
python3 tools/forkmesh_trust_lists.py drill
```

It prints the before and after states, the number of assertions removed,
and how long local recovery took, and exits non-zero if recovery did not
happen. `tools/forkmesh_trust_lists.py resolve <bundle.json>` and
`verify <bundle.json>` inspect any bundle of documents offline.

## Evidence and telemetry

Every client resolves the same documents to the same result:

| Client | Resolver | Test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web | `app/public/trust-lists.js` | `app/tests/test_trust_lists.py` (Node) |
| Worker and tools | `app/src/trust_lists.py` | `app/tests/test_trust_lists.py` |
| iOS | `native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMAccount/TrustLists.swift` | `native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Tests/FMAccountTests/ConformanceTests.swift` |
| Android | `native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/security/TrustLists.kt` | `native/android/core/src/test/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/security/TrustListsCryptoTest.kt` |
| Desktop | `desktop/src/TrustLists.cpp` | `forkmesh-trust-list-tests` |

Each resolution includes a `telemetry` object of counts only: lists by state,
revocations, rejected documents by reason, conflicts, overrides, and appeals
by status. It never includes keys, list names, or follows.

## Not yet available

Trust lists are resolved and verified on every client. The following are
still being built: publishing and fetching lists through relays and mirrors,
creating and signing lists in the apps, and settings screens for follows and
overrides.

pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh World community services

ForkMesh World uses D1 for its public Fediverse directory, authenticated
shared-media coordination, and UTC event announcements. The implementations
are migrations `0052_world_fediverse_media.sql` and
`0058_world_events.sql`, `0059_world_media_playback.sql`, and
`0061_world_social_directory.sql`.

These services do not use the multiplayer WebSocket. Directory records, room
lists, playlists, schedules, and moderation changes use ordinary HTTPS. The
socket remains limited to transient presence, movement, and small world events.

## UTC community events

`GET /api/world/events` and `GET /api/world/events/{event-id}` are public,
short-cacheable reads of scheduled events whose `endsAt` is still in the
future. The production client has no built-in event rows: an empty or
unavailable API produces an explicit empty or unavailable state, never a demo
announcement presented as live.

Only a signed-in platform administrator may create, update, or cancel:

- `POST /api/world/events`
- `PATCH /api/world/events/{event-id}`
- `DELETE /api/world/events/{event-id}`

Both `startsAt` and `endsAt` must be explicit ISO-8601 UTC strings ending in
`Z`. Events last at most seven days, may be scheduled at most two years ahead,
and use bounded type, title, description, and destination fields. `DELETE`
marks an event cancelled; cancelled and expired records are excluded from
public reads immediately. Retained old rows are pruned on later mutations and
by the hourly privacy-retention cron. A D1 trigger caps the catalog at 500 rows
even if administrator writes race.

Creates, updates, cancels, and denied attempts use the metadata-only sensitive
audit trail. The author blind index remains private and is never included in a
public response.

## Fediverse directory

`GET /api/world/fediverse` is public. It returns separate `mastodon`, `lemmy`,
`x`, and `reddit` arrays and the privacy policy applied to every record. The
world renders those records around their corresponding social centers.

The static `world/public/world/fediverse-directory.json` file is no longer the runtime data
source. An empty D1 directory is shown honestly as empty.

Only a signed-in platform administrator may mutate directory records:

- `POST /api/world/fediverse`
- `PATCH /api/world/fediverse/{instance-id}`
- `DELETE /api/world/fediverse/{instance-id}`

Every create or update must include:

```json
{
  "publicOnly": true,
  "consentConfirmed": true,
  "consentSource": "instance-operator",
  "consentCheckedAt": 1800000000000
}
```

`consentSource` is one of `instance-operator`, `public-api`,
`user-approved`, or `moderator-reviewed`. The timestamp is UTC milliseconds
and must describe a check within the previous year.

Instance base URLs must be public HTTPS origins. Credentials, fragments,
queries, paths below `/`, IP literals, localhost, internal names, and
non-default ports are rejected. Icons must be public HTTPS URLs on the same
instance host. Text, language, topic, community, relationship, and connection
lists all have server-side limits.

The API has no field for raw IPs, user agents, email addresses, search terms,
browsing history, private accounts, or an unfiltered follower/subscription
graph. A `consentedFollowers` or `approvedSubscriptions` entry is accepted only
when both `public` and `consent` are exactly `true`; a follower must also be a
public account. Invalid relationship data rejects the whole mutation rather
than being silently published.

X and Reddit use `consentedProfiles`. Each record requires a public platform
profile URL, explicit `public` and `consent` flags, public account visibility,
and an evidence source/time. Mastodon follower entries inherit the record
attestation unless a more specific valid source/time is supplied. The public
projection persists that bounded evidence as an `operator-attestation` and
always sets `oauthVerifiedByForkMesh` to `false`. It contains no OAuth token or
remote private identifier. These records describe an operator-recorded
attestation; they do not claim that ForkMesh independently verified remote
account ownership.

All create, update, delete, and authorization-denial decisions append
metadata-only entries to `sensitive_audit_log`. Audit targets are opaque/token
values; directory descriptions and relationship content are not copied into
the audit log.

## Shared media spaces

Every media endpoint requires a valid ForkMesh account session:

- `GET /api/world/media/spaces`
- `POST /api/world/media/spaces`
- `GET /api/world/media/spaces/{space-id}`
- `PATCH /api/world/media/spaces/{space-id}`
- `DELETE /api/world/media/spaces/{space-id}`
- `POST /api/world/media/spaces/{space-id}/items`
- `DELETE /api/world/media/spaces/{space-id}/items/{item-id}`
- `GET|POST|PATCH /api/world/media/spaces/{space-id}/playback`
- `POST /api/world/media/spaces/{space-id}/stop`
- `POST /api/world/media/spaces/{space-id}/schedules`
- `DELETE /api/world/media/spaces/{space-id}/schedules/{schedule-id}`
- `GET|POST /api/world/media/spaces/{space-id}/roles`
- `DELETE /api/world/media/spaces/{space-id}/roles/{role-id}`

The creator is the room owner. Owners may update/archive a room and
grant/revoke explicit moderator roles. Owners and explicit moderators may add
or remove playlist links, create or cancel schedules, and stop shared playback
state. A platform administrator does not automatically inherit media-room
control.

The Worker derives the actor from the signed session, never from a body
`owner`, `actor`, or `moderator` field. Role checks are repeated server-side for
every mutation. All sensitive changes and denied role checks use the existing
metadata-only audit log.

### Provider-link policy

Playlist entries are links, not media objects:

```json
{
  "title": "Community listening hour",
  "provider": "somafm",
  "url": "https://somafm.com/groovesalad/",
  "termsConfirmed": true,
  "noRebroadcast": true,
  "autoplay": false
}
```

Supported provider-page families are SomaFM, YouTube, Vimeo, SoundCloud,
Twitch, Internet Archive, and public PeerTube watch/embed pages. Hostnames and
provider-specific query keys are allowlisted. Raw `.mp3`, `.mp4`, `.m3u8`, and
similar media/playlist file URLs are rejected.

ForkMesh stores only the bounded title, validated external provider page, and
the no-autoplay/no-rebroadcast policy flags. It does not fetch, proxy, cache,
record, copy, or rebroadcast the linked media. Opening or playing a provider
page remains an individual, explicit client action subject to that provider's
terms and controls.

A playlist title is a user-supplied coordination label, not the provider's
current track. The API currently returns provider metadata as
`unavailable/not_received`; user input cannot override that result. The world
therefore says current provider track metadata is unavailable unless a future
provider-authorized integration actually supplies a permitted metadata event.
Locally generated focus tones are labeled as local synthesis, where provider
track metadata is not applicable.

The shared playback endpoint stores only item id, state, position, UTC change
time, and an optimistic revision. It coordinates clients but cannot start
playback on their devices. Every client must open the provider and consent
locally.

### UTC schedules and retention

Schedules use UTC millisecond `startsAt` and `endsAt` values. They may be at
most one year in the future and last at most 24 hours. The world converts the
start time for local display while retaining UTC as the shared event time.

Storage and response sizes are bounded:

- five active spaces per owner;
- 100 active playlist entries per space;
- 50 active schedules per space;
- 20 explicit moderators per space;
- 50 spaces in one listing response.

Removed/stopped playlist entries and completed/cancelled schedules are purged
after 30 days. A space with no activity for 180 days becomes archived; archived
spaces and their child records are purged after another 90 days. The hourly
privacy-retention cron applies this policy even when nobody opens the world.

## World rendering

The browser loads the D1 directory from `/api/world/fediverse` and unexpired
announcements from `/api/world/events`. Signed-in visitors also load
`/api/world/media/spaces` and a selected space detail. None of this service
state is persisted in local storage.

The social center renders Mastodon/Lemmy services and consent-attested X/Reddit
public-profile records plus only explicitly public, consented connection
markers. The Broadcast Garden renders shared-room
nodes, external playlist markers, and UTC schedule markers. These 3D objects
are visualizations of HTTPS API records; they are not media playback,
surveillance, or a claim that ForkMesh has content custody.

# ForkMesh World Song

The World entrance sign links to *ForkMesh Forever (Indie Pop)*, a first-party
track published by the project at
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EsQMZuS6lbE>. Clicking the sign opens that
video in a new tab; nothing is downloaded, decoded, or played by the World
itself, and no audio file is bundled with or served from ForkMesh’s own origin.

All other World sounds are short event effects synthesized locally with the
Web Audio API. No ambient music catalog or procedural soundtrack is bundled.

pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh World visual acceptance

The three supplied sample images are reference material for composition and
interaction density only. They are not ForkMesh production assets, and their
branding, character designs, text, logos, textures, and distinctive decorative
details are not copied.

## Patterns retained

- Sample 1: a layered city that remains legible as a whole, persistent
  edge-navigation, a readable code destination, visible collaboration
  activity, and chat that is reachable without leaving the spatial context.
- Sample 2: one strong infrastructure focal point, surrounding node/routing
  relationships, and compact status panels that explain the operational
  meaning of the visual.
- Sample 3: translucent operational panels, a clearly identified community
  destination, and nearby work/review destinations with different visual
  identities.

ForkMesh applies those general patterns through its original Town Square,
quick destination dock, organization and repository districts, routing
station, chat destination, and separate Support Center.
Every spatial metaphor keeps a technical explanation panel.

## Reproducible acceptance viewports

Playwright owns deterministic Chromium baselines for:

- Desktop: 1440 × 900, fine pointer.
- Portrait phone: 390 × 844, coarse pointer.
- Landscape phone: 844 × 390, coarse pointer.

The tests fix the UTC clock, API fixtures, day theme, reduced-motion mode, and
paused scene before comparison. They also exercise desktop keyboard movement, portrait
visual-viewport resizing, and landscape touch movement.

Run:

```sh
cd world/browser_tests
npx playwright test
```

Only an intentional visual review should refresh baselines:

```sh
npx playwright test --update-snapshots
```
