pages.markdown:
# Self-hostable service roles

ForkMesh's network services are split into eight roles. This page lists which
roles an independent operator can run today, how to start each one, what
replaces each optional dependency, and how to check a running deployment. It
matches the machine-readable manifest
[`conformance/service-roles/v1/manifest.json`](../../../conformance/service-roles/v1/manifest.json).
`tools/forkmesh_service_roles.py validate` fails if this page or the manifest
names a path, flag, source route, or heading that no longer exists.

Tracking issue: #502.

## Role status

| Role | Status | Independent profile | Contract checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `web-ui` | partial | Mirror gateway dashboard | `/health`, `/api/version`, `/dashboard`, `/api/accounts/sessions` |
| `relay` | partial | Mirror gateway Smart HTTP + `forkmesh-mirror-node` | clone advertisement, signed endpoint manifest |
| `public-index` | partial | Mirror gateway local catalog | `/api/repositories` |
| `search` | hosted-only | — | `/api/repositories/search` (hosted) |
| `identity-resolver` | partial | Node key, SSH broker `local` mode, portable sessions | evidence tests only |
| `collaboration-relay` | partial | Daemon intake, gateway submissions, SSH pull spool | evidence tests only |
| `automation-broker` | partial | Desktop ActionRunner + signed checks | evidence tests only |
| `organization-service` | hosted-only | — | none yet |

- **independent**: runs from this repository with open-source dependencies
  only, needs no default endpoint, and lists no gaps. No role has this status
  yet.
- **partial**: an independent profile covers part of the role. The manifest's
  `gaps` list says what still needs the hosted deployment.
- **hosted-only**: runs only on the hosted Worker today.

Print the current list with:

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_service_roles.py gaps
```

## Starting the independent profiles

Every partial role runs on the same two open-source processes:

1. `tools/mirror_gateway.py --config gateway.json` serves Git, the dashboard,
   the local catalog, and the signed endpoint manifest on a loopback port.
   Run `--check` first. Its configuration schema is
   [`mirror-gateway-config.schema.json`](../mirror-gateway-config.schema.json).
2. `forkmesh-mirror-node --config mirror-node.json` synchronizes repositories,
   supervises the gateway, commits collaboration submissions, and reports
   `/healthz`, `/readyz`, and `/v1/status`. Run `--preflight --json` first. See
   [Mirror node service](mirror-node.md).

For SSH pushes, pull submissions, and forks with no controller, add the SSH
gateway and the authorization broker in `localAuthorization` mode `local`
([Controller-free operation](git-ssh-gateway.md#controller-free-operation)).
Put any TLS-terminating reverse proxy in front of the loopback listeners.

## Optional dependencies and substitutes

| Dependency | Used by | Substitute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cloudflare Tunnel (`cloudflared`) | `web-ui`, `relay` | `--disable-cloudflared` (or `disableCloudflared`) with your own HTTPS reverse proxy |
| Hosted login origin | `web-ui` | Omit `dashboard.canonicalOrigin`; the dashboard stays signed out except for existing portable sessions |
| Hosted node event socket | `relay` | The `post-receive` doorbell (`POST /v1/control/sync`), direct peer upstreams, and `syncInterval` for third-party upstreams |
| Hosted catalog publication | `public-index` | `disableCatalog`, or `--catalog-url` pointing at another operator's catalog |
| Hosted account registry | `identity-resolver` | SSH broker `localAuthorization` mode `local` with a grants file |
| Hosted collaboration inboxes | `collaboration-relay` | `forkmesh-pull-submit` over SSH, or direct signed submissions to the gateway |
| Hosted agent CLIs | `automation-broker` | Leave website agent jobs off; workflows and signed required checks run without them |

## Default endpoints

`forkmesh-mirror-node` has three flags whose defaults point at forkmesh.com.
An independent deployment overrides all three. The contract test fails if a
new forkmesh.com default appears without a matching manifest entry.

| Flag | Default | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--upstream` | `https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` | `relay` |
| `--catalog-url` | `https://app.forkmesh.com/api/repositories` | `public-index` |
| `--accounts-url` | `https://app.forkmesh.com/api/accounts` | `identity-resolver` |

## Checking a running role

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_service_roles.py probe --role web-ui \
  --base-url https://mirror.example.org
python3 tools/forkmesh_service_roles.py probe --role relay \
  --base-url https://mirror.example.org --param owner=alice --param repository=demo
```

`probe` sends only read-only `GET` or `HEAD` requests. It prints a
`forkmesh-service-role-report-v1` JSON report with one result per check, the
role's status, `defaultPublicService` (true when the base URL is a
forkmesh.com host), and a `telemetry` block with request, transport error,
status class, and latency counts. The base URL is printed without credentials
or a query string.

| Verdict | Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pass` | 0 | Every check answered as specified. |
| `degraded` | 3 | Every check that did not pass returned the role's declared explicit degradation, such as `503` with a JSON `error`. |
| `fail` | 1 | A check answered outside both the contract and the declared degradation. |
| `unreachable` | 4 | Nothing answered. Treat this as service loss, never as an empty result. |

A usage or manifest error exits 2.

## Failure behavior and canonical data

Git objects, refs, and signed collaboration records under `.forkmesh/` stay in
repositories on configured nodes. Catalog rows, search results, and dashboard
pages are rebuilt from them. Losing a role never deletes canonical data:

- Without the hosted Worker, the gateway keeps serving clones and the last
  validated dashboard projection. The stable forkmesh.com URL cannot redirect
  to it.
- Submissions made while the Worker is down stay in the pull submission
  spool. Nothing is acknowledged until it is committed.
- In `fallback` mode the SSH broker uses local grants only when the Worker is
  unreachable, never after a denial, so cutting the uplink cannot bypass a
  revocation.
- Search answers `503 catalog_unavailable` when no catalog can be read.
- A required status check with no signed result keeps the merge gate closed.

Backups for every node-hosted role are covered by
[Node backup and recovery](node-backup-and-recovery.md).

## What is not proven yet

Issue #502 stays open until:

- `search` and `organization-service` have independent profiles;
- account registration, username resolution, stable-URL routing, live rooms,
  and the agent job queue run without the hosted Worker;
- workflows run in a headless service instead of only inside the desktop app;
- a clean-room deployment on fresh infrastructure serves browse, clone,
  collaboration, identity, and automation without forkmesh.com; and
- mixed-version and service-loss runs are recorded against real deployments.

`app/tests/test_service_roles_contract.py` starts a real mirror gateway with
no forkmesh.com configuration, runs the `web-ui`, `relay`, and `public-index`
contracts against it, and then stops it to check that the probe reports
`unreachable`. CI runs it as the `service-role-contract` quality gate.

## Changing the manifest

Change a role's status only in the same commit as the code and evidence that
justify it. A role can move to `independent` only when its gaps list is empty,
it has no proprietary required dependency, and it has a contract. The
validator enforces all three.

pages.title: Signed required checks
pages.description: A repository can require status checks before a pull request merges on a mirror node. Each check result is an Ed25519-signed attestation from a runner the repository trusts. The…
pages.markdown:
# Signed required checks

A repository can require status checks before a pull request merges on a
mirror node. Each check result is an Ed25519-signed attestation from a runner
the repository trusts. The gate never depends on a particular runner service,
on where a result was stored, or on who committed it. Forged, stale, replayed,
and unauthorized results cannot satisfy it.

This page covers the merge gate the Go mirror node (`forkmesh-mirror-node`)
enforces for web merges (`merge-pull`). It is one slice of issue #496, signed
delivery pipelines. Approval holds, protected-push enforcement, and deployment
events are separate work.

## Turning the gate on

Commit `.forkmesh/required-checks.json` to the base branch:

```json
{
  "schema": "forkmesh-required-checks-v1",
  "branches": ["main"],
  "maxAgeSeconds": 604800,
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "CI tests",
      "signers": ["<runner public key, 43-character base64url>"]
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | Exactly `forkmesh-required-checks-v1`. |
| `branches` | Base branches the gate covers. An empty list covers every base. |
| `maxAgeSeconds` | From 60 to 31,622,400. Older results do not count. |
| `checks` | 1–32 checks with distinct names (1–128 bytes, no control characters, no surrounding spaces). |
| `signers` | 1–16 distinct runner keys for each check. Keys must be canonical, prime-order Ed25519 keys (FM-SIG-001). |

The file must have exactly these keys. Any parse or validation failure locks
merges into the covered branches. It never switches the gate off.

The mirror reads the policy from the **base commit being merged into**. It
never reads the pull request's head, so a proposal cannot loosen its own gate.
To change or remove the gate, push to the base branch.

To get a runner key, run `forkmesh-mirror-node --config <path> --public-key` on
the runner node.

## Reporting a result

A runner signs one attestation per check run:

```sh
printf '%s' '{"schema":"forkmesh-check-v1","owner":"forkmesh","repository":"forkmesh","commit":"<head sha>","check":"CI tests","conclusion":"success","runId":"run-1234"}' \
  | forkmesh-mirror-node --config /etc/forkmesh/mirror-node.json --sign-check-attestation
```

The signer adds `issuedAt` from its own clock, plus `signer` and `signature`
from its node identity. A caller cannot supply any of the three. `conclusion`
is one of `success`, `failure`, `cancelled`, or `skipped`. Only `success`
satisfies a check.

Publish the signed JSON on the pull-request ledger branch (`forkmesh/pulls`) as
`.forkmesh/pulls/<N>/checks/<name>.json`. The file name must match
`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\.json`. The mirror reads at most 256 files, each up
to 8 KiB.

### Signing bytes

The signature covers this FM-ENC-007 canonical string: fields joined by LF,
with no trailing LF.

```
forkmesh-check-v1
<owner, lowercase>
<repository>
<commit, lowercase hex>
<hex SHA-256 of the check name>
<conclusion>
<runId>
<issuedAt, decimal milliseconds>
```

## What satisfies the gate

For each required check, the mirror discards every attestation that:

- does not parse with exactly the documented keys, or whose signature does not
  verify (**forged**);
- names a different owner, repository, or commit than the merge request's
  owner, repository, and exact head commit (**replayed**);
- is signed by a key the policy does not list for that check, including a key
  trusted only for another check (**unauthorized**);
- is older than `maxAgeSeconds`, or dated more than five minutes in the future
  (**stale**).

Of the attestations left, the newest `issuedAt` wins. When two share a
timestamp, a non-success result beats a success. An old success replayed
beside a newer failure therefore cannot mask it. A newer successful re-run does
supersede an earlier failure. The merge proceeds only when every required
check's winning result is `success`.

Otherwise the executor records `checks_required` and moves no refs. The
dashboard explains the refusal. The owner's review waiver (`overrideReview`)
waives the peer-review gate only, never required checks.

## Limits and fail-closed cases

- **Patch-backed pulls.** They have no published head commit for a runner to
  attest, so a covered patch-backed pull cannot merge on the web. Merge it from
  the desktop client, or exclude its base in `branches`.
- **Headless Python mirrors.** `tools/headless_mirror_refresh.py` has no
  Ed25519 verifier. It refuses every merge whose base carries a policy, with
  `checks_required`, so it cannot become a way around the gate.
- **Organization aliases.** An attestation is bound to the owner name in the
  merge request. Sign it for the name the repository is merged under.

## Evidence

- `server/checks_test.go` covers forged, edited, rebound, unauthorized, stale,
  future-dated, and cross-repository, cross-owner, or cross-commit replayed
  results. It also covers supersession and ties, multi-check policies, malformed
  policies, weak Ed25519 keys (identity, small-order, mixed-order,
  non-canonical, negative zero), and the signer helper.
- `server/merge_test.go` (`TestMergeExecutorEnforcesSignedRequiredChecks`)
  starts from a policy pushed to `main`. It shows the merge refused with no
  checks, with the review waiver, and with forged, stale, and replayed results,
  then merged once a trusted runner's fresh success lands.
  `TestMergeExecutorFailsClosedOnAnInvalidChecksPolicy` shows that an invalid
  policy locks merges.
- `app/tests/test_pull_merge_executor.py` shows the headless executor failing
  closed.

pages.title: Stock Git conformance operations
pages.description: The public compatibility matrix is generated from two sources: the claims in conformance/git/v1/matrix.json and the retained run reports in conformance/git/v1/evidence/, indexed…
pages.markdown:
# Stock Git conformance operations

The public [compatibility matrix](../git-compatibility.md) is generated from
two sources: the claims in `conformance/git/v1/matrix.json` and the retained run
reports in `conformance/git/v1/evidence/`, indexed by
`conformance/git/v1/results.json`. Do not hand-edit the Markdown, hosted HTML,
hosted JSON, the results index, or an evidence file. Change the versioned
source, add or update an executable probe, then run:

```sh
python3 tools/git_conformance.py validate
python3 tools/git_conformance.py render
python3 tools/git_conformance.py render --check
```

## Published status

No claim is published on its own authority. Each operation/path cell whose
matrix status is `supported`, `local`, or `conditional` is published with that
status only when a retained run covers the cell and passed within
`suite.freshnessDays` (30 days) of the attestation date. Otherwise the cell is
published as:

- `failing` — any retained run covering the cell failed or did not run it;
- `stale` — the newest passing run is older than the freshness window; or
- `unverified` — no retained run covers the cell.

Only smart-HTTP runs count for the relay and mirror-failover columns; a
file-transport oracle run verifies the direct column only. A hand-recorded
client certification (`"status": "tested"`) degrades to `stale` the same way.
The hosted page is static, so it re-checks every row's last-run date against
the reader's clock and shows `stale` even before the page is regenerated.
`/docs/git-compatibility/results.json` carries every published cell with its
covering run IDs, and `/docs/git-compatibility/evidence/<run>.json` is the raw
report.

## Attesting evidence

`attest` accepts runner reports, passing or failing, validates them (suite
version, operation inventory, summary consistency, privacy flags, and a scan for
unredacted paths, file URLs, or loopback addresses), stores them under content
addresses, and regenerates every public output:

```sh
python3 tools/git_conformance.py attest \
  artifacts/git-conformance-v0.json artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json
```

The newest report per client configuration (label, Git version, platform,
machine, protocol, and transport) replaces older ones, and an older report never
replaces a newer one. The results index is recomputed from the evidence during
`validate`, so editing either file fails CI. Bumping `suite.version` makes
existing evidence invalid until the suite is re-run and attested.

## Release gate

```sh
python3 tools/git_conformance.py gate
python3 tools/git_conformance.py gate --operations-only \
  --report artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json
```

`gate` exits non-zero and names each failing, stale, or unverified support claim
as of today. `--report` also counts a fresh, unattested run, which is how the
public workflow proves its own run backs every claim. `--operations-only` skips
hand-recorded client rows that a suite run cannot refresh; the `release` quality
gate profile runs the full gate, so a stale desktop certification blocks a
release until it is re-tested or its row is changed to `pending`.

## Evidence chain

The `Stock Git conformance` workflow runs Git protocol v0 and v2 on Ubuntu,
macOS, and Windows. Protocol v2 proves the supported partial-clone and lazy
fetch flow; protocol v0 proves the documented safe rejection without relaxing
hidden-object policy. Every matrix cell maps to one stable probe ID. Each job
retains a JSON report with the tested repository commit, exact Git/Python/OS
versions, status and elapsed time for every operation, generalized origin/proxy
counts, the signed fixture commit ID, and a digest of the final refs.

The offline smart-HTTP fixture exercises direct read/write, a masked relay
proxy, and a failed origin followed by a matching mirror. Focused production
gateway tests separately prove that:

- HTTPS receive-pack returns the actionable 501 before consuming a body;
- SSH receive-pack checks authorization, old ref IDs, incoming objects, quotas,
  hidden internal refs, and read-only configuration;
- upload-pack supports shallow clone and protocol-v2 partial clone while
  arbitrary hidden-object wants and protocol-v0 lazy fetches remain rejected;
- signature bytes and object IDs survive each read path; and
- damaged refs and packs fail strict fsck instead of becoming passing evidence.

The native ForkMesh Actions workflow runs the same suite with the runner's
system Git under `--transport auto`. Selecting HTTP requires a completed
loopback round trip, not merely a successful bind: a runner can accept a bind
on `127.0.0.1` and then drop the traffic, which would hang every Git command
until its timeout. IPv4 is probed first, then IPv6, so a runner that only
routes `::1` still produces real relay and failover evidence. Only when no
loopback family answers does the suite fall back to the clearly labeled
file-transport oracle for ref/object semantics; that report is not counted as
relay or failover network evidence. The public cross-platform workflow requires
`--transport http` and fails instead of silently falling back.

The Actions step runs each suite in its own network namespace
(`unshare -rn`, loopback brought up) whenever the sandbox allows it. A node
whose Actions policy enables network access runs steps in the host namespace,
where a host application firewall that queues new connections for a verdict
(OpenSnitch does this with NFQUEUE) can drop one loopback SYN for good: the
Git command then waits out its 90-second timeout and a probe fails while every
fresh connection still works. Run 784 lost `submodules` this way. A private
loopback keeps the smart-HTTP evidence and never meets the host rules. When a
run fails, the job log names each failed probe and its redacted reason, because
the report itself stays inside the disposable sandbox.

## Promoting a client row

Do not infer support from a brand name. Run the suite with the exact executable
shipped by the client:

```sh
python3 tools/git_conformance.py run \
  --git /path/to/client/bundled/git \
  --client-label "Client name and version" \
  --transport http \
  --protocol-version 0 \
  --output artifacts/git-conformance-client-v0.json
python3 tools/git_conformance.py run \
  --git /path/to/client/bundled/git \
  --client-label "Client name and version" \
  --transport http \
  --protocol-version 2 \
  --output artifacts/git-conformance-client-v2.json
```

Attest both reports so they become retained public evidence, record the
application and bundled-Git versions in the source matrix, and link the
evidence in review. A desktop UI remains pending until its authentication, clone/fetch,
push, branch, and recovery flows are exercised in the application itself; a
passing bundled-Git probe establishes protocol compatibility but does not
certify the UI or credential-store integration.

## Failure and recovery

A failed probe leaves all production repositories untouched: every origin,
key, bundle, hook, and corruption fixture lives under a temporary directory.
The report replaces that directory and loopback URLs with generic markers.
Keep a failed report and job log, reproduce with the same Git and protocol
version, and inspect the first failed probe.

Attest the failed report before a release rather than discarding it: the
affected cells are published as `failing` and `gate` blocks the release. Once
the fix lands, re-run the same client configuration and attest the new report;
it supersedes the failure. To retire a configuration that is no longer tested
(for example, an old Git version), run
`python3 tools/git_conformance.py attest --drop <run-id>`; the cells it covered
fall back to whatever other retained runs prove, or to `unverified`.

For a failed or interrupted production fetch, retry before deleting the clone;
Git reuses valid objects. Run `git fsck --full --strict` after any corruption
diagnostic. Before force-updating a production ref, create and verify a bundle.
The rollback probe restores the exact old object ID from that bundle and proves
the recovered ref can be cloned through every read path.

## Telemetry and privacy

Conformance reports are retained for 30 days. They contain no repository
contents, filesystem paths, URLs, credentials, SSH keys, client addresses, or
raw Git stderr. Generalized request and timing counts are sufficient to
calculate pass rate by operation/client/transport and locate a failed stage.
Production mirror counters remain aggregate clone/website totals and bounded
client classes; the conformance runner does not widen that collection.

## Rollout and rollback

The filter capability and bounded protocol-v2 forwarding are command-line and
transport policies on the HTTPS and SSH gateways. They require no repository
migration and do not change object bytes or refs. Roll them out through the
normal mirror-node and Worker packages, install the scoped
`AcceptEnv GIT_PROTOCOL` SSH drop-in after validating the combined
configuration with `sshd -t`, run the protocol-v0 safe-rejection and
protocol-v2 partial-clone hidden-ref tests, then the complete conformance
workflow. Rollback removes `uploadpack.allowFilter=true`, protocol-v2
forwarding, and the scoped SSH environment hint, then redeploys the prior
packages; existing full clones and repositories are unchanged, while new
partial-clone requests safely fail or fall back only when the stock client
permits it. Do not publish that rollback as partial-clone support—the generated
matrix and suite version must change with the contract.

pages.description: The ForkMesh iPhone app works with Apple Health. It uses Apple's HealthKit framework to connect seven optional tools to the Health app: Pedometer, Water Intake, Calorie Counter…
pages.markdown:
# Apple Health on iPhone

The ForkMesh iPhone app works with Apple Health. It uses Apple's HealthKit
framework to connect seven optional tools to the Health app: Pedometer, Water
Intake, Calorie Counter, Sleep, Sugar Break, Stretch Break and Food Guide. This
page lists
what each tool reads and writes, what reaches your ForkMesh account, and how
to turn it off.

Nothing is read or written until you turn on a tool's Apple Health switch and
allow it in the iOS permission sheet. The rest of ForkMesh does not use
HealthKit.

## Where to find it in the app

- **In each tool.** The Apple Health switch sits in a card marked **Works with
  Apple Health**, with the data that tool reads and writes listed under it and
  a **How ForkMesh uses Apple Health** button.
- **In Settings.** **Settings > Legal > Apple Health** opens the same guide for
  all seven tools, whether or not you have installed them.

The tools are installed from Market in the app. A tool you have not installed
never asks for Apple Health access.

## What each tool reads and writes

| Tool | Reads from Apple Health | Writes to Apple Health | Saved to your ForkMesh account |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pedometer | Steps, walking and running distance, flights climbed, active energy | Heart rate, only when you tap out your pulse and choose **Save to Apple Health** | One total per day, so your steps show on web and desktop. Heart rate is never sent. |
| Water Intake | Water that other apps logged | Each drink you log, as Water | Water from other apps is added to your drinks log |
| Calorie Counter | The meals ForkMesh wrote, so edits and deletions stay in step | Dietary energy, protein, carbohydrates and fat for the meals you log | Nothing from Apple Health |
| Sleep | Sleep that an Apple Watch or another app recorded | Nights your phone detected, only with **Save detected sleep to Apple Health** on | Each night's sleep |
| Sugar Break | Dietary sugar that other apps logged | Nothing | Nothing. Apple Health sugar never leaves the phone. |
| Stretch Break | Minutes of Flexibility and Mind and Body workouts | Each guided session you finish, as a workout | Nothing from Apple Health |
| Food Guide | The last 14 days of dietary energy, protein, fiber, sugar, saturated fat, sodium, iron, calcium, potassium, magnesium, folate and vitamins C, D and B12 that other apps logged | Nothing | Nothing. The nutrition history and the meal ideas worked out from it stay on the phone. |

Pedometer and Sleep also use the iPhone's motion sensor, which iOS asks about
separately under Motion & Fitness.

## What ForkMesh does with it

- The readings saved to your account are there so a tool shows the same
  numbers on web, desktop and mobile. They are encrypted with a key created
  for your account alone.
- ForkMesh does not use Apple Health data for advertising or marketing, does
  not sell it, and does not share it with data brokers or any other third
  party.
- ForkMesh does not store Apple Health data in iCloud.
- ForkMesh never deletes or changes health data that another app wrote.

The [privacy policy](https://forkmesh.com/privacy#apple-health) says the same.

## Turning it off

- Turn off the Apple Health switch in the tool. Reading and writing stop at
  once. What was already written to Apple Health stays there.
- Or open the iPhone **Settings** app, then **Health > Data Access & Devices >
  ForkMesh**, and turn off any type of data.
- Uninstalling a tool deletes its data from your ForkMesh account on every
  device. Deleting your account does the same for every tool. Apple Health
  keeps its own copy, which you manage in the Health app.

pages.title: Editing files and opening pull requests from the phone
pages.description: Status: IMPLEMENTED for Tier 1 (2026-09-20). A person browsing a repository in the iOS or Android app can edit one text file and propose it as a pull request, with no clone, no…
pages.markdown:
# Editing files and opening pull requests from the phone

Status: `IMPLEMENTED` for Tier 1 (2026-09-20). A person browsing a repository
in the iOS or Android app can edit one text file and propose it as a pull request,
with no clone, no fork and no push access. Tiers 2 and 3 are not built; see
[Delivery](#9-delivery) for what was deliberately deferred.

This document describes that flow and why it is shaped differently here than
on GitHub.

Companion documents: [`mobile-node-contract.md`](mobile-node-contract.md),
[`owned-git-engine-spec.md`](owned-git-engine-spec.md),
[`feature-parity-audit.md`](feature-parity-audit.md).

---

## 1. The finding that shapes this design

The obvious design is GitHub's: if you can write to the repository, edit it
directly; if you cannot, fork it, edit the fork, and open a pull request from
the fork. That shape exists because a GitHub pull request is **a pointer to a
branch in a repository you must be able to push to**. Without a fork there is
nowhere to put the commits, so the fork has to come first.

A ForkMesh pull request is not a pointer. It is **a signed patch**, and it
carries the change inside the submission:

- `app/src/events.py:277` — `verify_pull_event` checks only the author's own
  Ed25519 signature over `title`, `base`, `head`, `patch` and (in the current
  five-field form) `commits`. There is no write-access check, no membership
  check, and no check that the head branch exists anywhere.
- `app/src/entry.py:36239` — the `POST /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/pulls` handler
  gates on signature, byte size (`MAX_PULL_BYTES`, 100 MB), inbox depth
  (`MAX_PENDING_PULLS`, 200) and a per-author quota. Nothing else.
- `desktop/src/MainWindowPulls.cpp:6975` — when the desktop submits to a
  repository it does not own, it labels the head `<node>:<branch>` and records
  the reason in a comment: *the owner merges from the carried patch/commits,
  never by resolving head.* The head name is informational on the receiving
  side.
- `desktop/src/PullStore.cpp:3067` — a pull request that is not branch-backed
  is merged with `git apply --index --3way`, or `git am --3way` when the
  submission carried a `commits` mbox.

**Forking is therefore not a precondition for contributing.** The half of the
GitHub flow that says "no access, so fork first" is a habit imported from a
different protocol, and it happens to be the half a phone is worst at: it
demands a full clone, a hosted copy, and a second published repository before
anyone can fix a typo.

Dropping it removes the hardest piece of the feature and leaves a better one.

### What forking is actually for here

A fork on ForkMesh is a **durable, addressable copy you keep**: somewhere to
land many changes over time, a link other people can clone, a place to publish
work that is not ready to propose. That is a real thing to want, and §6
describes how the phone does it. It is simply not a gate that belongs in front
of an edit button.

---

## 2. What the phone already has

| Piece | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Read-only remote browse | `RepoFileScreen` — `native/ios/ForkMesh/Features/Code/RepoFileScreen.swift`, `native/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/feature/code/RepoFileScreen.kt` |
| Clone to device, capped at 96 MB | `native/ios/ForkMesh/Features/LocalRepos/CloneToDeviceButton.swift`, `native/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/feature/localrepos/CloneToDevice.kt`; `GitWorkspace.maxCloneBytes` |
| A real file editor over a local workspace | `LocalFileEditorScreen` — `native/ios/ForkMesh/Features/LocalRepos/LocalFileEditorScreen.swift`, `native/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/feature/localrepos/LocalFileEditorScreen.kt` |
| Stage, commit, branch, push, fetch, publish | `GitWorkspace`, `PublishService` — `native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMCode/Local/`, `native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/localrepos/` |
| Unified-diff builder with `index` lines for three-way apply | `PatchBuilder` — `native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMDiff/PatchBuilder.swift`, `native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/localrepos/PatchBuilder.kt` |
| Pull request prepare and submit | `PullRequestService` — `native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMCode/Local/PullRequestService.swift`, `native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/localrepos/PullRequestService.kt` |
| Signed submission over the wire | `InboxService.submitNewPull` — `native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMApi/Services/InboxService.swift`, `native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/api/InboxService.kt` |
| A dialog that asks the human to paste a unified diff | `showNewPullDialog` — `native/ios/ForkMesh/Features/Code/Collab/RepoPullsTab.swift`, `native/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/feature/code/collab/Composers.kt` |

When this design was written, most of the machinery existed, but
`PullRequestService` was reachable only by the coding agent and by nothing a
human could tap.

### Three gaps (closed by §9)

1. **`PullRequestService.submit` pushes the branch before submitting and hard
   fails when the push is rejected**. On
   a repository the person cannot push to, that fails before the pull request
   is attempted at all. The push has to become conditional.
2. **`submitNewPull` signs the four-field legacy canonical**
   and never sends `commits`, `description` or
   `authorName`. Every pull request opened from the phone today therefore
   arrives with an empty body and loses the contributor's commit authorship and
   message, because the owner merges it with `git apply` rather than `git am`.
   This is worth fixing on its own merits, independently of file editing.
3. Nothing tells the app whether the signed-in account can write to
   `owner/repo`, and there is no human-reachable "create pull request" action.

---

## 3. Three tiers, and what ships first

| Tier | What it is | Needs a clone |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Quick edit: change one file from the repository browser and propose it | No |
| 2 | Clone and work: the existing local workspace, with a pull request action | Yes |
| 3 | Fork: keep a published copy of your own | Yes |

**Round one is Tier 1, one file per pull request.** Tier 2 is mostly plumbing
on top of what exists. Tier 3 reduces to a single catalog field (§6).

Two decisions constrain the rest of this document:

- **Every edit opens a pull request, including when the person has write
  access.** Write access does not change the flow; it only means the branch can
  also be pushed so the pull request is fetchable. One code path, and nothing
  merges unreviewed from a phone.
- **One file per pull request to start.** The common case is a typo, a README
  line, a one-line patch. Multi-file work goes through a clone, where a real
  index and a real status view already exist.

---

## 4. Building a patch without a clone

A git blob id is `sha1("blob " + <byte length> + "\0" + <bytes>)`. Nothing
about that needs a repository, so the phone can compute both sides of an
`index` line from bytes it already has. That is what makes Tier 1 possible:

1. Fetch the file's **raw bytes** for the ref being browsed.
2. `oldId` = sha1 of those bytes in blob form. `newId` = sha1 of the edited
   text encoded as UTF-8.
3. Emit one `diff --git a/<path> b/<path>` section with an `index
   <oldId>..<newId>` line and hunks from the Myers differ already in
   `PatchBuilder`.
4. Sign and submit it as a pull request.

No clone, no 96 MB ceiling, works against a repository of any size, and the
round trip is seconds rather than minutes.

### Four rules that keep the patch valid

**Diff the raw bytes, not the decoded string.** `git apply --3way` resolves the
`index` ids to reconstruct the pre-image; if `oldId` is not the *real* blob id,
the three-way fallback has no anchor and the patch either applies by luck or
fails confusingly. `RepoBlob.content` is a `String` with a separate `encoding`
field, so it may have been decoded or
normalized in transit. The base side must come from the raw endpoint —
`ApiService.rawBytes`.

**Cross-check against the served blob id when there is one.**
`RepoTreeEntry.sha` carries the blob id when the serving
node supplies it. When it is present and disagrees with the computed id, the
bytes are not the bytes git has. Refuse the quick edit and offer the clone path
instead of submitting a patch with a wrong pre-image. A clean refusal beats a
silent corruption.

**Omit the mode suffix on the `index` line.** `PatchBuilder.between` always
writes one, which is correct when it read the mode out of a
real tree. The tree API does not expose file mode, so the clone-free path does
not know it. `index <old>..<new>` with no mode is valid git for a modification
and asserts nothing — which is exactly right. Writing `100644` on a guess would
silently strip the executable bit from any script edited on a phone.

**Refuse bytes that are not valid UTF-8 rather than decoding them lossily.**
This rule was not in the first draft of this design; it surfaced in
implementation and is the sharpest of the four. `PatchBuilder.between` decodes
lossily, which is safe there because the decoded text is
only ever *compared* and git applies the result against blobs it holds. In the
clone-free path the decoded text **becomes the new file content**, so a byte
that U+FFFD stood in for would be written back as U+FFFD and silently corrupt
the file. Refusing sends the person to the clone path, where the bytes survive
round-tripping.

### Shape of the change

`PatchBuilder` gains a sibling to `between()`: `forFile`, in
`native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/localrepos/PatchBuilder.kt`
and, on iOS, `LocalPatch.forFile` in
`native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMCode/Local/PullRequestService.swift`:

```swift
public static func forFile(
    path: String,
    beforeBytes: [UInt8],
    afterText: String,
    oldId: GitObjectId,
    newId: GitObjectId,
    context: Int = PatchBuilder.defaultContext
) -> PatchBuildResult
```

The per-file half of the diff is already parameterized on a blob id and
mode, which is trivially constructible from a computed id, so this is an
extraction rather than a rewrite. Binary detection, the trailing-newline
handling and the edit-distance ceiling all come along unchanged.

---

## 5. Write access, and why it does not gate round one

The relay authorizes a push when the presented key is the owner account's
primary key, **or** an enabled `owner_sign` device carrying `publish_repo`,
**or** the key of an account holding org write-or-better permission on a linked
repository (`app/src/entry.py:46715`, `_org_write_allowed` at
`app/src/entry.py:25545`). The third case cannot be computed on the phone.

Because every edit opens a pull request and Tier 1 has no branch to push,
**round one does not need to know the answer at all.** The question returns in
Tier 2, where pushing the branch makes the pull request fetchable.

When it does return, the client should not model the rule — it should ask. The
signed advertisement request is already the authorization oracle:

```
GET /{owner}/{repo}/info/refs?service=git-receive-pack
X-ForkMesh-Pubkey / X-ForkMesh-Ts / X-ForkMesh-Sig
```

It runs through the same `_git_push_authorize` with the empty-body digest
(`app/src/entry.py:46952`). `200` means the push would be accepted, `401` means
it would not, and `503 push_unavailable` means the mesh has no push target
right now — which is **not** a permission answer and must not be shown as one.
No new server code, and the result is the truth rather than an inference that
can drift from the rule it copies.

---

## 6. Forking, as the phone can do it

A mobile node cannot host: `mobile_node` capabilities are
`browse,comment,submit_issue,submit_pr,publish_repo,owner_sign` — no
`host_repo`, no `mirror_repo` (`mobile-node-contract.md:37`). It can publish,
and a first push lands on the configured hosted write endpoint. So a fork from
the phone is not a new mechanism at all:

> clone the upstream → publish as `<me>/<name>` with `forkedFrom` set to
> `<upstream owner>/<name>` in the signed catalog record.

The relay already normalizes that field, refuses a self-referential edge, and
indexes it into the parent's fork list (`app/src/catalog.py:388-394`). The
record it hashes must match byte for byte, so the field has to be **absent, not
empty**, when the repository is not a fork — an empty string would change the
canonical JSON and break catalog-v2 signatures from older clients.

That is one optional parameter threaded through `buildCatalogRecord`
(`PublishService`). It is worth landing on
its own, ahead of any fork button, so an already-published clone can be
correctly marked.

The relay's own fork endpoint (`POST /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/forks`) requires
a linked headless managed mirror and returns `409 headless_mirror_required`
otherwise. It is the right path for the website and the wrong one for a phone;
publish directly instead.

---

## 7. Wire shape of a Tier 1 submission

```json
{
  "pull": {
    "title":       "Fix the install command in the README",
    "base":        "main",
    "head":        "kaif:mobile-edit/readme-md-0919-1430",
    "patch":       "diff --git a/README.md b/README.md\nindex a1b2…..c3d4…\n…",
    "commits":     "",
    "description": "Typed on a phone.",
    "author":      "<node pubkey, base64url>",
    "authorName":  "kaif",
    "ts":          1758290000000,
    "sig":         "<Ed25519 over the canonical>"
  }
}
```

- **`base`** is the ref being browsed. `_CodeTab` only ever switches among
  branch names from `_BranchSelector`, so this is always a branch name and
  never a bare commit id — which matters, because the owner's node merges into
  it.
- **`head`** follows the desktop's cross-node convention: the account name, a
  colon, then a generated label. There is no branch behind it and none is
  needed; the receiving node never resolves it.
- **`commits`** is empty in Tier 1 — there are no local commits to format. It
  is populated in Tier 2, where the work happened on a real branch.
- The canonical is the five-field form,
  `"\x00".join([title, base, head, patch, commits])`, hashed and signed under
  `forkmesh-pull-event-v1` (`app/src/events.py:292-306`).

The relay assigns the number after verifying the signature, deliberately
outside the signed bytes, so the owner's node can renumber on a collision
without invalidating anything (`app/src/entry.py:36332-36340`).

---

## 8. Limits and failure modes

| Condition | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Binary file, or content that sniffs as binary | Named as such in the editor, with the clone path offered |
| Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 | Same: refused rather than decoded lossily (§4) |
| File over 512 KB | Refused, with the clone path offered |
| Served blob id disagrees with the computed one | Refuse, explain, offer the clone path (§4) |
| Signed out | `requireAccount`, as every other write action already does |
| Private repository | Already a 404 on the pulls endpoint for non-owners; browse does not reach it either |
| Upstream moved while the person was typing | Submitted anyway. `--3way` absorbs ordinary drift; a genuine conflict surfaces to the owner at merge, the same exposure the GitHub web editor carries |
| Repository inbox at `MAX_PENDING_PULLS` (200) | `429 inbox_full` — surface it as "this repository is not accepting pull requests right now", not as a failure of the edit |
| Author over per-repo quota | `429 author_quota` — same treatment |

Two things this design makes newly relevant. Patch size is a non-issue
(`MAX_PULL_BYTES` is 100 MB), but the **inbox depth and per-author quota** were
sized for desktop nodes; making contribution cheap on a phone will reach them
sooner. And a repository whose owner node never drains its inbox will swallow
submissions silently — the pending state deserves to be visible in the UI
before this feature is widely used.

---

## 9. Delivery

What shipped, in dependency order:

1. **The full pull request submission.** `submitNewPull` gained `commits`,
   `description` and `authorName`, and signs the five-field canonical. Stands
   alone; fixes gap 2 for the agent flow and the paste-a-diff dialog as well.
2. **Blob ids from bytes** — `BlobId` (`native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMCode/Local/BlobId.swift`,
   `native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/localrepos/BlobId.kt`), with
   `servedBlobIdAgrees` for the cross-check. Vectors are `git hash-object`
   output.
3. **Single-file diffing** — `PatchBuilder.forFile`, with the no-mode `index`
   line. Held to the suite's existing standard: every generated patch is fed
   to real `git apply`, including a test that builds a `100755` file and
   asserts the bit survives the round trip.
4. **`ApiService.rawBytes`** — the file's exact bytes, uncached, since a blob
   id computed from a round-tripped `String` is an id git disagrees with.
5. **The quick editor** — `QuickEditScreen` (`native/ios/ForkMesh/Features/LocalRepos/QuickEditScreen.swift`,
   `native/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/feature/code/QuickEditScreen.kt`), reached
   from an Edit action in `RepoFileScreen`. The Edit action is offered on path
   alone so it can sit in the app bar without waiting on the blob; the editor
   itself refuses binary, non-UTF-8, oversized and disagreeing content once it
   has the bytes.
6. **`forkedFrom` through `buildCatalogRecord`** (§6). This went one step
   past plumbing: the information was already on hand, since a cloned record's
   `publishedAs` names the upstream until the publish rewrites it, so
   publishing a clone under your own account now records the parent without
   any new UI.

Deferred, deliberately: the push-access probe (§5), the "create pull request"
action in `LocalRepoScreen`, multi-file quick edits, file creation and
deletion, and a fork button.

### Known limits of what shipped

- **A Tier 1 pull request carries no `commits` mbox**, because a change
  composed without local commits has none to format. The owner therefore
  merges it with `git apply --index --3way` under their own name, and the
  contributor is recorded by the relay rather than by git. Change 1 fixes this
  for the flows that *do* have commits; Tier 1 cannot, and an mbox writer in
  `PatchBuilder` is the work that would close it.
- **`InboxService` calls `http.post` directly** rather than through an
  injectable client, so the submission leg has no test double. The patch it
  submits is covered against real git, and the screen either side of it is
  covered, but the wire call itself is not. Making the client injectable —
  as `ApiService` already is — would close that gap.

`showNewPullDialog`, which asks a person to
paste a unified diff into a phone, is now redundant for the single-file case.
Retiring it belongs in its own change, not folded into a feature.

---

## 10. Evidence

| Claim | Where to check |
| --- | --- |
| A pull request is verified only against its author's signature | `app/src/events.py:277` |
| Submission gates are signature, size, inbox depth, author quota | `app/src/entry.py:36239`, `:557`, `:577`, `:578` |
| Cross-node pull requests carry the patch; head is informational | `desktop/src/MainWindowPulls.cpp:6975` |
| A non-branch-backed pull request merges by patch | `desktop/src/PullStore.cpp:3056-3067` |
| Branch-backing is decided by the receiving node, not the sender | `desktop/src/PullStore.cpp:2705-2745` |
| Push authorization rule | `app/src/entry.py:46715`, `:25545` |
| The advertisement GET runs the same authorization | `app/src/entry.py:46952` |
| `forkedFrom` is normalized and indexed by the relay | `app/src/catalog.py:382-394` |
| A mobile node may publish but never host | `www/docs/mobile/mobile-node-contract.md:37` |
| Mobile signs the five-field canonical | `native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMApi/Services/InboxService.swift`, `native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/api/InboxService.kt` |
| Clone ceiling on mobile | `GitWorkspace.maxCloneBytes` in `native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMCode/Local/GitWorkspace.swift`, `native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/localrepos/GitWorkspace.kt` |

pages.title: ForkMesh-Owned Git Engine Compatibility Matrix
pages.description: Status: IMPLEMENTED, AWAITING REVIEW as Phase G0 design evidence.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh-Owned Git Engine Compatibility Matrix

Status: `IMPLEMENTED, AWAITING REVIEW` as Phase G0 design evidence.

This matrix is structured for direct conversion into machine-readable records without changing its meaning.

`Status` means the intended initial engine behavior, not a claim that the behavior already exists.

`Oracle` names the required external compatibility evidence and is test-only where it refers to system Git.

| Feature | First phase | Initial status | Interoperability oracle | Security gate | Explicit non-goal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local non-bare SHA-1 init and open | G1 | Planned | System Git opens ForkMesh-created repository and ForkMesh opens system-Git fixture. | Repository layout, object ID, config, and ref validation. | Bare app repositories. |
| Loose blob objects | G1 | Planned | Bidirectional blob hash and body comparison. | Declared-size, zlib, object-size, and SHA-1 screen policy. | Unbounded blobs. |
| Loose tree objects | G1 read, G2 write | Planned | System Git `cat-file` and ForkMesh tree traversal agree. | Raw-byte ordering, duplicate, traversal, and mode rejection. | Gitlinks and submodule checkout. |
| Loose commit objects | G1 read, G2 write | Planned | Commit OID, parent, tree, author, and message agree. | Header injection and size limits. | Signed commit verification. |
| Annotated tags | G1 parse | Planned | System Git object inspection agrees. | Header and object-type validation. | Tag creation and signature verification. |
| SHA-1 repositories | G1 trusted local, G4.5 security gate, G5 network | Blocked for untrusted input | Published vectors, system-Git object IDs, and pinned SHA1DC adapter tests. | Full-frame fail-closed screening, corpus evidence, independent cryptography review, and Android validation before untrusted input. | Collision-safe claim from ordinary SHA-1 alone. |
| SHA-256 repositories | Later | Rejected | Future full SHA-256 fixture suite. | Complete object, index, pack, and protocol review. | Partial SHA-256 support. |
| Loose refs and symbolic `HEAD` | G1 | Planned | System Git sees created branch and detached HEAD state. | Ref grammar, lock, expected-old-OID, and atomic rename. | Arbitrary ref namespaces. |
| Packed refs read | G1 | Planned | System Git packed fixture resolves same refs and peeled tags. | Checksum-free format bounds, sorting, and duplicate rejection. | Packed-refs rewrite. |
| Reflogs | G2 | Planned | System Git reads local branch and HEAD log entries. | Append-after-commit transaction order and bounded messages. | Remote-tracking reflogs. |
| Repository-local config subset | G1 | Planned | System Git recognizes written remote and branch settings. | No includes, helpers, hooks, or global configuration. | Full Git config language. |
| Index v2 | G2 | Planned | System Git status and ForkMesh status agree on shared fixtures. | DIRC checksum, sort order, stage, path, and extension validation. | Index v3, v4, split, sparse, fsmonitor, and untracked cache. |
| Status and add | G2 | Planned | System Git index and working tree result match. | Worktree confinement and resource limits. | Rename heuristic parity. |
| Remove and delete | G2 | Planned | System Git sees expected deletion commit. | Path validation and atomic index/ref update. | Recursive destructive public API without caller confirmation. |
| Branch and checkout | G2 | Planned | System Git and ForkMesh resolve identical branch trees. | Symlink, traversal, platform collision, and staging-root checks. | Linked worktrees. |
| Commit creation | G2 | Planned | System Git verifies tree and commit OID. | UTF-8 and header controls, atomic index/ref/reflog transaction. | GPG or SSH signing. |
| Pack v2 read | G3 | Planned | System Git fixtures from multiple versions resolve identical objects. | Header, trailer, CRC, checksum, zlib, and total-resource limits. | Pack v3 and thin packs. |
| Pack index v2 read | G3 | Planned | OID lookup matches system-Git pack index. | Fanout, offset, large-offset, and checksum bounds. | Multi-pack index and reverse index. |
| OFS_DELTA and REF_DELTA | G3 | Planned | Reconstructed object IDs match system Git. | Base availability, depth, ratio, range, and allocation limits. | Unbounded delta chains. |
| Pack v2 write | G4 | Planned | System Git verifies and unpacks produced pack. | Streaming hash, cancellation, quarantine, and atomic install. | Delta writing before non-delta gate passes. |
| Pack index v2 write | G4 | Planned | System Git opens generated index. | Sorted OIDs, CRC, offset, and checksum verification. | Reverse index or multi-pack index. |
| pkt-line | G5 | Planned | Disposable smart-HTTP fixture exchanges exact packets. | Four-hex length, control packet, count, and output limits. | Text-line parsing. |
| Protocol v2 `ls-refs` and fetch | G5 | Planned | Disposable Git HTTP server and selected read-only fixture. | Capability allowlist, ref count, sideband, TLS, and pack quarantine. | Unsupported v2 commands. |
| Protocol v0 or v1 fallback | G5 | Opt-in only | Server without v2 and exact expected advertisement. | Same-origin HTTPS, no redirect, explicit caller opt-in, and valid MIME type. | Silent downgrade. |
| HTTPS clone and fetch | G5 | Planned | Disposable smart-HTTP server and mobile platform run in G7. | Strict TLS, host-scoped test trust, credential redaction, cancellation, and resource limits. | HTTP, `file`, Git native, SSH, and process transports. |
| Credential challenge | G5 | Planned | Wrong disposable credential fails typed and correct one succeeds. | No URL user-info, logging, persistence, or redirect forwarding of secrets. | Credential helpers. |
| Certificate challenge | G5 | Planned | Self-signed fixture is rejected by default and scoped test trust succeeds. | Host and certificate pin scope, TLS downgrade rejection, and no global trust mutation. | Broad trust-all policy. |
| Shallow clone | After normal G5 | Deferred | Future system-Git shallow fixture. | Shallow boundary and object reachability review. | Implicit depth handling. |
| Partial or promisor clone | Later | Rejected | Future protocol and promisor corpus. | Missing-object and server-trust review. | Filter negotiation. |
| Smart HTTP push | G6 | Planned | Disposable receive-pack server and system-Git verification. | Expected-old-OID, report-status, per-ref result, authentication, and cancellation. | Implicit force push. |
| Non-fast-forward rejection | G6 | Planned | Competing writer leaves remote OID unchanged after rejection. | Compare-and-swap ref commands and no force capability. | Last-writer-wins. |
| Ref deletion | G6 | Deferred within phase | Disposable receive-pack server. | Separate destructive API, caller confirmation, and explicit capability. | Empty refspec convenience behavior. |
| SSH transport | Later | Rejected | Future SSH fixture. | Host-key, key storage, and agent policy review. | Shell SSH fallback. |
| Git LFS | Later | Rejected | Future LFS server fixture. | Pointer, authorization, and large-object policy review. | Filter or pre-push emulation. |
| Submodules | Later | Rejected | Future nested-repository fixture. | Gitlink, URL, recursion, and trust review. | Automatic recursive update. |
| Linked worktrees | Later | Rejected | Future worktree interoperability fixture. | Cross-directory lock and path policy review. | Partial linked-worktree support. |
| Merge and rebase | G8 | Deferred | System-Git merge and conflict corpus. | Conflict index, recovery, and data-loss review. | Silent conflict resolution. |
| Hooks | Never | Rejected | Not applicable. | No code execution from repository configuration. | Hook compatibility. |
| Credential helpers | Never | Rejected | Not applicable. | Secret confinement and no process execution. | Helper protocol compatibility. |
| Signed commits and tags | Later | Deferred | Future signature corpus and verified key policy. | Independent cryptography and trust review. | Treating signature text as verification. |
| Android and iOS core execution | G7 | Planned | iOS simulator/device and Android emulator/device complete flow. | App-private storage, lifecycle cancellation, secure credential bridge, and quota evidence. | Public repository storage. |
| Desktop test hosts | G1 onward | Planned test-only | macOS and Windows interoperability suites. | Same path, malformed input, and case-collision tests. | Desktop-specific runtime dependency. |

The Phase 0 catalog capability IDs `repo.clone`, `repo.store`, `git.branch`, `git.commit`, and `git.push` remain `planned` until their respective engine and authorization phases have passed their gates.

No matrix row grants a capability merely because a local implementation phase is complete.

The node registration, repository role, capability-grant, and truthful availability checks defined by the version 1 contracts remain independent authorization gates.
