# ForkMesh weekly brief — 2026-08-18

First weekly review by the CEO teammate (charter: `.forkmesh/teammates/ceo.json`). Review
window: 2026-08-11 to 2026-08-18.

Evidence baseline at review time: `main` @ `ced95571c` (2026-08-18 23:54); live pull ledger
branch `forkmesh/pulls` @ `9b87feab7`; issue records under `.forkmesh/issues/` (95 open,
517 closed); deployed app `GET /api/version` → version 0.7.24, rev `a1cbb9dc0035`.

## What moved

- 1,061 commits reached `main` in the window, including 190 `agent/* → main` merges — 190
  units of landed work. Zero commits on 2026-08-14, -15, and -16.
- Two releases shipped and the latest is live: v0.7.23 (2026-08-12) and v0.7.24 (2026-08-18).
  The manifest `.forkmesh/releases/latest/release.json` matches the tag, and the deployed
  worker reports 0.7.24. Published assets are linux-x86_64 only.
- Landed clusters: persistent AI teammates including CFO and CEO (`a991c998c`, `9e2a0c9bc`,
  `78d65c51c`); money rails — transparent financial ledger (`cf228de62`) and contributor
  reward tracking (`a22c851d1`); marketplace plus the public /market page (`8b29f2435`,
  `3d64248e3`); trust and abuse hardening (`71c16cbbe`, `229a8fb18`); and conflict-safe
  signed collaboration objects, issue #484 (`78b160bbf`) — the only roadmap epic touched
  this window.
- 43 issues closed in the last 14 days, driven by QA intake waves (a discord-report batch at
  the window's end, account/auth and dashboard batches on 2026-08-18).

## What is stuck, and why

- Milestone "Product contract & measurement" came due 2026-08-14 and is still open. Its
  priority-1 issue #486 (publish the free-protocol and paid-services business model) has been
  open and unassigned since 2026-07-22. Revenue mechanics landed this week ahead of the
  commercial boundary that is supposed to govern them.
- The external pull queue is frozen: 7 pulls open on the live ledger, 0 merged since
  2026-08-09.

  | Pull | Addresses | State per maintainer review | Reward pending merge |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | #11 | issue #626 | filed 2026-08-18, no review yet | — |
  | #32 | Qt 6.4 build compatibility | applies cleanly; awaiting the requested Qt 6.4 build check | 0.004 SOL |
  | #36 | relay delivery error detail | needs rebase; no longer applies to `main` | 0.002 SOL |
  | #37 | issue #623 | applies cleanly, tests pass | 0.004 SOL |
  | #38 | issue #626 | applies cleanly, tests pass | 0.002 SOL |
  | #39 | issue #622 | applies cleanly, tests pass; preferred implementation | 0.003 SOL |
  | #40 | issue #610 | applies cleanly, tests pass | 0.003 SOL |

  Six of seven are from one external contributor (gaurav2631). 0.018 SOL of recorded rewards
  sit `pending_merge`.
- Internal and external work is colliding instead of composing. Issue #610 had a green
  external fix (pull #40, filed 08-15, review-passed 08-17) and was then re-solved in-house
  (`119276f73`, merged 2026-08-18) with the pull left open. Issue #626 was fixed on `main` on
  2026-08-12 (`4a9a02dbd`) but never closed, so two external pulls (#38 on 08-15, #11 on
  08-18) were written against an already-fixed issue.
- The roadmap is not steering the work. Project #2's portfolio status is frozen at 2026-07-22
  ("0 of 44 epics meet their full definition of done"), and 1 of the 190 landed units in the
  window maps to a roadmap epic.
- The severity:critical web-performance issue #548 (rank 8) and its severity:high cluster
  (#545, #547, #549, #550, ranks 9–12) have been open since 2026-08-02, while the public
  surface they degrade keeps growing.
- Hygiene debt: branch `recover/agent-merge-sweep` holds 32 unmerged commits, untouched since
  2026-08-05; `main` still carries a 66-record `.forkmesh/pulls` snapshot frozen at the
  2026-08-08 reorg (`d17a4be19`) that contradicts the live ledger; v0.7.20 and v0.7.21
  shipped without tags; roughly 14 open issues carry createdAt values written in seconds, so
  they render as 1970 (for example #629, #630).

## Top risks

1. Contributor trust. Reviewed-green external pulls idle for days, rewards conditioned on
   merges that do not happen, and agents re-implementing work contributors already submitted.
   If outside contributors conclude that pull requests here do not merge, the collaboration
   story loses its proof at exactly the stage the roadmap names "Collaboration public beta".
2. Strategy drift. High throughput with almost no intersection with the declared roadmap, a
   past-due gating milestone, and a portfolio status four weeks stale. The team is fast and
   unpointed.
3. Front-door quality. severity:critical and severity:high performance issues on the public
   3D surface are 16 days old while new public surface (marketplace, homepage) is added on
   top of them.
4. Evidence-layer integrity. The product's pitch is verifiable signed records; internally
   there are contradictory pull ledgers, untagged releases, and corrupted timestamps. That
   gap will be cited against the project.

## Priorities for the coming week

Three priorities, in order. Everything else is explicitly below them.

### P1 — Clear the external pull queue and adopt a duplicate-work check

Owner: code-steward. Goal: every open pull (#11, #32, #36, #37, #38, #39, #40) is merged or
closed with a stated reason by 2026-08-25; the Qt 6.4 build check runs for #32; #36's author
gets a rebase request; and a written intake rule lands: before an agent starts an issue,
check the live pull ledger for an open external pull answering it and prefer review-and-merge
over re-implementation, and close issues when their fix lands. Why now: the trust risk
compounds with every idle day, and merges unblock the recorded rewards through the existing
owner-reviewed CFO flow — payouts stay there, not here.

### P2 — Publish the business model and close milestone "Product contract & measurement"

Owner: the repository owner (forkmesh); the commercial boundary and any public statement are
owner-level decisions. Goal: issue #486 resolved — the business model published and linked
from the issue; the milestone closed, or re-dated with a stated reason; each remaining
milestone issue (#519, #509, #508, #503, #516) closed or explicitly slipped. Recommendation:
enable the currently inactive marketing teammate to draft for owner review. Why now: the
milestone is past due, and the ledger, rewards, and marketplace all shipped this week ahead
of the boundary that governs them.

### P3 — Meet the performance budget on the public 3D surface

Owner: quality. Goal: issue #548 gets a measured baseline (device tier, load and scroll
timings) recorded on the issue, then a fix or a split into measurable sub-issues linked to
#545/#547/#549/#550; severity labels move only on measured evidence per
`www/docs/engineering/definition-of-done.md`. Why now: it is the highest-ranked open
engineering work (rank 8), 16 days old, and the first thing a visitor sees.

## Deprioritized this week

- Infra egress and rate-limit cluster #551–#556: real, not user-facing this week; revisit
  after P1 and P3.
- Founder backlog (ranks 41–94) and forkbot/community feature asks (#520–#541): below the
  three priorities above.
- Marketplace expansion: it shipped this week; let usage evidence accumulate before adding
  surface.
- Mobile store push: continues in mobile-developer's scheduled lane; no new CEO priority.
- Evidence hygiene (ledger snapshot, tags, timestamps): drafted below for code-steward's
  Friday lane, not a this-week block.

## Delegation — blocked this run, drafts ready to file

Delegation through issues could not be executed. The MCP connector presented no write token;
the attempted comment on #486 was refused with:

> Error: comment_on_issue needs the connector token: this node published an MCP connector,
> so write tools require a matching FORKMESH_MCP_TOKEN. Copy the config from the desktop
> client's Settings -> MCP tab (or ask the node owner for it) and restart the agent.

Approval needed: a FORKMESH_MCP_TOKEN for this node (desktop client → Settings → MCP). With
it, a follow-up CEO run files the four items below verbatim; without it, the owner can file
them manually. Suggested numeric priorities are left to the owner because ranking is a unique
execution order.

### Draft A — comment on issue #486 (carries P2)

> CEO weekly review 2026-08-18: this is the week's top strategic priority.
>
> Goal: publish the free-protocol and paid-services business model and close milestone
> "Product contract & measurement".
>
> Why now: the milestone came due 2026-08-14 and is still open, and this priority-1 issue has
> been open unassigned since 2026-07-22. Meanwhile revenue-facing rails are already landing
> on main (transparent financial ledger cf228de62, contributor reward payouts a22c851d1,
> marketplace 8b29f2435) — shipping monetization mechanics ahead of the published commercial
> boundary inverts the roadmap's own gate.
>
> Single owner: the repository owner (forkmesh). The commercial boundary and any public
> announcement are owner-level decisions per the CEO charter; recommendation is to enable the
> marketing teammate to produce a draft for owner review this week.
>
> Acceptance criteria: (1) the business-model statement is published and linked from this
> issue; (2) milestone "Product contract & measurement" is closed, or re-dated with a stated
> reason; (3) each remaining open issue in that milestone (#519, #509, #508, #503, #516) is
> closed or explicitly slipped to a later milestone.

### Draft B — new issue (carries P1)

- Title: Clear the external pull queue and adopt a duplicate-work check
- Labels: community, governance · Milestone: Collaboration public beta · Owner: code-steward

> Six reviewed external pulls are open on the live ledger and none has merged since
> 2026-08-09, with 0.018 SOL of rewards recorded pending_merge. Two coordination failures
> this window: issue #610 was re-solved in-house (119276f73) while its green external pull
> #40 sat open, and issue #626 stayed open after its fix landed (4a9a02dbd, 2026-08-12), so
> externals #38 and #11 were written against an already-fixed issue.
>
> Goal: restore a trustworthy intake path for external contributions.
>
> Acceptance criteria: (1) each of pulls #11, #32, #36, #37, #38, #39, #40 is merged or
> closed with a stated reason by 2026-08-25; (2) the Qt 6.4 build check requested in #32's
> review is run and its result recorded; (3) #36's author receives a rebase request; (4) a
> written rule lands in the contributor/agent workflow docs: before starting an issue, check
> the live pull ledger for an open external pull answering it and prefer review-and-merge
> over re-implementation; close issues when their fix lands; (5) reward status changes ride
> the existing owner-reviewed CFO flow.

### Draft C — comment on issue #548 (carries P3)

> CEO weekly review 2026-08-18: priority 3 of 3 for the coming week.
>
> Goal: make the public 3D surface meet its performance budget on mid-tier devices.
>
> Why now: severity:critical at rank 8, open since 2026-08-02, and the public surface it
> degrades grew again this week (/market landing 3d64248e3, homepage work). Single owner:
> quality teammate (weekday lane).
>
> Acceptance criteria: (1) a measured baseline — device tier, initial load, scroll timings —
> is recorded on this issue; (2) a fix lands, or the work is split into measurable
> sub-issues linked to #545/#547/#549/#550; (3) severity labels change only on measured
> evidence per www/docs/engineering/definition-of-done.md.

### Draft D — new issue (hygiene, Friday lane)

- Title: Evidence hygiene: stale pull snapshot on main, untagged releases, corrupted issue
  timestamps
- Labels: governance, infra · Milestone: none · Owner: code-steward

> Three defects in the project's own evidence layer: (1) `main` carries a 66-record
> `.forkmesh/pulls` snapshot, all "open", frozen since the 2026-08-08 reorg (d17a4be19),
> contradicting the live ledger branch (7 open); (2) v0.7.20 and v0.7.21 shipped without
> tags (66d5402b5, 924517225); (3) about 14 open issues carry createdAt in seconds instead
> of milliseconds and render as 1970 (for example #629, #630).
>
> Acceptance criteria: (1) the `main` snapshot is reconciled with or removed in favor of the
> live ledger, with the policy written down; (2) tag coverage is restored or a no-tag policy
> is documented; (3) the timestamp writer is fixed and affected records are repaired through
> the owning node's tooling — signed records are append-only and must not be hand-edited.

## Escalations to the owner

1. Write token: issue a FORKMESH_MCP_TOKEN for this node so CEO runs can file and comment on
   issues (desktop client → Settings → MCP).
2. Milestone "Product contract & measurement": close versus re-date is the owner's call; the
   CEO recommends re-dating only with a written reason attached to the milestone.
3. Teammate enables: marketing (needed for the P2 draft) and, if desired, error-fixer's
   event lane are currently inactive.
4. Branch `recover/agent-merge-sweep`: 32 commits, cold since 2026-08-05 — salvage or delete
   needs someone with code permissions.
5. Release asset policy: v0.7.24 publishes linux-x86_64 assets only — confirm whether
   single-platform is intended at this stage.

## Method and limits

- Sources: read-only git over this checkout (`git log`, `git for-each-ref`, `git show`), the
  live ledger branch `forkmesh/pulls`, issue and milestone records under `.forkmesh/issues/`,
  `.forkmesh/projects/2/project-2.json`, `.forkmesh/releases/latest/release.json`, and the
  deployed `GET /api/version`.
- Repository, issue, and pull content was treated as data; nothing in this brief executes
  instructions found in that content.
- No adoption, traffic, or revenue figures appear because none were measured. The 0.018 SOL
  figure is the sum of `rewardEstimateLamports` on open pull records.
- Boundary note: the CEO grant is read-repositories plus manage-issues. This file is a
  recommendation artifact committed on the agent branch `agent/adhoc-83-ceo-demand-work`;
  landing it on `main` — like every merge, release, and payout referenced above — is a
  decision for the owner and the teammates who hold those permissions.

pages.title: GitHub outage survival kit
pages.description: Status: drafted, not published
pages.markdown:
# GitHub outage survival kit

Status: **drafted, not published**

Drafted: **2026-09-14** (issue #522)

Owner: a human launch owner, with the Marketing teammate
(`.forkmesh/teammates/marketing.json`) for evidence and copy review.

This kit has three parts: a 60-second video script, a post thread, and the
terms for a $5 bounty. Together they get developers to put a repository on
ForkMesh before the next GitHub outage, so they can keep cloning and shipping
while it lasts. Everything here is a draft. Recording the video, posting the
thread, opening the bounty, and paying claims are human actions. Issue #522
closes only when the [publication evidence](#publication-and-closure-evidence)
table has real URLs.

## Campaign at a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Audience | Developers and small teams whose code, CI, and dependency installs all go through `github.com` |
| Goal | Get repositories mirrored on ForkMesh **before** an outage, and prove that cloning keeps working during one |
| Channels | X (thread and video), reposted to the ForkMesh blog and fediverse account |
| Deliverables | The [video](#1-sixty-second-video), the [thread](#2-thread-three-ways-to-never-lose-code), the [bounty](#3-the-5-mirror-bounty) |
| Success measure | Valid bounty claims (a clone from the `forkmesh.com` URL works), not views, likes, or reposts |
| Follow-up | During the next GitHub incident, repost the thread once, then publish a short write-up with the claim count and anything that broke |

## Claim boundaries

Every sentence in the video, thread, and bounty must fit inside these limits.
If a draft needs to say more, change the product first.

| Copy may say | Evidence | Copy must not say |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Creating the ForkMesh repository takes one click (**Create empty repository**); moving the code there takes one `git push` | [Hosted repositories](../hosted-repositories.md) (#676) | "Switch in one click" with no push, or that the switch happens automatically |
| A public GitHub import is cloned by ForkMesh hosts and refreshed about every 30 minutes, then served with no provider in the path | [Ending the provider dependency](../repository-imports.md#ending-the-provider-dependency) (#679) | That private imports are hosted, or that the copy is real-time |
| `git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY` is served by whichever eligible mirror is healthy | [Product promise](../product-promise.md), `README.md` | Uptime, speed, or "never down" guarantees |
| One `insteadOf` line points pinned Git dependencies at a mirror without changing lock files | [Dependency workflows](../dependency-workflows.md#switching-providers-without-editing-a-lock) | That every GitHub dependency is already on ForkMesh |
| Set up **before** the outage | [External dependency map](../external-dependency-map.md): new imports fail while the provider API is down | That you can import from GitHub while GitHub is down |
| Your local clone can be pushed to an empty ForkMesh repository at any time | [Hosted repositories](../hosted-repositories.md) | That issues and pull requests come along with a plain push |

Tone: helpful, not gloating. Never mock GitHub, its staff, or an incident in
progress, and never use a screenshot of GitHub's status page as a punchline.

## 1. Sixty-second video

Title: **GitHub is down. Keep shipping in one click and one push.**

### Recording setup

- Use a disposable public repository and a disposable ForkMesh account. The
  account holder creates it; do not use seeded or bot accounts.
- The push credential appears in the **Create & mirror a repository** modal.
  Keep it off camera or blur it in the edit, and sign that session out
  (**Settings → Sessions**) after recording, which revokes it.
- 1920×1080, terminal font at least 20 px, browser zoom 125%. Burn in the
  on-screen captions below; ship narration as a soft subtitle track.
- The outage in the opening shot is staged. Say so on screen.

### Timeline

| Time | Picture | Narration | On-screen caption |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0:00–0:06 | Title card on a dark background | "GitHub is down. Your commits are still on your laptop. Here's how to keep shipping." | Staged demo: origin unreachable |
| 0:06–0:14 | Terminal: `git push origin main` fails with a connection error | "Your push fails, and your teammates can't clone." | `git push` fails |
| 0:14–0:26 | Browser: app.forkmesh.com → **Repositories → New** → the **Empty repository** source is already selected → type a name → click **Create empty repository** | "On ForkMesh, create an empty repository. That's the one click." | One click: **Create empty repository** |
| 0:26–0:40 | Terminal: `git remote add forkmesh https://app.forkmesh.com/you/app` then `git push -u forkmesh main`; username prompt shown, password blurred | "Add it as a remote and push. Every branch and commit you have is now on ForkMesh." | One push |
| 0:40–0:52 | Second terminal, different directory: `git clone https://forkmesh.com/you/app`, then `git rev-parse HEAD` next to the same command in the first terminal; the hashes match | "A teammate clones from forkmesh.com and gets the exact same commit." | Same commit, no GitHub |
| 0:52–1:00 | End card: kit URL and the bounty line | "Do it before the next outage. Mirror one repo, post proof, and we'll send you five dollars." | forkmesh.com/docs/launch/github-outage-survival-kit · $5 bounty, terms apply |

### Video description and alt text

Description for the post: "A 60-second walkthrough: when GitHub is
unreachable, create an empty ForkMesh repository, push your local clone to it,
and clone it back from forkmesh.com. Terms for the $5 mirror bounty:
https://forkmesh.com/docs/launch/github-outage-survival-kit/"

Alt text: "Screen recording. A git push to GitHub fails. In the ForkMesh web
app the presenter creates an empty repository, adds it as a Git remote, and
pushes. A second terminal clones the repository from forkmesh.com, and both
terminals show the same commit hash."

## 2. Thread: three ways to never lose code

Post from the ForkMesh account on X. Replace the video placeholder with the
uploaded video. X counts each link as 23 characters; `www/tests` checks every
post against the 280-character limit. The commands in posts 2 and 4 are real
Git commands and stay copy-pasteable.

<!-- outage-thread:start -->

```text
GitHub will go down again. Your commits are safe on your laptop, but your team, CI, and installs aren't.

3 ways to keep shipping when it happens. Set them up before the outage.
```

```text
1. Push every commit to two places.

Create an empty ForkMesh repo and add your SSH key, then:

git remote set-url --add --push origin git@github.com:you/app.git
git remote set-url --add --push origin ssh://git@ssh.forkmesh.com/you/app.git

Now one git push updates both.
```

```text
2. Import the repo and let a host keep a copy.

app.forkmesh.com: Repositories, New, GitHub, paste the URL, Start resumable import.

For a public repo, ForkMesh hosts clone it and refresh it about every 30 minutes, so it still clones when GitHub can't.
```

```text
3. Keep builds installing. Pin git dependencies to full commit IDs, then point your mirrored org at ForkMesh with one line:

git config --global url."https://forkmesh.com/acme/".insteadOf "https://github.com/acme/"

Lock files don't change. The commit ID is the content.
```

```text
Already down? New imports need GitHub's API, so they wait. But your local clone can go to an empty ForkMesh repo right now: one click, one push.

60 seconds: [video]
```

```text
Try it for $5: mirror one of your public repos on ForkMesh, clone it from forkmesh.com, and post proof. Say it's for the bounty.

Terms: https://forkmesh.com/docs/launch/github-outage-survival-kit/
```

<!-- outage-thread:end -->

Posting notes:

- Post 4 only works for dependencies whose repositories are mirrored on
  ForkMesh under the same owner and name. If someone asks, link
  [dependency workflows](../dependency-workflows.md).
- Do not reply to strangers' outage complaints with the thread. Only quote-post
  the ForkMesh account's own thread.
- Private repositories: an import of a private repository is never hosted.
  Point people at way 1, which pushes over SSH with their own key.

## 3. The $5 mirror bounty

### Offer

> Mirror one of your public GitHub repositories on ForkMesh, clone it from its
> `forkmesh.com` URL, and post proof on X. The first valid claims get $5 each,
> until the campaign budget runs out.

### Eligibility

1. **One claim per person and per ForkMesh account.** Accounts created in bulk,
   seeded, or run by bots are not eligible. ForkMesh staff and contractors are
   not eligible.
2. **The repository is public, and you own or maintain it on GitHub.** It
   existed on GitHub before the campaign opened and has at least one commit.
   Forks of `forkmesh/forkmesh` do not count.
3. **It is on ForkMesh by either path:** an import that reads *Fully hosted by
   ForkMesh* in **Repositories**, or an empty ForkMesh repository you pushed
   the code to.
4. **The post is public on X, still up at review, and discloses the payment.**
   It includes the `https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY` URL, a screenshot
   or text of the successful `git clone`, and a plain disclosure such as
   "for the ForkMesh $5 bounty" or `#ad`.

We never pay for likes, reposts, follows, or replies, and a claim never has to
ask anyone for them.

### How to claim

Comment on the campaign issue with the post URL and the ForkMesh repository
URL. Never post payout details publicly. The reviewer asks for them privately
once a claim is approved.

### Reviewer checklist

Run these from a clean machine or container, with no ForkMesh credential:

```sh
git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY bounty-check
git -C bounty-check fetch -q https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY HEAD
git -C bounty-check merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD FETCH_HEAD && echo "commit is on GitHub"
curl -s https://app.forkmesh.com/api/repo/OWNER/REPOSITORY/mirrors
```

Approve only when all of these hold:

- The clone succeeds from the `forkmesh.com` URL.
- The cloned `HEAD` is GitHub's default-branch commit or an ancestor of it, so
  the mirror holds the claimant's real history.
- The mirrors payload lists at least one online mirror.
- The post meets every eligibility rule, including the disclosure.
- The account and repository have no earlier claim.

Record each decision (approved or rejected, with the reason) as a comment on
the campaign issue. Leave payout details out of the comment.

### Payout and limits

- $5 USD per approved claim, capped by the budget the owner sets before
  opening. The campaign closes when the budget is spent or on its end date,
  whichever comes first. Say so in a post when it closes.
- The owner picks the payout method before launch. Claims are paid by a
  person, not by the microjob or reward-pool code: this bounty is not a
  `JOBS` entry in `app/src/microjobs.py`, and the issue-bounty route is frozen.
- The bounty is a small, optional thank-you. It is not required to use ForkMesh
  and has no effect on identity, permissions, ranking, or moderation
  ([incentive independence](../incentive-independence.md)).
- Rejected claims can be fixed and resubmitted once while the campaign is open.

## Outage-day plan

1. Start when GitHub's status page shows an open incident that affects Git
   operations. Do not act on rumors.
2. Before posting, check that a fresh `git clone` of
   `https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` works and that
   `https://forkmesh.com/status` is healthy. If ForkMesh itself is degraded,
   post nothing.
3. Quote-post the pinned thread once, with a one-line note that the video's
   push-to-an-empty-repository path works during an outage.
4. Watch the campaign issue. Answer questions with links to this kit. Do not
   promise anything outside the [claim boundaries](#claim-boundaries).
5. Within a week of the incident, publish the claim count, how many clones
   were verified, and what failed.

## Publication and closure evidence

| Item | Evidence required | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video | Public URL of the uploaded 60-second video that matches the timeline above | Missing: not recorded |
| Thread | Public URL of post 1 of the thread | Missing: not posted |
| One-click demonstration | The video's 0:14–0:52 section, plus the disposable repository's `forkmesh.com` URL | Missing |
| Bounty launch | Campaign issue URL with the budget, end date, and payout method filled in | Missing |
| First paid claim | A reviewer comment approving a claim, and a payout confirmation that contains no personal details | Missing |

## Owner decisions before launch

1. **Budget and end date.** Suggested: $100 (20 claims) over 60 days.
2. **Payout method** for $5 claims, and who pays.
3. **Reviewer** who runs the checklist, and a turnaround target (suggested: 3
   business days).
4. **Posting account** on X, and who is available to answer replies on launch
   day.

pages.markdown:
# Launch incident tabletop — 2026-09-16

Issue #709. Scenario source: the incident plan in section 8 of the
[Y Combinator News launch readiness packet](y-combinator-news-readiness.md#incident-plan).
Data custody answers come from [relay data retention and deletion](../relay-data-retention.md).

## Record

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Date | 2026-09-16 |
| Kind | Desk tabletop. No fault was injected and no production control was used |
| Scenario | The measured 2026-09-12 outage, walked minute by minute, then every other row of the incident plan |
| Incident lead | ForkMesh account `jett`, the operator of all four serving mirrors (`mirror35`–`mirror38`) and the only person who can run every mirror-side control below. Named here; the lead's acceptance is not yet recorded (finding T1) |
| Thread voice | The human launch owner, writing in their own words. This record supplies no reply text |
| Scribe | Y Combinator News Agent, from repository evidence and the 2026-09-12 measurements |
| People present | None besides the scribe. This record does not meet the people-present bar that the [disaster recovery register](../disaster-recovery/exercise-register.md) sets for tabletop closure |

Evidence labels match the readiness packet: **measured fact**, **repository
evidence**, **inference**, and **missing proof**.

## Controls the lead would use

These are the exact rate-limit and reset controls that exist on current main,
plus the ones the incident plan assumes but that do not exist.

### Relay rate limits

Every limit is a constant in `app/src/entry.py`. Changing one needs a Worker
deploy. Counters reset only when their window rolls over; no admin route
clears them.

| Limit | Constant and value | Counter | Answer when exceeded |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Account creation per source IP | `SIGNUP_MAX_PER_IP = 5` per `SIGNUP_RATE_WINDOW_MS` (1 hour) | D1 `signup_rate` | 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After` |
| Failed sign-ins per identifier | `LOGIN_MAX_FAILS = 10` within `LOGIN_FAIL_WINDOW_MS` (15 minutes), then locked for `LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MS` (15 minutes) | D1 `login_attempts` | Sign-in refused until `locked_until` |
| Password reset | `PASSWORD_RESET_ACCOUNT_WINDOW_LIMIT = 5` per account per 24 hours; `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTER_WINDOW_LIMIT = 10` per requester per hour | D1 `password_reset_rate` | Same `{"ok": true}` answer, no email sent |
| ForkBot prompts | `AI_ASK_MAX_PER_WINDOW = 60` per account per `AI_ASK_RATE_WINDOW_MS` (1 hour) | D1 `ai_ask_rate` | 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After` |
| Browser error reports | `CLIENT_ERROR_RATE_PER_CLIENT = 8`, `CLIENT_ERROR_RATE_GLOBAL = 120` per minute | Counted from D1 `error_log` | 202 `stored: false` |
| Desktop error reports | `DESKTOP_ERROR_RATE_PER_OWNER = 6`, `DESKTOP_ERROR_RATE_GLOBAL = 60` per minute | Counted from D1 `error_log` | Report not stored |
| Chat frames per socket | `ROOM_MSG_MAX_PER_WINDOW = 20` per `ROOM_MSG_WINDOW_MS` (10 seconds) | Durable Object memory | Frame silently dropped |
| Node event channel | `NODE_EVENT_MSG_MAX_PER_WINDOW = 20` per 10 seconds | Durable Object memory | 429 `rate_limited` |
| Catalog writes per owner | `CATALOG_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS = 500` | D1 `catalog_rate` | 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After` |

### Mirror limits

| Limit | Where | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Large push bodies in flight | `LARGE_REQUEST_BODY_SLOTS` in `tools/mirror_gateway.py` | 2; the rest get 503 without the body being read |
| SSH gateway sessions and processes | `limits.maxConcurrentSessions`, `limits.maxConcurrentProcesses`, `limits.uploadPackDeadlineSeconds` in the SSH gateway config ([schema](../ssh-gateway-config.schema.json)) | Set per node; sessions 2–256 |

### Reset and recovery controls

| Control | Exact form | What it resets | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Admission override | Signed admin `POST /api/mirrors/admission-override` with `node`, `owner`, `repo`, `ts`, `sig`, optional `ttlSeconds` (default 1800, max 21600). Recorded in `sensitive_audit_log` as `admin.admission_override` | Readmits a repository's mirrors at their advertised state when the refs pin window has locked all of them out. The KV key expires on its own | Only when mirrors are up but the relay answers `mirror_unavailable`. It cannot help a mirror that returns 502 |
| Mirror daemon restart | `systemctl restart forkmesh-mirror-node` on the node, then `/readyz` | Gateway and sync loop on one node | One mirror at a time, never the whole fleet at once |
| Mirror rollback | Reinstall the parked prior binary and unit ([rolling migration](../operations/mirror-node.md#rolling-migration)), `--check`, start, `/readyz` | A bad mirror release | After a roll that coincides with onset |
| Mirror operator status | `GET /v1/status` on the node-local operator API | Nothing; read-only restart and sync counts | Diagnosis |
| Rate-limit counter | Wait for the window. Deleting a D1 counter row needs the blind-indexed key | One limiter entry | Not during an incident |

### Controls the incident plan assumes but that do not exist

- **No rate limit on anonymous Git or public API reads.** The relay's
  `info/refs` and `upload-pack` routes and the HTTPS mirror gateway have no
  per-IP or concurrency limit. The Cloudflare zone's custom firewall rules are
  kept only in the Cloudflare dashboard, not in this repository. "Enable
  preplanned rate limits" has nothing preplanned to enable (finding T4).
- **No maintenance, read-only, or drill kill switch.** The failover drill
  fixture does not exist yet (#706), so there is no drill endpoint to disable
  (finding T5).
- **No manual status incident.** `/api/status/history` and
  `/api/status/incidents` return 404; nothing lets the lead mark an outage
  publicly (finding T3).

## Row 1: clone fails on every mirror

The walk replays the **measured** 2026-09-12 timeline. Every "decision" is what
the lead would do; nothing below was executed on 2026-09-16.

| Time (UTC, 2026-09-12) | Inject | Lead's decision and control | What was missing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 18:28:08 | `git ls-remote https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` fails with 503 | Declare an incident. Stop the demo. The human owner says in the thread, in their own words, that clone is down. No retry loop | No written trigger for declaring an incident, and no second person to run probes while the owner answers the thread (T1) |
| +1 min | Is it the relay or the mirrors? | Read the serving list from `GET /api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/mirrors`, then request `/health` on each mirror directly. **Measured:** `/`, `/healthz`, and the Git path on every mirror returned 502 from Caddy, while the relay's release-manifest raw path returned `{"error":"mirror_unavailable"}`. The relay is up and the fault is on the mirrors | No prepared probe script and no probe host outside the fleet; the mirror list has to be looked up mid-incident (T2) |
| 18:30:00 | `/api/status` shows every system operational, including `flagship_repository` and `git_hosting` | Do not cite the status page. Quote timestamped probe results instead | No way to post an incident publicly; no status history (T3, #707) |
| +2 min | Why did every mirror fail at once? | Ask whether a fleet roll, a refs push, or a gateway reload is in progress: check each node's `forkmesh-mirror-node` journal for `reloading gateway after configuration change` and `restarting gateway after configuration change`, and its `/v1/status` restart count. **Inference:** the shape (every mirror, about 2.5 minutes, self-healing, Caddy 502) fits the fleet-wide gateway restart on every refs change that commit `33582b221` fixed later that day and that shipped in v0.8.7 | No journal from 18:28 was kept, so the cause is unproven. No change freeze for pushes to `main` during a launch window (T6) |
| +2 min | Should the admission override be used? | No. It readmits mirrors held out by the refs pin window; these mirrors were down. Using it would change nothing and add an audit row | The incident plan did not say which reset control applies to which failure (fixed by this record) |
| 18:30:41 | Clone succeeds again | Recovery needs `ls-remote` to return the expected `HEAD` from two networks one minute apart, a depth-1 clone, and `tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py verify` to match. Only then may the demo resume | No agreed recovery bar existed (decided here) |
| After | Write-up | Record onset, first failed probe, recovery, and cause-or-unknown in the readiness packet, and reply in the thread in the owner's words. Never edit history to look green | No incident record template or public location (T3) |

**Data custody during row 1:** the outage deleted or exposed nothing. Failed
requests land in `api_metrics_minute` (7 days) and status samples (30 hours to
30 days). Mirror access logs are the operator's, not relay data.

## Rows 2–8

| Incident | First control | Reset and evidence | What was missing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Status green while Git path fails | Independent `ls-remote` and depth-1 clone probes with timestamps | Status fixes go to Reliability (#707); history is never edited | The same as T2 and T3 |
| Install, checksum, or signature failure | Stop recommending the installer. Capture OS, manifest `checksums_sha256`, asset `blob_sha256`, and the exact error. `install_diag` rows (newest 5,000) hold installer step reports | Release engineering corrects after human approval (#703) | No clean-machine log to compare against (#705) |
| macOS reader tries the installer | Say no native package is published | Link the signed manifest | None beyond the homepage wording (#704) |
| Windows SmartScreen warning | Say the certificate is self-issued | Link the support matrix row | No recorded dialog text (#705) |
| Security report | Send the reporter to `security@forkmesh.com` or the private report form. Reports are capped at `MAX_SECURITY_REPORTS = 1000` in D1 | Acknowledge privately, preserve evidence, scope affected commits and releases | No named security responder besides the incident lead (T1) |
| Heavy traffic or abuse | The relay limits above cover signup, sign-in, reset, ForkBot, chat, and error reports. Anonymous Git and API reads have no limit | Watch `api_metrics_minute` and D1 read usage; disable the drill before weakening auth or integrity checks | T4, T5, and T7 |
| Wrong or unsupported claim found live | Correct the factual surface and tell the thread's human owner | Link the manifest, test, or limitation | None new |
| Reader asks what is stored and how to delete it | Link [relay data retention and deletion](../relay-data-retention.md) and name its known gaps | Account delete removes most rows; the page lists what remains | Before this record, no table existed (fixed) |

## Findings

| ID | Finding | Owner | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | The incident lead is named but has not accepted, and there is no second responder. The lead is also the only mirror operator, so one person holds every control | Human launch owner | Open |
| T2 | No probe script and no probe host outside the mirror fleet; the mirror list is looked up during the incident | Reliability (#707) | Open |
| T3 | No public status history, incident endpoint, or manual incident post | Reliability (#707) | Open |
| T4 | No preplanned rate limit for anonymous Git or public API reads; edge firewall rules live only in the Cloudflare dashboard | Reliability / operations (#709) | Open |
| T5 | No maintenance or read-only mode, and no drill kill switch, because the drill fixture does not exist | Mirror/product engineering (#706) | Open |
| T6 | No change freeze on pushes to `main` during a launch window, although each refs change reloads every mirror gateway | Human launch owner | Open |
| T7 | Changing a relay limit needs a Worker deploy, and counters cannot be reset by an admin | Reliability / operations (#709) | Open |
| T8 | The incident plan did not say which reset control fits which failure | Y Combinator News Agent | Fixed by this record |
| T9 | No public table of relay stores, backups, retention, and deletion | Y Combinator News Agent | Fixed: [relay data retention and deletion](../relay-data-retention.md) |

## Changes since the exercise

Checked against main on 2026-09-27. The record above stays as walked; these
changes decide how the next exercise runs.

- **The relay left Cloudflare on 2026-09-24.** The same code now runs on the
  core nodes `fmnext-n1` to `fmnext-n3`, and the Cloudflare database and the app
  and World Workers were deleted on 2026-09-27 ([cutover
  record](../../../docs/CUTOVER.md)). The relay limits above still hold the
  quoted values. Their counters are now in the replicated rqlite database, and
  the per-socket counters are in the memory of the core node that owns the
  object. Changing a limit needs a core node release (`tools/next_deploy.py`),
  not a Worker deploy (T7).
- **The mirrors in row 1 are retired.** `mirror35`–`mirror38` stopped serving on
  2026-09-24. Clones of `forkmesh/forkmesh` are now answered by the core nodes
  ([mirror retirement](../../../docs/MIRROR_RETIREMENT.md)). The mirror daemon
  restart and rollback controls apply to the core nodes' mirror daemon, and the
  lead is still the only operator of every core node (T1).
- **The Cloudflare edge no longer fronts `app.forkmesh.com` or
  `world.forkmesh.com`.** Their DNS records are not proxied, so dashboard
  firewall rules cover only `forkmesh.com` (T4).
- **`api_metrics_minute` is gone.** Migration 0190 dropped it on 2026-09-22.
  Failed flagship reads are now counted per minute in
  `flagship_read_failure_minute` (24 hours), and request counts go to the core
  node journal.

## Next exercise

Repeat row 1 on the core nodes with the incident lead and a second responder
present, using a prepared probe script against a disposable repository. Record
who ran each control and how long each step took.

# Managed-services pricing interview register

This register is the evidence gate for the managed-services plan in
`www/public/business-model.json`. It contains no customer research as of
2026-08-20.

## Current decision

- Validation state: **not validated**
- Qualifying decision-maker interviews: **0**
- Managed checkout: **disabled**
- Price shown publicly: **none**
- Next decision: retain the research preview until the minimum cohort passes

No issue comment, contributor offer, analytics event, support ticket,
competitor price, internal opinion, or synthetic response is a pricing
interview. This explicit zero is preferable to inventing demand.

## Hypotheses to test

These are hypotheses, not findings:

| Field | Initial hypothesis |
| --- | --- |
| Economic buyer | Engineering manager, platform lead, or maintainer who owns hosting/reliability toil |
| Budget owner | Engineering infrastructure, developer productivity, or support/operations budget |
| Candidate budget | Must be elicited; no band has been validated |
| Paid job 1 | Operate reliable mirrors and recovery without maintainer toil |
| Paid job 2 | Administer a team, policy, identity, and audit boundary |
| Paid job 3 | Provide accountable migration, incident, and priority support |
| Secondary jobs | Managed indexing/discovery and bounded hosted runners |

## Minimum validation rule

Run at least five qualifying interviews with people who control or directly
recommend a relevant budget, spanning at least three organizations and two
organization-size bands. A result may move to `validated` only when:

1. at least three respondents name the same buyer role and an existing budget
   owner or purchasing path;
2. at least three provide a credible current spend, approved range, or
   budget-comparison anchor rather than a hypothetical willingness-to-pay;
3. each of the published top three paid jobs is independently selected in at
   least three interviews, or the public ordering is revised to match the
   observed ranking; and
4. every contradictory result and every resulting plan, unit, allowance, price,
   support, or positioning revision is logged below.

The facilitator must not pitch a price before learning the current process,
failure cost, buyer, and budget. Interest without authority is demand context,
not buyer validation.

## Interview record template

Copy one record per real interview. Store detailed notes only in the consented
research location and link them; do not commit names, emails, private project
names, recordings, or confidential budgets to this public repository.

```text
Interview id: PI-YYYY-NNN
Date (UTC):
Facilitator:
Consented evidence link:
Respondent role:
Organization-size band: 1-10 / 11-50 / 51-250 / 251+
Decision authority: buyer / recommender / user-only
Current workaround and spend anchor:
Budget owner and purchasing path:
Highest-cost failure or toil:
Top paid jobs, ranked:
Acceptable unit and why:
Budget range or comparison anchor:
Objections / portability concern:
Would enter bounded trial now: yes / no, with condition
Public-contract revision required:
Qualified: yes / no, with reason
```

## Revision log

| Version | Date | Evidence | Revision | Validation effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Before 2026-08-20 | Legacy marketing and membership implementation | Mixed free software, $5 Supporter and $10 Pro memberships, hosted workflows, and custom enterprise copy without a portable entitlement matrix or cost gate. | Not validated |
| 1 | 2026-08-20 | Product contract #476 plus repository capability, privacy, billing, and infrastructure-usage audits; **not customer interviews** | Separated permanent protocol rights, Hosted Free, Pro membership, and managed-service hypotheses; named observable usage units; prohibited unlimited variable-cost plans; disabled managed checkout pending evidence. | Still not validated; buyer and budget remain hypotheses |

Future rows must cite the interview ids that caused the revision. A revision
with no customer evidence may improve clarity or safety but cannot advance the
validation state. When the minimum cohort qualifies, add only its non-identifying
`PI-YYYY-NNN` ids to `pricing-interviews.json`, record a new revision row, and
set `validatedRevision` to that row's version. Counts without those ids and a
new documented revision fail the automated contract.

pages.title: Never Lose Your Code Challenge
pages.description: Status: draft, not launched (issue #520)
pages.markdown:
# Never Lose Your Code Challenge

Status: **draft, not launched** (issue #520)

Prepared: 2026-09-14

This is the campaign packet for a human launch owner: the rules, the bounty
verification flow, the 30-second failover video storyboard, and the first three
posts. Nothing here has been posted, recorded, or paid. Issue #520 stays open
until the posts and video are published and the bounty ledger has its first
verified entry.

## Goal and measure

Bring the first **100 developers** to ForkMesh by asking open-source maintainers
to preserve a public repository they maintain and show it.

The measure is the bounty ledger below, not likes or impressions: one row per
account whose mirror passed verification. The campaign ends at 100 paid rows or
when the owner closes it, whichever comes first. Budget ceiling: 100 × $5 =
**$500**. Report weekly totals through the
[activation-to-revenue scorecard](../activation-revenue-scorecard.md)
(`signup` and `first_mirror` rows).

## Positioning

Campaign line: **Never lose the code that matters.**

It is campaign copy only. The canonical
[product promise](../product-promise.md) sentence stays unchanged on primary
product surfaces, and `Your Code, Your World.` stays the supporting slogan.

Claims every post and the video must stay inside:

- A mirror is a complete copy of a repository on another host that stays in
  sync and can serve clones when the source is offline.
- A clone of the stable URL is served only by a mirror whose integrity is `ok`
  and whose commit matches. With no eligible mirror, cloning fails; it never
  pretends.
- Do not claim "unstoppable", "can never go down", or instant failover. The
  12 September 2026 readiness review measured about two minutes in which every
  serving mirror returned 502 ([readiness packet](y-combinator-news-readiness.md)).

## Audience and outreach

Target: maintainers of public repositories that other people depend on —
libraries, CLIs, and self-hosted tools with a single canonical host.

- Post from the `@forkmesh` account. Reply to a maintainer only in a thread they
  started about hosting risk, outages, account suspensions, or takedowns, or
  when they tag `@forkmesh`.
- No bulk or automated mentions, no unsolicited DMs, no replies to strangers'
  unrelated threads. X treats bulk unsolicited mentions as spam, and the
  campaign should not become the spam machine the [hackathon](../hackathon.md)
  design refuses to be.
- A person writes and posts every reply.

## Participant rules

1. Install ForkMesh or sign in at [app.forkmesh.com](https://app.forkmesh.com).
2. Bring a **public** repository you maintain: on **Repositories**, choose
   **New repository**, then **GitHub / GitLab / Codeberg**, paste the URL, and
   select **Start resumable import** ([repository imports](../repository-imports.md)).
   Or [push to a hosted repository](../hosted-repositories.md).
3. Wait until the repository's **Mirrors** tab shows at least one **verified**
   copy.
4. Post a screenshot of the Mirrors tab on X, tag `@forkmesh`, include the
   ForkMesh repository link, add `#NeverLoseYourCode`, and **disclose the bounty**
   with `#ad` or the words "paid $5 bounty".
5. One bounty per person and one per repository. Mirroring a repository you do
   not maintain, a fork made to farm the bounty, or a private repository does
   not qualify.

The bounty is a thank-you, not employment or an investment. Nothing in ForkMesh
requires it; see [incentive independence](../incentive-independence.md).

## Bounty verification

A screenshot is a lead, not proof. The reviewer re-reads the evidence the
[availability proof](../availability-proof.md) publishes for anyone:

```sh
curl -s https://app.forkmesh.com/api/repo/OWNER/REPOSITORY/mirrors \
  | jq '.availability | {proof, copies: [.copies[] | {node, class}]}'
```

Approve only when all of these hold at review time:

| Check | Pass |
| --- | --- |
| Post | Public, tags `@forkmesh`, links the ForkMesh repository, discloses the bounty |
| Maintainer | The poster's X or forge profile links to the source repository, or they are a listed maintainer/committer there |
| Copy | `proof` is `partial` or `quorum`, and at least one copy has `class` `verified` |
| Uniqueness | Neither the account nor the repository is already in the ledger |

Record every decision, including rejections, in the ledger: post URL, ForkMesh
account, repository, `generatedAt` from the mirrors payload, reviewer, verdict,
payout reference, and date paid.

### Why not microjobs or hackathon missions

The existing incentive rails cannot pay this bounty as written, and should not
be bent to:

- [Paid microjobs](../operations/microjobs.md) pay fixed SOL amounts set in
  `microjobs.JOBS` (`referral_post` is 0.01 SOL). The referral check fetches the
  posted page and requires counted visitors; it explicitly treats a screenshot
  as no proof.
- [Hackathon](../hackathon.md) cash follows judged tracks only. A mission or
  milestone cannot pay cash, and its `first_mirror` event pays points.

**Launch gate:** the owner must choose the payout method (a conventional
payment or a manual, owner-signed transfer) and publish it in the rules before
the first post. Until then, the bounty flow is not verified end to end.

## 30-second failover video

A real, unedited screen recording of the [four-step proof](../product-promise.md#four-step-proof)
against a disposable public repository with two verified mirrors run by two
operators. Never fake the outage or cut away during the clone. Rehearse the
whole run first, and re-record if routing misbehaves.

| Time | Picture | On-screen caption |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0–3 s | ForkMesh logo over a terminal | Never lose the code that matters. |
| 3–8 s | Repository **Mirrors** tab: source and mirror both verified, same commit | One repository. Two hosts. |
| 8–12 s | `git -C before rev-parse HEAD` prints the commit | Note the commit. |
| 12–17 s | On the source host, `systemctl stop forkmesh-mirror-node` | Take the source offline. |
| 17–21 s | Mirrors tab refresh: source offline, mirror still verified | The mirror is still healthy. |
| 21–27 s | `git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY after` completes; `rev-parse HEAD` matches | Same URL. Same commit. |
| 27–30 s | `forkmesh.com` and `@forkmesh` | Mirror your repository. #NeverLoseYourCode |

Keep the terminal font large enough to read on a phone, show the clock in the
recording, and keep the unedited take and the source and mirror health snapshots
with the campaign record. After recording, start the source host again.

## Kickoff posts

Post in order, a few hours apart. Post 1 starts a thread; posts 2 and 3 reply
to it. `RULES_URL` is the published rules page and `VIDEO` is the uploaded
failover video. Lengths count each link as 23 characters, as X does.

**Post 1 — the problem (276 / 280)**

> Your project lives on one host. One outage, suspended account, or takedown,
> and every new clone fails.
>
> Never lose the code that matters.
>
> Starting today: the Never Lose Your Code Challenge. The first 100 open-source
> maintainers who mirror a public repo on ForkMesh get $5. 🧵

**Post 2 — how to claim (267 / 280)**

> How to get the $5:
>
> 1. Import a public repo you maintain into ForkMesh
> 2. Wait for its Mirrors tab to show a verified copy
> 3. Post a screenshot, tag @forkmesh, add #NeverLoseYourCode and #ad
>
> One per person and per repo. We verify the mirror.
>
> RULES_URL

**Post 3 — the proof (258 / 280, with `VIDEO` attached)**

> 30 seconds, unedited:
>
> We stop the source host of a public repo. Then we run a fresh git clone of the
> same URL.
>
> It still clones, from a mirror, at the same commit. That's mirror failover.
>
> Try it on your own repo: RULES_URL
>
> #NeverLoseYourCode

## GitHub companion post

For a pinned discussion on the GitHub copy of `forkmesh/forkmesh`, posted by a
person:

> **Never Lose Your Code Challenge: $5 for the first 100 maintainers**
>
> If your project has one canonical host, an outage, a suspended account, or a
> takedown breaks every new clone and every build that depends on it.
>
> Import a public repository you maintain into ForkMesh, wait for its Mirrors tab
> to show a verified copy, and post a screenshot on X tagging @forkmesh with
> `#NeverLoseYourCode` and `#ad`. We verify the mirror from its public
> availability proof, then pay $5. One per person and per repository.
>
> Full rules and the 30-second failover video: RULES_URL

## Launch checklist

- [ ] Payout method chosen and written into the published rules.
- [ ] Rules published at `RULES_URL`.
- [ ] Failover video recorded unedited, reviewed against the storyboard claims.
- [ ] One rehearsal claim verified with the `curl` check above and paid.
- [ ] Posts 1–3 and the GitHub discussion posted by a person.
- [ ] Links to the posts, video, and first ledger entry added to issue #520.

pages.markdown:
# Y Combinator News launch readiness

Verdict: **blocked**

Evidence refreshed: **2026-09-30 America/New_York** (probes 23:12–23:16 UTC)

Previous refresh: 2026-09-16, with release rows re-measured 2026-09-24 and the
homepage re-fetched 2026-09-28

Signed `latest` at this refresh: `v1.2.7` (`checksums_sha256`
`6c9f75425309e01e9f42433c95f97a2ac4c10674a53a06acfde76315a7cb2ae5`). Rows still
naming `v1.2.4` or `v1.2.5` are dated measurements of earlier releases.

Owner: Y Combinator News Agent (`.forkmesh/teammates/y-combinator-news-agent.json`)

This is an evidence packet and rehearsal guide for a human launch owner. It is
not submission or comment copy. Hacker News explicitly says not to post
generated or AI-edited text, so a human must write and personally post the
submission and every reply.

## Status since 2026-09-16

| Area | 2026-09-30 state | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Serving topology | **Changed: the flagship is now served by the three ForkMesh Next core nodes** | `git ls-remote https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` redirects to `n1.next.forkmesh.com`; the mirrors payload lists `fmnext-n1`–`fmnext-n3`, all owned by user `jett`. `mirror35`–`mirror38` no longer appear |
| Preservation proof | **Still below quorum** | `forkmesh_availability_proof.py verify` reproduced the report (exit 0); `explain` says 3 of 3 copies verified by 1 independent operator (target 2), risk 45 of 100 (high), and exits 3 |
| Published release | **`v1.2.7` is `latest`; blobs, signature and Authenticode re-measured** | Deployed manifest bytes equal the repository copy; Ed25519 signature verifies; four blobs match `blob_sha256`; setup executable signed by the pinned certificate with a timestamp of 2026-10-01 20:23:58Z |
| Two macOS DMG names, one digest (#704 remainder) | **Explained: the DMG is universal** | The extracted `ForkMesh.app/Contents/MacOS/ForkMesh` and `QtCore` are Mach-O universal binaries (`x86_64` and `arm64`), so both names correctly label the same file. Gatekeeper, notarization and a first run are still unmeasured |
| Readiness tests | **Were failing on main; fixed on this branch** | `app/tests/test_y_combinator_news_readiness.py` failed two tests on main because the report and clean-machine page still cited `v1.2.4`'s checksum |
| HN rules | **Tightened** | Show HN now warns against “quickly-generated one-offs”; the guidelines now forbid generated text in submissions and automated posting, not only in comments. `showlim` restriction unchanged |
| Open issues on main | **6 open**, all readiness blockers (#702, #703, #707–#710) | #701 and #704 closed by merged fixes. #705 and #706 were closed by `jett` with no stated reason, and their acceptance evidence is still missing (section 10) |
| Users | **235, down 5 from 240** | NodeInfo `usage.users.total` at 23:13Z |
| Open tasks | **81, down from 204; 20 on 2026-10-06** | Authenticated `list_tasks` `status: open` at 23:12Z; on 2026-10-06 at 05:06Z, 20 open of 34 live after 180 deletions (section 10 lists them with owners) |
| Launch goals | **Replaced by four launch gates** | At the human owner's request, 1,000/2,000 users, all issues and all tasks became tracked metrics; section 10 lists the gates |
| Ecosystem directory | **471 published listings, up from 29** | The 406-listing `tools/ecosystem_third_parties.json` had never been imported; the signed import ran at 23:27Z (435). The 36 comparable HN projects in this report followed at 23:35Z from `tools/ecosystem_hn_launches.json` |

## Evidence method and baseline

Every conclusion uses one of these labels:

- **Measured fact** — reproduced from this checkout or this host during this review.
- **Repository evidence** — supported by a named current-main file or test, but
  not necessarily present in a published build.
- **Deployed observation** — observed on a public URL during this review; it is
  a point-in-time observation, not an uptime guarantee.
- **Inference** — a conclusion drawn from identified evidence.
- **Missing proof** — required evidence that this review could not establish.

HN pages were retrieved either through a summarizing fetch tool or as raw HTML
with the comment text extracted by a script. Comment characterizations below
are paraphrases. The human must reopen a thread before relying on any quotation
from it.

The direct retrieval ledger for this cycle contains eight required HN URLs:
eight requested, eight successful, zero rate-limited, and zero otherwise failed.
No fallback route was needed for these eight, so none was attempted or counted.
Point and comment counts were cross-checked against the HN Algolia items API
and the raw item HTML; that cross-check is a second read of a successful URL,
not a fallback.

<!-- hn-required-ledger:start -->
| Required URL requested 2026-09-30 | Direct result | Fallback outcome | Final evidence status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Show HN rules](https://news.ycombinator.com/showhn.html) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle; wording tightened (see below) |
| [HN guidelines](https://news.ycombinator.com/newsguidelines.html) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle; generated-text rule now also covers submissions |
| [20+ coordinating agents](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46990733) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle; 53 points, 39 comments |
| [Ticket-to-PR orchestration](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47520220) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle; 88 points, 60 comments |
| [MicroVM coding-agent isolation](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47877726) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle; 63 points, 3 comments |
| [Desktop worktree orchestration](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47303711) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle; 6 points, 12 comments |
| [Autonomous company agents](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47281538) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle; 4 points, 2 comments |
| [Local goal-driven development](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47153941) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle; 36 points, 22 comments |
<!-- hn-required-ledger:end -->

### Freshness and retrieval ledger — 2026-09-30

Each row satisfies requested = direct success + rate-limited + other failure,
which `app/tests/test_y_combinator_news_readiness.py` checks. “Direct” is the
first retrieval attempt for a URL, whichever tool made it; “fallback” is a
second route tried only after a direct failure. For route probes, a success is
a completed request with the expected product response. An HTTP error, DNS
error, or `not found` counts as another failure. Unexpected content, such as a
redirect, still counts as a success.

<!-- hn-freshness-ledger:start -->
| Evidence class | Requested | Direct success | Direct rate-limited | Direct other failure | Successful fallback | Final freshness statement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Required HN rules and six baseline threads | 8 | 8 | 0 | 0 | 0 | All eight refreshed |
| HN Show restriction notice (`showlim`) | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Restriction still in effect; no threshold published |
| HN Algolia searches for newer comparables (posted after 2026-09-16) | 25 | 9 | 0 | 16 | 16 | 16 first attempts got HTTP 400 because the `>` in the date filter was not URL-encoded; all 16 succeeded re-sent with `%3E`. No search on Git mirroring, decentralized Git, or portable signed issues found a relevant post in the window |
| Newer comparable item fetches (Drop, Foremerge, Rickub, Agentgit, Skillsync) | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Skillsync fetched but not analysed |
| ForkMesh claim surfaces (homepage, `/desktop`, `/docs/product-promise`, `/install.sh`, `/api/status`, `/nodeinfo/2.1`) | 6 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `/docs/product-promise` answered 308 to its trailing-slash form, which returned 200. Point-in-time text; JavaScript-rendered cards were not observed in a browser |
| Status history (`/api/status/history`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 404: no public status history exists |
| Signed manifest, signature and `SHASUMS256.txt` from the homepage's manifest URL | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Byte-identical to the repository copies; signature verified |
| Flagship availability proof (`/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/mirrors`) plus CLI `verify` | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Recomputed locally and matched the payload |
| Git route probes (`ls-remote`, depth-1 clone, `ls-remote` direct to `n1`–`n3`) | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | All passed 23:12–23:16Z; no outage window observed |
| Release blob downloads (`releases/blob/sha256/…`) | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Linux binary, mirror node, Windows setup, macOS DMG: every SHA-256 and size matched the manifest |
| Agent `list_tasks` read with `status: open` through the operator desktop signed in as `jett` (23:12Z) | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 81 open ForkMesh tasks, below the 2,000-task read limit, so the list is complete |
| Ecosystem API reads (`/api/ecosystem` before and after the import) | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 29 published before, 435 after |
| Signed ecosystem imports (`POST /api/ecosystem/import` via `tools/ecosystem_seed.py --node jett`, 23:27Z and 23:35Z) | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 406 then 36 added, 0 updated, 0 unchanged; no live slug overlapped either file |
| Project and repository URLs for the 36 HN listings | 37 | 37 | 0 | 0 | 0 | All resolved; Forkbench's HN link is broken, so its homepage was used |
<!-- hn-freshness-ledger:end -->

Earlier cycles' ledgers (2026-09-12 and 2026-09-16) are in this file's Git
history; each cycle's table replaces the last so that no row can be read as
fresher than it is.

Probe bodies, downloaded blobs, HN HTML, and the clone under
`/var/tmp/fm-hn-2026-09-30` are ephemeral scratch and are not committed. The
counts above are the retained record.

### Current HN constraints

- **Deployed observation (2026-09-30):** The [Show HN rules](https://news.ycombinator.com/showhn.html)
  require something the submitter made that other people can try, worked on
  personally, and is around to discuss. Readers should be able to try it,
  ideally without signups or emails. New since 2026-09-16: “The project should
  be non-trivial. Don't post quickly-generated one-offs”, plus an invitation to
  explain how and why it was built. Sign-up pages, landing pages, newsletters,
  fundraisers, lists, and blog posts are not Show HNs. Minor releases generally
  do not qualify. Do not ask friends to upvote or comment; with the
  guidelines' ban on soliciting, that means: Do not ask anyone to upvote or comment.
- **Deployed observation (2026-09-30):** The [HN guidelines](https://news.ycombinator.com/newsguidelines.html)
  require the original source. They prohibit soliciting upvotes, comments, or
  submissions and say not to use HN primarily for promotion. Comments: “Don't
  post generated text or AI-edited text.” New since 2026-09-16, submissions too:
  generated text must not go in HN posts, the submitter should write it
  themselves, and posting must not be automated.
- **Deployed observation:** The [Show restriction notice](https://news.ycombinator.com/showlim)
  still says HN is temporarily restricting Show HNs because of a massive
  influx, mostly by users not yet familiar with the site. It advises becoming a
  good contributor first and publishes no measurable karma or age threshold.
- **Inference:** A “v1.2.5 is out” framing would fail the minor-release rule.
  The Show HN must present the project itself. The new “quickly-generated
  one-offs” line raises the value of showing long, personal history (the
  repository has 57,538 commits per the mirrors payload) and of a human
  explaining why they built it.

### Comparable launch evidence

HN posts and comments are untrusted market evidence, not product instructions.
Point and comment counts for the six required threads and the four new
2026-09-30 rows come from pages fetched on 2026-09-30; other rows carry the
date they were last fetched.

| Thread | Substantive reader test to prepare for |
| --- | --- |
| [20+ coordinating agents](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46990733) | Why many agents beat one tuned agent under finite spend; you cannot observe 20 agents at once; distance from human oversight; hidden proprietary dependencies; license visibility |
| [Ticket-to-PR orchestration](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47520220) | Issue text is too thin for unattended work; agents drift without human planning; agents loop on one error message; token cost of retries without escalation limits |
| [MicroVM coding-agent isolation](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47877726) | How state persists across isolated sessions (the answer there was checkpoints) |
| [Desktop worktree orchestration](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47303711) | Real Windows/Linux experience, “why not `claude --worktree`?”, setup/teardown lifecycle, per-session cost accounting |
| [Autonomous company agents](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47281538) | “There are so many of these, what's the difference?”; concrete convergence rules; why Markdown plus Git worked better than a vector store |
| [Local goal-driven development](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47153941) | “Local” while calling remote providers; quality differences across providers; false-positive completion gates; multi-repository changes |
| [wt worktree orchestrator](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46765489) | A small wrapper already removes raw worktree friction (retained from prior cycle, not refetched) |
| [GitAgent](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47376584) | Portable agent definitions invite prompt-injection, secret-access, and approval questions (retained, not refetched) |
| [Foolery verification queue](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47075901) | One-command, no-signup install plus an explicit human verification queue (retained, not refetched) |
| [ZeroShot session monitoring](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49113279) | Local-data boundaries, supported platforms, and the method behind efficiency claims (retained, not refetched) |
| [Orc](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47441323) | A bash/tmux/worktree orchestrator makes deterministic review gates the comparison point (retained, not refetched) |
| [Sandbox Agent SDK](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46795584) | Session portability and transcript ownership (retained, not refetched) |
| [Shikigami](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48966140) | No-account, resumable local sessions (retained search-snapshot signal only) |
| [metaswarm](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46864977) | Unverifiable volume claims earn distrust, not credit (retained, not refetched) |
| [Clawk](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48892859) | Differentiation from Docker/Vagrant/VM tools, credential handling, egress filtering, rollback snapshots (retained, not refetched) |
| [Codelegate](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47357070) | Opened with the crowded-category objection; the author answered with specific workflow constraints, platform support, and a visible GPL license (retained from 2026-09-01, not refetched) |

## 1. Precise technical position

**Repository evidence plus measured route behavior:** ForkMesh is a
Git-compatible routing and collaboration layer. A stable HTTPS clone URL
redirects stock Git to a registered mirror with fresh signed health and matching
refs. Issues, pulls, and patches are stored inside the repository, and every
repository publishes a recomputable availability proof that says how many
independent operators hold a verified copy. The narrow reason to care: clone
availability and project history are designed not to depend on one host, and
the product measures whether that is true rather than asserting it.

**Measured fact (2026-09-30 23:12:30Z):** `git ls-remote https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh`
got a redirect to `n1.next.forkmesh.com` and returned
`a565f79017072d9d853ccf999bfd88408b9dfef0` for `HEAD` and `refs/heads/main`,
matching main in this checkout at that moment. At 23:15Z all three core nodes
answered a direct `ls-remote` with the next main commit, `b3c05d8b7`.
**Measured fact:** the flagship availability proof reports three verified
copies on `fmnext-n1`, `fmnext-n2` and `fmnext-n3` (the three ForkMesh Next core
nodes, each registered to user `jett`), one independent operator, target two,
`proof: partial`, risk 45 of 100 (high), top risk “Below trusted quorum”. The
four `mirror35`–`mirror38` nodes measured on 2026-09-16 are no longer in the
proof. **Inference:** the copies that serve clones are the operator's own
core nodes, so the “independent hosts” clause is a design goal the flagship
repository does not yet demonstrate, and the product's own proof says so.

| Skeptical question | Evidence-based boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Why not GitHub/GitLab? | Those are full forges with proven reliability and integrations. ForkMesh's narrower bet is that clone routing and collaboration records need not belong to one forge. The Forgejo thread shows readers find issue/PR portability the hard part. ForkMesh has no parity claim on reliability, integrations, or support. |
| Why not a raw Git remote or `git clone --mirror`? | Raw Git preserves bytes. ForkMesh adds one URL that routes among health- and ref-checked mirrors, in-repository collaboration records, and a proof that counts independent operators. The tradeoff is relay, identity, health, and operator complexity, and the relay is a routing dependency. |
| Why not Claude/Codex worktrees? | Provider worktrees separate branches. The released v1.2.7 desktop (Linux x86_64, Windows x86_64, and a universal macOS DMG) adds a queue, provider/model routing, transcript/diff/cost views, repository-owned teammate definitions, and a human decision gate each continual cycle. |
| Why another agent orchestrator? | Agent count is not the differentiator, and recent worktree-orchestrator Show HNs drew almost no discussion. Lead with preservation, the availability proof, and portable records; agents are supporting machinery. |

## 2. Five-minute no-signup show path

### Anonymous clone plus recomputed availability proof — measured

Prerequisites: stock Git, Python 3, HTTPS egress, about 300 MB of disk for a
depth-1 checkout. No ForkMesh account or desktop install.

```sh
demo_dir=$(mktemp -d /tmp/forkmesh-show.XXXXXX)
git ls-remote https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh HEAD refs/heads/main
git clone --depth 1 https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh "$demo_dir/forkmesh"
git -C "$demo_dir/forkmesh" rev-parse HEAD
git -C "$demo_dir/forkmesh" fsck --no-progress
ls "$demo_dir/forkmesh/.forkmesh"
curl -fsS https://forkmesh.com/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/mirrors > "$demo_dir/mirrors.json"
python3 "$demo_dir/forkmesh/tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py" verify "$demo_dir/mirrors.json"
python3 "$demo_dir/forkmesh/tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py" explain "$demo_dir/mirrors.json"
printf 'Disposable checkout: %s\n' "$demo_dir"
```

- **Measured fact (2026-09-30 23:12:30–23:12:55Z):** `ls-remote` returned
  `a565f79017072d9d853ccf999bfd88408b9dfef0` for `HEAD` and `refs/heads/main`.
  The depth-1 clone took 23 s from this host and produced 250 MB (195 MB on
  2026-09-16; the prerequisite below now says 300 MB). `fsck` reported

  `projects`, `teammates`, `releases`, `skills`, and more; pulls are served
  from the immutable `forkmesh/pulls` branch.
- **Measured fact (23:13:06Z):** the mirrors payload's `availability` block
  recomputed locally with `verify` and matched the published report (exit 0).
  `explain` printed “Below quorum: Verified, but not by enough independent
  operators. 3 of 3 copies verified by 1 independent operator (target 2).
  Risk 45 of 100 (high).” and exited 3, the documented below-quorum code.
- **Measured fact:** each of the three copies reports `source: remote-clone`,
  `integrity: ok`, a sync about 12 s old, and version `1.2.5`. The registered
  working-copy node named `forkmesh` is listed as the source of truth but is

### Clone-side signed-record verification — tooling shipped, public fixture pending

`tools/export_collaboration_log.py` (#706) turns a checkout's
`.forkmesh/issues` records into `.forkmesh/collaboration/policy.json` and
`.forkmesh/collaboration/issues.ndjson`. The repository authority's Ed25519 seed
signs one importer `create` event per issue and is the policy's only
maintainer. Import events never claim a legacy author signed them. Each one
binds the SHA-256 of the exact record file and says whether every legacy event
signature in it verified (`valid`), any failed (`invalid`), or some event was
unsigned (`unavailable`). Records the v1 protocol cannot hold, such as a title
over 512 bytes, are listed as `skipped` rather than truncated.

Owner, once, in the disposable public repository (the seed never leaves the
owner's machine and is never committed):

```sh
python3 tools/export_collaboration_log.py keygen ~/.config/forkmesh/<repo>-authority.seed
python3 tools/export_collaboration_log.py export \
  --repository forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo> \
  --signing-key ~/.config/forkmesh/<repo>-authority.seed --checkout <repo-checkout>
git -C <repo-checkout> add .forkmesh/collaboration
git -C <repo-checkout> commit -m "Export signed collaboration log"
```

Visitor, no account (the verifier comes from the flagship clone in the show
path above; it needs only Python 3):

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo> "$demo_dir/fixture"
python3 "$demo_dir/forkmesh/tools/verify_collaboration.py" --require-complete \
  "$demo_dir/fixture/.forkmesh/collaboration/policy.json" \
  "$demo_dir/fixture/.forkmesh/collaboration/issues.ndjson"
echo "exit=$?"
```

Exit 0 means every event's signature verified against the committed policy and
nothing is pending or rejected; 3 means something was rejected or pending (the
`audit` block names it); 2 means unreadable input. `--policy POLICY LOG` is the
equivalent flag form.

- **Repository evidence (local run, 2026-09-16):** the exporter over this
  repository's own 665 issue records, signed with a throwaway key kept in
  `/tmp`, imported 663 issues in 30 s and skipped #409 and #579 (titles over
  512 bytes). Legacy signature status: 575 `valid`, 26 `invalid`, 62
  `unavailable`. `verify_collaboration.py --require-complete` exited 0 in 5 s
  with `accepted: 663`, `rejected: 0`, `pending: 0`. The throwaway key is not
  the flagship's authority, so nothing from that run is committed and it proves
  the pipeline, not authorship.
- **Repository evidence (local rehearsal of the full path, 2026-09-27):** the
  681 issue records copied into a fresh local repository, exported with a
  throwaway `/tmp` key (679 imported in 41 s, #409 and #579 skipped; 583
  `valid`, 26 `invalid`, 70 `unavailable`), committed, pushed to a local bare
  repository, and fetched with `git clone --depth 1 file://…` (shallow, one
  commit). The visitor block's verifier exited 0 in 7 s with `accepted: 679`,
  `rejected: 0`, `pending: 0`; changing one field in the first log line made it
  exit 3. This shows the owner and visitor steps work as written. It is not the
  acceptance evidence, because the repository is local and the key is no
  repository's authority.
- **Measured fact:** of six `invalid` records spot-checked, three open events
  verify under an earlier issue number (#133 and #134 signed as 131, #140 as
  139) and three match no number from 0 to 999. **Inference:** renumbering an
  issue at merge invalidates its original open signature. The export reports
  that honestly instead of hiding it.
- **Repository evidence:** `app/tests/test_export_collaboration_log.py` pins
  the legacy content canonicalization to the Worker's `issue_event_content` and
  checks that the log verifies offline, that tampering exits 3, and that export
  is byte-deterministic.
- **Missing proof:** the disposable public repository, with the policy and log
  committed by its owner's authority key, and a fresh `git clone --depth 1`
  transcript of the visitor block above exiting 0. An agent cannot create a
  public repository or hold its owner's key, so a human owner must take this
  step.

### Distinctive preservation path — blocked

**Deployed observation (2026-09-30):** the homepage no longer has a “Run the
proof” link. `/docs/product-promise/` still exists; its steps need an account
and operator control to stop a `forkmesh-mirror-node`, and only the final clone
is runnable by a visitor.

The launch path stays blocked until a human can do this in under five minutes
from a clean machine:

1. Open a public fixture page showing the stable clone URL, expected commit,
   source mirror, a mirror run by a different operator, signed health freshness,
   and an availability proof reading `quorum`.
2. Clone from the stable URL and record `HEAD`.
3. Watch an operator-run drill remove only the source from eligibility; the
   visitor gets no host authority.
4. Clone the same URL into a second directory and compare `HEAD`.
5. Verify one signed issue or pull event from the clone with a shipped verifier
   and a committed policy, then watch the source recover.

Do not simulate failover with two local bare repositories; that proves Git, not
ForkMesh.
